original_scope.summary:
Rebuild, as native Rust Handshake tools hosted in the WP-KERNEL-011 shell, the two editor surfaces that currently exist as React (KERNEL-009 'Notes'): (1) the VS-Code-class CODE editor and (2) the Obsidian/Notion-class RICH-TEXT + knowledge editor. Achieve FULL feature parity with what KERNEL-009 already delivered in React, then make them deeply interconnect with each other and with CKC (Pillar 18/19 + KERNEL-005) and Loom (Pillar 7). REUSE the existing Rust backend (handshake_core: knowledge documents, loom, code-nav, CRDT, search) - do NOT rebuild backend storage/APIs. The legacy React editors (app/src) stay as the parity reference until native parity is proven, then are retired. original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement the foundational text buffer and syntax highlighting layer for the native code editor panel. This is the root MT that all other E1 MTs build on. Expected diff shape: new Rust module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/buffer.rs` (ropey-based text buffer with edit/query API), new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/highlight.rs` (tree-sitter highlight pipeline), new `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` wiring them, and integration into the egui panel struct at `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs`.

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — declares buffer and highlight submodules, exports the top-level `CodeEditorPanel` egui widget struct.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/buffer.rs` — wraps the `ropey` crate `Rope` type. Exposes: `TextBuffer::new(text: &str) -> Self`, `insert(byte_offset: usize, text: &str)`, `delete(byte_range: Range<usize>)`, `slice_to_string(line_range: Range<usize>) -> String`, `len_bytes() -> usize`, `len_lines() -> usize`, `line_to_byte(line_idx: usize) -> usize`, `byte_to_line(byte_offset: usize) -> usize`. The buffer is the sole owner of document text; all other subsystems (highlight, folding, minimap) borrow slices from it.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/highlight.rs` — uses `tree-sitter` + language grammars (start with `tree-sitter-rust` and `tree-sitter-javascript` as bundled crates; add more via a `LanguageRegistry` map keyed on file extension). Exposes `Highlighter::new(language: Language) -> Self`, `highlight(source: &[u8]) -> Vec<HighlightSpan>` where `HighlightSpan { byte_range: Range<usize>, scope: HighlightScope }`. `HighlightScope` is an enum: `Keyword`, `String`, `Comment`, `Number`, `Function`, `Type`, `Operator`, `Other`.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` (create if not yet existing) — mounts a `CodeEditorPanel` egui widget: renders visible lines from the buffer, applies highlight spans as colored text runs via `egui::RichText`, provides a stable `egui::Id` for the panel, and sets AccessKit metadata.

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `ropey = "1.6"` — battle-tested rope data structure; handles large files and incremental edits cheaply.
- `tree-sitter = "0.25"` single pinned core + `tree-sitter-language` LanguageFn shim + `tree-sitter-rust = "0.24"` + a shim-compatible `tree-sitter-javascript` + `tree-sitter-highlight` [RESEARCH-CORRECTED wf_ffa74d6d 2026-06-22 from 0.22/0.21: field converged on 0.25.x core + tree-sitter-language LanguageFn shim where grammars expose LANGUAGE: LanguageFn, decoupling grammar version from core and avoiding the duplicate-core/ABI wall as more Monaco-parity languages are added; load via the shim, NOT the deprecated language() fn] — canonical grammar crates; parse incrementally using `Parser::parse_with` and the old tree for re-use.
- `egui` text rendering: `ui.painter().galley(...)` or `ui.label(egui::RichText::new(text).color(color))` per span.
- AccessKit metadata via the existing WP-011 accessibility layer (`src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/` — `mod.rs`, `registry.rs`, `snapshot.rs`, `live.rs`): register the outer panel node as `Role::TextInput` with `author_id` = `"code_editor_buffer"` through the project's accessibility registry rather than building raw AccessKit nodes directly.

React reference: `app/src/components/MonacoCodeBlockView.tsx` — the Monaco-based code block that this native surface replaces. Study the language field, readOnly flag, and status-dispatch pattern. Note that Monaco handled highlighting internally; here tree-sitter replaces it.
Backend: No direct backend call in this MT. The buffer is purely in-process. Backend code-nav APIs are wired in MT-008. Backend access is via the existing API client `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs` (reuse only; no backend rewrite).

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Add `ropey`, `tree-sitter`, `tree-sitter-rust`, `tree-sitter-javascript` to `src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml`.
2. Implement `TextBuffer` in `buffer.rs`. Keep all methods panic-free for out-of-range inputs (clamp or return `Err`).
3. Implement `Highlighter` in `highlight.rs`. Parse the full buffer on first call; on subsequent calls pass the previous tree as `old_tree` for incremental re-parse. Map tree-sitter `Highlight` indices to `HighlightScope` using a fixed lookup table against the `highlights.scm` capture names (e.g. `keyword` -> `Keyword`, `string` -> `String`).
4. Implement `CodeEditorPanel::show(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui)` in `mod.rs`. For now render all lines (virtualization is MT-002). Use a `egui::ScrollArea` for vertical scroll. Each line: iterate spans overlapping the line, split text into colored runs, render with `egui::RichText`. Use the existing theme layer (`src/frontend/handshake_native/src/theme/` — `palette.rs`, `syntax.rs`, `egui_apply.rs`) for code background and syntax colors rather than hardcoded hex.
5. Wire `CodeEditorPanel` into the WP-011 docking surface by registering it through `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs` and placing it via `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/split_layout.rs` so it appears as a named pane.
6. Register AccessKit metadata through the existing accessibility layer (`src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/registry.rs`): an `author_id = "code_editor_panel"` `Role::GenericContainer` on the outer `Frame` and `author_id = "code_editor_text"` `Role::TextInput` on the inner text area so swarm agents can address the widget.

Dependencies/unblock conditions: None — this is the root MT. Requires `ropey` and `tree-sitter` crates available in the `handshake-native` crate.
Risk if missed: All other E1 MTs are blocked; no text foundation means no virtualization, no multi-cursor, no find/replace, no folding.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: `cargo test -p handshake-native` passes with tests for TextBuffer insert/delete/slice covering at least: empty buffer, single-line insert, multi-line insert, delete spanning lines, byte-to-line and line-to-byte round-trips.
AC-002: `cargo test -p handshake-native` passes with a test that parses a 10-line Rust snippet through Highlighter and returns at least one span with scope=Keyword and one with scope=Function.
AC-003: `cargo test -p handshake-native` passes with a test that parses a JS snippet and returns at least one span with scope=String.

AC-004: An egui_kittest screenshot of the CodeEditorPanel rendering a 5-line Rust snippet shows colored text (at least two distinct foreground colors present, verified by pixel sampling of the test image).
AC-005: The AccessKit tree exported by egui_kittest contains a node with author_id='code_editor_panel' and role=GenericContainer and a child node with author_id='code_editor_text' and role=TextInput.
AC-006: No `unwrap()` calls on buffer range operations in production code paths — all fallible operations return `Option` or `Result`.

implementation_notes: Use `ropey::Rope` not `String` from the start — retrofitting later when files are large is expensive.
tree-sitter incremental re-parse: always pass `Some(&old_tree)` to `parser.parse_with` after the first parse to get O(edit) re-parse cost.

For highlight colors, define a `fn scope_to_color(scope: HighlightScope, visuals: &egui::Visuals) -> egui::Color32` function backed by the existing theme layer (`src/frontend/handshake_native/src/theme/syntax.rs`) — keep theme-aware, not hardcoded hex.
Do not call `.to_string()` on the full rope for every frame — slice only the visible range (even before MT-002 virtualization, limit to first 1000 lines as a guard).
Wrap tree-sitter `Language` in a `Send + Sync` newtype if the egui event loop requires it.
HighlightScope must derive Clone, Debug, PartialEq for tests.

Cross-WP dependency: this MT builds on WP-011 modules (`pane_registry.rs`, `split_layout.rs`, `theme/*`, `accessibility/*`, `backend_client.rs`) already present under `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/`. These are reused, not re-created.

SALVAGE: buffer.rs + panel.rs from the prior run are high-quality and version-independent - keep/refine, do not rewrite; port highlight.rs + Cargo.toml to the 0.25.x + tree-sitter-language stack; keep the public HighlightSpan{byte_range,scope} + HighlightScope output type stable so panel.rs is unaffected.
tree-sitter safety: after porting, cargo tree -d MUST show exactly one tree-sitter core (no duplicates).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Replace the naive full-buffer render from MT-001 with a virtualized line renderer that only paints lines currently visible in the scroll viewport. This keeps frame time under 4 ms for files up to 100 000 lines. Expected diff shape: new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/virtual_lines.rs` implementing the viewport-line calculator, and changes to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` and `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` to use it.

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/virtual_lines.rs` — implements `VirtualLineLayout`. Constructor: `VirtualLineLayout::new(line_count: usize, line_height_px: f32, viewport_height_px: f32, scroll_offset_px: f32)`. Key method: `visible_range(&self) -> Range<usize>` returns the first and last line indices that intersect the viewport (inclusive), with a configurable overscan of ±8 lines. Also: `total_height_px(&self) -> f32` (line_count * line_height_px, used to size the egui ScrollArea content rect so the scrollbar thumb is correctly proportioned), `y_for_line(line: usize) -> f32` (pixel offset of a given line from the content top).
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `VirtualLineLayout` to the CodeEditorPanel state. On each `show()` call, compute the layout from the current scroll offset (read from `egui::ScrollArea::state`) and render only the visible range from the TextBuffer.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` — wrap the text area in `egui::ScrollArea::vertical().show_rows(...)` using `VirtualLineLayout::total_height_px()` as the virtual content height and `VirtualLineLayout::visible_range()` to feed the row closure.

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `egui::ScrollArea::vertical().show_rows(ui, row_height, total_rows, |ui, row_range| { ... })` — this is the idiomatic egui virtualized list API. It handles scroll-state internally and passes only the visible row range to the closure.
- `ropey::Rope::line(idx)` — O(log n) line access, so rendering only visible lines is O(visible * log N) not O(N).
- No additional crates needed beyond MT-001 dependencies.

Performance budget:
- Target: frame time for a 100 000-line Rust file (no syntax highlighting on invisible lines) must stay below 4 ms on a mid-range CPU (measured via `egui::Context::frame_time()` in a benchmark harness).
- Highlight spans: only compute tree-sitter highlights for the visible line range on each frame. Keep the full parse tree cached in `CodeEditorPanel` state; do NOT re-parse the whole file each frame — use incremental edit application.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Implement `VirtualLineLayout` in `virtual_lines.rs`. `visible_range` formula: `first = max(0, floor(scroll_offset_px / line_height_px) - overscan)`, `last = min(line_count - 1, ceil((scroll_offset_px + viewport_height_px) / line_height_px) + overscan)`.
2. In `CodeEditorPanel::show()`, replace the naive all-lines loop with `ScrollArea::vertical().show_rows(ui, line_height, buffer.len_lines(), |ui, visible_rows| { for line_idx in visible_rows { ... } })`.
3. For highlight spans: add a `highlight_cache: Option<(Vec<HighlightSpan>, usize)>` field where the usize is the buffer version counter. Recompute only when version changes. Clip the span list to the visible range before rendering each frame.
4. Expose a `perf_stats()` method on `CodeEditorPanel` returning `{ frame_lines_rendered: usize, buffer_len_lines: usize }` for the swarm diagnostics surface.
5. Add an AccessKit `author_id = "code_editor_scroll_area"` `Role::ScrollView` wrapping the virtualized area, registered via the existing WP-011 accessibility surface (reuse `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/registry.rs` for author_id registration and `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/snapshot.rs` for tree snapshot verification; do not introduce a parallel a11y mechanism).

Dependencies/unblock conditions: MT-001 must be DONE (TextBuffer and Highlighter exist). `egui::ScrollArea::show_rows` must be available (egui 0.27+).
Risk if missed: Without virtualization, opening files over ~5000 lines will cause frame drops that make the editor unusable and violate HBR-VIS frame budget.

The committed code (40b63602) stores the overscan-padded VirtualLineLayout range, which over-reports the painted window by ~8 lines and will misposition the cursor/gutter/selection overlay in MT-003+. Strengthen scroll_mid_virtualizes to assert last_visible_range() EQUALS the painted row_range (not merely contains(100)/excludes(0)).

Do not re-query `buffer.len_lines()` inside the row closure — cache it before the ScrollArea call.
Highlight cache invalidation: use a `buffer_version: u64` counter incremented on every edit; cache is valid while `highlight_cache.version == buffer_version`.
For the benchmark, use `std::time::Instant` around the egui frame call in a headless test; egui_kittest supports headless rendering via software rasterizer.
overscan constant: `const OVERSCAN_LINES: usize = 8;` defined in `virtual_lines.rs`.

FORWARD NOTE: the editable cursor/selection/multi-cursor overlay (MT-003+) must be a custom egui painter layer over the virtualized rows, NOT an egui TextEdit (TextEdit cannot virtualize and forces full materialization). Keep MT-001 HighlightSpan{byte_range,scope} output stable.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement multi-cursor editing and column/box selection parity with the React Monaco surface. Monaco supports: Alt+Click to add a cursor, Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down to add cursor above/below, Alt+Shift+drag for box selection, Ctrl+D to select the next occurrence of the current word. All four must work in the native editor. Expected diff shape: new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/cursor.rs` containing the cursor and selection model, and edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` and `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` to handle multi-cursor input and render all cursors.

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/cursor.rs` — defines `Cursor { anchor: usize, head: usize }` (byte offsets into the TextBuffer), `Selection` (alias for a `Cursor` where anchor != head), `CursorSet { cursors: Vec<Cursor> }`. Methods on `CursorSet`: `add_cursor(byte_offset: usize)` (deduplicates by offset), `remove_overlap()` (merges cursors whose selections overlap), `move_all(direction: MoveDir, buffer: &TextBuffer)` (moves all cursors), `insert_at_all(text: &str, buffer: &mut TextBuffer)` (inserts text at each cursor, adjusting subsequent cursor offsets), `delete_at_all(buffer: &mut TextBuffer)` (deletes the character/selection at each cursor). `MoveDir` enum: `Left, Right, Up, Down, LineStart, LineEnd, WordLeft, WordRight`.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `cursor_set: CursorSet` to `CodeEditorPanel`. Process egui input events: `PointerButton::Primary` click sets single cursor; `Alt` + click adds a cursor; `Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down` adds cursor above/below; `Alt+Shift` drag sets box selection (compute column range from drag start/end, add one cursor per line in range); `Ctrl+D` finds next occurrence of the word at the primary cursor and adds a selection cursor on it.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` — render all cursors as 2px vertical bars using `ui.painter().rect_filled()` at the correct pixel position (use `y_for_line` from MT-002 and character-width from the monospace font metrics). Render selections as colored rect overlays (semi-transparent). For column/box selections, render one rectangle per line in the column range.

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `egui::PointerState::button_clicked`, `egui::InputState::modifiers` — for detecting Alt+click and Ctrl+D.
- `egui::Painter::rect_filled` — draw cursor caret and selection highlight.
- `egui::FontId` and `ui.fonts().glyph_width()` — measure monospace character width for column alignment.
- No additional crates needed.
- AccessKit: add `author_id = "code_editor_cursor_{n}"` `Role::TextCursor` for each cursor (n = cursor index) via `accesskit::NodeBuilder`. Reuse the existing AccessKit integration in `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/` (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs) for node registration and tree snapshotting — do not stand up a new AccessKit pipeline.

React reference (Monaco parity surface):
- Monaco multi-cursor: Alt+Click, Ctrl+Alt+Up, Ctrl+Alt+Down, Alt+Shift drag, Ctrl+D — these are the canonical VS Code multi-cursor keybindings. The native editor must respond to the same bindings.
- `app/src/components/MonacoCodeBlockView.tsx` — Monaco handles multi-cursor internally; here the native implementation must replicate the behavior.
- `app/src/lib/editor/editor_keymap.ts` — the keymap system used by the rich editor; the code editor has its own keymap (see MT-010) but Ctrl+D and Alt+Click must be wired now as they are core to multi-cursor.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Implement `CursorSet` in `cursor.rs`. Keep cursors sorted by `head` byte offset at all times (sort after each mutation). `remove_overlap` merges any two cursors where one's selection range contains the other's head.
2. In `CodeEditorPanel::show()`, after the ScrollArea, check `ui.input(|i| i.events.clone())` for: `egui::Event::PointerButton { button: Primary, pressed: true, modifiers: { alt: true, .. } }` -> add cursor at clicked position; `egui::Event::Key { key: D, modifiers: { ctrl: true }, pressed: true }` -> Ctrl+D logic (see step 4).
3. For Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down: detect `egui::Event::Key { key: Up/Down, modifiers: { ctrl: true, alt: true }, pressed: true }` -> add cursor one line above/below each existing cursor.
4. Ctrl+D implementation: get the word at the primary cursor's head byte offset using `buffer.word_at(byte_offset)` (implement this helper: scan left/right from offset while char is alphanumeric or `_`). Search the buffer bytes for the next occurrence after the primary cursor. Add a new cursor with anchor=occurrence_start, head=occurrence_end.
5. Box/column selection: track `drag_start: Option<(line, col)>` in CodeEditorPanel state. On Alt+Shift drag, compute the column range as `(min_col..=max_col)` and the line range as `(min_line..=max_line)`. Replace cursor_set with one cursor per line in the range, each selecting from column start to column end on that line.
6. Render: for each cursor in cursor_set, compute pixel rect (x from column * glyph_width, y from `y_for_line(line)`, w=2, h=line_height for caret; x from selection_start_col * glyph_width, w = selection_width_chars * glyph_width for selection rect). Use `egui::Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied(100, 149, 237, 80)` for selection overlay.
7. On text input (key events that produce chars), call `cursor_set.insert_at_all(text, &mut buffer)` — must adjust each subsequent cursor's byte offset by the byte length of the inserted text.

Reuse pointers (real WP-011 modules under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/):
- Shared selection/clipboard/command bus: reuse `command_registry.rs` + `event_bus.rs` for dispatching the multi-cursor commands (Alt+Click add-cursor, Ctrl+D select-next-occurrence, Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down add-cursor-above/below) and for broadcasting selection-change events; do not invent a new interaction bus.
- Command palette / Ctrl+D wiring: register the multi-cursor commands through `command_palette.rs` + `command_registry.rs` so they are discoverable and rebindable.
- AccessKit cursor nodes: reuse `accessibility/` (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs).

Dependencies/unblock conditions: MT-001 DONE (TextBuffer exists with byte-offset API).
Risk if missed: Multi-cursor is a core VS Code parity feature; operators who use column-select for bulk edits will be blocked. MT-004 (find/replace) and MT-010 (keymap) both build on the cursor model.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: `cargo test -p handshake-native cursor` passes — tests: add two cursors, verify both present; add overlapping cursors, verify merged; insert text with two cursors, verify both insertions happened and offsets are correct after the second insertion.
AC-002: `cargo test -p handshake-native cursor_column_select` passes — test: column select lines 2-4 columns 3-7 on a 5-line buffer, verify 3 cursors each with correct anchor/head byte offsets.

AC-003: `cargo test -p handshake-native ctrl_d` passes — test: buffer 'foo\nfoo\nbar', cursor at line 1 col 1, Ctrl+D adds selection at line 2 col 0-3 (second 'foo' occurrence), second Ctrl+D wraps to line 1.
AC-004: egui_kittest interactive test simulates Alt+Click at two positions and verifies two cursor nodes in the AccessKit tree (author_id='code_editor_cursor_0' and 'code_editor_cursor_1').
AC-005: egui_kittest screenshot shows two distinct cursor carets (two vertical pixel columns of cursor color) for a two-cursor state.
AC-006: `insert_at_all` with two cursors at offsets 0 and 5 inserting 'X' results in buffer text with 'X' at position 0 and 'X' at position 6 (offset adjusted by 1 for the first insertion).
proof_targets: PT-001: `cargo test -p handshake-native cursor` — GREEN, logged.
PT-002: `cargo test -p handshake-native cursor_column_select` — GREEN, logged.
PT-003: `cargo test -p handshake-native ctrl_d` — GREEN, logged.
PT-004: egui_kittest test `multi_cursor_accesskit` (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_multi_cursor_accesskit.rs) — AccessKit JSON dump contains both cursor_0 and cursor_1 nodes.
PT-005: egui_kittest screenshot `test_output/MT-003-two-cursors.png` pixel-verified for two caret columns.
implementation_notes: Cursor byte offsets must always be clamped to `0..=buffer.len_bytes()` — never allow an out-of-bounds cursor.
After every CursorSet mutation, call `remove_overlap()` then re-sort by head offset.
For `insert_at_all`: process cursors in reverse order by head offset so earlier insertions don't invalidate later offsets.
Character width for column alignment: use `ui.fonts(|f| f.glyph_width(&FontId::monospace(font_size), ' '))` — all monospace chars have the same width.
Do not use `egui::TextEdit` — we own the text buffer and render it manually.

Cross-WP dependency: this MT builds on the WP-KERNEL-011 native shell. The TextBuffer (MT-001 of this WP) plus the WP-011 AccessKit pipeline in `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/` and the command bus in `command_registry.rs` + `event_bus.rs` must already exist; wire the multi-cursor commands through those existing surfaces rather than creating new ones.

POSITIONING-UNIT DEPENDENCY (KERNEL_BUILDER gate 2026-06-22, from the MT-002 AC-007 harden): MT-002 zeroed item_spacing.y on the scroll-area ui so egui row-height == sans-spacing line_height, and last_visible_range()/perf now report egui ScrollArea::show_rows ACTUAL painted row_range. MT-003 caret/selection positioning MUST use the SAME units: y_for_line(line) (= line*line_height, sans spacing) for vertical, the monospace glyph_width from the SAME FontId the renderer uses for horizontal, and render only cursors within the painted row_range (last_visible_range()) so carets align exactly with rendered glyphs. Do NOT reintroduce a with-spacing vs sans-spacing unit mismatch - that was the MT-002 scroll-to-line bug.

CURSOR MODEL (research provenance wf_ffa74d6d): Cursor{anchor,head} byte offsets + CursorSet{Vec<Cursor>} IS the field-converged Helix Selection model - keep it. The reverse-order insert_at_all offset adjustment is acceptable for MT-003 multi-cursor insert/delete; a LATER MT MAY generalize to a Helix-style OT Transaction position-mapping for uniform edit/undo handling (not required here). Continue to render carets/selections via ui.painter() over the virtualized rows; never egui::TextEdit.

Goal: Implement in-file find/replace with regex support, matching the feature set of the React editor's find panel (driven by `app/src/lib/editor/editor_find_request.ts` and `app/src/lib/editor/code_block_find_registry.ts`). The panel appears at the top of the CodeEditorPanel when triggered (Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H). Expected diff shape: new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/find_replace.rs` (search engine + match model), edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` (find panel state), and `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` (find panel UI rendering).

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/find_replace.rs` — defines `FindQuery { pattern: String, case_sensitive: bool, whole_word: bool, is_regex: bool }` (matches `EditorFindOptions` in the React reference). Implements `FindEngine::search(query: &FindQuery, buffer: &TextBuffer) -> Vec<Match>` where `Match { byte_range: Range<usize>, line: usize, col: usize }`. For regex: use the `regex` crate. For plain text: use `memchr` or `str::find` iteration. For whole-word: check that chars immediately before and after the match are not alphanumeric or `_`. For case-insensitive plain: lowercase both needle and haystack. `FindEngine::replace_one(buffer: &mut TextBuffer, m: &Match, replacement: &str)` and `replace_all(buffer: &mut TextBuffer, matches: &[Match], replacement: &str)` — replace_all processes matches in reverse order to preserve byte offsets.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `find_state: Option<FindState>` to `CodeEditorPanel`. `FindState { query: FindQuery, matches: Vec<Match>, current_match: usize, replace_text: String, show_replace: bool }`. Methods: `open_find(show_replace: bool)`, `close_find()`, `next_match()`, `prev_match()`, `replace_current()`, `replace_all()`. Opening find with an active cursor selection pre-populates the query with the selected text.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` — render the find bar as a `egui::Frame` pinned to the top-right of the editor area (VS Code style: Ctrl+F opens in a floating widget, not a side panel). The bar contains: a `egui::TextEdit` for the query, toggle buttons for case/whole-word/regex, Next/Prev buttons, a match counter (`N of M`), and when `show_replace=true` a second TextEdit for replacement and Replace/Replace-All buttons. Render match highlights in the text area as colored overlays (use a distinct highlight color from selection color, e.g. yellow for matches, orange for current match).

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `regex = "1"` — for regex pattern compilation and matching; compile once per query change, cache in `FindState`.
- `memchr` — optional but fast for plain-text byte search.
- `egui::TextEdit::singleline` — for the find/replace input fields.
- `egui::Button` — for Next, Prev, Replace, Replace-All.
- AccessKit (reuse existing `accessibility/` module — accessibility/mod.rs, accessibility/registry.rs, accessibility/live.rs, accessibility/snapshot.rs): `author_id = "code_editor_find_bar"` `Role::SearchBox` on the find input; `author_id = "code_editor_replace_bar"` `Role::TextInput` on the replace input; `author_id = "code_editor_find_next"` `Role::Button` on the Next button.

React reference files:
- `app/src/lib/editor/editor_find_request.ts` — `EditorFindOptions` type: `{ query: string, caseSensitive: boolean, wholeWord: boolean, isRegex: boolean }`. Port this as the Rust `FindQuery` struct (field names use snake_case).
- `app/src/lib/editor/code_block_find_registry.ts` — the registry that lets the document-wide find panel reveal matches inside a Monaco code block. The native equivalent is that `FindEngine::search` operates on the `TextBuffer` directly; no registry needed since the editor owns its buffer.
- `app/src/lib/editor/editor_keymap.ts` lines 38-40 — `FIND_OPEN_ACTION = 'find.open'`, `REPLACE_OPEN_ACTION = 'replace.open'`. Wire these as Ctrl+F and Ctrl+H in the code editor keymap, registered through the existing `command_registry.rs` command system (MT-010 will formalize; pre-wire here as direct key handlers).

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Implement `FindEngine` in `find_replace.rs`. For regex: `regex::Regex::new(&query.pattern)` — return empty match list on compile error and surface the error string in `FindState`. For whole-word: add `\b` anchors around the pattern or check adjacent chars after match.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement code folding derived from the tree-sitter parse tree. Foldable regions are identified from tree-sitter node types (function bodies, class bodies, block statements, if/else branches, comment blocks). Folded regions are collapsed to a single summary line with an ellipsis. The gutter (rendered in MT-007) shows fold triangles; this MT only computes fold regions and applies them to the virtual line layout. Expected diff shape: new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/folding.rs`, edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` and `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs`.

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/folding.rs` — defines `FoldRegion { start_line: usize, end_line: usize, folded: bool, label: String }` where `label` is the first line of the region plus `...` (e.g. `fn main() {…}`). Implements `FoldProvider::compute(tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, buffer: &TextBuffer) -> Vec<FoldRegion>` — walks the tree-sitter syntax tree using `tree.root_node().children()` recursively, identifies nodes whose type is in a configurable set (`FoldableNodeTypes`), and extracts their start/end row from `node.start_position().row` / `node.end_position().row`. Returns only regions spanning at least 2 lines. Also: `FoldSet { regions: Vec<FoldRegion> }` with methods `toggle(start_line: usize)`, `is_line_visible(line: usize) -> bool` (returns false if the line falls inside a folded region that is not the start line), `visible_line_to_buffer_line(visible_line: usize) -> usize` (maps from visible (post-fold) line index to actual buffer line index, accounting for collapsed regions).
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `fold_set: FoldSet` to `CodeEditorPanel`. After each buffer edit or tree-sitter re-parse, call `FoldProvider::compute` and update `fold_set`. In `show()`, wrap the `VirtualLineLayout` visible_range computation with `FoldSet::is_line_visible` filtering so folded lines are skipped.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` — in the line rendering loop, when the current line is the start line of a folded region, render the summary label line (first line text + `…`) instead of the actual line, and skip all subsequent lines until `end_line`. The gutter click handler (for fold triangles, to be rendered in MT-007) calls `fold_set.toggle(start_line)`.

Foldable node types (initial set for Rust and JS):
- Rust: `function_item`, `impl_item`, `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `block`, `match_expression`, `use_declaration` (group).
- JS/TS: `function_declaration`, `arrow_function`, `class_declaration`, `block_statement`, `object`, `array`.
- Store in a `HashMap<&'static str, &'static [&'static str]>` keyed by language id.

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `tree-sitter` — already a dependency from MT-001. Use `Node::kind()`, `Node::start_position()`, `Node::end_position()`, `Node::children()` cursor API.
- No additional crates needed.
- AccessKit: add `author_id = "code_editor_fold_{start_line}"` `Role::TreeItem` nodes for each foldable region, with `actions: [Action::Expand, Action::Collapse]` depending on fold state. Reuse the AccessKit integration in `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/` (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs) from WP-011 rather than introducing a new accessibility surface.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Implement `FoldProvider::compute` using a tree-sitter `TreeCursor` traversal (more efficient than recursive children). Push a `FoldRegion` whenever `cursor.node().kind()` is in `FoldableNodeTypes` for the current language and `end_row - start_row >= 1`.
2. Sort `FoldSet::regions` by `start_line` ascending. `is_line_visible`: binary-search for the last region with `start_line <= line`; if found and `folded == true` and `line > region.start_line` and `line <= region.end_line`, return false.
3. `visible_line_to_buffer_line`: iterate regions in order, accumulate skipped lines (for each folded region before the visible line, add `region.end_line - region.start_line` to a running offset), return `visible_line + offset`.
4. In the rendering loop: iterate visible line indices from VirtualLineLayout, map each to buffer line via `visible_line_to_buffer_line`, render normally unless the buffer line is the start of a folded region, in which case render the fold label.
5. Keyboard shortcut for fold/unfold: Ctrl+Shift+[ folds the region at the cursor; Ctrl+Shift+] unfolds. Wire these in the code editor key handler (MT-010 will formalize; pre-wire here).
6. Total line count for VirtualLineLayout must account for folds: compute `visible_line_count` as `buffer.len_lines() - sum(folded_region.end_line - folded_region.start_line for all folded regions)` and pass this to `VirtualLineLayout::new`.

Dependencies/unblock conditions: MT-001 (tree-sitter parse tree available in CodeEditorPanel), MT-002 (VirtualLineLayout — folding modifies the effective line count that it receives). Cross-WP: the AccessKit accessibility surface (accessibility/*) comes from WP-011 and is reused, not rebuilt.
Risk if missed: Large files (thousands of lines) are harder to navigate without folding. The gutter (MT-007) renders fold triangles and needs the fold region list.

AC-003: `cargo test -p handshake-native fold_set_mapping` passes — tests: visible_line_to_buffer_line with one folded region of 5 lines correctly offsets buffer lines after the region.

AC-005: AccessKit tree contains a node with author_id='code_editor_fold_0' and role=TreeItem and action=Expand when that region is folded.
AC-006: Toggle fold twice returns to original unfolded state (idempotency test).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement three navigation aids that port the React editor workbench chrome (MT-245 era) into the native editor: (1) a minimap panel on the right side of the editor showing a scaled-down view of the whole file with the current viewport highlighted, (2) an outline/heading tree panel (symbols extracted from tree-sitter: functions, classes, structs) with click-to-scroll, (3) a go-to-line palette command (Ctrl+G) that opens a numeric input and scrolls the editor. Expected diff shape: new `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/minimap.rs`, new `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/outline.rs`, edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` and `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs`.

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/minimap.rs` — `Minimap` struct. `Minimap::render(ui: &mut egui::Ui, buffer: &TextBuffer, highlight_spans: &[HighlightSpan], visible_range: Range<usize>, total_lines: usize)` draws a narrow panel (default width: 80px, configurable) with one pixel row per file line (or one per N lines if file is very large — use `max(1, total_lines / panel_height_px)` as the compression ratio). Each row is colored with the average highlight color of that line's spans (or a neutral gray for unhighlighted lines). Draws a semi-transparent viewport rect over the rows corresponding to `visible_range`. Click on the minimap scrolls the editor to that line. Hover shows a tooltip with the line number.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/outline.rs` — `OutlineProvider::compute(tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, buffer: &TextBuffer) -> Vec<OutlineItem>` where `OutlineItem { kind: OutlineKind, name: String, line: usize, indent: usize }`. `OutlineKind` enum: `Function`, `Method`, `Class`, `Struct`, `Enum`, `Constant`, `Module`. Extracts named identifiers from tree-sitter node types (e.g. for Rust: `function_item` -> name from child `identifier`, `impl_item` -> type name). `OutlinePanel::show(ui: &mut Ui, items: &[OutlineItem], on_navigate: impl FnOnce(usize))` renders a collapsible tree list; clicking an item calls `on_navigate(item.line)` to scroll the editor.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `outline_items: Vec<OutlineItem>` (recomputed on tree re-parse), `show_outline: bool`, `show_minimap: bool`, `goto_line_state: Option<GotoLineState>` (where `GotoLineState { input: String, parsed: Option<usize> }`). Methods: `open_goto_line()` opens the palette; Ctrl+G triggers it.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` — split the panel into a horizontal layout: `[outline panel (optional, left)] [editor area (center)] [minimap (optional, right)]`. The go-to-line palette renders as a modal overlay centered in the editor area (small `egui::Window`).

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `egui::Painter::rect_filled` — for minimap rows and viewport indicator.
- `egui::ScrollArea` — for the outline panel (outline can be long).
- `egui::Window` — for the go-to-line palette modal.
- `egui::CollapsingHeader` — for the outline tree hierarchy.
- AccessKit (reuse the existing `accessibility/` subsystem — `accessibility/mod.rs`, `accessibility/registry.rs`, `accessibility/live.rs`, `accessibility/snapshot.rs`): `author_id = "code_editor_minimap"` `Role::ScrollBar` on the minimap (clicking scrolls); `author_id = "code_editor_outline"` `Role::Tree` on the outline panel; `author_id = "code_editor_goto_line"` `Role::TextInput` on the go-to-line input.

React reference files:
- `app/src/harness/editor_workbench_chrome_harness.tsx` — `ED-NAV-004` (prose outline panel heading tree + click-to-scroll) and `ED-NAV-006` (go-to-line inside code block from palette). The native implementation provides the same features for the code editor surface.
- `app/src/lib/editor/editor_chrome.ts` — `DocumentChromeStatus` and the status bar; the outline panel in the native editor is analogous to the heading tree in the rich editor.
- `app/src/harness/editor_workbench_chrome_harness.tsx` lines 9-10 — `ED-NAV-006: go-to-line inside the focused embedded code block (palette)`. Native equivalent is the go-to-line palette (Ctrl+G).

Reuse pointers (existing WP-011 native modules under `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/`):
- Command-palette / Ctrl+G command registration: reuse `command_registry.rs` + `command_palette.rs` to register and surface the go-to-line command.
- Shared selection/clipboard/command/event bus: reuse `command_registry.rs` + `event_bus.rs` (there is NO shared `interaction_bus.rs`).
- AccessKit nodes: reuse the `accessibility/` subsystem (`accessibility/mod.rs`, `accessibility/registry.rs`, `accessibility/live.rs`, `accessibility/snapshot.rs`).

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Minimap: paint each row as a 1px-tall, 80px-wide rect. Color: `scope_to_color(dominant_scope_of_line, visuals)` if any highlight spans cover the line, else `visuals.window_fill()` darkened by 10%. For very large files (>5000 lines), draw one pixel per `ceil(total_lines / panel_height_px)` lines (group average color). Use `ui.input(|i| i.pointer.press_origin())` on the minimap Rect to detect click-to-scroll.
2. Outline: use the same `TreeCursor` as `FoldProvider` (potentially share a single tree traversal for both). Compute indent by tracking depth in the TreeCursor walk.
3. Go-to-line: open with Ctrl+G. The modal window has a single `TextEdit::singleline` pre-populated with the current cursor line. On Enter: parse the input as `usize`, subtract 1 for 0-indexing, clamp to `0..buffer.len_lines()`, set the editor scroll offset to `y_for_line(target_line)` and move the primary cursor to byte offset of that line.
4. Layout split: use `egui::SidePanel::left("outline").resizable(true).default_width(180)` for the outline and `egui::SidePanel::right("minimap").resizable(false).exact_width(80)` for the minimap. The center is the main editor ScrollArea.
5. Outline click-to-scroll: `on_navigate(line)` updates `CodeEditorPanel::scroll_to_line = Some(line)`. In the next `show()` call, if `scroll_to_line.is_some()`, compute the scroll offset and set it on the ScrollArea state via `scroll_area.scroll_to_row(...)`.

Dependencies/unblock conditions: MT-001 (tree-sitter tree), MT-002 (VirtualLineLayout and visible_range), MT-005 (fold region list needed to correctly compute visible line count for minimap).
Risk if missed: Navigation in large files is poor without minimap and outline — a significant operator workflow deficiency for code review tasks.

implementation_notes: Minimap rendering cost: for a 10k-line file at 80px panel height, we paint 80 rows of 80px each = 6400 rect calls. Use a single `egui::Shape::Vec` batch to reduce draw calls.

Outline reuse: share the tree traversal with FoldProvider — both walk the same tree. Consider a single `TreeAnalyzer::analyze(tree, buffer) -> TreeAnalysis { fold_regions, outline_items }` function called once per tree re-parse.
SidePanel memory: egui stores SidePanel state by Id. Use stable Ids: `egui::Id::new("code_editor_outline_panel")` and `egui::Id::new("code_editor_minimap_panel")`.
Minimap viewport indicator: use `egui::Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied(255, 255, 255, 30)` overlay rect covering the visible_range rows.

Cross-WP dependency: this MT depends on WP-011 native shell modules (`command_registry.rs`, `command_palette.rs`, `event_bus.rs`, and the `accessibility/` subsystem) which already exist under `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/`; register the Ctrl+G go-to-line command through `command_registry.rs` rather than introducing a new command bus.

POSITIONING + FOLD CORRECTNESS (from MT-002 AC-007 + MT-005 harden 4300e976): minimap viewport indicator, outline click-to-scroll, and go-to-line MUST use the MT-002-corrected units (sans-spacing line_height, y_for_line, the corrected scroll_to_line / actual painted row_range) AND the MT-005-corrected FoldSet::visible_line_count + visible_line_to_buffer_line. The nested-fold double-count was fixed - use visible_line_count, do NOT reintroduce a naive per-region collapsed sum. Minimap-click->line and go-to-line must map through the fold-aware visible<->buffer line mapping so navigation lands on the correct line when folds are active.

TREE TRAVERSAL REUSE (MC-002 / RISK-002): MT-005 FoldProvider already walks the highlighter's cached tree via Highlighter::tree() (added MT-005). Prefer a single TreeAnalyzer::analyze(tree, buffer) -> {fold_regions, outline_items} per buffer_version, or have OutlineProvider reuse the same TreeCursor pattern + Highlighter::tree(), rather than a third independent parse.

ACCESSKIT VARIANT: if accesskit 0.21.1 (pinned by eframe 0.33) lacks the literal Role::ScrollBar / Role::Tree / Role::TextInput named here, use the field-correct nearest existing variant and document inline (as MT-003 used Caret, MT-005 confirmed TreeItem). The ACs assert the author_id, not the literal role string.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement the editor gutter: a narrow left-margin strip that renders line numbers, diagnostic severity icons (error/warning/info sourced from backend diagnostics), fold triangles (toggle fold state from MT-005), and breakpoint toggles (click to add/remove a breakpoint; breakpoints are sent to the debug adapter protocol client when it is attached). Expected diff shape: new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/gutter.rs`, edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` and `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs`.

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/gutter.rs` — `GutterConfig { show_line_numbers: bool, show_fold_triangles: bool, show_diagnostics: bool, show_breakpoints: bool }`. `GutterMarker { line: usize, kind: GutterMarkerKind }` where `GutterMarkerKind` is an enum: `Diagnostic(DiagnosticSeverity)`, `Breakpoint`, `FoldTriangle(bool)` (bool = is_open). `Gutter::render(ui, visible_range, buffer, markers: &[GutterMarker], config: &GutterConfig, on_fold_click: impl FnMut(usize), on_breakpoint_click: impl FnMut(usize)) -> GutterResponse` — renders the gutter as a left strip. Returns `GutterResponse { fold_toggled: Option<usize>, breakpoint_toggled: Option<usize> }`. `DiagnosticSeverity` enum: `Error`, `Warning`, `Info`, `Hint`.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/breakpoints.rs` — `BreakpointSet { lines: HashSet<usize> }`. Methods: `toggle(line)`, `iter() -> impl Iterator<Item=usize>`, `contains(line) -> bool`. Also defines `BreakpointEvent { file_path: String, line: usize, action: BreakpointAction }` where `BreakpointAction { Set, Clear }`. When a breakpoint is toggled, the `CodeEditorPanel` should publish a `BreakpointEvent` to a channel that the debug adapter client (future MT) will consume. The breakpoint publish channel reuses the existing `event_bus.rs` pattern from WP-011 for in-app event fan-out.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `gutter_config: GutterConfig`, `breakpoint_set: BreakpointSet`, `diagnostic_markers: Vec<GutterMarker>` to `CodeEditorPanel`. `diagnostic_markers` is populated by the LSP client (MT-008 will push diagnostics here; this MT prepares the slot). Wire `GutterResponse` from the gutter render call to `fold_set.toggle()` and `breakpoint_set.toggle()` in each frame.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs` — render the gutter as a fixed-width left strip (default 52px: ~4 chars for line number + icon columns) using a custom painter area. Render line numbers as right-aligned gray text. Render diagnostic icons as colored dots (red for error, yellow for warning, blue for info). Render fold triangles as `▶` (collapsed) or `▼` (expanded). Render breakpoints as filled red circles.

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `egui::Painter::circle_filled` — for breakpoint dots.
- `egui::Painter::text` — for line numbers and fold triangles.
- `egui::Painter::rect_filled` — for diagnostic severity color bars (VS Code style: a 3px left border on the line).
- `egui::Response::on_hover_text` — for diagnostic hover tooltip (show the diagnostic message).
- `std::sync::mpsc::channel` — for BreakpointEvent publishing to the debug adapter.
- AccessKit (reuse the WP-011 accessibility/ module — accessibility/registry.rs + accessibility/live.rs for node registration): `author_id = "code_editor_gutter"` `Role::Group` on the gutter strip; `author_id = "code_editor_breakpoint_{line}"` `Role::ToggleButton` on each breakpoint toggle; `author_id = "code_editor_diagnostic_{line}"` `Role::StaticText` on each diagnostic marker.

Diagnostics source (this MT): `diagnostic_markers` is initialized as empty. MT-008 will populate it via `CodeEditorPanel::push_diagnostics(markers: Vec<GutterMarker>)`. This MT must define the `push_diagnostics` method stub so MT-008 can call it without a re-implementation.

Debug adapter integration: This MT does NOT implement the debug adapter client. It only publishes `BreakpointEvent` to a `std::sync::mpsc::Sender<BreakpointEvent>`. The receiver is a stub `None` until the debug adapter MT is implemented. Guard all send calls with `if let Some(sender) = &self.breakpoint_sender { sender.send(event).ok(); }`.

React reference files:
- `app/src/components/operator/ProblemsView.tsx` — displays diagnostics from the backend `listProblemGroups` API. The gutter diagnostic markers in the native editor consume the same backend data (see MT-008 for the API binding).
- `app/src/lib/monaco/code_intelligence.ts` lines 447-484 — `refreshHandshakeCodeIntelligenceMarkers`: sets Monaco marker data from backend symbol staleness. The native gutter must accept equivalent marker data from MT-008's LSP client.
- `app/src/harness/mt249_code_intelligence_harness.tsx` lines 292-297 — `monaco.editor.getModelMarkers({ owner: 'handshake-code-intelligence' })` — proof that markers are per-editor; native equivalent is `CodeEditorPanel::diagnostic_markers`.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Gutter width: compute from the number of digits in `buffer.len_lines()` using `(buffer.len_lines() as f64).log10().ceil() as usize + 1` chars, multiplied by the monospace char width from MT-003.
2. Render order per line (left to right): breakpoint circle, fold triangle, line number, diagnostic icon. Each occupies a fixed sub-column within the gutter width.
3. Interaction: use `ui.interact(rect, id, egui::Sense::click())` for each clickable gutter row. The entire line row in the gutter is clickable for breakpoints; only the fold triangle sub-rect is clickable for fold.
4. Diagnostic hover: iterate `diagnostic_markers` for the hovered line; collect all messages and join with '\n' for the hover tooltip.
5. `push_diagnostics` method: replace `self.diagnostic_markers = markers; self.buffer_version += 1` (increment version to trigger highlight cache invalidation is not needed for diagnostics, but flushing the list is required).

Dependencies/unblock conditions: MT-001 (buffer, line count), MT-002 (VirtualLineLayout, visible line range — gutter must render only visible lines), MT-005 (fold_set — gutter reads fold state for fold triangle direction). MT-008 depends on the `push_diagnostics` stub defined here.
Risk if missed: No gutter means no line numbers (poor navigation), no diagnostic visibility (operators can't see errors inline), no breakpoints (debug workflow broken).

implementation_notes: Gutter painter area: use `ui.painter_at(gutter_rect)` to paint inside the gutter without affecting the main editor layout.
Line number color: `visuals.weak_text_color()` — slightly dimmer than main text, matching VS Code convention.
Diagnostic icon: a 6px diameter circle at `(gutter_rect.right() - 8, y_for_line(line) + line_height / 2)`. Color: Error=Color32::RED, Warning=Color32::YELLOW, Info=Color32::from_rgb(100,149,237).

Fold triangle: render as a small right-pointing triangle (▶ U+25B6) or down-pointing (▼ U+25BC) using `painter.text()`. Unicode rendering in egui requires the font to include these glyphs — use the bundled Noto Sans or FiraMono and verify glyph support.

BreakpointEvent channel: initialize the channel in `CodeEditorPanel::new()` and store `sender: Option<mpsc::Sender<BreakpointEvent>>`. Expose a `subscribe_breakpoints() -> mpsc::Receiver<BreakpointEvent>` method for the debug adapter to call.

DO NOT increment buffer_version on push_diagnostics - that counter triggers the MT-002 highlight-cache / tree re-parse, and bumping it on every diagnostics push would needlessly re-highlight. If using std::sync::mpsc instead, use an UNBOUNDED mpsc::channel + sender.send(event).ok() - std mpsc::Sender has NO try_send (try_send is SyncSender on a bounded channel). RISK-003/MC-003 'try_send' is loose terminology; the real intent is non-blocking + discard on dropped receiver, which send().ok() satisfies.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement an LSP (Language Server Protocol) client for the native code editor that provides: completion (triggered on `.`, `:`, `_` or Ctrl+Space), hover documentation (on cursor dwell), go-to-definition, find-references, and diagnostics (pushing results to the gutter from MT-007 via `push_diagnostics`). Additionally, bind the existing Handshake backend knowledge/code-nav APIs (`/knowledge/code/symbols`, `/knowledge/code/symbols/{id}`, `/knowledge/code/symbols/{id}/references`, `/knowledge/code/files/{path}/lens`) as a fallback intelligence source when no language server is attached. Port the `CodeSymbolPanel` component and `code_intelligence.ts` logic.

Expected diff shape: new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/lsp_client.rs` (LSP JSON-RPC client over stdio to a language server process), new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/code_nav.rs` (Handshake backend code-nav API calls via the existing HTTP client), edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` (wiring completion and hover popups into the editor panel), and `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/editor_view.rs` (completion popup widget and hover tooltip widget).

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/lsp_client.rs` — `LspClient { process: Option<Child>, sender: mpsc::Sender<LspRequest>, receiver: mpsc::Receiver<LspResponse> }`. Uses `tower-lsp` client-side or raw JSON-RPC over stdio. Implements: `initialize(root_uri)`, `did_open(uri, language_id, text)`, `did_change(uri, version, changes)`, `completion(uri, position) -> Vec<CompletionItem>`, `hover(uri, position) -> Option<HoverResult>`, `goto_definition(uri, position) -> Option<Location>`, `references(uri, position) -> Vec<Location>`, `publish_diagnostics callback -> Vec<LspDiagnostic>`. All requests are async; results are returned via a `tokio::sync::oneshot` channel. The LSP process is launched lazily on first `did_open`. If no language server is configured or the process fails to start, all methods return empty/None gracefully.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/code_nav.rs` — `CodeNavClient` that wraps the Handshake backend HTTP calls. Ports the logic from `app/src/lib/monaco/code_intelligence.ts`. Methods: `lookup_symbols(workspace_id: &str, prefix: &str, limit: usize) -> Vec<CodeSymbolNavProjection>`, `get_symbol(entity_id: &str) -> Option<CodeSymbolResponse>`, `get_references(entity_id: &str) -> CodeSymbolReferencesResponse`, `get_file_lens(workspace_id: &str, path: &str, content_hash: &str, parser_version: &str) -> CodeFileLensResponse`. REUSE the existing `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs` HTTP client for all backend code-nav calls (do NOT introduce a second HTTP stack); add the code-nav routes as new methods on that client. Reuse `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/error.rs` for error typing.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `lsp_client: Option<LspClient>`, `code_nav_client: CodeNavClient`, `completion_state: Option<CompletionState>`, `hover_state: Option<HoverState>`. On each `did_change` event (after TextBuffer edit), call `lsp_client.did_change(...)` async. On cursor dwell (500ms without movement), trigger `hover(cursor_position)`. On Ctrl+Space or trigger characters, trigger `completion(cursor_position)`. Wire diagnostics: `lsp_client.on_publish_diagnostics(|diags| panel.push_diagnostics(diags_to_markers(diags)))`.  
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/editor_view.rs` — render completion popup as a floating `egui::Window` at the cursor position with a scrollable list of `CompletionItem` (label, kind icon, detail). Arrow keys navigate; Enter accepts; Escape dismisses. Render hover tooltip as a floating `egui::Frame` with markdown-rendered documentation (use `egui_commonmark` if available, otherwise plain text). Render go-to-definition link in the hover (click opens the target file in a new editor pane or scrolls to the line if same file). REUSE the existing command-palette popup pattern from `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_palette.rs` + `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs` for the keyboard-navigable floating list (selection/keyboard semantics), rather than reinventing list navigation.

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `tower-lsp = "0.20"` or `lsp-types = "0.95"` + raw stdio JSON-RPC — use `lsp-types` for the type definitions and implement a lightweight JSON-RPC stdio transport rather than the full tower-lsp server stack (tower-lsp is server-side). Use `tokio::process::Command` to spawn the language server.
- `tokio` — already required for async backend calls. LSP requests run on the tokio runtime.
- backend HTTP via `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs` — for CodeNavClient HTTP calls (reuse the existing client; do not add a separate reqwest stack).
- `serde_json` — for LSP JSON-RPC serialization.
- `egui_commonmark` (optional) — for markdown rendering in hover tooltips.
- AccessKit (via `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/*`): `author_id = "code_editor_completion_popup"` `Role::ListBox` on the completion popup; `author_id = "code_editor_completion_item_{n}"` `Role::Option` on each item; `author_id = "code_editor_hover"` `Role::Tooltip` on the hover widget. Register nodes through the existing accessibility registry rather than emitting raw AccessKit.

React reference files:
- `app/src/lib/monaco/code_intelligence.ts` — the entire file is the reference. Ports: `ensureHandshakeCodeIntelligenceProviders` -> `CodeNavClient` methods; `completionKind` -> native equivalent; `refreshHandshakeCodeIntelligenceMarkers` -> `push_diagnostics` call; `codeSymbolStalenessLabel` -> same utility function in Rust.
- `app/src/components/CodeSymbolPanel.tsx` — displays symbol detail from `getCodeSymbol` and `getCodeFileLens`. The native equivalent is the hover tooltip showing the same data.
- `app/src/lib/api.ts` functions: `getCodeSymbol` -> `GET /knowledge/code/symbols/{entity_id}`, `lookupCodeSymbols` -> `GET /knowledge/code/symbols?workspace_id=...&prefix=...`, `getCodeSymbolReferences` -> `GET /knowledge/code/symbols/{id}/references`, `getCodeFileLens` -> `GET /knowledge/code/files/{path}/lens?workspace_id=...&content_hash=...&parser_version=...`.
- `app/src/harness/mt249_code_intelligence_harness.tsx` — the proof harness for the backend code-nav integration; the native equivalent must pass equivalent real-backend tests.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. LSP client stdio transport: open `tokio::process::Command::new(server_bin).stdin(Stdio::piped()).stdout(Stdio::piped())`. Spawn a tokio task that reads stdout line-by-line (LSP messages are header+content), parses JSON-RPC responses, and routes them to pending request futures via a `HashMap<RequestId, oneshot::Sender<Value>>`.
2. `completion` request: send `textDocument/completion` with `TextDocumentPositionParams`. Map response `CompletionItem.kind` integers to a `CompletionItemKind` enum using the LSP spec table.
3. `hover` request: send `textDocument/hover`. Extract `contents.value` (MarkupContent) for display.
4. Diagnostics: LSP servers push `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` notifications (not responses to requests). The reader task must detect notification messages (no `id` field) and route them to a notification channel. The `on_publish_diagnostics` callback is called from there.
5. CodeNavClient: all methods are `async fn`; call them from the egui frame using `tokio::task::spawn` and a `std::sync::mpsc::channel` to return results to the next frame (avoid blocking the egui thread).
6. Completion popup rendering: on each frame, if `completion_state.is_some()` and the popup has items, render a `Window::new("completion").fixed_pos(cursor_px_pos).show(ui.ctx(), ...)`. Intercept Arrow Up/Down in the window to navigate `selected_index`. On Enter: insert the selected item's `insert_text` at the cursor using `cursor_set.insert_at_all`.
7. Staleness markers: for CodeNavClient responses, check `staleness.fresh` field (as in `refreshHandshakeCodeIntelligenceMarkers`); if not fresh, push a `GutterMarker::Diagnostic(Warning)` for the affected lines.

Dependencies/unblock conditions: MT-001 (TextBuffer, Highlighter), MT-007 (`push_diagnostics` stub). Requires a real PostgreSQL backend (`handshake_core`) running for proof targets that call the backend code-nav APIs. If backend is unavailable, LSP and CodeNav return empty results gracefully. Cross-WP note: the backend HTTP client this MT reuses (`backend_client.rs`) was delivered by WP-KERNEL-011; this dependency is a reuse pointer, not a depends_on edge.
Risk if missed: No code intelligence means operators cannot use completion, hover, or go-to-definition — the primary productivity features of the VS Code parity goal. Diagnostic markers from LSP are also missing from the gutter.

implementation_notes: Do not call backend HTTP or spawn LSP tasks from the egui render loop — only poll result channels. Spawn async tasks via `tokio::spawn` in response to input events (key presses, cursor movement).
Completion trigger debounce: only trigger completion if the user has not typed for 200ms. Use a `last_edit_instant: Option<Instant>` in the code editor module and check the elapsed time.
Hover dwell trigger: 500ms dwell at the same cursor position. Use a `hover_dwell: Option<(byte_offset, Instant)>` field.
CodeNavClient result caching: cache `lookup_symbols` results for the same `prefix` string for 2 seconds to avoid hammering the backend on every keypress.
lsp-types crate version: pin to `0.95.*` — this is the version compatible with the LSP 3.17 spec.
Mock LSP server for tests: implement a minimal stdio-based mock in the test module that responds to `initialize` and `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` with canned data.

LSP TRANSPORT (research wf_ffa74d6d): prefer async-lsp (CLIENT side; correct synchronous notification ordering) OR a lightweight raw JSON-RPC-over-stdio transport + lsp-types. Do NOT use tower-lsp (server-side, ~3yr stale, semantically-incorrect async notification ordering) despite the contract prose mentioning it. lsp-types for the type defs. PROCESS SUPERVISION (research MT-077 + HBR-QUIET / MC-001): caller-owned lifecycle with Drop -> shutdown+exit (bounded timeout), restart/health, FOCUS-SAFE spawn (never SetForegroundWindow/steal focus, no zombie processes - reuse quiet_mode/focus_guard). Skip malformed non-JSON server stdout lines without panicking (RISK-003).

ATTEMPT to start the managed backend + seed a code-indexed workspace and run the backend ACs for real, OR use an explicit real PG URL via HANDSHAKE_TEST_DB_URL. If the managed backend genuinely cannot be started/seeded here, GATE the backend ACs behind the integration Cargo feature AND emit a typed BLOCKER (NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF naming the missing resource) - do NOT fake/mock the backend binding as proof of those ACs. AC-004 (graceful, no LSP) + AC-008 (mock-LSP publishDiagnostics) MUST pass standalone with no backend. Write the CodeNavClient + LspClient code REAL regardless; only the live-PG proof may be an honest deferred blocker.

POPUP POSITIONING + FOCUS (MT-002/003/005 + RISK-005/HBR-QUIET): anchor the completion popup + hover tooltip at the cursor pixel position from y_for_line + monospace glyph_width using the MT-002-corrected sans-spacing units, the MT-003 cursor byte->line/col mapping, and the MT-005 fold-aware visible mapping. original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement a diff and merge editor panel supporting side-by-side and inline (unified) diff views for both prose and code content. This provides parity with the KERNEL-009 MT-247 diff surface and ports the `document_diff_merge.ts` logic from the React codebase into a native egui panel. Also handles CRDT conflict UI: when a CRDT merge conflict exists in the workspace (signalled via a workspace state update), the merge editor opens with local/base/remote three-way view and per-block accept/reject controls. Expected diff shape: new `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_engine.rs`, new `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs`, edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs`.

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_engine.rs` — ports `document_diff_merge.ts`. Defines `DiffBlock { left_lines: Range<usize>, right_lines: Range<usize>, status: DiffStatus }` where `DiffStatus` is an enum: `Equal`, `Added`, `Removed`, `Modified`. `DiffEngine::diff(left: &TextBuffer, right: &TextBuffer) -> Vec<DiffBlock>` — uses the Myers diff algorithm (implement from scratch or use the `similar` crate which is MIT-licensed and production-grade). For prose mode: works at the paragraph/block level (port `buildRichDocumentDiff` behavior for line-level comparison). `MergeBlock { base_lines: Range<usize>, local_lines: Range<usize>, remote_lines: Range<usize>, status: MergeStatus, chosen: Option<MergeChoice> }` where `MergeStatus: LocalOnly | RemoteOnly | BothSame | Conflict` and `MergeChoice: Local | Remote | Both`. `MergeEngine::three_way(base: &TextBuffer, local: &TextBuffer, remote: &TextBuffer) -> Vec<MergeBlock>` — computes local vs base diff and remote vs base diff, then aligns them to produce merge blocks.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs` — `DiffEditorPanel` egui widget. State: `left: TextBuffer`, `right: TextBuffer`, `diff: Vec<DiffBlock>`, `mode: DiffMode` (enum: `SideBySide`, `Inline`). `DiffEditorPanel::show(ui)` renders: (a) SideBySide: two `CodeEditorPanel` instances side by side, synchronized scroll (when left scrolls, right scrolls to the same line, accounting for added/removed blocks), diff block backgrounds highlighted (green=added, red=removed, yellow=modified). (b) Inline: single panel showing both left and right lines interleaved with change markers. Toggle button for SideBySide vs Inline in the panel header. Also supports `MergeMode`: three panes (local, base, remote) with per-block accept buttons.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `open_diff(left: TextBuffer, right: TextBuffer)` and `open_merge(base, local, remote: TextBuffer)` factory methods that construct a `DiffEditorPanel` and place it in the egui tile layout as a new tile. Reuse the existing WP-011 layout primitives `split_layout.rs` and `pane_registry.rs` (under `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/`) to register and place the new tile rather than introducing a parallel layout system.

Exact crates/functions/APIs to use:
- `similar = "2"` (MIT) — production-grade diff library used by many Rust projects; provides Myers diff over slices. Use `similar::ChangeTag` and `similar::TextDiff::from_lines` for line-level diff.
- `egui::SidePanel` or manual `ui.columns(2, ...)` for the side-by-side layout.
- `egui::Painter::rect_filled` — for diff block background highlights.
- `egui::Button` — for merge choice accept buttons (Accept Local, Accept Remote, Accept Both).
- AccessKit (reuse `accessibility/*` under `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/`): `author_id = "diff_editor_panel"` `Role::Group`; `author_id = "diff_block_{n}_accept_local"` `Role::Button` on each merge accept button; `author_id = "diff_mode_toggle"` `Role::ToggleButton` on the SideBySide/Inline toggle.

React reference files:
- `app/src/lib/editor/document_diff_merge.ts` — complete reference for diff and merge data structures. Port: `RichDocumentDiff`, `RichDocumentDiffBlock`, `RichDocumentDiffStatus`, `RichDocumentMergePlan`, `RichDocumentMergeBlock`, `RichDocumentMergeStatus`, `buildRichDocumentDiff`, `buildRichDocumentMergePlan`, `applyRichDocumentMergeChoices`. Native equivalents use `TextBuffer` instead of `JSONContent` (the prose format). For code buffers, the diff is line-level not block-level.
- `app/src/lib/editor/document_diff_merge.test.ts` — test cases for the diff/merge logic; port these tests as Rust unit tests.
- `app/src/harness/rich_document_diff_harness.tsx` — the visual harness for the React diff editor; the native egui panel must match its feature surface.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Use `similar::TextDiff::from_lines(left_text, right_text)` for line-level diff. Map `ChangeTag::Equal` -> `DiffStatus::Equal`, `Insert` -> `Added`, `Delete` -> `Removed`, and consecutive Delete+Insert at the same position -> `Modified`.
2. Side-by-side sync scroll: maintain a `sync_scroll: SyncScrollState { left_scroll_offset: f32, right_scroll_offset: f32, last_changed: Side }`. When the left ScrollArea changes scroll offset, compute the corresponding right offset by counting visible lines in diff blocks and mapping them. Use `VirtualLineLayout` from MT-002 for each pane.
3. Diff block backgrounds: before rendering each line in the virtual line loop, check if the line falls in a `DiffBlock` and set `ui.painter().rect_filled(line_rect, 0, diff_color)` where `diff_color` is: Added=Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied(0,255,0,30), Removed=Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied(255,0,0,30), Modified=Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied(255,200,0,30).
4. Inline mode: render left lines normally; for Added blocks, add a green `+ ` prefix; for Removed, a red `- ` prefix; for Equal, a gray `  ` prefix. No side-by-side layout needed.
5. Merge mode per-block UI: for each `MergeBlock` with `status=Conflict`, render three rows (local, base, remote) with Accept Local / Accept Remote / Accept Both buttons. On accept, set `block.chosen` and recompute the merged output buffer.
6. Synchronized scroll algorithm: maintain a `line_map: Vec<(Option<usize>, Option<usize>)>` where each entry is (left_line, right_line) for the corresponding visual row (None for lines that only exist on one side). When left scrolls to visual row R, find `line_map[R].1` and scroll right to that row.

Dependencies/unblock conditions: MT-001 (TextBuffer for both panes), MT-002 (VirtualLineLayout for both panes). Does NOT require MT-005, MT-007, or MT-008 — the diff editor is a standalone panel.
Risk if missed: No diff view means code review workflows are blocked. CRDT conflict resolution has no UI. This is parity with KERNEL-009 MT-247 which is already validated.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement a complete Monaco/VS Code parity keymap for the native code editor, with configurable keybindings stored in the operator's shell settings file. This is the unifying MT that consolidates all the per-MT pre-wired key handlers (Ctrl+D from MT-003, Ctrl+F/H from MT-004, Ctrl+Shift+[/] from MT-005, Ctrl+G from MT-006) into a single deterministic dispatch table — the canonical reference for 'what does this key do in the code editor'. The keymap is also exposed to swarm agents via AccessKit command nodes (reuse accessibility/* from WP-011) and via MCP tools (reuse mcp/* from WP-011) so agents can dispatch editor commands without simulating keystrokes. Expected diff shape: new `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap.rs` (the binding table and resolver), new `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap_settings.rs` (settings file loader/writer), edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` (replace all ad-hoc key handlers with the single dispatcher).

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap.rs` — ports `editor_keymap.ts` to Rust. Defines `KeyChord { key: egui::Key, modifiers: egui::Modifiers }`. `KeyBinding { chord: KeyChord, action: CodeEditorAction, description: &'static str }`. `CodeEditorAction` enum — complete VS Code parity set: `MoveCursorLeft`, `MoveCursorRight`, `MoveCursorUp`, `MoveCursorDown`, `MoveCursorWordLeft`, `MoveCursorWordRight`, `MoveCursorLineStart`, `MoveCursorLineEnd`, `MoveCursorDocStart`, `MoveCursorDocEnd`, `SelectLeft`, `SelectRight`, `SelectUp`, `SelectDown`, `SelectWordLeft`, `SelectWordRight`, `SelectLineStart`, `SelectLineEnd`, `SelectAll`, `DeleteLeft`, `DeleteRight`, `DeleteWordLeft`, `DeleteWordRight`, `DeleteLine`, `InsertNewline`, `InsertTab`, `IndentLine`, `DedentLine`, `ToggleComment`, `DuplicateLine`, `MoveLineUp`, `MoveLineDown`, `AddCursorAbove`, `AddCursorBelow`, `SelectNextOccurrence`, `CancelMultiCursor`, `OpenFind`, `OpenReplace`, `FindNext`, `FindPrev`, `CloseFind`, `FoldAtCursor`, `UnfoldAtCursor`, `FoldAll`, `UnfoldAll`, `GoToLine`, `GoToDefinition`, `ShowReferences`, `ShowHover`, `TriggerCompletion`, `AcceptCompletion`, `DismissCompletion`, `Undo`, `Redo`, `Save`, `OpenCommandPalette`. `Keymap { bindings: Vec<KeyBinding> }`. `Keymap::default_vscode()` returns the canonical Monaco-parity binding table. `Keymap::resolve(chord: KeyChord) -> Option<CodeEditorAction>` — O(N) lookup (N is small, <60 bindings). `Keymap::from_settings(settings: &KeymapSettings) -> Keymap` — merges user overrides over the default table.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap_settings.rs` — `KeymapSettings { overrides: Vec<KeymapOverride> }` where `KeymapOverride { action: String, chord: String }`. `KeymapSettings::load_from_file(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, Error>` reads a JSON file (the shell settings file that already exists for the operator). `KeymapSettings::save_to_file(path: &Path, settings: &Self) -> Result<(), Error>` writes back. The settings file path is `~/.handshake/keymap.json` (use `dirs::home_dir()` for portability — no hardcoded paths per GLOBAL-PORTABILITY-004). `KeymapSettings::chord_from_str(s: &str) -> Result<KeyChord, Error>` parses human-readable chords like `"Ctrl+Shift+P"`, `"Mod+F"`, `"Alt+Up"` into `KeyChord`. Mod = Ctrl on Windows/Linux, Command on macOS (detect via `cfg!(target_os = "macos")`).
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — remove all ad-hoc `egui::Event::Key` handlers added in MT-003, MT-004, MT-005, MT-006. Replace with a single `process_keymap(input: &egui::InputState, keymap: &Keymap) -> Vec<CodeEditorAction>` call, then dispatch each action to the appropriate handler method. This is the single key dispatch point.

Default binding table (canonical Monaco/VS Code parity — key subset, full table in implementation):
| Chord                | Action                  |
|----------------------|-------------------------|
| Ctrl+F               | OpenFind                |
| Ctrl+H               | OpenReplace             |
| Ctrl+G               | GoToLine                |
| Ctrl+D               | SelectNextOccurrence    |
| Ctrl+Alt+Up          | AddCursorAbove          |
| Ctrl+Alt+Down        | AddCursorBelow          |
| Escape               | CancelMultiCursor / CloseFind / DismissCompletion (context-sensitive) |
| Ctrl+Shift+[         | FoldAtCursor            |
| Ctrl+Shift+]         | UnfoldAtCursor          |
| Ctrl+K Ctrl+0        | FoldAll (two-chord)     |
| Ctrl+K Ctrl+J        | UnfoldAll (two-chord)   |
| Ctrl+Shift+P         | OpenCommandPalette      |
| F12                  | GoToDefinition          |
| Shift+F12            | ShowReferences          |
| Ctrl+Space           | TriggerCompletion       |
| Tab                  | AcceptCompletion (when popup open) / InsertTab |
| Ctrl+Z               | Undo                    |
| Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z| Redo                    |
| Ctrl+S               | Save                    |
| Ctrl+/               | ToggleComment           |
| Alt+Up/Down          | MoveLineUp / MoveLineDown |
| Ctrl+Shift+K         | DeleteLine              |
| Ctrl+D               | DuplicateLine (when no selection) |

Note on two-chord bindings: maintain `pending_chord: Option<KeyChord>` in `CodeEditorPanel`; if a binding has a prefix chord (e.g. Ctrl+K), set pending_chord after the first chord and resolve the action after the second chord.

AccessKit command surface: for each `CodeEditorAction` variant, add an `author_id = "code_editor_cmd_{action_name}"` `Role::Button` node in the AccessKit tree with no visual representation (hidden from the UI but accessible to agents), reusing the WP-011 accessibility integration (accessibility/mod.rs, accessibility/live.rs, accessibility/registry.rs, accessibility/snapshot.rs). Agents can trigger commands by activating these nodes. The same actions are also exposed to swarm models through the WP-011 MCP surface (mcp/tools.rs, mcp/action.rs) so swarm models can dispatch editor commands without knowing key bindings.

Configurable keybindings: when the operator changes a binding in `~/.handshake/keymap.json`, the next frame reloads the keymap (watch the file for changes using `notify` crate or poll on a timer). original_scope.summary:
Create the ProseMirror-style block document model for the native Rust rich-text editor. This is the BRAIN of the entire E2 cluster: every other MT depends on it. The model must support a document tree of typed nodes (doc, paragraph, heading[1-3], blockquote, code_block, ordered_list, bullet_list, list_item, table, table_row, table_cell, task_item, hard_break, horizontal_rule) and inline marks (bold, italic, underline, strike, code, link, wikilink). It is built on the 'ropey' crate for O(log n) rope-backed text storage per text leaf, with a typed Transform/Step system for atomic document mutations and a bounded undo/redo history (UndoManager, default 200 steps).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: create new module tree at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/document_model/ containing: mod.rs (re-exports), node.rs (BlockNode/InlineNode/NodeKind enums + Mark enum), schema.rs (compile-time schema registry, validates node/mark combinations), rope_text.rs (ropey::Rope wrapper with char-index helpers), transform.rs (Step enum: InsertText, DeleteText, InsertNode, DeleteNode, SplitNode, MergeNodes, AddMark, RemoveMark; Transaction struct collecting Steps; apply_transaction(&mut DocNode, Transaction) -> Result<TransactionReceipt>), history.rs (UndoManager: push_transaction, undo, redo, can_undo, can_redo, history capped at 200 entries), position.rs (DocPosition: resolved path through the tree = Vec<(node_index, char_offset)>; resolve(doc, absolute_offset) -> DocPosition; absolute_offset(doc, DocPosition) -> usize), selection.rs (Selection: TextSelection{anchor,head} and NodeSelection{node_path}), and doc_json.rs (DocJson: serde serialize/deserialize to/from the same JSONContent shape used by Tiptap in the React reference, schema_version = 'rich_document_v1', compatible with the backend knowledge/documents content_json field).

VERTICAL-SLICE PROOF FIRST: before filling every node/mark variant, ship: paragraph node + bold/italic marks + InsertText/DeleteText/AddMark/RemoveMark steps + UndoManager + DocJson round-trip. Extend to the full set in the same MT; the acceptance criteria require all node/mark types.
