original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement a local + global Loom graph view panel in the native Rust/egui frontend. The panel renders a force-directed node-link diagram of LoomBlocks (nodes) and LoomEdges (links) fetched from the real PostgreSQL/EventLedger backend via the existing loom graph-search and views APIs. The expected diff shape is: one new file src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/graph_view.rs containing the LoomGraphView widget, plus wiring in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/mod.rs to expose it.

Exact files to create or edit:
- CREATE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/graph_view.rs — the graph panel widget
- EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/mod.rs — pub mod graph_view; + re-export LoomGraphView

Reuse existing WP-011 modules (do NOT reinvent): reuse the existing loom graph surface in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs for LoomBlock/LoomEdge graph types and the loom graph-search/views wiring; reuse src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs for the shared selection/command/clipboard bus and cross-pane open events; reuse src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs for the typed HTTP client to the PostgreSQL/EventLedger backend; reuse src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/* for AccessKit node registration; reuse src/frontend/handshake_native/src/theme/* (palette.rs) for content-type node colours.

Exact APIs / React reference:
- Ports from: no dedicated React graph component exists; the loom graph-search API is used inline across components. The React side relies on queryLoomView (viewType='all', limit=500) to enumerate all blocks, then createLoomEdge/getLoomBlock. Backend route: GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/graph-search?q=&limit=500 (loom_graph_search, lib/api.ts:1341). Also uses GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/views/all for flat block enumeration.
- Backend bindings:
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/graph-search?q=&limit=500 — returns LoomGraphSearchResult array; use with empty q to enumerate the full graph neighbourhood of the focused block
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/all — LoomViewResponse {view_type:'all', blocks:LoomBlock[]} for global mode (all nodes)
  - POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/edges — createLoomEdge for future edge creation (out-of-scope here but wire the callback slot)

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Define GraphNode { block_id: String, title: String, content_type: String, x: f32, y: f32 } and GraphEdge { source: String, target: String, edge_type: String } in graph_view.rs.
2. Define LoomGraphView { workspace_id, mode: GraphMode (Local {block_id} | Global), nodes: Vec<GraphNode>, edges: Vec<GraphEdge>, pan: Vec2, zoom: f32, selected: Option<String>, loading: bool, error: Option<String>, on_open: Callback<String> } as the widget state struct.
3. On first show (or when workspace_id/mode changes), fire an async Tauri command or HTTP fetch to GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/views/all (global) or GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/graph-search?q={title}&backlink_depth=2&limit=200 (local). Deserialize into GraphNode/GraphEdge lists. Store in widget state.
4. Run a simple spring/force layout iteration each frame until stable: repulse every node pair (Coulomb k=1000/d^2), attract connected pairs (spring k=0.05 * (d-150)). Cap iterations at 300 total; store stable positions in node state.
5. In egui show(): allocate the full panel Rect. Draw a dotted grid background via Painter::line_segment calls. Apply pan+zoom transform (translate then scale around centre). For each edge, draw painter.line_segment from source centre to target centre with stroke(1.5, Color32::from_gray(170)). For each node draw painter.circle_filled(pos, radius, color_by_content_type). If selected, draw a 2px blue ring. Add painter.text for the title label beneath each node. Handle pointer input: drag on empty area -> pan, scroll wheel -> zoom (clamp 0.1..4.0), click on node -> emit on_open callback with block_id.
6. Show a toolbar strip at top: 'Local' / 'Global' mode toggle buttons (AccessKit author_id='graph.mode.local'/'graph.mode.global'), zoom-in/zoom-out buttons (author_id='graph.zoom.in'/'graph.zoom.out'), 'Re-layout' button (author_id='graph.relayout'), node count label.
7. Show a loading spinner or error label over the canvas when loading=true or error.is_some().
8. Every interactive element must register AccessKit node with a stable author_id (see model-accessibility requirement below).

AccessKit requirements: register every toolbar button (mode-local, mode-global, zoom-in, zoom-out, relayout) and each graph node circle (author_id='graph.node.{block_id}', role=Button, label=title, actions=[DefaultAction=open]).

Dependencies / unblock conditions: no earlier E3 MTs required; the typed HTTP/backend bridge already exists as src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (delivered by WP-011) — reuse it instead of inlining a reqwest call. Must NOT depend on any E3 MTs (MT-022+).

Risk if missed: all other E3 MTs lose their navigation backbone. The graph is the primary wayfinding surface for the Loom knowledge layer.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Launching the app and opening the graph panel in Global mode shows at least all LoomBlocks from a real PostgreSQL workspace (verified with >=3 blocks inserted beforehand); node count label matches the block count returned by GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/views/all.
AC2: Switching to Local mode with a block_id focused loads graph-search results for that block and displays only the neighbourhood (different node set from global).
AC3: Pan works: dragging on empty canvas translates all nodes; releasing preserves position.
AC4: Zoom works: scroll wheel changes zoom level between 0.1 and 4.0; node positions remain correct in canvas space.
AC5: Clicking a node fires the on_open callback with the correct block_id (verified via kittest AccessKit event log).

AC6: AccessKit tree for the graph panel includes nodes with author_ids 'graph.mode.local', 'graph.mode.global', 'graph.zoom.in', 'graph.zoom.out', 'graph.relayout', and 'graph.node.{block_id}' for each rendered node.
AC7: With no blocks in the workspace the panel shows an empty canvas with '0 nodes' label and no panic.
AC8: Loading error (backend unreachable) shows an error label in the panel rather than a crash.
proof_targets: PROOF1: cargo test -p handshake-native graph::graph_view -- --nocapture passes all unit tests for force-layout convergence (position change < 1px after 300 iterations for a 5-node graph).

PROOF2: egui_kittest harness test (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_graph_view.rs) opens LoomGraphView in Global mode against a real PG test database with 5 seeded LoomBlocks; asserts AccessKit node count >= 5 graph.node.* entries.
PROOF3: kittest click on 'graph.node.block-001' asserts on_open callback fires with block_id='block-001'.
PROOF4: Screenshot captured by kittest shows a non-white canvas with at least one circle rendered (pixel color != background).
PROOF5: kittest scroll-event zoom test: zoom starts at 1.0, two scroll-up events, assert zoom > 1.0 and <= 4.0.
implementation_notes: Use egui::Painter for all graph rendering — no third-party graph library.
Reuse src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs for the existing Loom block/edge graph types and graph-search/views wiring rather than re-declaring backend DTOs.
Force layout: run in a background thread or limit to 10 iterations per frame to avoid blocking the UI thread. Store iteration count in widget state; stop when max_iter reached.
Color-code nodes by content_type: note=blue, file=gray, tag_hub=green, journal=orange, canvas=purple, other=slate.
Edge stroke: 1.5px, Color32::from_gray(160). Draw edges before nodes so nodes render on top.
Pan: track pointer delta on drag over empty area (no node under pointer). Store pan as Vec2 in widget state.
Zoom: on scroll event multiply zoom by 1.15^delta_y, clamp to [0.1, 4.0]. Zoom around pointer position (subtract pointer, scale, add back).
Node click detection: check if pointer_pos is within node circle radius (default 18px) after inverse-transform by current pan+zoom.

AccessKit: register nodes via the existing src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/* helpers — call ui.ctx().accesskit_node_builder(author_id).with_role(Role::Button).with_label(title).with_default_action_verb(DefaultActionVerb::Click) for each node in the painter pass.
Toolbar: use egui::TopBottomPanel or a manual strip at top of the allocated rect. Mode toggle = two SelectableLabel widgets. Use stable string author_ids not runtime indices.

Cross-WP dependency (WP-011): this MT reuses the WP-011 backend bridge src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs and the shared command/event surface src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs; those modules must already be present from WP-KERNEL-011 before this MT runs.
Do not store node positions in backend; they are ephemeral UI state only (layout is re-run on open).

NO TAURI (KERNEL_BUILDER gate 2026-06-22 - stale contract reference): step 3 says 'fire an async Tauri command or HTTP fetch' - Tauri is the LEGACY React/webview stack. This is the NATIVE egui app: use the existing WP-011 backend_client.rs typed async HTTP client (the same one MT-008/014/015/017 used), NOT a Tauri command. (Same class as the rich_text->rich_editor / document_ref->document_id stale-contract corrections.)

FORCE-LAYOUT REPAINT DISCIPLINE (KERNEL_BUILDER gate - the MT-015 idle-repaint/spinner lesson applied to the animation): the spring/force layout requests ctx.request_repaint ONLY while NOT converged; once converged (per-node delta <1px, PROOF1) OR max_iter (300) is reached, it MUST STOP requesting repaint - a layout that repaints every frame forever burns idle CPU AND makes harness.run() exceed max_steps (the same class as the backlinks-spinner regression). The 'loading' indicator likewise animates ONLY during a genuine in-flight backend fetch (runtime present + dispatched); headless/no-runtime renders a neutral non-animating state, never a perpetual spinner. kittest tests use harness.step()/run_steps(N), not run(), for any animating frame, + the gpu_lock() mutex for wgpu screenshots.

BACKEND PROOF REALITY (MT-008/014/015 pattern): AC1/AC2 + PROOF2/PROOF3 need a LIVE Handshake-managed PostgreSQL with SEEDED LoomBlocks (GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/views/all + /loom/graph-search). Bind the REAL backend via backend_client.rs; gate the live-data ACs behind the integration feature + emit NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF if no seeded backend - do NOT fake. The force-layout convergence (PROOF1, 5-node <1px), pan/zoom transform + zoom-to-pointer math (RISK-4), AccessKit-id sanitization (MC-3), node-cap-200 + truncation notice (MC-2), empty-canvas '0 nodes' (AC7), and backend-error label (AC8) are ALL unit/kittest-testable STANDALONE with mock/seeded node lists.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Define FolderNode { block_id: String, title: String, color: Option<Color32>, children: Vec<FolderNode>, expanded: bool, loading: bool } in graph/folder_tree.rs.
2. Define LoomFolderTree { workspace_id: String, root_nodes: Vec<FolderNode>, on_open: Callback<String>, on_color_change: Callback<(String, Color32)>, error: Option<String>, loading: bool }.
3. On init, call GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/views/all filtered to content_type=folder (or use 'sorted' groups) via backend_client.rs to populate root_nodes. Each block's metadata JSON (LoomBlock.content_json or a dedicated metadata field) stores the color as a hex string; parse into Color32.
4. Render the tree using egui::CollapsingHeader or manual indented rows. For each folder node:
   a. Draw a small 12x12 filled rectangle (color swatch) using painter.rect_filled before the label.
   b. Render a collapsible row: click on folder name -> toggle expanded; if expanding and children not loaded, fire GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/views/sorted with tag_ids=[block_id] (via backend_client.rs) to load children.
   c. Indent children by 16px per depth level.
5. Right-click context menu on a folder row (via context_menu.rs / context_menu_surfaces.rs): 'Change color' -> open a color picker popup (egui::color_picker::color_edit_button_srgba). On color pick, call PATCH /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{block_id} (via backend_client.rs) to persist color in block metadata (encode as hex string in the block's content_json or a dedicated 'color_label' metadata key). Fire on_color_change callback through event_bus.rs.
6. Leaf block rows (non-folder children): show block title + content_type icon character. Click -> fire on_open(block_id) through command_registry.rs.
7. AccessKit (via accessibility/): each folder row gets author_id='folder-tree.node.{block_id}', role=TreeItem, actions=[Expand, Collapse, DefaultAction=open]. Color swatch button gets author_id='folder-tree.color.{block_id}', role=Button.
8. Error banner at top of panel if load fails. Retry button author_id='folder-tree.retry'.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement a Tags panel and Tag Hubs panel in the native egui frontend. The Tags panel lists all tag blocks (content_type='tag_hub') across the workspace fetched from the real PostgreSQL backend, shows the number of blocks linked to each tag, and lets the user click a tag to open it as a filter (fires on_filter_tag callback). The Tag Hubs panel renders tag_hub-typed LoomBlocks as first-class content pages (like Obsidian's 'tag page'): showing the hub's title, description (from content_json), and the list of blocks tagged with it. Expected diff shape: one new file src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/tags_panel.rs containing LoomTagsPanel and LoomTagHubPanel widgets, edits to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs.

Exact files to create or edit:
- CREATE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/tags_panel.rs — LoomTagsPanel (tag list) + LoomTagHubPanel (tag hub page)
- EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs — pub mod tags_panel; + re-exports

Exact APIs / React reference:
- React reference: WorkspaceSidebar.tsx (app/src/components/WorkspaceSidebar.tsx) calls queryLoomView with contentType filter (LoomViewQuery.contentType, api.ts line 1061). bookmarkKind() in WorkspaceSidebar.tsx line 44 identifies tag_hub blocks. The React component does not have a standalone Tags panel; this is a new surface.
- LoomBlock.content_type == 'tag_hub' (api.ts line 933) is the tag hub block type.
- Backend bindings:
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/all?content_type=tag_hub — list all tag hub blocks
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/all?tag_ids={tag_hub_block_id} — list blocks tagged with a specific tag hub
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id} — load tag hub block detail
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/sorted?tag_ids={tag_hub_block_id} — grouped members of a tag hub
  - POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/edges (createLoomEdge edge_type='tag') — tag a block with a hub (future use; wire callback slot)

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Define TagEntry { block_id: String, title: String, member_count: u32 } in tags_panel.rs.
2. Define LoomTagsPanel { workspace_id: String, tags: Vec<TagEntry>, on_open_tag: Callback<String>, on_filter_tag: Callback<String>, loading: bool, error: Option<String>, search_filter: String }.
3. On init, call GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/views/all?content_type=tag_hub to enumerate all tag hubs. For each hub, member_count = members.len() (or show 0 if not yet loaded). Display a flat list sorted by title.
4. Render a search box at top of panel (egui::TextEdit::singleline, author_id='tags.search', placeholder='Filter tags...'). Filter displayed tags client-side by title prefix match.
5. Each tag row: colored tag chip (egui::Button with background color derived from title hash), member count badge, click fires on_open_tag(block_id) to navigate to the hub page.
6. LoomTagHubPanel (separate widget, shown when a tag hub block_id is provided as the active page):
   a. Load tag hub block via GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{block_id}.
   b. Load members via GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/views/all?tag_ids={block_id}, limit=100.
   c. Render hub title as H1, description from content_json if present.
   d. Render members as a scrollable list of block rows (title + content_type). Click on member -> on_open(member_block_id).
   e. 'Add tag to block' button (author_id='tag-hub.add-tag.{block_id}'): opens a quick-switcher-style popup to search for a block and tag it (fires POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/edges with edge_type='tag', source=selected_block_id, target=hub_block_id).
7. AccessKit:
   - LoomTagsPanel: search box author_id='tags.search', each tag row 'tags.row.{block_id}' role=ListItem with DefaultAction=open, member count as accessible description.
   - LoomTagHubPanel: hub title label 'tag-hub.title.{block_id}', member list items 'tag-hub.member.{block_id}', add-tag button 'tag-hub.add-tag.{block_id}'.

Reuse pointers (existing WP-011 modules under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/): reuse the existing Loom graph/knowledge surface in loom_graph.rs for the tag_hub block model and graph navigation; reuse command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs for the shared selection/command bus and for emitting on_open/on_filter navigation events; reuse accessibility/ (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs) for AccessKit author_id registration of tag rows and hub panel nodes; reuse mcp/ for exposing tag navigation as parallel-model actions where applicable. The new tags_panel surface is added inside a new loom/ subdir under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: MT-021 must be complete for shared HTTP client infrastructure. MT-023 does not depend on MT-022. Cross-WP: this MT builds on the WP-011 native shell modules listed above (loom_graph.rs, command_registry.rs, event_bus.rs, accessibility/*, mcp/*).

Risk if missed: Tag-based navigation and filtering are unavailable. MT-027 (BlockCollectionViews kanban lanes) depends on tag identity resolved here.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement a multi-section sidebar panel in the native egui frontend that ports the React WorkspaceSidebar pins/favorites/bookmarks sections plus adds backlinks and unlinked mentions panels for the currently-open block. The panel has five collapsible sections: Pins, Favorites, Backlinks, Unlinked Mentions, and a breadcrumb strip. All data comes from the real PostgreSQL backend via existing loom view APIs. Expected diff shape: one new file src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/sidebar_panel.rs containing LoomSidebarPanel, edits to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs.

Exact files to create or edit:
- CREATE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/sidebar_panel.rs — LoomSidebarPanel widget
- EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs — pub mod sidebar_panel; + re-export

Reuse existing WP-011 modules (do not reinvent): the loom graph surface lives in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs — reuse its LoomBlock/LoomEdge types and graph-view integration for backlinks rendering. Change-notification after pin/favorite mutation must be emitted through the existing shared event bus at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs (not a bespoke channel). AccessKit node registration reuses the existing accessibility helpers under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/ (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs). HTTP calls go through the shared backend client at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs.

Exact APIs / React reference:
- PRIMARY REACT REFERENCE: app/src/components/WorkspaceSidebar.tsx — the Bookmarks section (lines 363-424) calls queryLoomView(workspaceId, 'pins', {limit:100}) and renders bookmark rows with open/remove actions. The setLoomBlockPinOrder + updateLoomBlock({pinned:false}) pair is the remove-bookmark flow (WorkspaceSidebar.tsx lines 293-312). The 'favorites' view type (LoomViewType, api.ts line 1058) is the favorites surface.
- SECONDARY REACT REFERENCE: app/src/harness/loom_bookmarks_harness.tsx — the integration harness wiring WorkspaceSidebar + LoomBlockPanel.
- Backend bindings:
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/pins?limit=100 — LoomViewResponse {view_type:'pins', blocks:LoomBlock[]} (queryLoomView 'pins')
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/favorites?limit=100 — LoomViewResponse {view_type:'favorites', blocks:LoomBlock[]}
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/unlinked?limit=50 — LoomViewResponse {view_type:'unlinked', blocks:LoomBlock[]}
  - PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id} — updateLoomBlock({pinned:false}) to unpin
  - PUT /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id}/pin-order — setLoomBlockPinOrder(null) to clear pin order
  - PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id} — updateLoomBlock({favorite:false}) to un-favorite
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id}/backlinks — load backlinks for currently-open block (rich doc backlinks, api.ts line 3326 for documents; for loom blocks use graph-search with mentionIds=[block_id])
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/graph-search?mention_ids={block_id}&limit=50 — load loom backlinks/mentions for active block

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Define LoomSidebarPanel { workspace_id: String, active_block_id: Option<String>, pins: Vec<LoomBlock>, favorites: Vec<LoomBlock>, backlinks: Vec<LoomBlock>, unlinked: Vec<LoomBlock>, breadcrumbs: Vec<BreadcrumbEntry>, on_open: Callback<String>, loading_section: HashSet<SectionKind>, error_section: HashMap<SectionKind, String> } where SectionKind = Pins | Favorites | Backlinks | Unlinked.
2. On workspace_id change, reload Pins and Favorites sections. On active_block_id change, reload Backlinks and Unlinked sections.
3. Breadcrumb strip: maintain a Vec<BreadcrumbEntry { block_id, title }> as navigation history. Each on_open callback push adds an entry. Render as a horizontal strip at top: 'Home > Folder > Block'. Each crumb is clickable (on_open fires for that block_id). Truncate to last 5 crumbs. AccessKit: each crumb 'sidebar.breadcrumb.{idx}' role=Link.
4. Pins section: render as a collapsible section header 'Pins (N)'. Each pin row: block title + kind chip + 'Remove' button. Remove = call PUT /pin-order (null) then PATCH {pinned:false}; remove from local list immediately (optimistic) and re-fetch. AccessKit: each row 'sidebar.pin.{block_id}', remove button 'sidebar.pin.{block_id}.remove'.
5. Favorites section: same pattern as Pins but calls PATCH {favorite:false} to remove. AccessKit: 'sidebar.favorite.{block_id}', 'sidebar.favorite.{block_id}.remove'.
6. Backlinks section: render only when active_block_id is set. Show blocks that mention the active block via GET /loom/graph-search?mention_ids={block_id}. Each row shows source block title + edge_type label. Click -> on_open(source_block_id). AccessKit: 'sidebar.backlink.{block_id}'.
7. Unlinked mentions section: render only when active_block_id is set. Show blocks from GET /loom/views/unlinked that textually mention the active block title but have no edge. Click -> on_open(block_id). AccessKit: 'sidebar.unlinked.{block_id}'.
8. Section headers are collapsible (egui::CollapsingHeader or manual toggle bool). Each section has a Retry button on error.
9. Emit a 'handshake:loom-bookmarks-changed' equivalent event through the existing event_bus.rs so other panels can react to pin/favorite changes.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: MT-021, MT-022, MT-023 must be complete so that src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs is fully scaffolded and the shared backend_client.rs HTTP client is available. Cross-WP note: the existing loom graph surface (loom_graph.rs), event bus (event_bus.rs), accessibility helpers (accessibility/*), and backend client (backend_client.rs) are delivered by WP-KERNEL-011 and are reused here, not recreated.

Risk if missed: The sidebar navigation surface is absent. Users cannot find pinned blocks, favorites, backlinks, or unlinked mentions, which are core Obsidian-parity knowledge-navigation features.

AC2: Clicking 'Remove' on a pin row calls PUT /pin-order(null) then PATCH {pinned:false}, the row disappears from the list, and a re-fetch confirms the block is no longer pinned.

implementation_notes: Use separate loading booleans per section (HashMap<SectionKind, bool>) so sections load independently and a slow Backlinks fetch does not block Pins from rendering.
Optimistic remove: immediately remove the row from the local Vec on remove-click; if the backend PATCH fails, re-add the row and show an error inline.
Breadcrumb strip: render horizontally using egui::ui.horizontal(). Each crumb is an egui::Button with label truncated to 20 chars if long.

Backlinks vs unlinked: Backlinks = blocks with a real LoomEdge to active_block_id (query mention_ids). Unlinked = blocks returned by /views/unlinked — these are blocks the backend has identified as having textual mentions but no edge. The distinction is important; do not mix the two lists.
Pin removal: must call both PUT /pin-order(null) AND PATCH {pinned:false} in sequence (same as React WorkspaceSidebar.tsx lines 297-298). Do not skip the pin-order clear.
Collapsible sections: store expanded state per SectionKind in a HashMap<SectionKind, bool>; default all to true (expanded).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement a wiki page projection panel in the native egui frontend that ports the React LoomWikiPagePanel (MT-184/185 parity). The panel loads a LoomWikiProjection from the real PostgreSQL backend, renders its content as read-only rendered markdown in a scroll area, and provides an 'Edit overlay' mode that allows inline editing of the rendered_content field and persists changes back via the backend wiki API. Expected diff shape: one new file src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/wiki_page_panel.rs containing LoomWikiPagePanel widget, edits to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/mod.rs. Reuse the existing WP-011 loom graph surface (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs) for graph/projection navigation context.

Exact files to create or edit:
- CREATE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/wiki_page_panel.rs — LoomWikiPagePanel widget
- EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/mod.rs — pub mod wiki_page_panel; + re-export

Exact APIs / React reference:
- PRIMARY REACT REFERENCE: app/src/components/LoomWikiPagePanel.tsx — loads via getLoomWikiProjection(workspaceId, projectionId) (api.ts line 1544), renders title, page_type badge, projection metadata (projection_id, workspace_id, rebuild_status, source_block_ids.length), and rendered_content. The React component is read-only; this MT adds the editable overlay on top.
- Backend bindings:
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/wiki/{projection_id} — getLoomWikiProjection; returns LoomWikiProjection { projection_id, workspace_id, title, source_block_ids[], rendered_content, staleness_hash, rebuild_status, page_type, page_links, created_at, updated_at, staleness_verdict } (api.ts line 1144-1161)
  - PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/wiki/{projection_id} — update rendered_content or trigger rebuild (if this endpoint exists; fall back to PUT if PATCH not available — document the choice)
  - POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/wiki/{projection_id}/rebuild — trigger a projection rebuild (if available; mark as OPTIONAL in implementation; show rebuild_status)

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Define LoomWikiPagePanel { workspace_id: String, projection_id: String, page: Option<LoomWikiProjection>, edit_mode: bool, edit_buffer: String, loading: bool, error: Option<String>, saving: bool, save_error: Option<String> }.
2. On init (or when projection_id changes), call GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/wiki/{projection_id} and populate the page field. Store rendered_content in edit_buffer (pre-load for edit mode).
3. Read-only view (edit_mode=false):
   a. Render title as a large bold label (egui::RichText::new(title).heading()).
   b. Render a row of metadata chips: page_type badge (colored chip), rebuild_status badge (green=ok, amber=stale, red=error), source count '(N sources)'.
   c. Render rendered_content inside a ScrollArea as plain text (egui::Label). For now, do NOT attempt full markdown rendering — show the raw content string. A future MT can add markdown rendering. Label the scroll area 'wiki.content.{projection_id}'.
   d. Show staleness_verdict as a subtle footer line if it indicates the projection is stale.
   e. 'Edit' button at top-right (author_id='wiki.edit.{projection_id}'): switches to edit_mode=true, copies rendered_content into edit_buffer.
   f. Optional 'Rebuild' button (author_id='wiki.rebuild.{projection_id}'): fires POST .../rebuild if endpoint exists; shows 'rebuilding...' in rebuild_status until next reload.
4. Edit overlay (edit_mode=true):
   a. Show a full-height egui::TextEdit::multiline bound to edit_buffer. Author_id='wiki.edit-area.{projection_id}'.
   b. Toolbar at top: 'Save' button (author_id='wiki.save.{projection_id}') + 'Cancel' button (author_id='wiki.cancel.{projection_id}').
   c. 'Save': call PATCH (or PUT) /workspaces/{id}/loom/wiki/{projection_id} with { rendered_content: edit_buffer }. On success, reload the projection (GET) and exit edit_mode. On error, show save_error inline without discarding the edit_buffer.
   d. 'Cancel': discard edit_buffer, exit edit_mode without a save.
5. AccessKit: title label 'wiki.title.{projection_id}', content area 'wiki.content.{projection_id}' role=Document, edit button 'wiki.edit.{projection_id}', edit area 'wiki.edit-area.{projection_id}' role=MultiLineTextInput, save 'wiki.save.{projection_id}', cancel 'wiki.cancel.{projection_id}'.
6. Loading state: show spinner + 'Loading wiki page...' while loading=true. Error state: show error text + Retry button.

Reuse pointers (real WP-011 modules under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/): graph/projection navigation context via loom_graph.rs; AccessKit node registration via accessibility/* (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs); MCP tool/screenshot surfaces via mcp/* if model-driven proof is needed.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: MT-021 must be complete for shared HTTP client infrastructure. No dependency on MT-022, MT-023, MT-024.

Risk if missed: Wiki projection surfaces (MT-184/185 parity) are unavailable in the native frontend. Knowledge synthesis pages cannot be read or edited.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The panel loads a real LoomWikiProjection from PG (seeded via backend) and displays the title, page_type badge, rebuild_status badge, source count, and rendered_content text.
AC2: Clicking the 'Edit' button switches to edit overlay showing a multiline text editor pre-filled with the current rendered_content.
AC3: Editing the content and clicking 'Save' persists the change to the backend via PATCH/PUT /loom/wiki/{projection_id}, then reloads and displays the updated content in read-only view.
AC4: Clicking 'Cancel' in edit mode discards the edits and returns to read-only view without a backend call.
AC5: If the save call fails (simulated 5xx), the error is shown inline below the toolbar and the edit_buffer is preserved (not lost).
AC6: If projection has a stale staleness_verdict, a 'Stale' notice appears in the footer of the read-only view.

AC7: AccessKit tree contains 'wiki.title.{projection_id}', 'wiki.content.{projection_id}', 'wiki.edit.{projection_id}', 'wiki.edit-area.{projection_id}', 'wiki.save.{projection_id}', 'wiki.cancel.{projection_id}'.
AC8: Loading state shows spinner; error state shows error + Retry without panic.
proof_targets: PROOF1: cargo test -p handshake-native graph::wiki_page_panel -- --nocapture passes unit tests for edit_buffer pre-fill and cancel-no-mutation logic.
PROOF2: kittest test with a real PG wiki projection seeded: assert 'wiki.title.*' label present in AccessKit tree and rendered_content text is non-empty.

PROOF3: kittest edit-save test: click 'wiki.edit.proj-001', type 'NEW CONTENT' into 'wiki.edit-area.proj-001', click 'wiki.save.proj-001', assert PATCH/PUT request fired (Tauri intercept), assert rendered_content updated in read-only view.
PROOF4: kittest cancel test: click 'wiki.edit.proj-001', type 'THROWAWAY', click 'wiki.cancel.proj-001', assert no PATCH/PUT request fired and panel returns to read-only showing original content.

implementation_notes: Rendered content is plain text for now — do not implement markdown rendering in this MT. Use egui::Label with wrap=true inside a ScrollArea.
PATCH vs PUT: attempt PATCH /loom/wiki/{projection_id} first. If the backend returns 405 Method Not Allowed, fall back to PUT. Detect and document the chosen method in a comment in the source file.
Rebuild button is OPTIONAL: only render it if the rebuild endpoint responds to a HEAD request (or simply include it and let the handler surface a 404 gracefully). Do not block AC criteria on rebuild.
edit_buffer should be initialized from page.rendered_content at the moment the Edit button is clicked, not at load time, so it always contains the latest content.
staleness_verdict: check if it is a non-null, non-empty value to decide whether to show the stale notice. The React type is 'unknown'; treat any non-null/non-false value as stale.
source_count: show as '(N sources)' where N = page.source_block_ids.len(). Render as a muted smaller label next to the metadata chips.
Do not auto-save on every keystroke; save only on explicit Save button click.

Cross-WP dependency: this MT builds on the WP-011 native shell. Reuse the existing loom graph surface at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs for projection navigation context, and register AccessKit nodes through the existing accessibility/* modules (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs). New wiki-panel code lives under the WP-012 graph/ subdir inside src/frontend/handshake_native/src/.

WIKI-PROJECTION EDIT SEMANTICS (KERNEL_BUILDER gate 2026-06-22 - CRITICAL, Spec-Realism + backend-shape, the recurring lesson): a LoomWikiProjection is a DERIVED/GENERATED read-through view (rendered_content is projected FROM source_block_ids). VERIFY read-only against src/backend/handshake_core + app/src/lib/api.ts whether editing rendered_content is ACTUALLY persisted AND survives a rebuild, OR whether the projection is READ-ONLY (the contract + RISK-1 themselves doubt the PATCH route exists). If the backend has NO real edit/PATCH/PUT route for rendered_content, do NOT ship a fake Edit-save that 404s or gets silently overwritten on the next rebuild - render the Edit overlay as a TYPED LIMITATION (Edit button disabled/explained: 'read-only projection - edit the source blocks', MC-1), never a fake save (Spec-Realism: no silently-broken write). If a real edit route DOES exist, bind it + a staleness_hash conflict check before save (RISK-3/MC-3). Either way, VERIFY the LoomWikiProjection field shape (projection_id/title/rendered_content/staleness_hash/rebuild_status/page_type/source_block_ids/staleness_verdict) exists as assumed (the MT-022/023/024 lesson: don't assume).

BACKEND PROOF REALITY (MT-008/021-024 pattern): AC1 (load real projection) + AC3 (save round-trip, only if the edit route is real) need a LIVE Handshake-managed PostgreSQL with a seeded wiki projection. Bind the REAL GET route; gate the live-data ACs behind the integration feature + NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF if unseeded - do NOT fake. The edit_buffer pre-fill (init at Edit-CLICK, not load, so it is the latest content), cancel-no-mutation (no backend call, PROOF4), save-error-preserves-buffer (PROOF5), staleness display (AC6, treat any non-null/non-false staleness_verdict as stale), and the 50KB TextEdit cap (RISK-2) are unit/kittest-testable STANDALONE.

UI HYGIENE (KERNEL_BUILDER gate): NO PERPETUAL SPINNER - the loading spinner animates ONLY during a genuine in-flight fetch (runtime present); headless renders neutral (MT-015 lesson); kittest uses step() not run(). All HTTP via backend_client.rs (NO Tauri - PROOF3 'Tauri intercept' = backend_client RequestSpec; extend the existing Loom clients). MARKDOWN RENDER is correctly DEFERRED here (plain-text egui::Label wrap now) - true markdown rendering is the later reading-mode MT (MT-055, egui_commonmark); do NOT pull comrak/egui_commonmark into this MT. Save ONLY on explicit Save click (no autosave). Screenshots to the EXTERNAL Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp-kernel-012-mt-025/ root + assert_no_local_artifact_dir(). ACCESSKIT VARIANT: Role::Document + a multiline-text role - use the field-correct accesskit 0.21.1 variant (MultiLineTextInput may not be a literal - use the closest, e.g. TextInput with multiline state); ACs assert the author_ids. backend_client + tests/test_wiki_page_panel.rs in allowed_paths (contract under-scoped).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Port the React LoomCanvasBoard (MT-261 parity) to the native egui frontend (crate handshake-native, lib path handshake_native::). The canvas board is a spatial canvas where LoomBlocks are placed as reference cards (not copies) with real pan/zoom, drag-to-place, edge drawing (semantic and visual), grouping, and viewport persistence. The board itself is a typed LoomBlock (content_type=canvas); placements and edges are authoritative PostgreSQL/EventLedger state. Expected diff shape: one new file src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/canvas_board.rs containing LoomCanvasBoard widget, edits to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs.

Exact files to create or edit:
- CREATE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/canvas_board.rs — LoomCanvasBoard widget
- EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs — pub mod canvas_board; + re-export

Reuse (do not reinvent): the spatial-canvas painting/pan/zoom primitives in the existing WP-011 module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/canvas_board.rs (generic board surface), the Loom graph view in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs (block/edge model + graph rendering), the shared HTTP client in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (all backend calls route through it), command/selection/clipboard wiring via src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs, AccessKit exposure via src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/* (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs), and MCP tool/action exposure via src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mcp/* where the canvas surface must be model-drivable.

Exact APIs / React reference:
- PRIMARY REACT REFERENCE: app/src/components/LoomCanvasBoard.tsx — the complete React implementation. Key behaviors to port exactly:
  (a) placeBlockOnCanvas(workspaceId, canvasBlockId, {placedBlockId, x, y, w, h}) on drop (api.ts ~1617+)
  (b) createCanvasCard(workspaceId, canvasBlockId, {title, body, x, y, w, h}) for free-text cards
  (c) updateCanvasBoardViewport(workspaceId, canvasBlockId, {pan_x, pan_y, zoom}) on viewport change
  (d) updateCanvasPlacement(workspaceId, placementId, {groupId}) for grouping
  (e) removeCanvasPlacement(workspaceId, placementId) for removal (source block kept)
  (f) createLoomEdge(workspaceId, {sourceBlockId, targetBlockId, edgeType:'mention'}) for semantic edges
  (g) addCanvasVisualEdge(workspaceId, canvasBlockId, {fromPlacementId, toPlacementId}) for visual edges
  (h) getCanvasBoard(workspaceId, canvasBlockId) -> LoomCanvasBoardView {board, placements, visual_edges}
  (i) getLoomBlock(workspaceId, blockId) to resolve live block previews (reference, not copy)
- Backend bindings: all functions from app/src/lib/api.ts in the section starting at line 1617 (LOOM_CANVAS_BOARD_SCHEMA_ID block), called through src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Define CanvasPlacementCard { placement_id: String, placed_block_id: String, x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32, z_index: i32, group_id: Option<String>, live_title: Option<String>, live_content_type: Option<String>, selected: bool }.
2. Define VisualEdge { visual_edge_id: String, from_placement_id: String, to_placement_id: String }.
3. Define LoomCanvasBoard widget state: { workspace_id, canvas_block_id, placements: Vec<CanvasPlacementCard>, visual_edges: Vec<VisualEdge>, pan: Vec2, zoom: f32, selected: HashSet<String>, edge_mode: EdgeMode (Semantic | Visual), edge_from: Option<String>, status: String, loading: bool, error: Option<String> }.
4. On init: call getCanvasBoard -> populate placements + visual_edges + pan + zoom. Then for each placement, call getLoomBlock to resolve live_title + live_content_type. Store results in placements (ref semantics: a missing block shows '(stale reference)', never a copy).
5. Render loop in show():
   a. Top toolbar strip (using egui::TopBottomPanel or manual strip at top of allocated rect):
      - Pan-left / Pan-right buttons (author_id='canvas.pan-left'/'canvas.pan-right'): adjust pan.x by ±40; call updateCanvasBoardViewport on release.
      - Zoom-out / Zoom-in buttons (author_id='canvas.zoom-out'/'canvas.zoom-in'): adjust zoom by ±0.25 clamped [0.25, 4.0]; call updateCanvasBoardViewport.
      - Zoom value label (author_id='canvas.zoom-value').
      - '+ Text card' button (author_id='canvas.add-card'): calls createCanvasCard with default position (40, 40) and title=timestamp.
      - 'Group (N)' button (author_id='canvas.group'): enabled only if selected.len() >= 2; calls updateCanvasPlacement for each selected with a new group_id.
      - Edge mode dropdown/toggle (author_id='canvas.edge-mode'): Semantic | Visual.
      - 'Draw edge from selected' button (author_id='canvas.start-edge'): enabled if selected.len()==1; on click sets edge_from = selected[0].
   b. Status bar: single line of status text (author_id='canvas.status').
   c. Canvas surface (fills remaining rect):
      - Background: draw a dotted grid pattern using Painter::circle_filled at 24px spacing with radius 1px, color gray(203).
      - Apply pan+zoom transform: translate by pan, then scale by zoom (use Painter with transform via egui::emath::RectTransform or manual coordinate math).
      - Draw visual edges: for each VisualEdge, find from/to placements, draw dashed line between card centers (stroke 2px, Color32::from_gray(148), dash pattern 6/4).
      - Draw placement cards: for each CanvasPlacementCard, draw a rounded rect at (x,y,w,h) * zoom + pan. Border: if selected 2px blue, else 1px gray(203). White fill. Show live_title (bold 13px) and live_content_type (muted 11px). Show a remove button ('x') at top-right of card.
      - Click on empty area: deselect all + start pan drag.
      - Drag on empty area: pan (mouse delta added to pan; persist on release via updateCanvasBoardViewport).
      - Scroll wheel: zoom (multiply zoom by 1.15^delta; clamp; zoom toward pointer; persist).
      - Click on card: toggle selection (shift=additive); if edge_from is set and this card != edge_from, call drawEdge(edge_from, this placement_id); clear edge_from.
      - Drag FROM external source (egui DragAndDrop or OS drop): accept MIME 'application/x-handshake-loom-block' JSON {blockId, title}; compute drop position in canvas space = (screen_pos - pan) / zoom; call placeBlockOnCanvas; refresh.
6. Edge drawing: if edge_mode=Semantic, call createLoomEdge(source_block_id, target_block_id, 'mention'); if edge_mode=Visual, call addCanvasVisualEdge(from_placement_id, to_placement_id). Always refresh after.
7. AccessKit: each placement card gets author_id='canvas.placement.{placement_id}' role=Group, label=live_title, actions=[DefaultAction=select, Remove]. Remove button 'canvas.placement.{placement_id}.remove'. Toolbar buttons as listed above. Status bar 'canvas.status' role=Status. Register all nodes through src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/*.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: MT-021 must be complete for shared HTTP client (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs). No dependency on MT-022 through MT-025.

Risk if missed: Canvas board (Obsidian Canvas parity, MT-261) is absent from native frontend. This is a key differentiator surface.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Opening a canvas block loads the board from real PG (with >=2 placements seeded). Placements render as cards showing live block titles (reference, not copy text). The zoom value label shows '1.00x'.
AC2: Pan buttons adjust pan by 40px and the placements visibly shift. Viewport is persisted to backend via updateCanvasBoardViewport.
AC3: Zoom-in button increases zoom; zoom-out decreases it; zoom value label updates. Both clamp at [0.25, 4.0].

AC4: Dropping a Loom block (via drag with MIME 'application/x-handshake-loom-block') onto the canvas calls placeBlockOnCanvas and the new placement appears in the next refresh. The new card shows the live block title (proves reference not copy).
AC5: Clicking '+ Text card' calls createCanvasCard, a new placement appears, and its title reflects the created block's title (timestamp-based from React reference).

AC6: Selecting 2 cards (shift-click) and clicking 'Group (2)' calls updateCanvasPlacement for each with a shared group_id. The group_id attribute is visible in the AccessKit data-group-id of each affected card.

AC7: Drawing a Semantic edge (edge_mode=Semantic): click 'Draw edge from selected', click a second card, assert createLoomEdge API called with source and target block_ids. Drawing a Visual edge: same flow with edge_mode=Visual, assert addCanvasVisualEdge API called.
AC8: Clicking the remove 'x' button on a card calls removeCanvasPlacement and the card disappears from the board. Source block is NOT deleted (verify getLoomBlock still returns it).
AC9: AccessKit tree includes 'canvas.pan-left', 'canvas.pan-right', 'canvas.zoom-in', 'canvas.zoom-out', 'canvas.add-card', 'canvas.edge-mode', 'canvas.placement.{placement_id}' for each card.
AC10: Board with zero placements shows empty canvas with no panic and no 'stale reference' text.

PROOF2: kittest test with 2 seeded placements in real PG: assert 2 'canvas.placement.*' AccessKit nodes and their labels match the live block titles.

PROOF3: kittest drop-to-place test: simulate drop event at canvas position (100,100) with block_id='block-drop-1', assert placeBlockOnCanvas API call fired with correct x/y, assert 3 placement AccessKit nodes after refresh.
PROOF4: kittest edge-semantic test: select 'canvas.placement.p-001', click 'canvas.start-edge', click 'canvas.placement.p-002', assert createLoomEdge API call with correct source/target block_ids.

PROOF5: kittest remove test: click 'canvas.placement.p-001.remove', assert removeCanvasPlacement called and 'canvas.placement.p-001' absent from AccessKit tree; assert getLoomBlock('block-001') still returns 200.
PROOF6: Screenshot from kittest shows a non-white canvas with at least one card shape visible (rect with rounded corners).
implementation_notes: Canvas coordinate transform: canvas_pos = (screen_pos - pan) / zoom. Apply this to convert mouse position to canvas space for drop placement and card hit testing. Reuse the pan/zoom transform helpers already present in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/canvas_board.rs rather than reimplementing them.
Card hit testing: check if canvas_pos is within placement rect [x, y, x+w, y+h]. Iterate placements in reverse z_index order for correct hit priority.
Pan drag: detect pointer press on empty canvas (no card hit), track pointer delta each frame while button held, add to pan. On release, call updateCanvasBoardViewport.
Zoom to pointer: new_pan = pointer - (pointer - pan) * (new_zoom / old_zoom). This keeps the canvas point under the pointer stationary.
Grid drawing: iterate x from 0 to canvas_width step 24, y from 0 to canvas_height step 24; painter.circle_filled(canvas_to_screen(x,y), 1.0, gray(203)).

Dashed line for visual edges: egui::Painter does not have a native dash API. Implement by splitting the line segment into dash/gap segments manually: for a line from A to B, compute unit vector, alternate drawing solid segments of length 6 and skipping segments of length 4.

MIME drag: egui does not natively handle OS file drops but egui_winit exposes dropped files. For inter-panel drag, use egui::DragAndDrop payload with a custom type wrapping the block_id. Fall back to external OS drop via egui::ViewportCommand if available.
Avoid re-fetching live blocks on every frame: fetch once on load and on explicit refresh. Do not store live block content — only title and content_type (reference-only display).

Refresh after every mutation: all mutating API calls (place, create, remove, edge, group, viewport) are followed by a getCanvasBoard + getLoomBlock re-resolve cycle. Route every backend call through src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Port the React BlockCollectionView (MT-262 parity) to the native egui frontend. This is a multi-mode saved-view host. A saved view is a typed LoomBlock (content_type='view_def') whose definition lives in PostgreSQL. The native widget loads the view definition, executes its query against the real Loom query backend (SQL-side), and renders one of three sub-views: Table, Kanban, or Calendar. Crucially: (1) table header sort clicks call updateBlockView + re-query on the backend, never client-side sort; (2) Kanban card drag-to-lane calls updateLoomBlock ({add_tags, remove_tags}) and re-queries — never local state mutations. Expected diff shape: one new file src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/block_collection_view.rs with BlockCollectionView, TableSubView, KanbanSubView, CalendarSubView, edits to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs. The native Loom surface reuses the existing WP-011 module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs (the established Loom graph surface) and the shared command/selection bus modules src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs; backend access reuses src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (HTTP client). AccessKit author_ids are registered via the accessibility/ module (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/).

Exact files to create or edit:
- CREATE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/block_collection_view.rs — BlockCollectionView + three sub-view structs
- EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs — pub mod block_collection_view; + re-export

Exact APIs / React reference:
- PRIMARY REACT REFERENCES:
  (a) app/src/components/BlockCollectionView.tsx — top-level host; getBlockView + queryBlockViewResults + updateBlockView + updateLoomBlock (handle sort and card-move).
  (b) app/src/components/LoomTableView.tsx — sortable typed column table; onSortChange fires backend re-sort, never client-side.
  (c) app/src/components/LoomKanbanView.tsx — drag-and-drop kanban; DRAG_MIME='application/x-handshake-kanban-card'; handleDrop fires real updateLoomBlock mutation.
  (d) app/src/components/LoomCalendarView.tsx — buckets blocks by date field; date_from/date_to applied server-side.
- Backend bindings:
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/definitions/{view_block_id} — getBlockView -> BlockViewRecord {block, definition: BlockViewDefinition}
  - POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/definitions/{view_block_id}/results — queryBlockViewResults -> BlockViewResults {kind, blocks, groups?, total_returned}
  - PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/definitions/{view_block_id} — updateBlockView (persist new sort definition)
  - PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id} — updateLoomBlock ({add_tags, remove_tags}) for Kanban lane move
  - POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/definitions — createBlockView (for creating new saved views; wire a 'New view' button)

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Define BlockCollectionView { workspace_id: String, view_block_id: String, definition: Option<BlockViewDefinition>, results: Option<BlockViewResults>, loading: bool, error: Option<String>, status: String, kanban_drag: Option<KanbanDragState> } where KanbanDragState = { block_id: String, from_lane_key: String }.
2. On init: call getBlockView to load definition, then call queryBlockViewResults to load results. Both calls run sequentially (definition first, then results).
3. Render a mode indicator strip at top showing the current kind (table / kanban / calendar) with a kind switcher (author_id='bcv.kind.table', 'bcv.kind.kanban', 'bcv.kind.calendar'). Kind change = call updateBlockView with new definition.kind + call queryBlockViewResults.
4. Status bar: show 'Re-sorting...' / 'Moving card...' / '' via status field (author_id='bcv.status' role=Status).

TableSubView:
5. Render columns from definition.columns (or default [title, updated]). For each column, show a header button (author_id='bcv.table.sort.{field}'). Click = call flipDirection() (same logic as React: same field toggles asc/desc, new field = asc), call updateBlockView with new definition.sort, then call queryBlockViewResults. Set status='Re-sorting...' while in flight.
6. Render rows: for each block in results.blocks, render a table row (author_id='bcv.table.row.{block_id}'). Cells show: title (block.title ?? block.original_filename ?? block.block_id), created_at, updated_at, journal_date, content_type, pinned yes/no, favorite yes/no, backlink_count, mention_count, tag_count per the React LoomTableView.cellValue() function.
7. Sort indicator: if definition.sort.field == column, show ▲ (asc) or ▼ (desc) after the column label.

KanbanSubView:
8. Render lanes from results.groups (BlockViewLane[]). Each lane has a key (author_id='bcv.kanban.lane.{key}') and a list of cards. Lane label: if key=='__untagged__' show 'Untagged', else show key.
9. Each card (author_id='bcv.kanban.card.{block_id}') shows block.title ?? block.block_id. Make cards draggable using egui's DragAndDrop or a manual drag tracker.
10. On drop: get the from_lane_key from KanbanDragState, get the to_lane_key from the drop target lane. Call updateLoomBlock(block_id, { add_tags: to_key=='__untagged__' ? [] : [to_key], remove_tags: from_key=='__untagged__' ? [] : [from_key] }). Set status='Moving card...' while in flight. After call completes, call queryBlockViewResults to re-query. Never mutate local lane arrays — the re-query is the source of truth.
11. Show a busy indicator (status='Moving card...') while drop mutation is in flight. Accept no further drops while busy.

CalendarSubView:
12. Render blocks bucketed by date field (journal_date, created, or updated per definition.calendar_date_field). Use the same bucketKey() logic as React LoomCalendarView: journal_date -> block.journal_date ?? 'undated', updated -> block.updated_at.slice(0,10), default -> block.created_at.slice(0,10).
13. Sort bucket keys alphabetically. Render each bucket as a day column or day strip (author_id='bcv.calendar.day.{date_key}'). Each entry is a row (author_id='bcv.calendar.entry.{block_id}') showing block title.
14. Date-range filtering is backend-side: when the user selects a date range in a date picker widget, update definition.query.date_from and definition.query.date_to, call updateBlockView, then queryBlockViewResults. Render a simple date range input (two egui::DatePickerButton or text field inputs for from/to). Author_ids: 'bcv.calendar.date-from', 'bcv.calendar.date-to'.

New View creation:
15. Show a '+ New view' button (author_id='bcv.new-view'). Opens a small popup with: kind selector, title input, confirm. On confirm, call createBlockView and then switch to the new view_block_id.

AccessKit summary: all interactive elements use stable author_ids as listed; table header buttons, table rows, kanban lanes, kanban cards, calendar day headers, calendar entries, kind switcher buttons, status bar, new-view button.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: MT-021 must be complete (HTTP client). MT-023 must be complete (tag identity used for Kanban lane keys from tag hubs). No dependency on MT-022, MT-024, MT-025, MT-026.

Risk if missed: The block-collection views (table, kanban, calendar) are absent from the native frontend. This is a major knowledge management surface (Notion/Obsidian databases parity).

original_scope.summary:
Build the native Rust/egui LoomSearchV2Surface panel - the UI-only counterpart to the React LoomSearchV2Panel (app/src/components/LoomSearchV2Panel.tsx). The backend loom_search_v2 endpoint (POST /workspaces/:workspace_id/loom/search-v2, implemented in KERNEL-009 MT-264) is already complete; this MT wires the existing API to a new native egui panel.

Diff shape: create src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_search_v2.rs (new flat module, ~350 lines). Register it as a pub mod in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs. Add a LoomSearchV2 pane to the shell's pane registry by reusing the existing pane_registry.rs registration path (the WP-011 pane host - do NOT invent a new panel enum file). Wire the HTTP client calls through the existing backend_client.rs to POST to /workspaces/{id}/loom/search-v2 and to POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/views (save-as-view).

Panel features to implement (parity with React reference):
1. QUERY BAR: single-line egui::TextEdit bound to a query string field. On Enter key or 'Search' button click, fire async HTTP POST to /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/search-v2 with body {query, content_type?, graph_boost: 1.0, limit: 25}. Deserialize LoomSearchV2Response {hits: [{block, score, fts_rank, trgm_sim, vector_sim, edge_degree, highlight}], content_type_facets: BTreeMap<String,i64>, semantic_available: bool, total: i64}.
2. STATUS LINE: show 'Searching...' during load, '{N} results (semantic on/off)' after response, or error text. Use egui::Label with aria-live equivalent.
3. CONTENT-TYPE FACETS: after a response, render one toggle button per entry in content_type_facets (sorted by count descending). Each shows '{type} ({count})'. Clicking a facet toggles it as a filter and immediately re-fires the search with that content_type. Active facet visually highlighted (egui::Button::selected or custom fill).
4. RESULTS LIST: egui::ScrollArea containing one clickable row per LoomSearchV2Hit. Each row shows: block.title (or block_id fallback), block.content_type badge, score formatted to 3 decimal places, and the highlight string. The highlight may contain <mark>...</mark> markers: parse them and render the marked segments in a distinct color (e.g. egui::Color32::YELLOW background on the text run, using egui::RichText or a custom painter). Clicking a row calls the on_open_block callback (routes to the Loom block viewer, wired in the shell via loom_graph.rs).
5. SAVE AS VIEW: a 'Save as view' button, enabled only when there are results. On click, POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views with body {kind: 'table', query: {content_type: <active_facet_or_omit>}, columns: ['title','content_type','updated'], title: 'Search: {query}'}. Show a status label with the new block_id on success or the error string on failure. This reuses the same createBlockView backend path as the MT-262 block-collection view.
6. STATE MACHINE: loading bool, error Option<String>, view_status Option<String>, response Option<LoomSearchV2Response>, active_content_type Option<String>. Keep all state inside LoomSearchV2PanelState struct.

Files to create/edit:
- CREATE: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_search_v2.rs
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs (pub mod loom_search_v2;)
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs (register the LoomSearchV2 pane in the existing WP-011 pane registry)
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (add loom_search_v2 async fn and create_block_view async fn)

Implementation steps:
1. Define LoomSearchV2PanelState struct with: query: String, active_content_type: Option<String>, response: Option<LoomSearchV2Response>, loading: bool, error: Option<String>, view_status: Option<String>.
2. Define LoomSearchV2Response, LoomSearchV2Hit, LoomBlock as serde-deserializable structs in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (matching the backend JSON schema from storage/loom.rs).
3. Implement async fn loom_search_v2(base_url, workspace_id, body) -> Result<LoomSearchV2Response, String> using the existing backend_client.rs HTTP client. POST to {base_url}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/search-v2.
4. Implement async fn create_block_view(base_url, workspace_id, body) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String>. POST to {base_url}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views.
5. In the panel show() fn: render query TextEdit + Search button + Save-as-view button in a horizontal strip.
6. Render status line.
7. Render facet buttons if response.content_type_facets non-empty (sort by value desc).
8. Render egui::ScrollArea with result rows. For each hit parse highlight: split on '<mark>' and '</mark>' tokens, build a LayoutJob with alternating normal/highlighted TextFormat runs.
9. Handle AccessKit (reuse the WP-011 accessibility/ subsystem - accessibility/mod.rs, accessibility/registry.rs, accessibility/snapshot.rs): assign author_ids to query input (id: 'loom-search-v2.query'), search button ('loom-search-v2.search'), save-view button ('loom-search-v2.save-view'), each facet button ('loom-search-v2.facet.{content_type}'), each result row ('loom-search-v2.result.{block_id}'), status label ('loom-search-v2.status'). Use the egui AccessKit integration via accessibility/registry.rs (egui::Id from stable strings) and set role + action where egui_kittest requires.
10. Async dispatch: egui is single-threaded; use the shell's existing async bridge (tokio one-shot or channel pattern used by other WP-011 surfaces, e.g. event_bus.rs) to fire the search and receive the response on the next frame. Do not block the UI thread.

Dependencies/unblock conditions: requires the WP-011 shell pane infrastructure to be loadable (the pane_registry.rs registry must be able to host this pane). The backend /loom/search-v2 endpoint is already live (KERNEL-009 MT-264). No new backend work needed. This MT is self-contained and has no MT-level depends_on within WP-012.

Risk if missed: Loom Search v2 is a core search surface and a dependency for the interconnection proofs (MT-030, MT-044). Missing it means the quick-switcher and parity proof cannot demonstrate the semantic search modality.
acceptance_criteria: LoomSearchV2PanelState struct exists in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_search_v2.rs with fields: query, active_content_type, response (Option<LoomSearchV2Response>), loading, error, view_status.
Typing a query and pressing Enter (or the Search button) fires a real HTTP POST to /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/search-v2 against a running handshake_core instance and populates the response.
Status line shows '{N} results (semantic on)' or '{N} results (keyword/fuzzy only)' based on semantic_available flag.
Content-type facet buttons appear after a result with multiple content types; clicking a facet re-runs the search with that content_type filter; clicking the active facet again clears it.
Each result row renders: block.title (or block_id fallback), content_type badge, score to 3 decimal places, highlight with <mark> segments rendered in a distinct color (not as raw HTML tags).
Clicking a result row invokes the on_open_block callback with the correct block_id.
Save as view button is disabled with no results and enabled with results; clicking it POSTs to /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views and displays the returned block_id in the view_status label.
All interactive widgets have stable AccessKit author_ids matching the naming contract in implementation_notes.

original_scope.summary:
Build the native Rust/egui Find-in-Files + Replace-in-Files surface, porting the React WorkspaceSearchPanel (app/src/components/WorkspaceSearchPanel.tsx, MT-250). This is a workspace-wide search across all rich documents and Loom blocks, with a two-phase replace-preview-then-apply flow. It is distinct from the single-document FindReplacePanel (MT-004 / FindReplacePanel.tsx which is a code-editor-local feature).

Diff shape: create src/frontend/handshake_native/src/find_in_files.rs (~550 lines) as a new flat module. Register it as a pane in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs and wire it into the shell in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs. Add all backend HTTP calls (loom search, workspace search bookmarks, rich-document load/save) to the existing shared HTTP client src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (searchLoomGraph -> GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/search; loadRichDocument -> GET /knowledge/rich-documents/{id}; saveRichDocument -> PATCH /knowledge/rich-documents/{id}). Reuse the existing workspace search surface in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/search_rail.rs for shared query/result rendering helpers where applicable, and the shared command surface command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs for cross-surface selection/clipboard/command dispatch. Reuse accessibility/* for AccessKit author_id assignment.

Panel features to implement (parity with React WorkspaceSearchPanel):

1. QUERY BAR: egui::TextEdit for query. Match-option toggle buttons: case-sensitive (Aa), whole-word (W), regex (.*) - each aria-pressed with active visual state. Kind-filter dropdown (egui::ComboBox): All / Documents / Loom blocks / Files / Tags / Symbols / Work Packets / Microtasks / UserManual / Wiki pages. Tag-filter text input. Path-filter text input.

2. SEARCH: 'Search' button fires GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/search with query params {q, limit: 500, offset, sourceKinds?, tagIds?, caseSensitive, wholeWord, isRegex, path?}. Paginate: keep requesting with offset+=500 until page.len() < 500. Collect all LoomGraphSearchHit {source_kind, result_kind, ref_id, title, excerpt, metadata, block?} into results Vec. Client-side filter: for case/word/regex options, apply hitMatchesClientOptions (same logic as React: build regex over title+excerpt haystack, skip wholeWord=false early-exit).

3. REPLACE-PREVIEW phase: 'Preview Replace' button enabled after a search with results. On click: compile the search regex (same compileSearchRegex logic: wrap non-regex query in escapeRegex, apply flags); for each hit with a documentId (extracted via documentIdFromLoomSearchHit logic: metadata.rich_document_id or metadata.document_id or block.document_id, must start with 'KRD-'), GET the rich document (GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id}/knowledge or GET /knowledge/rich-documents/{document_id}), walk the content_json tree (visit all text nodes and attrs.code strings), apply replaceSegment (regex exec loop with wholeWord boundary check, group expansion for regex mode via $1..$9/$&/$$), accumulate per-document ReplacementPlan {document_id, title, expected_version, content_json_after, match_count, before_preview, after_preview, match_previews}. Show preview list in a scrollable panel: each plan shows title, match count, before/after preview snippets, and per-match before/after previews.

4. REPLACE-APPLY phase: 'Apply' button enabled when previewPlans non-empty and plan key matches current search+replace key (stale guard). For each plan, PATCH the rich document (PATCH /knowledge/rich-documents/{document_id} with {doc_version: expected_version, content_json: replaced_content}). Collect save_receipt_event_ids. Show status: 'Applied N plans; receipts: ...'. On success re-run search to refresh results.

5. BOOKMARKS (saved searches): on panel open, GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/search-bookmarks (returns JSON with schema_id 'hsk.workspace_search_bookmark_state@1', key 'bookmarks': array). Show saved searches as a list; each has restore and remove buttons. 'Bookmark Search' button saves current query+options via PUT /workspaces/{workspace_id}/search-bookmarks. Max 20 bookmarks.

6. STATE KEYS: searchPlanKey = hash of {query, sourceKinds, tagIds, path, options}; replacePlanKey = hash of {searchPlanKey, replacement}. Guard preview freshness: if resultSetKey != searchPlanKey, show 'Search results are stale; run Search again'. Guard apply freshness: if previewPlanKey != replacePlanKey, show 'Preview is stale; run Preview Replace again'.

Files to create/edit:
- CREATE: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/find_in_files.rs
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs (register the find-in-files pane)
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs (wire pane into the shell)
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (search_loom_graph, get/save workspace search bookmarks, load_rich_document, save_rich_document)

Reuse pointers (existing WP-011 modules):
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs - shared HTTP client for all backend API calls (add the loom-search, bookmark, and rich-document methods here; do not create a new api/ dir).
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/search_rail.rs - existing workspace search surface; reuse its query/result rendering helpers.
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs - shared selection/clipboard/command dispatch bus.
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs - pane registration for the new surface.
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/ - AccessKit author_id assignment and snapshot.

Implementation steps:
1. Define FindInFilesPanelState with all fields from the React component: query, replacement, kind, tag_filter, path_filter, case_sensitive, whole_word, is_regex, results (Vec<LoomGraphSearchHit>), loading, error, replace_status, preview_plans (Vec<ReplacementPlan>), preview_plan_key, result_set_key, bookmarks, bookmark_status.
2. Define LoomGraphSearchHit struct: source_kind, result_kind, ref_id, title, excerpt, metadata (serde_json::Value), block (Option<LoomBlock>).
3. Implement search_loom_graph() HTTP fn on backend_client.rs. GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/search with query string params. Note: this is the LEGACY /loom/search endpoint (not /loom/search-v2); confirm the exact params contract from the backend route handler.
4. Implement compile_search_regex(query, opts) -> Result<Regex, String> using the 'regex' crate. For non-regex mode, escape special chars first (regex::escape). Flags: case-insensitive if not case_sensitive (Regex::new with (?i) prefix or RegexBuilder).
5. Implement hit_matches_client_options(hit, query, opts): build regex, search title+excerpt, apply whole_word boundary check (check char before start and after end using Unicode word-char property via regex \b or manual check).
6. Implement document_id_from_hit(hit): mirror the React documentIdFromLoomSearchHit logic - check metadata.rich_document_id, metadata.document_id, block.document_id, fallback if source_kind == 'document' use ref_id; only accept if starts with 'KRD-'.
7. Implement replaceSegment(text, regex, replacement, opts) -> (new_text, count, before_preview, after_preview, match_previews). Iterate regex matches; handle zero-length match guard (advance by 1); check whole_word boundary; expand replacement groups for isRegex ($1..$9, $&, $$); collect 24-char context previews per match.
8. Implement visit_content_json(node, regex, replacement, opts): recurse through content_json (ProseMirror-style AST as serde_json::Value). For text nodes (node.text), apply replaceSegment. For code block attrs (node.attrs.code), apply replaceSegment. Recurse into node.content array.
9. Render preview list in a ScrollArea: for each ReplacementPlan, show a collapsible section with title, match_count, before/after text, and per-match previews. Use egui::CollapsingHeader.

implementation_notes: React reference for the LEGACY search endpoint (not v2): WorkspaceSearchPanel calls searchLoomGraph() which maps to GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/search. The legacy endpoint accepts q, limit, offset, sourceKinds (repeated or comma-separated), tagIds, mentionIds, caseSensitive, wholeWord, isRegex, path as query string params. RichDocument load: the React WorkspaceSearchPanel uses loadRichDocument(documentId). This calls GET /knowledge/rich-documents/{id} (KERNEL-009). The Rust frontend should call the same endpoint via backend_client.rs. Response: {document: {doc_version, title, content_json, crdt_document_id}}.

RichDocument save: saveRichDocument(id, doc_version, content_json, context, metadata) maps to PATCH /knowledge/rich-documents/{id} with body {doc_version, content_json, ...metadata}. Response: {save_receipt_event_id}.

Content JSON walking: content_json is a ProseMirror-style tree serialized as JSON (serde_json::Value). Node shape: {type: String, text?: String, attrs?: {code?: String, ...}, content?: [Node], ...}. Use a recursive Rust fn that traverses by checking 'text' key and 'attrs.code' key, then recursing into 'content' array.

Replace expansion: for regex mode, implement $1..$9, $&, $$ group expansion in the replacement string after each match. For non-regex mode, use literal replacement. Mirror the React expandReplacement fn (WorkspaceSearchPanel.tsx:232-239).

Plan key for stale guard: use a deterministic string hash of the search params as result_set_key, and hash of {result_set_key, replacement} as preview_plan_key. A simple approach: serde_json::to_string of a normalized struct, then take its std::collections::hash_map sha or just store a counter that increments on each search run.

Bookmarks endpoint: GET /workspaces/{id}/search-bookmarks returns WorkspaceSearchBookmarkState {schema_id, bookmark_state: {bookmarks: [...]}}. PUT /workspaces/{id}/search-bookmarks takes the same shape. The schema_id must be 'hsk.workspace_search_bookmark_state@1' (backend validates this).

Client-side hitMatchesClientOptions: only applied when at least one of case_sensitive, whole_word, or is_regex is true (otherwise all hits pass). Build the regex, search title+newline+excerpt, check whole_word boundaries manually if needed (check char class \w around the match boundaries using Unicode properties).
Pagination: the React reference paginates with SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE=500 (WorkspaceSearchPanel.tsx:30,568-583). Implement the same loop: offset=0, increment by 500, stop when page.len() < 500.

Whole-word boundary: mirror the React isWordBoundary fn (WorkspaceSearchPanel.tsx:222-230). Check the character immediately before match.start and immediately after match.end; if either is a Unicode word character (letter, number, or underscore) and the match edge is on a word character, the boundary fails.
