original_scope.summary:
Integrate the native editors with the WP-011 shell quick-switcher (WP-011 MT-017 target), extending the existing native quick-switcher module (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/quick_switcher.rs) that ports the React QuickSwitcher (app/src/components/QuickSwitcher.tsx). The quick switcher is a global keyboard-activated overlay (Ctrl+P / Cmd+P) that searches the full project graph (loom_block, file, tag_hub, document, symbol, work_packet, micro_task, user_manual_page, wiki_page) and opens the selected target in the appropriate editor or panel.

This MT has two distinct responsibilities:
(A) Implement/extend the QuickSwitcher panel (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/quick_switcher.rs): the floating modal overlay with search input and result list, bound to GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/graph-search and GET/POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/quick-switcher/recents. Reuse the existing WP-011 command surface (command_registry.rs + command_palette.rs) for shortcut activation and the shared selection/dispatch bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs).
(B) Wire the open-target dispatch: resolve each LoomGraphSearchHit to a NavigationTarget and dispatch it to the correct editor/panel in the shell - opening documents in the rich-text editor (MT-011 surface), loom blocks in the Loom viewer (MT-021, reuse loom_graph.rs), code symbols in the code editor (MT-001), work packets/microtasks in the GOV viewer, user manual pages, and wiki pages. This is the 'integration' part: after this MT, selecting any quick-switcher result navigates inside the native shell.

Diff shape: edit/extend src/frontend/handshake_native/src/quick_switcher.rs (~300 lines of net additions). Add a QuickSwitcher overlay entry to the shell's modal/overlay stack (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs). Register the global keybinding for Ctrl+P (or platform shortcut) through the existing command_registry.rs command surface. Add HTTP fns in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs: search_loom_graph (graph search endpoint) and list/record quick_switcher_recents.

Features to implement:

1. MODAL OVERLAY: the quick switcher is a full-screen semi-transparent overlay containing a centered card. It is activated by Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS). Pressing Escape or clicking outside the card closes it. On open, the search input receives focus immediately (first-frame autofocus).

2. QUERY INPUT: single-line TextEdit, placeholder 'Open by title, block, symbol, WP, MT, manual, or wiki page'. On each keystroke, after a 150ms debounce, fire GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/graph-search with {q: trimmed, limit: 25, sourceKinds: [loom_block, file, tag_hub, document, symbol, work_packet, micro_task, user_manual_page, wiki_page]}. Cancel previous in-flight request (use a generation counter or cancel token).

3. RECENTS: on open (when workspace_id is Some), GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/quick-switcher/recents?limit=20. Store recents as Vec<String> (hit_keys = '{source_kind}:{ref_id}'). When ordering results, promote recents to the top (sort: recents-first by position in the recents list, then remaining results in original order). Mirror the React orderedResults useMemo (QuickSwitcher.tsx:154-164).

4. RESULT LIST: scrollable list of LoomGraphSearchHit items. Show up to 25 items. For each hit: source_kind badge (from SOURCE_LABELS map: loom_block->'Loom Block', file->'File', tag_hub->'Tag Hub', document->'Document', symbol->'Symbol', work_packet->'Work Packet', micro_task->'Microtask', user_manual_page->'UserManual Page', wiki_page->'Wiki Page'), title, excerpt, and the open-target label (from resolve_open_target). Keyboard navigation: ArrowDown/ArrowUp moves selection; Enter activates the selected item. Mouse hover also updates selection.

5. STATUS LINE: 'Type to search the project graph' (no query), 'No workspace selected' (no workspace), 'Searching graph...' (loading), error string, or '{N} result(s)' (loaded). If recents failed to load, append '; durable recents unavailable: {error}'.

6. OPEN-TARGET DISPATCH (the integration core): implement resolve_open_target(hit: LoomGraphSearchHit) -> NavigationTarget porting the React openTargetForLoomSearchHit (app/src/lib/loom_search_open_target.ts). Navigation targets:
   - wiki_page + non-empty ref_id -> NavigationTarget::WikiPage { projection_id }
   - user_manual_page -> NavigationTarget::UserManualPage { slug } (from metadata.page_slug or ref_id)
   - document with KRD-prefixed doc id -> NavigationTarget::Document { document_id } (check metadata.rich_document_id, metadata.document_id, block.document_id)
   - loom_block with document_id -> NavigationTarget::Document { document_id } (open source doc)
   - loom_block with no document_id -> NavigationTarget::LoomBlock { block_id: ref_id }
   - file, tag_hub -> NavigationTarget::LoomBlock { block_id: ref_id }
   - symbol -> NavigationTarget::CodeSymbol { symbol_entity_id: ref_id }
   - work_packet -> NavigationTarget::WorkPacket { wp_id } (from metadata.work_packet_id, metadata.wp_id, or parsed from ref_id via WP-xxx pattern)
   - micro_task -> NavigationTarget::MicroTask { mt_id, wp_id? }
   - fallback -> NavigationTarget::None (disabled item)
   Each NavigationTarget arm dispatches to the appropriate panel via the shell's navigation bus (a channel or trait object built on the existing event_bus.rs + command_registry.rs surface): open_document(id), open_loom_block(id), open_code_symbol(id), open_work_packet(id), open_micro_task(mt_id, wp_id?), open_user_manual_page(slug), open_wiki_page(projection_id).

7. RECENT RECORDING: on successful open, POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/quick-switcher/recents with body {result_kind, source_kind, ref_id, title, excerpt, metadata}. On success, prepend the returned hit_key to the local recents Vec (deduplicated, max 20). Mirror QuickSwitcher.tsx:177-187.

8. DISABLED ITEMS: if resolve_open_target returns NavigationTarget::None, render the result item as disabled (grayed, not clickable). Mirror target.enabled check in React.

Files to create/edit:
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/quick_switcher.rs (existing WP-011 module; extend with graph-search, recents, resolve_open_target, dispatch)
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs (module wiring if a new submodule is added)
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs (modal overlay stack, Ctrl+P keybind registration via command_registry, navigation dispatch)
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs (register the Ctrl+P quick-switcher command if not already present)
- EDIT: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (search_loom_graph if not already from MT-029, list_quick_switcher_recents, record_quick_switcher_recent)

Implementation steps:
1. Define QuickSwitcherState: query, results (Vec<LoomGraphSearchHit>), recents (Vec<String>), selected_index, loading, error, recents_error, debounce_generation (u64).
2. Implement search_loom_graph() in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs: GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/graph-search with params {q, limit, sourceKinds}. This is the SAME endpoint WorkspaceSearchPanel uses (verify the route). Return Vec<LoomGraphSearchHit>.
3. Implement list_quick_switcher_recents(workspace_id, limit): GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/quick-switcher/recents?limit=20. Returns Vec<QuickSwitcherRecent {hit_key, ...}>.
4. Implement record_quick_switcher_recent(workspace_id, payload): POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/quick-switcher/recents. Returns QuickSwitcherRecent {hit_key}.
5. Implement resolve_open_target(hit) -> NavigationTarget in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/quick_switcher.rs (port of loom_search_open_target.ts).
6. Render the modal overlay: use egui::Area or a full-window egui::Window with no title bar, full-screen semi-transparent background. The card is a fixed-width (e.g. 600px), auto-height window centered. On click outside the card bounds, close.
7. Render query TextEdit with autofocus on first open (use a one-shot focus flag in state).
8. On each query change: increment debounce_generation; spawn a tokio task that sleeps 150ms, checks generation still matches (cancel token pattern), then fires the HTTP request. Return results via channel (reuse event_bus.rs for delivery if appropriate).
9. Compute ordered_results: let recent_rank = recents.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, k)| (k, i)).collect HashMap; sort results by recent_rank presence and position.
10. Render result list with keyboard navigation. Track selected_index. On ArrowDown/Up adjust index. On Enter call select_hit. On mouse hover update index.
11. On select_hit: call record_quick_switcher_recent (fire-and-forget, don't block), then dispatch resolve_open_target result through the shell navigation bus, then close the modal.
12. Register Ctrl+P (egui input: egui::Key::P + Modifiers::CTRL) as the global shortcut to toggle the quick switcher open/closed, via command_registry.rs.
13. Assign AccessKit author_ids (reuse accessibility/* infrastructure): 'quick-switcher' (overlay), 'quick-switcher.search' (input), 'quick-switcher.status' (status label), result items 'quick-switcher.result.{source_kind}.{stable_ref_id}' where stable_ref_id is ref_id with [^a-zA-Z0-9_-] replaced by '-'.

WP-011 MT-017 integration note: WP-011 MT-017 defined the quick-switcher target in the shell (app.rs) and shipped the base quick_switcher.rs module. This MT delivers the integration (graph search + dispatch). The shell navigation bus interface (trait/channel built on event_bus.rs) should be designed to be extensible so E5 interconnection MTs (MT-031 etc.) can add new dispatch targets without touching this file.

Dependencies/unblock conditions: depends on MT-028 (LoomSearchV2Surface, for on_open_loom_block being wired in the shell) and MT-029 (FindInFiles, for search_loom_graph HTTP fn potentially shared). In practice both can be parallelized if the HTTP fn is extracted first. The shell navigation bus interface must be defined (can be a stub trait with NotImplemented arms) before this MT finalises, or this MT defines it.

Risk if missed: the quick switcher is the primary keyboard-driven navigation surface used by both humans and swarm agents. Without it, agents must navigate by clicking panel buttons, which is fragile and violates HBR-SWARM. It also directly affects HBR-MAN (swarm navigability).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: implement a single app-wide SharedInteractionBus — the substrate that lets all editor panes (code, rich-text, graph, canvas) share one selection model, one clipboard, and one command registry. The expected diff shape is: (a) one new Rust module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/interaction_bus.rs (~350–500 lines) defining the bus types and an egui-integrated singleton, building on the existing WP-011 command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs rather than reinventing a command/dispatch substrate, (b) thin adapter shims in each existing pane module (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs, rich_text/mod.rs, graph/mod.rs, and the existing canvas_board.rs) that register into the bus rather than own ad-hoc clipboard/command state, (c) a kittest integration test src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interaction_bus.rs proving cross-pane selection propagation and clipboard round-trip.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/interaction_bus.rs  — defines SharedSelection, ClipboardPayload, CommandBus, CommandDescriptor, CommandHandler; holds an Arc<Mutex<InteractionBus>> accessible through egui's app data storage via Context::data_mut. Reuses command_registry.rs (command descriptor / registration substrate) and event_bus.rs (cross-pane event/notification fan-out) instead of defining a parallel command or event system.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/mod.rs  — declares the interop subdir module(s) including interaction_bus (if not already created by an earlier interop MT).

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs  — add `pub mod interop;` (or extend the existing interop module declaration).
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs  — replace per-pane clipboard + keybinding dispatch with bus calls; call bus.clipboard_write / bus.clipboard_read; register editor commands (Copy, Cut, Paste, SelectAll, Find) via the bus, routing registration through the existing command_registry.rs.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/mod.rs  — same pattern.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/mod.rs  — register node-selection into SharedSelection; clipboard writes (copy node ref as loom:// URI). Reuse loom_graph.rs for graph node identity/selection state.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/canvas_board.rs  — same as graph; canvas node selection feeds SharedSelection (reuse the existing canvas_board.rs surface rather than a new canvas pane).

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Define SharedSelection as an enum: None | TextRange { pane_id: PaneId, start: usize, end: usize, text: String } | BlockRef { pane_id: PaneId, block_id: String } | NodeRef { pane_id: PaneId, node_id: String }. Pane that holds focus owns the active variant; others observe. PaneId comes from the existing pane_registry.rs.
  2. Define ClipboardPayload as an enum: PlainText(String) | LoomBlockRef(String) | AtelierRef(String) | RichContent { mime: String, bytes: Vec<u8> }. Write through arboard (add to src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml if not present; it is pure Rust, MIT licensed). On read, return the richest available variant the pane can consume.
  3. Define CommandDescriptor { id: &'static str, label: String, keybind: Option<egui::KeyboardShortcut>, handler: CommandHandler } where CommandHandler = Arc<dyn Fn(&mut egui::Ui, &mut InteractionBus) + Send + Sync>. Register descriptors through the existing command_registry.rs rather than holding a parallel Vec; CommandBus wraps/extends the registry for the cross-pane dispatch surface.
  4. The command palette is the existing WP-011 command_palette.rs driven by the command bus: collect all registered descriptors from command_registry.rs, display in a fuzzy-searchable egui modal with AccessKit id "command-palette-list" + role List; on confirm call handler. Extend command_palette.rs rather than building a second palette.
  5. Store the InteractionBus in egui Context app data: ctx.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(egui::Id::new("handshake_interaction_bus"), bus.clone())). Every pane retrieves it the same way.
  6. Keybind dispatch: each pane, in its update() call, calls bus.dispatch_keybind(ctx, ui) after its own event handling. The bus iterates registered descriptors and checks egui::InputState::consume_shortcut.
  7. AccessKit: register the command palette trigger button with AccessKit author_id="command-palette-trigger", role=Button, actions=[Press]. Register the search input with author_id="command-palette-search", role=TextField. Each command list item uses author_id="cmd-{descriptor.id}", role=ListItem. Use the existing accessibility/ subsystem (accessibility/registry.rs, accessibility/live.rs) for node registration.
  8. Add a pane_focus_changed notification: when a pane receives click focus, it publishes through event_bus.rs and calls bus.set_focus_owner(pane_id) so SharedSelection.pane_id tracks which pane currently owns selection.
  9. Cross-pane Copy: when the user presses Ctrl+C in any pane, that pane builds a ClipboardPayload and calls bus.clipboard_write(payload). The bus calls arboard::Clipboard::set_text for PlainText, and also caches the richest variant in-memory for same-session cross-pane Paste.
  10. Tests: src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interaction_bus.rs — (a) unit: build a bus, register two panes, simulate selection change in pane A, read SharedSelection and assert it reflects pane A; (b) kittest harness: open code pane, select text, Ctrl+C, focus rich-text pane, Ctrl+V, assert pasted text equals source; (c) command bus: register a test command, call dispatch_command by id, assert handler invoked.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-001 (code editor pane exists at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/) must be merged first.
  - MT-011 (rich-text editor pane) must be merged.
  - MT-021 (graph pane) must be merged.
  - arboard crate (^3.x, pure Rust, MIT) must be added to src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml if not already present.
  - Reuses the WP-011 substrate: command_registry.rs, event_bus.rs, command_palette.rs, pane_registry.rs, canvas_board.rs, loom_graph.rs, and accessibility/* (these already exist from WP-011 and are not created by this MT).

Risk if missed: every downstream E5 MT (MT-032 through MT-035) requires the bus as a common substrate. Without it, each subsequent MT would build its own ad-hoc selection/clipboard, fragmenting the 'melt-together' invariant and making the parity proof suite impossible.

implementation_notes: Reuse the WP-011 substrate: command_registry.rs is the canonical command descriptor/registration store; event_bus.rs is the canonical cross-pane event/notification fan-out. The interaction_bus wraps and coordinates these — it must NOT define a parallel command list or a parallel event system.

Cross-WP dependency: this MT depends on WP-KERNEL-011 having shipped command_registry.rs, event_bus.rs, command_palette.rs, pane_registry.rs, canvas_board.rs, loom_graph.rs, and accessibility/* under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/. These are reused, not recreated, by this WP-012 MT.
Use egui::Id::new("handshake_interaction_bus") as the stable key for ctx.data_mut storage; every pane retrieves the bus by this id in its update() fn.
arboard ^3 is cross-platform (Windows/macOS/Linux) pure Rust; add under [dependencies] in src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml.
CommandDescriptor.keybind uses egui::KeyboardShortcut { modifiers, key }; standard VS Code bindings: Copy=Ctrl+C, Cut=Ctrl+X, Paste=Ctrl+V, SelectAll=Ctrl+A, Find=Ctrl+F, CommandPalette=Ctrl+Shift+P.

Reuse command_palette.rs for the modal surface; if it currently anchors via egui::Window::new("Command Palette").anchor(egui::Align2::CENTER_TOP, [0.0, 48.0]).show(ctx, ...), drive its open state from bus.command_palette_open rather than introducing a new window.

Pane focus: each pane's update() fn calls bus.set_focus_owner(self.pane_id) only when ui.memory(|m| m.has_focus(self.pane_egui_id)) is true, avoiding spurious resets; pane_id is sourced from pane_registry.rs.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: let users drag CKC (Atelier/KERNEL-005) media items, characters, and moodboards into a native note or canvas pane as embedded loom:// references, and route any note selection or document to a Stage pane. Expected diff shape: (a) a new drag-source on the AtelierSidePanel widget that emits a DragPayload::AtelierRef; (b) a drop-target in the rich-text editor that converts a dropped AtelierRef into an embed node (similar to how React LoomTransclusionView.tsx inserts a loomTransclusion TipTap node); (c) a drop-target in the canvas pane that places a canvas node pinned to the atelier item; (d) a 'Route to Stage' command dispatched through the existing command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs that takes the current selection or document and opens/focuses the Stage pane with that content; (e) integration tests using a real PG backend to assert the embed survives a save/reload cycle.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/drag_payload.rs  — defines DragPayload enum: AtelierRef { item_id: String, item_kind: AtelierItemKind, label: String, loom_block_id: Option<String> }, LoomBlockRef { block_id: String, workspace_id: String }, PlainText(String). Also defines AtelierItemKind enum: Media | Character | Moodboard. (New interop/ subdir created INSIDE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/.)
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/atelier_side_panel.rs  — an egui side-panel listing AtelierIntakeBatch items and AtelierCommandCorpus entries fetched from the existing backend via backend_client.rs (GET /atelier/intake/batches, GET /atelier/command-corpus). Each item row supports egui drag-source: on drag-start stores DragPayload::AtelierRef in ctx.data_mut. Rows display thumbnail path + label. Reuse the existing rail layout patterns from left_rail.rs / search_rail.rs. AccessKit: panel container author_id="atelier-side-panel", role=List; each row author_id="atelier-item-{item_id}", role=ListItem, actions=[Press, StartDrag].

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs  — add `pub mod interop;` and `pub mod atelier_side_panel;` (module registration for the new interop/ subdir and the new flat atelier_side_panel module).
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/editor.rs  — (rich-text editor pane created by WP-012 / MT-013) add an egui drop-target zone over the editor area. When a drop is received from ctx.data(|d| d.get_temp::<DragPayload>(...)), match on AtelierRef: insert an embed node { node_type: 'atelierEmbed', item_id, item_kind, label, loom_block_id } into the document tree at the caret position. Serialize as a custom ProseMirror-style block in the rich doc JSON. On save, the block is stored as part of content_json and round-trips through saveRichDocument.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/canvas_board.rs  — add drop-target at canvas level. On AtelierRef drop at screen position: call PUT /canvas/{canvas_id}/graph (via backend_client.rs) with a new CanvasNodeInput { kind: 'atelier_ref', atelier_item_id, x, y, width, height, label }. Backend stores it; reload canvas graph. The placed node's header shows AtelierItemKind badge + label + loom:// chip if loom_block_id is Some.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/stage_pane.rs  — add or extend a StagePane widget (new flat module, registered in the existing pane_registry.rs and docked via split_layout.rs; header via pane_header.rs). The Stage pane accepts a StageContent enum: Document(RichDocLoad) | Selection(String, String) | AtelierItem(AtelierRef). Register a 'route-to-stage' command in command_registry.rs (MT-031): args = StageRouteArgs { content: StageContent }; the command opens the Stage pane tile (via split_layout.rs / egui_tiles) and sets its content.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs  — register the 'route-to-stage' command descriptor; the route-to-stage handler emits the open/focus event over event_bus.rs and passes StageContent to stage_pane.rs.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. egui drag-source: call ui.dnd_drag_source(egui::Id::new(item_id), payload, |ui| { ui.label(&row.label) }). The payload is DragPayload::AtelierRef. This is egui 0.28+ API; confirm version in src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml.
  2. egui drop-target in rich-text pane: call let response = ui.dnd_drop_zone::<DragPayload, _>(egui::Frame::none(), |ui| { ... }); then check response.1 (the dropped payload) in each frame.
  3. Embed node in rich doc JSON: define a custom block type "atelier_embed" in the document schema. Store as a JSONContent object node with attrs: { item_id, item_kind, label, loom_block_id }. The rich-text editor renders it as a small card widget inline (thumbnail if available, else text label with badge).
  4. Canvas node creation for atelier drop: map screen position (egui Pos2) to canvas coordinates. Call updateCanvasGraph (api.ts ~1719: PUT /canvas/{id}/graph body { nodes: [{ kind, label, x, y, width, height, atelier_item_id }], edges: [] }) via the Rust backend_client.rs IPC client. Then reload via GET /canvas/{id}.
  5. Route to Stage: the Stage pane is an egui_tiles tile in the docking layout managed by split_layout.rs. 'route-to-stage' command handler: find the Stage tile id in the tree, call tree.set_active_tile(stage_tile_id), then set stage_pane.content = StageContent::from(args). If Stage tile does not exist yet, insert it as a new floating pane (reuse popout_window.rs for the floating case).
  6. Right-click context menu on rich-text selection: show 'Route to Stage' menu item via context_menu.rs / context_menu_surfaces.rs. This dispatches the 'route-to-stage' command through command_registry.rs with StageRouteArgs::Selection(selected_text, document_id).
  7. Right-click context menu on canvas node: show 'Route to Stage' item (context_menu.rs) that routes the node's document or atelier item.
  8. AtelierSidePanel data loading: call GET /atelier/intake/batches + GET /atelier/command-corpus via backend_client.rs on mount. Display in two sections: 'Media / Characters / Moodboards' (from intake items) and 'Command Corpus'. Refresh button fires a reload.
  9. AccessKit (accessibility/*): atelier_side_panel rows have actions=[Press, StartDrag]; the Stage pane container has author_id="stage-pane", role=Region. Use the existing accessibility/registry.rs + accessibility/snapshot.rs surfaces.
  10. Tests: src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_ckc_embed.rs — (a) unit: DragPayload::AtelierRef serializes and deserializes correctly; (b) integration (real PG): create a canvas, PUT /canvas/{id}/graph with an atelier_ref node, reload, assert node appears with correct atelier_item_id; (c) integration: create a rich doc, insert an atelier_embed block, saveRichDocument, reload, assert the atelier_embed block survives round-trip; (d) kittest: simulate drag from atelier panel, drop on canvas, assert canvas node count increases by 1.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-031 (command registration via command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) merged.
  - MT-032 (LoomBlockAddr, loom:// URI) merged — needed for loom_block_id in AtelierRef.
  - MT-013 (rich-text embed NodeView infrastructure, rich_text/ module) merged — needed so the atelier_embed block has a renderer in the rich-text pane.
  - Cross-WP: relies on WP-011 modules command_registry.rs, event_bus.rs, canvas_board.rs, pane_registry.rs, split_layout.rs, pane_header.rs, context_menu.rs, context_menu_surfaces.rs, accessibility/*, backend_client.rs, left_rail.rs, search_rail.rs (already merged in handshake-native).
  - egui 0.28+ for dnd_drag_source / dnd_drop_zone API; confirm version in src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml.

Risk if missed: CKC<->editor interconnection is one of the four named interconnection edges in the packet contract. Without this MT, dragging a character or moodboard into a note is impossible, breaking the 'melt-together' proof in MT-046.

original_scope.summary:

original_scope.summary:
Goal: define and enforce a unified undo scope policy across all editor panes (code, rich-text, graph, canvas), integrating the undo stack with the InteractionBus (MT-031). Handshake's rule: Ctrl+Z always undoes the most recent action in the focused pane; cross-pane actions (e.g. route-to-stage, embed-from-atelier) are recorded as atomic operations in the cross-pane undo stack. Expected diff: (a) a new UndoStack type in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/undo_stack.rs that holds undo/redo rings per pane and a cross-pane ring; (b) each pane registers its local undo/redo with the bus; (c) the bus dispatches Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y to the focused pane's local undo first, falling back to the cross-pane ring; (d) unit tests proving undo/redo round-trips within and across panes.

The key policy decisions this MT must encode:
  POLICY-1 (local-first): Ctrl+Z in a focused pane undoes the most recent action IN THAT PANE, not the most recent action globally. This matches VS Code and Obsidian behavior.
  POLICY-2 (cross-pane ring): actions that touch multiple panes atomically (embed-from-atelier in MT-033, route-to-stage in MT-033, code-ref insertion in MT-034) are pushed to a cross-pane undo ring. A dedicated 'Undo Cross-Pane' command (Ctrl+Shift+Z) undoes the most recent cross-pane action.
  POLICY-3 (persistence scope): undo history is session-scoped only; it is NOT persisted to the backend. On app restart, undo history is empty. Document this explicitly in code comments.
  POLICY-4 (canvas undo): canvas node moves/creations that call the backend immediately (PUT /canvas/{id}/graph) are NOT in-memory undoable via this stack alone — they require a compensating backend call (re-PUT the previous graph). The cross-pane ring records the compensating call as the undo action.
  POLICY-5 (undo stack cap): local pane undo rings are capped at 200 operations; cross-pane ring is capped at 50 operations. Exceeding the cap silently drops the oldest entry.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. UndoAction closures capture the minimum state needed. For code/rich-text local undo: capture a clone of the rope/doc tree snapshot BEFORE the edit. undo_fn replaces current rope/doc with snapshot; redo_fn re-applies the edit.
  2. Rope snapshot cloning (ropey::Rope) is O(1) due to ropey's arc-based persistent data structure — safe to clone per edit.
  3. Rich-text doc snapshot: clone the JSONContent tree (serde_json::Value). For large documents this is O(n); apply a debounce: group edits within the same 500ms window into a single undo entry to avoid O(n) per keystroke.
  4. Canvas undo: the undo_fn for a canvas node creation calls PUT /canvas/{canvas_id}/graph with the previous nodes list (minus the created node). This is a compensating backend call. It must be async; in the UndoAction, undo_fn should be an async fn wrapped in Arc<dyn Fn() -> BoxFuture<UndoResult>>. Alternatively, use a channel to dispatch the compensating call to the async runtime.
  5. Keybind dispatch: in bus.dispatch_keybind, match Ctrl+Z -> undo(focused_pane_id), Ctrl+Y -> redo(focused_pane_id), Ctrl+Shift+Z -> undo_cross_pane(). Each call returns Option<UndoResult>; if Some(result) and !result.ok, log the error to the Flight Recorder (MT-036).
  6. Undo menu indicator: in the code pane and rich-text pane title bar, show a small 'Undo ({n})' indicator using the count of items in the local ring. AccessKit: author_id="undo-count-{pane_id}", role=StaticText.
  7. original_scope.summary:
Bind the native Rust editor layer to the existing /knowledge/documents/* backend APIs. No backend changes are permitted; this MT is pure frontend wiring.

Goal: create a typed Rust client module at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend/knowledge_documents.rs that exposes async functions for every route in the backend knowledge_documents API. The diff shape is one new file plus a re-export wiring it into the handshake-native crate. Reuse the existing WP-011 backend_client.rs module (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs) for the shared HTTP client and base-URL resolution; do NOT introduce a new bespoke config struct if backend_client.rs already provides it.

Exact files to create/edit:
  - CREATE: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend/knowledge_documents.rs
  - CREATE: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend/mod.rs  (new `backend` subdir module: `pub mod knowledge_documents;`)
  - EDIT:   src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs  (add `pub mod backend;` if not already present; reachable as handshake_native::backend::knowledge_documents)

The backend HTTP surface (read from handshake_core/src/api/knowledge_documents.rs) exposes these routes, all under the base URL served by the running handshake_core server (obtained from the existing backend_client.rs BackendClient):
  POST   /knowledge/documents                          -> create_document
  POST   /knowledge/documents/import                   -> import_document
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id             -> load_document (returns document + tree + code_nodes)
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/draft       -> load_document_draft
  PUT    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/draft       -> upsert_document_draft
  DELETE /knowledge/documents/:document_id/draft       -> clear_document_draft
  PUT    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/save        -> save_document (optimistic-concurrency, expected_version field)
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/blocks      -> load_blocks
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/history     -> load_history (paginated: ?limit=&offset=)
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/history/:v  -> load_history_version
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/projection  -> export_projection (?format=markdown|html|plain_text|wiki_loom|context_bundle)
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/embeds      -> list_embeds
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/embeds/broken -> list_broken_embeds
  POST   /knowledge/documents/embeds/:embed_id/repair  -> repair_embed
  GET    /knowledge/documents/:document_id/backlinks   -> list_backlinks
  POST   /knowledge/documents/:document_id/backlinks   -> rebuild_backlinks
  POST   /knowledge/documents/:document_id/rename      -> rename_document
  POST   /knowledge/documents/:document_id/move        -> move_document
  POST   /knowledge/documents/batch                    -> batch_documents

Every request MUST include the mandatory identity headers:
  x-hsk-actor-id           (required)
  x-hsk-kernel-task-run-id (required)
  x-hsk-session-run-id     (required)
  x-hsk-actor-kind         (optional; omit for least-privileged read-only)
  x-hsk-correlation-id     (optional)
Missing required headers cause the backend to return 400. Provide a HskDocumentHeaders struct and a helper that populates them from editor session context.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Define Rust structs mirroring the backend request/response bodies (use serde::Deserialize/Serialize):
     - CreateDocumentRequest { workspace_id, title, content_json?, schema_version?, project_ref?, folder_ref? }
     - SaveDocumentRequest { expected_version: i64, content_json, crdt_document_id?, crdt_snapshot_id?, promotion_receipt_event_id? }
     - UpsertDraftRequest { base_doc_version: i64, base_content_sha256, content_json }
     - ImportDocumentRequest { workspace_id, title, format, snippet }
     - MoveDocumentRequest { project_ref?, folder_ref? }  // double-option semantics
     - BatchOperation (serde tagged union: rename/move/set_authority_label)
     - BatchRequest { operations: Vec<BatchOperation> }
  2. Define the response projection types:
     - RichDocumentResponse (contains all KnowledgeRichDocument fields; use serde_json::Value for content_json to avoid schema coupling)
     - BlockTreeResponse { schema_version, schema_matches, block_ids, blocks }
     - DocumentLoadResponse { document, tree, code_nodes }
     - DocumentDraftResponse { rich_document_id, current_doc_version, current_content_sha256, draft? }
     - SaveDocumentResponse { document, save_receipt_event_id?, receipt_error?, backlinks_persisted, embeds_persisted, knowledge_indexed, ... }
     - HistoryListResponse { rich_document_id, current_version, versions, total_versions, limit, offset }
     - ProjectionResponse { rich_document_id, projection }
  3. Define HskDocumentHeaders struct and a build_headers(ctx: &EditorSessionContext) -> HeaderMap helper.
  4. Implement one async fn per route using the HTTP client owned by the existing backend_client.rs BackendClient (reuse its reqwest::Client rather than constructing a new one). Each fn:
     a. Accepts typed request arguments.
     b. Builds the URL from the BackendClient base_url provided by src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs.
     c. Attaches HskDocumentHeaders.
     d. Deserializes the response body into the typed response struct.
     e. Maps HTTP error codes (400/403/404/409/500) to a typed KnowledgeDocumentsError enum.
  5. Handle the 409 Conflict response from save_document specially: return a SaveConflict variant carrying the current server version so the editor layer can show a conflict UI.
  6. The draft endpoint (PUT) uses double-option semantics for project_ref/folder_ref in MoveDocumentRequest: use Option<Option<String>> with a custom serializer that omits the field when outer is None and serializes null when inner is None.
  7. Add AccessKit accessibility metadata note: this MT creates backend client code only, no widgets. Accessibility annotations (via the existing accessibility/* modules under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/) apply when a calling widget (editor toolbar, save button, history panel) is built in later MTs.
  8. Register the module: create src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend/mod.rs with `pub mod knowledge_documents;` and ensure `pub mod backend;` is declared in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs.

The save_document route (PUT /knowledge/documents/:id/save) uses `expected_version` for optimistic concurrency; a 409 response means version conflict. Surface this as SaveConflict { server_version: Option<i64> } by parsing the 409 response body.

Move document uses double-option: `project_ref: Option<Option<String>>` serialized as: absent field when outer=None, `null` when inner=None, string when inner=Some(s). Use a custom serde helper or #[serde(skip_serializing_if)] on the outer option.
Do not hold any document state in this module. It is a stateless HTTP adapter only.
All route functions are public (pub async fn). No internal state.

SaveConflict reuses MT-020's pattern. A duplicated load/save is a FAILURE (the panel will check).

Bind ONLY verified shapes; record any drift.

MOCK-SERVER FIXTURES MUST USE REAL PAYLOADS (KERNEL_BUILDER gate - Spec-Realism Gate, the load-bearing rule for a binding MT): the ACs use a MOCK HTTP server (good - this MT is fully provable WITHOUT live PG, NO NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF needed). BUT the mock JSON responses MUST be REAL backend response shapes - captured from the live backend OR field-verified byte-for-byte against the handshake_core response structs - NOT self-serialized from the client's own Rust types (a fixture that feeds the client its own serialization is a TAUTOLOGY that proves nothing - the Spec-Realism Sub-rule 2). Document where each fixture JSON came from. The mock server (wiremock/httpmock - add as dev-dependency if not present) asserts: load_document deserializes a real DocumentLoadResponse; save 409 -> SaveConflict (not generic); missing actor-id header -> 400 BadRequest variant; double-option move serializes 3 ways; batch>100 -> BatchTooLarge client-side BEFORE send; history limit clamped 1..=200. base_url from backend_client.rs config (NOT hardcoded - GLOBAL-PORTABILITY). Stateless adapter (no doc state held). NO GUI (no screenshot/accesskit this MT - pure client). Full suite stays green.

original_scope.summary:
Bind the native Rust editor layer to the existing /knowledge/crdt/* backend APIs for collaborative editing: Yjs update push, Yjs update pull (replay feed), and conflict state query. No backend changes are permitted; this MT is pure frontend wiring.

Goal: create a typed Rust client module at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/knowledge_crdt.rs that exposes three async functions mirroring the backend CRDT push/pull/conflict_state surface. The diff shape is one new file plus a `pub mod knowledge_crdt;` re-export from src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs. Reuse the existing WP-011 HTTP client module backend_client.rs (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs) for the base_url and reqwest::Client wiring rather than constructing a new transport.

The backend HTTP surface (read from handshake_core/src/api/knowledge_crdt.rs) exposes three routes:
  POST /knowledge/crdt/updates/push  -> push_update
  GET  /knowledge/crdt/updates/pull  -> pull_updates
  GET  /knowledge/crdt/conflict_state -> conflict_state

All three routes enforce the spec 2.3.13.11 backend-navigation receipt law:
  push: actor_id, session_id, trace_id inside the YjsUpdateEnvelopeV1 body.
  pull: actor_id, session_id, correlation_id as query params.
  conflict_state: actor_id, session_id, correlation_id as query params.
Missing required identity fields return 400. This is NOT the x-hsk-* header contract of knowledge_documents; it is an in-body / query-param identity scheme specific to the CRDT routes.

Request and response shapes (derived directly from knowledge_crdt.rs):

PUSH:
  Request body: PushUpdateRequest { envelope: YjsUpdateEnvelopeV1 }
  YjsUpdateEnvelopeV1 { crdt_document_id, update_id, actor_id, session_id, trace_id, base_update_seq: u64, update_bytes: Vec<u8> (base64-encoded in JSON), update_schema_id }
  Response (200 or 409): PushUpdateResponse { result: YjsPushOutcomeV1, receipt: KnowledgeNavigationReceiptV1 }
  YjsPushOutcomeV1 is a tagged enum:
    Stored { update_seq, update_id, event_ledger_event_id, head_state_vector }
    AlreadyStored { update_seq, update_id, event_ledger_event_id, head_state_vector }
    Denied { denial: YjsPushDenialV1 }
  YjsPushDenialV1 { schema_id, crdt_document_id, update_id, actor_id, reason: YjsPushDenialReasonV1 }
  YjsPushDenialReasonV1 is a tagged enum:
    StaleBase { head_update_seq, head_state_vector, ordering }
    EnvelopeInvalid { messages: Vec<String> }
  Backend returns 200 for Stored/AlreadyStored, 409 for Denied.

PULL:
  Query params: workspace_id, document_id, crdt_document_id, since_update_seq (u64, default 0), document_schema_id, actor_id, session_id, correlation_id
  Response: PullUpdatesResponse { result: YjsUpdatePullResponseV1, receipt: KnowledgeNavigationReceiptV1 }
  YjsUpdatePullResponseV1 { crdt_document_id, updates: Vec<StoredYjsUpdate>, head_update_seq: u64, head_state_vector }
  StoredYjsUpdate { update_seq, update_id, update_bytes: Vec<u8> (base64 in JSON), actor_id, session_id, trace_id, created_at }

CONFLICT_STATE:
  Query params: workspace_id, document_id, crdt_document_id, actor_id, session_id, correlation_id
  Response: ConflictStateResponse { result: ConflictUiStateV1, receipt: KnowledgeNavigationReceiptV1 }
  ConflictUiStateV1 { has_conflict: bool, conflict_kind?: String, head_update_seq: u64, head_state_vector, denial_count: u32, latest_denial? }

KnowledgeNavigationReceiptV1 (common to all three): { receipt_kind, actor_id, session_id, correlation_id, target_authority_ref, operation, served_at_utc }

Exact files to create/edit:
  - CREATE: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/knowledge_crdt.rs
  - EDIT:   src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs (add `pub mod knowledge_crdt;`)

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Define YjsUpdateEnvelopeV1 in Rust. The update_bytes field is Vec<u8> in Rust but base64-encoded in JSON. Use #[serde(with = "base64_bytes")] or a custom serde module that calls base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD encode/decode.
  2. Define the YjsPushOutcomeV1 enum as a serde tagged union matching the backend variant names: 'Stored', 'AlreadyStored', 'Denied'.
  3. Define YjsPushDenialReasonV1 as a tagged enum: 'StaleBase', 'EnvelopeInvalid'.
  4. Implement push_update:
     a. POST to /knowledge/crdt/updates/push.
     b. Body: PushUpdateRequest { envelope }.
     c. Content-Type: application/json.
     d. On 200: deserialize PushUpdateResponse -> return Ok(YjsPushOutcomeV1::Stored or AlreadyStored).
     e. On 409: deserialize PushUpdateResponse -> return Ok(YjsPushOutcomeV1::Denied) (NOT an Err; 409 is a valid domain outcome, not a network error).
     f. On other non-2xx: return Err(CrdtError::HttpError { status, body }).
  5. Implement pull_updates:
     a. GET /knowledge/crdt/updates/pull with query params.
     b. since_update_seq defaults to 0 when caller passes None.
     c. Return YjsUpdatePullResponseV1 (the caller uses updates Vec<StoredYjsUpdate> to replay Yjs operations).
     d. StoredYjsUpdate.update_bytes must be base64-decoded from the JSON string back to Vec<u8>.
  6. Implement conflict_state:
     a. GET /knowledge/crdt/conflict_state with query params.
     b. Return ConflictUiStateV1 (has_conflict, conflict_kind, denial counts).
     c. This is a read-only diagnostic query; the result drives the conflict UI shown to the operator.
  7. The receipt field (KnowledgeNavigationReceiptV1) is present in all responses. Preserve it in the typed response struct even if the initial consumer does not use it (spec 2.3.13.11 audit requirement).
  8. CrdtError enum: { HttpError { status: u16, body: String }, SerializationError(String), IdentityMissing(String) }.
  9. AccessKit note: this MT creates backend client code only. When the collaborative editing UI surface is built, the conflict resolution panel MUST expose each conflict item as an AccessKit node with Role::Alert (for unseen conflicts) or Role::ListItem, with Action::Click to accept/reject, reusing the existing accessibility/ helpers (accessibility/mod.rs, accessibility/registry.rs, accessibility/live.rs). Add this note in the module doc comment.
  10. Emit a local in-process event or call a provided callback when push_update returns YjsPushOutcomeV1::Denied so that the calling editor layer can trigger the conflict UI immediately. Do not silently swallow denials. Prefer publishing on the existing event_bus.rs rather than inventing a new channel.
  11. Register the module in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs.

implementation_notes: Reuse the existing WP-011 HTTP transport: backend_client.rs (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs) already owns the base_url and reqwest::Client; build the CRDT client on top of it rather than constructing a fresh transport.

update_bytes base64 encoding: the backend uses base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD encode/decode (from the base64 crate). Use the same engine on the client to ensure byte-level compatibility. Do NOT use base64url or padding-stripped variants.

The CRDT identity scheme is different from knowledge_documents: actor_id/session_id/trace_id are inside the envelope body for push, and in query params for pull/conflict_state. There are no x-hsk-* HTTP headers on these routes.

A push denial (409) is a valid domain outcome that the editor layer must handle by showing a conflict UI. It MUST NOT be converted to Err in the client's return type. Return Ok(YjsPushOutcomeV1::Denied { denial }).
The head_state_vector in push and pull responses is an opaque Yjs state vector (Vec<u8> base64-encoded). Preserve it as Vec<u8> in Rust; the CRDT engine consumes it opaquely.

The since_update_seq parameter for pull_updates is a monotonically increasing u64 sequence number. The client must track the last seen update_seq and pass it on subsequent pulls to avoid replaying old updates.

MT-037 depends_on relationship: if MT-037's BackendClient is not yet merged, define a minimal LocalBackendClient { base_url: String, client: reqwest::Client } inline in this module and add a TODO to consolidate with the backend_client.rs surface from MT-037.

Cross-WP reuse (prose, not a depends_on edge): the existing event_bus.rs and accessibility/* modules ship from WP-011-Native-Frontend; this MT consumes them as already-merged WP-011 surfaces. Surface push denials on event_bus.rs and plan the conflict-panel AccessKit nodes against accessibility/registry.rs.

Do not implement CRDT merge/apply logic in this MT. This MT is ONLY the HTTP client for the CRDT push/pull/conflict_state transport layer. The Yjs merge engine (yrs crate or equivalent) is a separate concern for a later MT.
The document_schema_id query param for pull_updates is the schema version string (e.g. 'prosemirror-v1'); pass it through from the calling editor context.

PLACEMENT + 409-DENIED=Ok LOAD-BEARING INVARIANT (KERNEL_BUILDER gate 2026-06-23): place in backend/knowledge_crdt.rs (CONSISTENT with MT-037/038/039 backend/ client subdir + re-export via backend/mod.rs) - NOT a root src/knowledge_crdt.rs module; reachable as handshake_native::backend::knowledge_crdt. THE LOAD-BEARING DATA-INTEGRITY RULE: a 409 push denial is a VALID DOMAIN OUTCOME returned as Ok(YjsPushOutcomeV1::Denied{denial}) - NEVER mapped to Err (RISK-1/MC-1). The whole conflict-resolution UI depends on the editor seeing the typed Denied (StaleBase/EnvelopeInvalid); a 409->Err would hide data-loss risk behind a generic error. Module doc must call this out. Only NON-2xx-non-409 -> Err(CrdtError::HttpError). Surface the Denied on the existing bus (interop/interaction_bus.rs or event_bus.rs) so the editor triggers the conflict UI - do NOT silently swallow (note 10).

base64 STANDARD + Vec<u8> + IDENTITY PRE-FLIGHT (KERNEL_BUILDER gate): update_bytes AND head_state_vector are Vec<u8> in Rust, base64 in JSON - use base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD (the EXACT engine the backend uses; NOT base64url, NOT padless - RISK-2/MC-2; a mismatch silently drops updates). head_state_vector MUST be Vec<u8> NOT String (RISK-4/MC-6 - the CRDT engine consumes it opaquely; a String breaks state comparison -> phantom conflicts). Roundtrip test: random bytes -> JSON -> decode == byte-for-byte. IDENTITY scheme is CRDT-specific (NOT x-hsk-* headers): actor_id/session_id/trace_id IN the envelope BODY for push; actor_id/session_id/correlation_id as QUERY PARAMS for pull/conflict_state - do NOT add x-hsk headers. Pre-flight GUARD: Err(CrdtError::IdentityMissing) if any required identity field is empty BEFORE sending (RISK-5/MC-3). since_update_seq default 0, passed through + asserted on the wire (?since_update_seq=N, MC-5). Verify base64 crate is in the tree (don't add a dup).

TRANSPORT-ONLY + VERIFY + HYGIENE (KERNEL_BUILDER gate - Spec-Realism): this MT is ONLY the HTTP transport client for push/pull/conflict_state - do NOT implement the Yjs MERGE/apply engine (yrs crate) - that is a separate later concern (note 12). VERIFY read-only against src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/knowledge_crdt.rs: the 3 routes + YjsUpdateEnvelopeV1 + YjsPushOutcomeV1 (Stored/AlreadyStored/Denied tagged) + YjsPushDenialReasonV1 (StaleBase/EnvelopeInvalid) + PullUpdatesResponse + ConflictUiStateV1 + KnowledgeNavigationReceiptV1 (preserve ALL 7 fields in ALL 3 responses, RISK-7/MC-4). Mock-server fixture JSON MUST be REAL backend shapes (captured/field-verified vs the handler json! blocks + confirm the backend base64 engine - cite lines; NOT self-serialized tautology). FULLY provable WITHOUT live PG (mock server) - no NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF. empty-CRDT-doc pull = empty updates + head_update_seq=0 is NOT an error (RISK-8). Stateless adapter; base_url from backend_client.rs config. NO GUI this MT (no screenshot/accesskit - pure client; document the conflict-panel AccessKit Role::Alert requirement for the future widget). Full suite green; clippy clean; no tracked artifacts.

The WP-KERNEL-011 spike chose egui + AccessKit; its model-accessibility surface is src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/ (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs). Each egui widget that calls `ui.add(widget)` can be given a stable `Id` via `egui::Id::new('editor.code.find-open')` and then the AccessKit node is derived from that Id. For custom action dispatch (actions that are not native egui interactions), use the egui custom-action API to register an action handler keyed by Id + action_id. IN-041-02: author_id convention. Format: `editor.<pane_type>.<action_id>` where pane_type is `code` or `rich`, and action_id is the kebab-case action name. The instance_index is stable for the lifetime of the pane and is assigned by the EditorActionRegistry at pane registration time. implementation_notes: IN-042-01: Graph node AccessKit registration. The native graph pane maintains a Vec<GraphNode> (each GraphNode has block_id: Uuid, title: String, position: Vec2, expanded: bool). On every frame where the node set has changed (content hash differs), update the KnowledgeActionRegistry with the current node set. Each node registers as AccessKit node author_id='graph.node.<block_id>' with role=TreeItem. Do NOT re-register unchanged nodes each frame; only push diffs. The registry must keep a BTreeMap<Uuid, u64> of per-node content hashes to detect changes cheaply.

IN-042-02: Canvas placement AccessKit registration. The native canvas pane maintains a Vec<CanvasPlacement> (placement_id: Uuid, placed_block_id: Uuid, x, y, w, h). Register each placement as author_id='canvas.card.<placement_id>'. The placed_block_id is surfaced as an AccessKit property (key: 'block_id', value: placed_block_id string) so a swarm agent can correlate placements to their source blocks. Role=Group. Actions=['activate' (opens the referenced block), 'move' (requires x, y parameters passed via AccessKit custom-action payload), 'delete'].

IN-042-03: Collection row AccessKit registration. The native collection pane (table/Kanban/calendar) maintains a Vec<CollectionRow> (block_id, fields). Register each row as author_id='collection.row.<block_id>' with role=Row. For Kanban, additionally register lane containers: author_id='collection.lane.<lane_tag>' with role=Group so a swarm agent can assert which lane a card is in.

IN-042-04: Parameterized actions. AccessKit's custom-action payload is a string. Encode parameters as JSON in the payload string. Example: `canvas.place-block` receives payload `{"block_id":"<uuid>","x":100,"y":100}`. The canvas pane's action handler parses this JSON and calls `place_block_on_canvas`. Use `serde_json::from_str` for parsing; log and discard malformed payloads with an error log line (never panic in release builds).

No keyboard simulation, no screen-scraping, no direct Rust function calls from the test into the application under test. The agent talks to the running Handshake native UI through the AccessKit IPC mechanism only.

This MT is a PROOF task, not a feature task. It delivers:

If a gap is found (an action is missing, an author_id is wrong, a backend call does not happen), the MT raises a TYPED BLOCKER against MT-041 or MT-042 and does NOT patch application code inline.

implementation_notes: IN-043-01: Proof harness architecture. Use egui_kittest as the in-process headless UI host. The 'out-of-process agent' is simulated by a separate Rust thread within the test that communicates with the UI thread ONLY via the AccessKit action channel (using the same channel that a real out-of-process agent would use). The separation of concerns is enforced by: the agent thread holds only an AccessKit channel handle (no Arc pointers into the application state); the application state is owned by the UI thread. This mimics real out-of-process swarm agent behavior without requiring an actual external process for the proof.

IN-043-02: AccessKit action channel. The WP-011 AccessKit adapter (handshake_native::accessibility plus handshake_native::mcp::action) must expose a cloneable action sender (e.g. mpsc::Sender<AccessKitActionRequest>) that can be given to the agent thread. If the WP-011 adapter does not yet expose this, this MT files a typed blocker against WP-KERNEL-011 (cross-WP dependency on the AccessKit/MCP action channel in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/* and src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mcp/*). Do NOT add a new channel or bypass mechanism in the application code for this test.

IN-043-03: STEP 1 implementation detail. 'create note' in the native rich editor. The slash command picker is opened via 'editor.rich.insert-slash-command'. The test then dispatches a secondary action to select '/note' from the picker (via AccessKit list navigation: 'slash-picker.item.note' with action 'activate') or supplies the item selection as a parameter in the payload. After the note block is created, the editor auto-saves (or the test dispatches 'editor.rich.save'). The test waits for the AccessKit node 'graph.node.<id>' (registered by handshake_native::loom_graph) to appear (poll with a 100 ms tick, 5 s total timeout).

IN-043-04: STEP 2 implementation detail. 'edit code' in the code editor. After STEP 1, the test opens the newly created note in the code editor pane by dispatching 'graph.open-node' with the new block_id and a target='code-editor' parameter (or by dispatching 'editor.rich.insert-slash-command' with a code-block payload to embed a code block in the rich note, then dispatching an action to focus the code block in the standalone code editor pane). The test inserts code via AccessKit: dispatch 'editor.code.multi-cursor-add' to place a cursor at position 0, then dispatch a custom action 'editor.code.insert-text' with payload '{"text":"print(\"swarm-proof\")"}'. If 'editor.code.insert-text' is not in the MT-041 action set, the test must file a typed blocker; do NOT add a workaround key-simulation.

IN-043-05: STEP 3 implementation detail. 'add backlink'. After STEP 2 + save, the test navigates the rich editor to insert a wikilink. Dispatch 'editor.rich.insert-slash-command' with payload '{"kind":"wikilink","ref_kind":"note","ref_value":"<target_block_id>"}'. After insert + save, query the backend. The target block 'SwarmProofTarget' must be seeded in the test fixture before the test begins. This is the only permitted pre-test DB mutation; the test must seed and clean it up.

IN-043-06: STEP 4 implementation detail. 'run search'. Dispatch the AccessKit search action. If the Loom Search v2 AccessKit surface (MT-028) is available and exports author_id 'search.query', use that. If not, use the find-open action in the rich editor. After dispatching the search, poll for AccessKit nodes with the prefix 'search.result.' or 'editor.rich.find-panel.match' (depending on which surface is available). The test succeeds if at least one result node references the block_id created in STEP 1.

IN-043-07: Proof log format. Write one line per action dispatched using the format:
  [<ISO8601_timestamp>] DISPATCH author_id=<id> action=<action> payload=<payload_or_null>
  [<ISO8601_timestamp>] RESPONSE tree_change=<description> db_result=<PASS|FAIL|SKIP>
End the file with a single line: 'PROOF_PASS' (or 'PROOF_FAIL: <reason>' if the test detected a failure during log generation). The proof log is written to a file (not just stdout) so it can be checked in as evidence. Use std::fs::write to atomically overwrite the file at the end of the test run.

IN-043-08: Idempotency and cleanup. The test uses a transaction-scoped fixture: BEGIN TRANSACTION at test start for the pre-seeded 'SwarmProofTarget' block. At the end, ROLLBACK to clean up all created rows including 'SwarmProofNote-<timestamp>' and its edges. This requires the test to have a direct DB connection (use the same test PG pool established by the E6 cluster test infrastructure). Do NOT use TRUNCATE or DELETE on production tables.

IN-043-09: No keyboard simulation constraint. Add a Clippy lint or a custom lint in the test file that fails if any of the following identifiers appear in the test body: 'send_key', 'send_char', 'write_text', 'simulate_key', 'press_key', 'type_text'. Add a comment at the top of the file: '// SWARM_PROOF_CONSTRAINT: only AccessKit action dispatch is permitted in this test. Any keyboard simulation fails the proof.'

IN-043-10: React parity reference for this MT (READ ONLY). The four proof steps correspond to these React surfaces:

original_scope.summary:
GOAL: Author and execute the Parity Proof Suite — a structured runtime test harness that maps every KERNEL-009-delivered editor/knowledge feature to a passing native proof in the WP-KERNEL-012 Rust implementation. This is the parity gate: no feature is declared ported until it has a passing proof in this suite.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: Creates flat integration test files under src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/ — (a) a machine-readable parity manifest (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/parity_manifest.json) that catalogs every KERNEL-009 feature, its source React file, its native impl location, and its proof status, and (b) Rust test modules (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_parity_code_editor.rs, test_parity_rich_editor.rs, test_parity_knowledge.rs, test_parity_search.rs) each with #[test] or #[tokio::test] functions that exercise the native implementation against a real PostgreSQL test database using the existing handshake_core backend APIs. NO mocks for any spec-required runtime behavior.

FEATURE CATALOG TO PROVE (map each to a passing test):

CLUSTER E1 — Code editor (VS Code parity). React reference: app/src/components/MonacoCodeBlockView.tsx, app/src/components/CodeSymbolPanel.tsx, app/src/components/FindReplacePanel.tsx. Features to prove: (1) syntax highlighting loads and applies a tree-sitter grammar for Rust, TypeScript, and Python without panic; (2) large-file virtualization: a 10 000-line synthetic file renders without freeze (timing assertion <= 200 ms first paint); (3) multi-cursor insert: insert text at 5 cursor positions simultaneously, result matches expected; (4) find/replace: search a 500-line buffer, collect match spans, apply replace-all, verify final content; (5) code folding: fold a function range, verify hidden-line count; (6) minimap glyph count matches buffer line count; (7) go-to-line: jump to line 42, verify cursor row; (8) gutter diagnostics: inject a fake LSP diagnostic, verify gutter badge appears at the correct line; (9) LSP round-trip: send a completion request via the tower-lsp client stub to the in-process LSP and receive at least one CompletionItem; (10) diff editor: open a two-buffer diff, verify added/removed line counts match expected.

CLUSTER E2 — Rich-text editor (Obsidian/Notion parity). React reference: app/src/components/DocumentView.tsx, app/src/components/LoomTransclusionView.tsx, app/src/components/HsLinkView.tsx. Backend API: POST /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents (create), GET /…/{doc_id} (load), PUT /…/{doc_id} (save) from src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/knowledge_documents.rs. Features to prove: (11) block document model: create a doc with heading/paragraph/list/table/code-block nodes, serialize to JSON, reload, verify node count and types; (12) WYSIWYG heading render: H1-H6 render at visually distinct sizes (egui TextStyle check); (13) table: insert 3x3 table, set cell (1,1) text, read back via doc model; (14) embed image: insert an [[HS_images:assetId]] node pointing to a real PG-stored asset, verify embed resolves (HTTP GET /workspaces/{id}/assets/{asset_id}); (15) wikilink [[note:blockId]]: insert, verify typed node persisted, backend GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{block_id} returns the linked block; (16) transclusion: create source doc, embed transclusion node, verify read-through resolves via GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{block_id}/transclusion; (17) slash command: trigger '/' menu, select 'heading', verify node inserted; (18) properties panel: set a doc property key/value, save, reload, verify property present; (19) find/replace in rich doc: insert text, find 'foo', replace with 'bar', verify final content; (20) daily note: call open_daily_journal endpoint (PUT /workspaces/{id}/loom/journals/{date}), verify block created with date as title; (21) save-to-format HTML: export a doc to HTML projection via GET /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents/{doc_id}/projection?format=html, verify non-empty HTML string; (22) draft recovery: write a draft, simulate crash (drop in-memory state), reload, verify draft content restored.

CLUSTER E3 — Knowledge surface (Obsidian graph parity). React reference: app/src/components/LoomBlockPanel.tsx, app/src/components/LoomWikiPagePanel.tsx, app/src/components/LoomCanvasBoard.tsx, app/src/components/BlockCollectionView.tsx. Backend API: GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/graph, GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/folders, POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/canvas-boards from src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/loom.rs. Features to prove: (23) local graph: create 3 blocks with edges, call graph API at depth 2, verify node+edge counts; (24) global graph: call graph API at depth 1 over workspace, verify workspace root appears; (25) folder tree: create folder, create child block, call list_loom_folders, verify hierarchy; (26) color labels: set color on folder, reload, verify color preserved; (27) tags + tag hubs: add a tag edge to a block, query tag hub, verify block appears in hub results; (28) pins: pin a block (set pinned flag), query pinned view, verify block in result; (29) backlinks: create block A -> B edge, call GET /…/B/backlinks, verify A appears; (30) unlinked mentions: insert block A content containing B's title, call scan_loom_block_unlinked_mentions for B, verify A surfaces; (31) breadcrumbs: create parent->child hierarchy, call GET /…/child/breadcrumbs, verify path; (32) wiki-page projection: call wiki-page endpoint for a block, verify wikilinks resolved; (33) canvas board: create canvas board, place a real Loom block via POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/canvas-boards/{board_id}/placements, verify placement returned in board view; (34) block-collection table view: create a block_view (content_type='view_def'), call queryBlockViewResults, verify row count > 0; (35) block-collection Kanban: move a Kanban card (update tag edge), re-query, verify card appears in new column; (36) block-collection calendar: query calendar view for today's date, verify daily journal block appears.

CLUSTER E4 — Search surfaces. React reference: app/src/components/LoomSearchV2Panel.tsx, app/src/components/FindReplacePanel.tsx. Backend API: POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/search-v2, GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/quick-switcher from src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/loom.rs. Features to prove: (37) full-text search: index a known string in a block content, call loom_search_v2 with that string, verify block_id in hits; (38) fuzzy search: call loom_search_v2 with a single typo in the query, verify same block still surfaces; (39) semantic search (pgvector): call loom_search_v2 with mode=semantic, verify hits list non-empty (requires pgvector extension and embedded vector on the test block — use the fixture from src/backend/handshake_core/src/bin/mt250_workspace_search_fixture.rs); (40) faceted filter: call loom_search_v2 with content_type filter, verify all returned hits match that type; (41) save-results-as-view: after a search, call createBlockView with the query, verify the new view block has content_type='view_def' and query embedded; (42) find-in-files: call find-in-files endpoint for a known string across 3 code files, verify all 3 file paths appear in result; (43) quick-switcher: call quick-switcher endpoint with a partial block title, verify the matching block surfaces.

CLUSTER E5-E7 — Interconnection and model-vision. Proved in MT-045 and MT-046 respectively; this suite contains stubs for E5-E7 features that cross-reference those MTs.

original_scope.summary:
GOAL: Author and execute the Large-Document and Large-Codebase Performance Proof suite. This MT proves that the native editors handle realistic large-payload scenarios within defined latency and memory budgets — scenarios that the legacy React/Monaco implementation handles but at the cost of webview overhead. The native implementation must meet or exceed the React baseline on these dimensions.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: Creates flat perf-proof test files under src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/ containing: (a) src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/perf_proof/perf_manifest.json recording each scenario's budget, measured value, and PASS/FAIL verdict; (b) src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_perf_large_code.rs covering large-codebase code editor scenarios; (c) src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_perf_large_rich.rs covering large rich-text document scenarios; (d) src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_perf_large_knowledge.rs covering large graph/index scenarios. No mocks for any spec-required runtime behavior.

SCENARIO CATALOG:

CODE EDITOR LARGE-FILE SCENARIOS (test_perf_large_code.rs):

LC-01 — Initial render, 10k-line file: Synthesize a 10 000-line Rust source file (~500 KB). Load it into CodeEditor (ropey rope), trigger syntax highlighting pass (tree-sitter), measure wall time from buffer-load call to first highlighted-range emission. Budget: <= 200 ms. Implementation: use std::time::Instant; the tree-sitter parse must complete, not be deferred. The 10k-line file must be generated in-process (no fixture file on disk required).

LC-02 — Scroll to bottom, 10k-line file: After load, move the viewport to the last line. Measure time from viewport-move call to the correct last line appearing in the egui layout. Budget: <= 16 ms (one egui frame at 60fps). This requires the virtual-line-range renderer introduced in MT-002 to only paint the visible window, not all 10k lines.

LC-03 — Find/replace across 10k-line file: Search for a string that appears 200 times across the 10k-line buffer. Measure time from search-start to all 200 match spans collected. Budget: <= 100 ms. Then apply replace-all. Measure replace time. Budget: <= 100 ms. Assert the final buffer has exactly 200 replacements.

LC-04 — Multi-cursor, 1k cursor positions: Insert text simultaneously at 1 000 cursor positions (programmatic multi-cursor insert via the CodeEditor::apply_multi_edit API). Measure time. Budget: <= 500 ms. Assert all 1 000 positions have the inserted text.

LC-05 — Memory budget, 10k-line file: Load the 10k-line file, trigger a syntax highlight pass, then measure RSS delta (before vs. after load). Use /proc/self/status on Linux or a platform equivalent via the sysinfo crate (already in the workspace or add it). Budget: delta <= 50 MB. On Windows, use GetProcessMemoryInfo via the windows-sys crate.

LC-06 — Large codebase index, 500 files: Create a synthetic 'codebase' of 500 Rust files each with ~200 lines (total ~100k lines) by writing them to a temp dir. Trigger the code-nav indexer (handshake_native::code_editor::code_nav::index_workspace or equivalent). Measure time to completion. Budget: <= 10 s. Assert the resulting symbol count >= 500 (at least one symbol per file).

LC-07 — Minimap at 10k lines: Call the minimap renderer for a 10k-line buffer. Measure glyph-layout time. Budget: <= 50 ms. Assert glyph count == buffer line count (10 000).

LC-08 — LSP diagnostics, 500 items: Inject 500 fake diagnostic items into the gutter/diagnostic overlay. Measure render time for the overlay pass. Budget: <= 16 ms. Assert all 500 badges are recorded in the diagnostic map (not that they are all visually rendered, but that none are dropped).

RICH EDITOR LARGE-DOCUMENT SCENARIOS (test_perf_large_rich.rs):

LR-01 — Load large rich document, 1 000 blocks: Create a KnowledgeRichDocument via POST /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents containing 1 000 paragraph nodes (~50k chars total). Load via GET. Measure round-trip + native parse time. Budget: <= 2 s including network. Measure native block-tree build time from parsed JSON. Budget: <= 100 ms.

LR-02 — Scroll through large rich document: After loading 1 000 blocks, drive the virtual scroll from block 0 to block 999 in a simulated render loop (call the layout engine for each viewport position). Measure total time for 100 viewport steps (simulating a fast drag). Budget: <= 1 000 ms total (10 ms per step). Assert no layout panic.

LR-03 — Find in rich document, 500 matches: Insert the string 'FINDME' into every other block (500 occurrences). Trigger find-in-rich-doc. Measure time to collect all 500 spans. Budget: <= 200 ms.

LR-04 — Save large rich document: Save the 1 000-block document via PUT /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents/{doc_id}. Measure round-trip time. Budget: <= 3 s. Assert the EventLedger receives a KNOWLEDGE_RICH_DOCUMENT_SAVED receipt (verify via GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{doc_block_id} returns updated_at changed).

LR-05 — Transclusion chain, 50 hops: Create 50 documents each transcluding the previous. Load the outermost document and resolve the full transclusion chain via GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{block_id}/transclusion called recursively up to depth 50. Measure total resolution time. Budget: <= 5 s. Assert no infinite loop (the resolver must detect cycles; a cyclic chain of 5 must return an 'unresolved' state with reason 'cycle_detected', not panic).

LR-06 — Memory budget, 1 000-block document: Load and parse the 1k-block document. Measure RSS delta. Budget: delta <= 30 MB.

LR-07 — Export projection, 1 000-block HTML: Call GET /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents/{doc_id}/projection?format=html on the 1k-block document. Measure server response time. Budget: <= 2 s. Assert returned HTML length > 50 000 chars.

LARGE KNOWLEDGE GRAPH SCENARIOS (test_perf_large_knowledge.rs):

LK-01 — Graph load, 1 000 nodes: Create 1 000 Loom blocks with edges forming a random sparse graph (~2 000 edges total). Call GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/graph with depth=2. Measure response time. Budget: <= 3 s. Assert node count >= 1 000 in response.

LK-02 — Graph render layout, 1 000 nodes: Take the graph payload from LK-01 and run the native graph layout algorithm (force-directed or tree layout in handshake_native::graph::graph_layout). Measure time for one layout pass. Budget: <= 1 000 ms.

LK-03 — Tag hub query, 5 000 blocks tagged: Attach a single tag to 5 000 blocks (batch POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks + edge creation). Query the tag hub for that tag. Measure response time. Budget: <= 2 s. Assert hit count == 5 000.

LK-04 — Search index, 5 000 blocks: After creating 5 000 blocks with distinct content, call POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/search-v2 with a query that matches ~100 of them. Measure response time. Budget: <= 2 s. Assert hits list length between 50 and 200 (fuzzy tolerance).

LK-05 — Folder tree, 200 folders: Create a folder hierarchy with 200 folders and 1 000 child blocks. Call GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/folders. Measure response time. Budget: <= 1 s. Assert folder count == 200.

PERF MANIFEST (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/perf_proof/perf_manifest.json): Machine-readable record with one entry per scenario: { scenario_id, category, description, budget_ms (or budget_mb), measured_value, unit, status }. Updated by the test runner on each run. After a passing run all entries have status PASS.

FILES TO CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/perf_proof/perf_manifest.json (initial skeleton)
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_perf_large_code.rs (LC-01 through LC-08)
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_perf_large_rich.rs (LR-01 through LR-07)
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_perf_large_knowledge.rs (LK-01 through LK-05)

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Reuse the same test DB setup pattern as MT-044 (workspace fixture builder from storage/tests.rs).
2. For each timing scenario, bracket the measured operation with std::time::Instant::now() / elapsed(). Assert elapsed <= budget. Print measured value to stdout (--nocapture output).
3. For memory scenarios, add the 'sysinfo' crate as a dev-dependency if not already present. On Windows use the 'windows' crate GetProcessMemoryInfo. Measure RSS before and after; delta must be below budget.
4. Synthetic file/block generators must be deterministic (seeded): use a simple counter loop, not random, so failures are reproducible.
5. For LR-05 (transclusion chain), implement a recursive resolver in the test that calls the backend transclusion endpoint up to depth 50, detecting cycles by tracking visited block IDs in a HashSet.
6. After each scenario function, write its measured_value and status to perf_manifest.json (same pattern as MT-044 parity_manifest.json).
7. Register the perf suite under [[test]] in src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml: name = 'test_perf_large_code' / 'test_perf_large_rich' / 'test_perf_large_knowledge', harness = true.
8. Accept timing budget overrides via env vars: PERF_BUDGET_LC01_MS, PERF_BUDGET_LR01_MS, etc., so CI can widen budgets on slow machines without code changes.
9. Every scenario that creates PG rows must clean up (DELETE) after itself in a defer/drop guard, so test runs are idempotent.
