original_scope.summary:
GOAL: Author and execute the Interconnection Scenario Proof suite. This MT proves that the four core 'melt-together' interconnection edges declared in the WP-KERNEL-012 interconnection_contract actually work at runtime — not as assertions in unit isolation but as end-to-end scenarios that cross surface boundaries. These are the hardest proofs in the WP because they require multiple surfaces to be running simultaneously, sharing real state through the existing backend.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: Creates the flat interconnection proof test files under src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/: (a) test_interconnect_manifest.json with one entry per scenario; (b) test_interconnect_ckc_to_note.rs (CKC media -> note embed scenarios); (c) test_interconnect_note_code_crossref.rs (note <-> code cross-reference scenarios); (d) test_interconnect_loom_backlink_search.rs (Loom backlink + search across surfaces); (e) test_interconnect_shared_undo_ledger.rs (shared undo + event-ledger scenarios). Each file tests a complete cross-surface workflow with real PG state, not mocked connections.

INTERCONNECTION EDGE 1 — CKC media -> note embed (test_interconnect_ckc_to_note.rs)

Scenario IC-01 — Drag CKC image into note: Simulate the drag-and-drop flow where a CKC media asset (stored as a real PG asset row) is dragged from the CKC/Studio surface into an open rich-text note. Expected result: the note's block document gains an hsLink node of kind 'HS_images' pointing to the asset's PG ID; the note is saved via PUT /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents/{doc_id}; loading the note back returns the hsLink node with the correct asset_id. Implementation: (1) create a test asset via POST /workspaces/{id}/assets (or direct DB insert via the storage layer); (2) call the native rich-editor API for InsertEmbed { kind: HsLinkKind::Image, ref_value: asset_id.to_string() }; (3) call save on the native editor, which calls PUT /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents/{doc_id}; (4) load the doc back, assert the hsLink node with kind='HS_images' and ref_value==asset_id exists in the block tree. Verify the embed renders by calling GET /workspaces/{id}/assets/{asset_id} and asserting 200.

Scenario IC-02 — Drag CKC video into note: Same as IC-01 but with content_type='video/mp4'. Assert hsLink node kind='video' in the saved doc.

Scenario IC-03 — Drag CKC moodboard card into canvas: Simulate dragging a CKC moodboard-type Loom block (a block with content_type='ckc_moodboard') onto the Loom canvas board. Expected result: POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/canvas-boards/{board_id}/placements succeeds with the moodboard block_id; GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/canvas-boards/{board_id} returns the placement with block_id == moodboard_block_id. This proves the canvas board accepts CKC-typed blocks as first-class citizens.

Scenario IC-04 — CKC character referenced in note: Create a Loom block with content_type='ckc_character'. In the note, insert a [[loom_block:character_block_id]] wikilink. Save the note. Assert: the note's block tree contains the hsLink node referencing the character block. Call GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{character_block_id}/backlinks and assert the note's block ID appears as a backlink. This proves that wikilinks to CKC entities create real Loom backlinks.

Scenario IC-05 — Route note selection to Stage pane: Select a text range in an open note. Trigger the 'route-to-stage' command (implemented in MT-034). Assert: a Stage pane event is emitted via the command bus with the selected text and source block_id. The Stage pane (CKC surface) receives the event and displays the selection. Verify via AccessKit: the Stage pane widget with author_id='stage.selection.preview' has updated label text matching the selected text.

INTERCONNECTION EDGE 2 — Note <-> code cross-reference (test_interconnect_note_code_crossref.rs)

Scenario IC-06 — Open code block from note: In a rich-text note, insert a [[symbol:rust::src/lib.rs::my_function]] hsLink node. Click the link (simulate via AccessKit action Activate on the widget with author_id matching the hsLink node). Assert: the Code editor pane opens to the file 'src/lib.rs' and scrolls to the line range of 'my_function' as returned by GET /workspaces/{id}/code-nav/symbols/{symbol_entity_id}. Requires: a real code-nav symbol exists in PG (create one via the code-nav indexer or direct insert).

Scenario IC-07 — Reference code symbol from note: In the Code editor, place the cursor on a function name. Trigger 'Copy as note reference' (MT-033 command). Assert: the clipboard receives a string '[[symbol:rust::path/to/file.rs::function_name]]'. Paste into the note. Assert: the note's block tree gains an hsLink node of kind='symbol' with the correct ref_value. Save and reload. Assert the node persists.

Scenario IC-08 — Shared find/replace across code and note: Open the global find/replace surface (MT-029 find-in-files + rich doc find, bridged via the shared command bus from MT-031). Enter a query string that exists in BOTH a code file and a note. Assert: results contain entries from BOTH surfaces (at least one code file hit and one note hit). This proves the shared command bus routes the find request to both editor backends.

Scenario IC-09 — Code diagnostics surface note reference: Inject a fake LSP diagnostic with a 'related information' entry pointing to a note's KRD block ID. Assert: the Code editor's gutter diagnostic for that line includes a hyperlink chip referencing the note. Clicking the chip (AccessKit action on the diagnostic chip widget) triggers navigation to the note in the rich editor pane. Verify via AccessKit: after the click, the rich editor pane with author_id='rich_editor.pane.{doc_id}' gains focus.

INTERCONNECTION EDGE 3 — Loom backlink + search across surfaces (test_interconnect_loom_backlink_search.rs)

Scenario IC-10 — Backlink appears across surfaces: Create a rich-text note A (KRD-based, Loom block loom_A). In the note, add a wikilink to a code-block document B (another Loom block loom_B). Save note A. Assert: GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{loom_B}/backlinks returns an entry whose source_block_id == loom_A. This proves that saving a note with a wikilink registers a real Loom backlink edge in PG, not a local-only reference.

Scenario IC-11 — Loom Search v2 surfaces results from both editors: Create one rich-text note and one code-file Loom block, both containing the string 'XSEARCH_PROBE'. Call POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/search-v2 with query='XSEARCH_PROBE'. Assert: hits contain BOTH block IDs. Assert: content_type_facets includes both 'knowledge_rich_document' and 'code_file' (or equivalent content types).

Scenario IC-12 — Graph view shows cross-surface edges: After IC-10, call GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/graph with depth=2 and block_id=loom_A. Assert: the graph response contains both loom_A and loom_B as nodes, with an edge connecting them. Render the graph layout in the native knowledge surface (force-directed layout call). Assert no layout panic and that both nodes appear at distinct positions.

Scenario IC-13 — AI Loom job proposes cross-surface link: Create a rich-text note whose content describes 'my_function' from a code file. Run the link-suggest AI job (POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/ai-jobs with kind='link_suggest', block_ids=[note_block_id]). Assert: at least one suggestion targets the code file's Loom block. Accept the suggestion (POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/ai-suggestions/{suggestion_id}/accept). Assert: GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{note_block_id}/backlinks now includes the code file block. (This scenario requires a real AI model endpoint; if SKIP_AI_TESTS=1, mark #[ignore] with explicit console output.)

Scenario IC-14 — Quick-switcher surfaces items from both editors: Call GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/quick-switcher?q=XSEARCH_PROBE. Assert: results contain entries from BOTH the note (content_type='knowledge_rich_document') and the code block (content_type='code_file'). Assert: each result has a block_id, title, content_type, and updated_at.

INTERCONNECTION EDGE 4 — Shared undo + event-ledger across surfaces (test_interconnect_shared_undo_ledger.rs)

Scenario IC-15 — Undo crosses rich editor edit: Edit a rich-text note (insert 'EDIT_A'). Trigger global undo (Ctrl+Z via the shared undo stack implemented in MT-035). Assert: the note's content no longer contains 'EDIT_A'. Assert: GET /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents/{doc_id} returns the pre-edit version (optimistic concurrency version decremented or document body reverted). This proves the shared undo stack is wired to the backend save pathway.

Scenario IC-16 — Undo crosses code editor edit: Edit a code buffer (insert 'CODE_EDIT' at line 1). Trigger global undo. Assert: the buffer no longer contains 'CODE_EDIT' at line 1. Assert: if the code buffer is backed by the PG code-file store, the persisted version is also reverted.

Scenario IC-17 — Event-ledger records cross-surface actions: Perform a sequence: (1) insert text in note, (2) save note, (3) insert wikilink to code block, (4) save note again. Call GET /workspaces/{id}/events?source_block_id={note_loom_block_id}&limit=10. Assert: at least 2 KNOWLEDGE_RICH_DOCUMENT_SAVED events appear in the ledger, in order. Assert: the second event's payload contains the wikilink block reference. This proves the event-ledger captures real-time cross-surface authoring history.

Scenario IC-18 — Shared undo stack policy: scoped per-pane vs. global: Open two panes simultaneously (rich editor note A and code editor file B). Edit both. Trigger undo once. Assert: the undo reverts the MOST RECENTLY EDITED surface (not both). This proves the shared undo stack respects the per-pane scope policy declared in MT-035. The assertion checks: if the code edit was last, the code buffer reverts; the note is unchanged.

SHARED UNDO BACKEND CONTRACT: The native undo stack (MT-035) must write an undo snapshot before every save. Snapshot format: { surface: 'rich_editor' | 'code_editor', doc_id, version_before, content_before: bytes }. On undo, the system re-saves content_before to the backend. These tests verify this contract without reimplementing it (the contract is implemented in MT-035; these tests call it).

INTERCONNECT MANIFEST (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interconnect_manifest.json): one entry per scenario: { scenario_id, edge, description, surfaces_involved: [], backend_apis_called: [], proof_fn, status }. Updated by the test runner. 18 entries total (IC-01..IC-18).

FILES TO CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interconnect_manifest.json
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interconnect_ckc_to_note.rs (IC-01..IC-05)
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interconnect_note_code_crossref.rs (IC-06..IC-09)
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interconnect_loom_backlink_search.rs (IC-10..IC-14)
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interconnect_shared_undo_ledger.rs (IC-15..IC-18)

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Reuse the workspace fixture builder and PG setup from MT-044/MT-045.
2. For AccessKit-based interaction proofs (IC-05, IC-09): use egui_kittest to build the widget tree and simulate actions by author_id. Assert the resulting egui context has the expected focus or label state. Reuse the AccessKit registration/snapshot helpers in handshake_native::accessibility::* (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs).
3. For the command-bus proofs (IC-08): instantiate the shared command bus built on handshake_native::command_registry (commands) and handshake_native::event_bus (cross-surface dispatch) in-process, subscribe both editor surfaces, dispatch a FindQuery command, and collect results from both.
4. For IC-13 (AI job), gate with SKIP_AI_TESTS=1 env var and mark #[ignore] with explicit console output. Never assert on specific AI content; only assert that the suggestion list is non-empty and the accept endpoint writes a real edge.
5. IC-15 and IC-16 (undo): the test must call the real shared undo stack push(snapshot) before the edit, then undo() after, and then verify backend state via GET, not by inspecting in-memory state only.
6. All scenarios must clean up their PG rows in a DropGuard.
7. The interconnection proof files are flat integration tests under src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_interconnect_*.rs; each is automatically picked up by cargo's integration-test harness. No [[test]] stanza is required for flat tests/test_*.rs files.
8. Each test function that calls an AccessKit surface must call the accessibility flush helper in handshake_native::accessibility (e.g. accessibility::flush_pending_updates() or the snapshot refresh in accessibility::snapshot) after simulating an action, to ensure the AccessKit tree is up-to-date before asserting labels or focus.

implementation_notes: CROSS-WP DEPENDENCY (WP-011): The interconnection proofs reuse foundation surfaces delivered by WP-KERNEL-011 — the command registry/event bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs), command palette (command_palette.rs + command_registry.rs), context menus (context_menu.rs + context_menu_surfaces.rs), the Loom canvas board (canvas_board.rs) and graph (loom_graph.rs), settings (settings_dialog.rs + workspace_settings.rs), AccessKit (accessibility/*), and MCP tools (mcp/*). These WP-011 modules already exist under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/ and are reused, not recreated. This cross-WP dependency on WP-KERNEL-011 is recorded here as prose; lifecycle.depends_on lists only intra-WP MT ids.

EDGE 1 (CKC->note): The native InsertEmbed editor command lives in the WP-012 rich_editor module created under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/ (EditorCommand::InsertEmbed). Call it directly in the test, passing the HsLinkKind and ref_value. Then call the rich editor save() which dispatches to PUT /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents/{doc_id}. Use the axum test client for the save, not a real HTTP connection.

EDGE 1 IC-03 (moodboard on canvas): Create a Loom block with content_type='ckc_moodboard' via POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks. Then call POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/canvas-boards/{board_id}/placements with { block_id: moodboard_block_id, x: 100.0, y: 100.0 }. The canvas surface reuses the existing handshake_native::canvas_board module. The acceptance test is that the placement is returned in GET /workspaces/{id}/loom/canvas-boards/{board_id}.

EDGE 2 (note<->code): The cross-surface navigation (IC-06, IC-09) reuses the shared command bus built on handshake_native::command_registry (commands) and handshake_native::event_bus (cross-surface dispatch), instantiated with both editor surfaces registered. In the test, create the bus, attach a MockCodeEditorReceiver and MockRichEditorReceiver that record received commands. Send the NavigateTo command. Assert the correct receiver recorded the navigation. Then verify with the AccessKit helpers in handshake_native::accessibility that focus moved to the correct pane.

EDGE 2 IC-07 (copy as note reference): The 'Copy as note reference' command is implemented in the WP-012 code_editor module created under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/ (CodeEditorCommand::CopyAsNoteReference). It must write to the system clipboard. In the test, use the egui_kittest clipboard capture (or a test-only ClipboardCapture trait) to intercept the clipboard write without touching the real OS clipboard.

EDGE 3 IC-11 (search across surfaces): The two Loom blocks (note and code) must both be indexed by the search backend before the query. The native search surface reuses handshake_native::search_rail. Verify indexing by calling POST /workspaces/{id}/loom/search-v2 immediately after creation and checking that both block IDs appear. If indexing is async, poll with a 5-attempt retry with 200ms sleep (budget: 1 s total) before asserting.
EDGE 3 IC-12 (graph): The native graph render reuses handshake_native::loom_graph for the force-directed layout call. Assert no layout panic and that both nodes appear at distinct positions.

EDGE 4 IC-15/IC-16 (undo): The shared undo stack (MT-035) must be the SAME instance shared between the code editor and the rich editor. In the test, create one undo stack, pass it (Arc<Mutex<...>>) to both editor instances. After both edits, pop undo once and assert only the last edit is reverted.

EDGE 4 IC-17 (event-ledger): The event-ledger endpoint is GET /workspaces/{id}/events (or the Flight Recorder query endpoint, whichever exists). PostgreSQL EventLedger only; there is NO SQLite path. The backend is reused via API only; do not modify src/backend/**. If the endpoint accepts a source_block_id query param, use it. If not, query all events and filter by block_id client-side.

For IC-05 (AccessKit Stage pane check): the Stage pane must have a stable author_id registered in MT-034 (the WP-012 CKC stage widget under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/, with author_id='stage.selection.preview', registered via handshake_native::accessibility::registry). If MT-034 did not register this id, this test surfaces a gap and must be marked with a typed blocker comment rather than silently asserting on a stale label.
All scenario functions follow the naming pattern: interconnect_ic{NN}_{snake_case_description}. The manifest proof_fn field must match exactly.

SKIP_AI_TESTS=1 handling for IC-13: use #[cfg_attr(not(feature = 'ai_tests'), ignore)] or check the env var at test start with std::env::var('SKIP_AI_TESTS').is_ok() and call return; with a println! before returning.

REALITY: COMMAND-BUS/UNDO/AccessKit SCENARIOS PROVABLE NOW, BACKEND-BINDING GATED (KERNEL_BUILDER gate 2026-06-26, the FINAL MT - same honest split as MT-044/045/065/074): the MELT-TOGETHER SUBSTRATE scenarios are IN-PROCESS provable NOW (no PG) - prove these GREEN: IC-05 (route-to-Stage command -> AccessKit stage.selection.preview), IC-08 (shared find/replace command bus -> both surfaces), IC-15/IC-16 (shared undo stack reverts edit), IC-18 (undo scope policy: last surface reverts), IC-06/IC-07/IC-09 (note<->code nav via the shared command bus + AccessKit focus). These prove the ACTUAL interconnection claim (the editors share ONE bus + ONE undo) at the substrate level. original_scope.summary:
Goal: Add LSP `textDocument/signatureHelp` (parameter hints) to the native code editor, with a graceful fallback to the Handshake backend code-nav symbol signature when no language server is attached. This is a PURE ADDITION layered on top of MT-008's LSP JSON-RPC request/response plumbing and MT-010's editor wiring — it introduces a new request method on the existing `LspClient`, a new floating parameter-hint popup widget, and a new fallback path through the existing `CodeNavClient`. It does not modify the text buffer, the completion popup, the hover tooltip, or any backend code.

Behavior to implement (VS Code parity): while the user is typing a function call, signature help is requested automatically when an open-paren `(` or a comma `,` trigger character is typed, and can also be requested manually via Ctrl+Shift+Space. The request sends `textDocument/signatureHelp` at the current cursor position. The response (`SignatureHelp { signatures: Vec<SignatureInformation>, active_signature: u32, active_parameter: u32 }`) is rendered as a small floating parameter-hint popup anchored just above the cursor line. The popup shows the active signature's `label` (e.g. `fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32`) with the currently-active parameter span rendered bold / emphasized (color + bold weight, derived from the signature's `parameters[active_parameter].label`, which may be either a string slice or a `[start,end]` offset pair into the signature label per the LSP 3.17 spec — handle both). The popup is dismissed when the user types a close-paren `)`, presses Escape, or moves the cursor outside the active call's argument list. If a server returns multiple `signatures` (overloads), show the active one and a small `1/N` indicator; Up/Down arrow cycles overloads (active_signature index).

Fallback path: when `lsp_client` is None or returns an empty/None `SignatureHelp`, derive a single synthetic signature from the Handshake backend code-nav symbol under the cursor. Resolve the symbol via the existing `CodeNavClient` (from MT-008): look up the call-target identifier with `lookup_symbols`, take the best match, then `get_symbol(entity_id)` and build the signature label from `CodeSymbolResponse.display_name` plus its `params` (parameter names/types as returned by the backend). The fallback `active_parameter` is computed locally by counting the number of top-level commas between the open-paren of the current call and the cursor (a small paren-depth scanner over the buffer slice). If the backend is unreachable or no symbol matches, render nothing and never panic.

Files to CREATE:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/signature_help.rs` — the core of this MT. Defines:
    * `SignatureHelpState { signatures: Vec<SignatureInfo>, active_signature: usize, active_parameter: usize, anchor_byte: usize, source: SignatureSource }` where `SignatureSource` is an enum `Lsp | CodeNavFallback`.
    * `SignatureInfo { label: String, parameters: Vec<ParamSpan>, documentation: Option<String> }` and `ParamSpan { label: String, range_in_label: Option<Range<usize>> }` (range_in_label resolved from the LSP `[start,end]` offset form when present, otherwise computed by substring search of `label` in the signature label).
    * `fn active_parameter_from_commas(buffer_slice: &str, open_paren_byte: usize, cursor_byte: usize) -> usize` — top-level-comma counter using a paren/bracket/brace depth scanner that skips commas inside nested calls, string literals, and char literals.
    * `fn render_signature_popup(ui: &mut egui::Ui, state: &SignatureHelpState, cursor_screen_pos: egui::Pos2)` — draws the floating popup (see step-by-step) and registers AccessKit metadata.
    * `fn signature_label_runs(sig: &SignatureInfo, active_param: usize) -> Vec<(String, bool)>` — splits the signature label into (text, is_active) runs so the active parameter renders bold; the active run is the `ParamSpan.range_in_label` for `parameters[active_param]`.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/lsp_client.rs` — add ONE new method `signature_help(&self, uri: &str, position: LspPosition) -> Option<SignatureHelp>` that sends a `textDocument/signatureHelp` JSON-RPC request over the existing stdio transport (same pending-request / oneshot-channel routing established in MT-008) and deserializes the `lsp_types::SignatureHelp` response. Reuse the existing request-id allocation and reader task — do NOT add a second transport. Return None gracefully when no process is attached or the server has no signatureHelp capability (check the cached `ServerCapabilities.signature_help_provider` from `initialize`; if absent, skip the LSP call and let the caller fall back).
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/pane.rs` — wire the trigger and the render. This is the editor pane integration module (see Conventions note). Add a `signature_help_state: Option<SignatureHelpState>` field to the editor pane struct. In the per-frame update: (a) on input, detect the `(` and `,` trigger characters and the Ctrl+Shift+Space shortcut, and on each trigger spawn an async signature-help request (LSP first, then code-nav fallback) using the same non-blocking channel pattern MT-008 uses for completion/hover (spawn `tokio::task`, poll a result channel on the next frame — never block the egui thread); (b) on `)` or Escape or cursor leaving the call, clear `signature_help_state`; (c) if `signature_help_state.is_some()`, call `signature_help::render_signature_popup(...)` after the text is laid out so the popup floats above the cursor line.

Files to EDIT (module wiring):
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — add `pub mod signature_help;` so the new module is part of the code_editor module tree (mirror how MT-008 added `lsp_client` / `code_nav`).

Conventions / path reconciliation (READ THIS): MT-008 (the dependency that owns the LSP plumbing) places the editor pane widget at one of two filenames inside `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/` (e.g. `pane.rs` or `panel.rs`), while later E1/E5 MTs reference the pane integration module under that same directory. Both candidate filenames are listed in this contract's allowed_paths so the coder may edit whichever exists in the repo at execution time; the binding rule is: edit the SINGLE existing editor pane/panel module that already owns the cursor + LSP wiring from MT-008/MT-010, and do not create a duplicate. If neither file exists yet, the dependency (MT-008/MT-010) is not merged and this MT is blocked — emit a typed blocker rather than scaffolding a new panel. The native crate layout is FLAT under `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/`; there is no `panes/`, `panels/`, `shared/`, or `interop/` directory at `src/frontend/` — the editor and all its submodules live under `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/`.

Exact crates / APIs:
- `lsp-types = "0.95"` (already added in MT-008) — use `lsp_types::SignatureHelp`, `SignatureInformation`, `ParameterInformation`, `ParameterLabel::{Simple, LabelOffsets}`, `SignatureHelpParams`, `TextDocumentPositionParams`. Map `lsp_types` shapes into the local `SignatureHelpState` so the renderer is transport-agnostic (LSP and code-nav fallback both produce `SignatureHelpState`).
- `egui` — render the popup with `egui::Area::new(egui::Id::new("code_editor_signature_help")).order(egui::Order::Tooltip).fixed_pos(anchor_pos).show(ctx, |ui| { egui::Frame::popup(ui.style()).show(ui, ...) })`. Build the label as a sequence of `egui::RichText` runs from `signature_label_runs`, the active run with `.strong()` and an emphasis color from `ui.visuals()`. Anchor the popup ABOVE the cursor line (offset cursor_screen_pos.y by minus the popup height) so it does not cover the text being typed; if there is no room above, fall back to below.
- `accesskit` — register the popup root node with `author_id = "code_editor_signature_help"` and `Role::Tooltip` (matches the hover-tooltip convention from MT-008, and reuse the existing AccessKit registration helpers in `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/`). Include the full active-signature label as the node's name/value so a no-context swarm agent can read the hint without pixels.
- `tokio` — reuse the existing async runtime and the MT-008 non-blocking result-channel pattern; do NOT introduce a new runtime or block the frame.

Handshake backend API bound (fallback only): `GET /knowledge/code/symbols/{entity_id}` (the existing `CodeNavClient::get_symbol` from MT-008) supplies `display_name` + `params` for the synthetic fallback signature, and `GET /knowledge/code/symbols?workspace_id=...&prefix=...` (`CodeNavClient::lookup_symbols`) resolves the call-target identifier to an entity_id. No NEW backend route is introduced or required. PostgreSQL/EventLedger backend only (no SQLite). LSP `textDocument/signatureHelp` is stdio JSON-RPC, NOT an HTTP route.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Add `pub mod signature_help;` to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs`.
2. In `lsp_client.rs`, cache `signature_help_provider` (and its `trigger_characters` / `retrigger_characters`) from the `initialize` response `ServerCapabilities`; expose a `supports_signature_help() -> bool` and the trigger char set so the pane uses server-declared triggers when available, defaulting to `(` and `,` otherwise.
3. Add `LspClient::signature_help` reusing the existing JSON-RPC send/await: allocate a request id, send `textDocument/signatureHelp` with `SignatureHelpParams`, await the oneshot, deserialize to `lsp_types::SignatureHelp`, convert to local `SignatureHelpState` (resolve `ParameterLabel::LabelOffsets([u32;2])` into `range_in_label`, and `ParameterLabel::Simple(String)` into a substring search of the signature label).
4. In the editor pane, add the trigger detection in the input phase: a typed `(` or `,` (only when not inside a string/char literal at the cursor — reuse the depth scanner), or Ctrl+Shift+Space. On trigger, spawn the request task; on result, set `signature_help_state`.
5. Compute `active_parameter` from the LSP response when present; for the fallback path, compute it locally via `active_parameter_from_commas` over the buffer slice from the call's open-paren to the cursor.
6. Fallback resolution: identify the call-target identifier token to the left of the open-paren; `lookup_symbols(prefix)` -> best match -> `get_symbol(entity_id)` -> build `SignatureInfo` from `display_name` + `params`. Cache the resolved signature per (identifier, open_paren_byte) for the lifetime of the popup so commas do not re-hit the backend.
7. Render with `render_signature_popup`: floating Area, popup frame, label runs with the active parameter bold, optional `1/N` overload indicator, optional first line of documentation. Anchor above the cursor line.
8. Dismissal: clear state on `)`, Escape, cursor exiting the argument list (paren depth returns to the call's base depth), or when the editor loses focus.
9. AccessKit: emit the `code_editor_signature_help` Tooltip node with the active signature label text whenever the popup is visible.
10. Tests: see expected_tests / proof_targets — one mock-LSP request test (active param parsing), one graceful fallback test (no LSP -> code-nav signature, no panic), one kittest screenshot proving the active parameter is emphasized, one kittest AccessKit test proving the Tooltip node exists.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: MT-008 (LspClient stdio JSON-RPC transport + CodeNavClient backend code-nav bindings) and MT-010 (editor pane wiring that this hooks into) must be merged. arboard/clipboard are NOT involved. If the LSP transport or the editor pane wiring is absent, emit a typed blocker rather than re-implementing them.
Risk if missed: No parameter hints while typing function calls — a core IntelliSense parity gap versus the React Monaco surface, which provided signature help via Monaco's built-in provider. This blocks MT-044 (the E1 parity proof / aggregation that asserts the full IntelliSense feature set).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement VS Code parity 'Rename Symbol' (F2) for the native egui code editor. The operator places the cursor on an identifier, presses F2 (or chooses 'Rename Symbol' from the Editor Body Context Menu code-pane entry), an inline rename input opens pre-filled with the identifier text and fully selected; on confirm the editor sends an LSP `textDocument/rename` request, receives a `WorkspaceEdit`, shows a multi-file preview of every change, and on accept applies the edits atomically across all open buffers and writes-to-disk for files that are not currently open. When no LSP server is attached, the path degrades gracefully to a `handshake_core` references-based single-file rename (only occurrences in the current file are renamed) with an explicit warning banner reading 'LSP-required for cross-file rename'. This is the primary refactoring affordance — without it the VS Code parity claim fails.

Expected diff shape: (a) one new Rust module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/rename.rs` (~400-600 lines) holding the rename state machine, the inline rename input widget, the WorkspaceEdit preview model, and the apply logic; (b) edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/lsp_client.rs` to add the `textDocument/rename` request/response wiring over the existing stdio LSP transport from MT-008; (c) edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/pane.rs` to add the F2 keybind hook (action arrives via the MT-010 keymap dispatcher), the inline rename input render call, and the new Editor Body Context Menu 'Rename Symbol' entry (build the context-menu surface via the existing WP-011 context_menu.rs + context_menu_surfaces.rs modules).

Files to CREATE:
  - `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/rename.rs`
     * `pub struct RenameState` — holds the current phase: `Idle | Editing { entity_id: String, original: String, draft: String, anchor_byte: usize, ident_range: std::ops::Range<usize> } | Previewing { workspace_edit: WorkspaceEditPreview } | Error { message: String }`.
     * `pub struct WorkspaceEditPreview { files: Vec<FileEditPreview> }` where `FileEditPreview { uri: String, is_open_buffer: bool, edits: Vec<TextEdit>, hunks: Vec<PreviewHunk> }`. `TextEdit { range: LspRange, new_text: String }`. `PreviewHunk { line: usize, before: String, after: String }` (used to render the before/after diff list in the preview, ported visually from the React references panel).
     * `pub fn begin_rename(buffer: &TextBuffer, cursor_byte: usize) -> Option<RenameState>` — find the identifier under the cursor using tree-sitter node-at-byte from the MT-001 highlight tree (walk to the nearest `identifier`/`type_identifier`/`field_identifier` named node); return `Editing` with the ident text pre-filled and `ident_range` set, or `None` if the cursor is not on an identifier.
     * `pub fn confirm_rename(...) -> RenameRequest` — build the LSP rename request (entity_id -> file uri + LSP position) OR, when no LSP is connected, build a `CoreReferencesRenameRequest`.
     * `pub fn build_preview(workspace_edit: LspWorkspaceEdit, open_buffers: &OpenBufferRegistry) -> WorkspaceEditPreview` — sort edits per file descending by start offset so applying later edits does not shift earlier offsets; mark each file as `is_open_buffer` true/false.
     * `pub fn apply_preview(preview: &WorkspaceEditPreview, buffers: &mut OpenBufferRegistry) -> Result<RenameApplyReport, RenameError>` — for open buffers, apply edits to the in-memory `TextBuffer` (descending offset order; adjust `ropey` byte offsets correctly); for unopened files, read file -> apply edits -> write atomically (write to temp + rename, never partial). Returns a report of files changed and total edit count.
     * `pub fn render_inline_input(ui: &mut egui::Ui, state: &mut RenameState)` — draws the inline `egui::TextEdit::singleline` overlaid at the identifier screen position; set AccessKit `author_id = "code_editor_rename_input"`, `Role::TextInput`; request focus on first frame; select-all on open; Enter = confirm, Escape = cancel.
     * `pub fn render_preview(ui: &mut egui::Ui, preview: &WorkspaceEditPreview) -> PreviewAction` — lists every changed file with its hunks before apply; an 'Apply' button (`author_id = "code_editor_rename_apply"`, `Role::Button`) and a 'Cancel' button (`author_id = "code_editor_rename_cancel"`, `Role::Button`).
     * `pub fn render_no_lsp_banner(ui: &mut egui::Ui)` — a visible warning banner with `author_id = "code_editor_rename_no_lsp_banner"`, `Role::Label`, text 'LSP-required for cross-file rename'.

Files to EDIT:
  - `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/lsp_client.rs` — add `pub async fn rename(&mut self, uri: &str, position: LspPosition, new_name: &str) -> Result<LspWorkspaceEdit, LspError>`; serialize the JSON-RPC `textDocument/rename` params `{ textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character }, newName }`; deserialize the `WorkspaceEdit` response (support both the `changes` map form `{ [uri]: TextEdit[] }` and the `documentChanges` array form `[{ textDocument, edits }]`). Reuse the existing stdio JSON-RPC framing/transport added in MT-008 — do NOT add a second transport. Map a null/empty WorkspaceEdit to `Ok(LspWorkspaceEdit::empty())` (no-op rename), and any LSP error to `LspError`.

Exact crates/egui/AccessKit patterns:
  - tree-sitter (from MT-001): use `Tree::root_node().named_descendant_for_byte_range(start, end)` then walk up to the nearest identifier-kind node to resolve the symbol under the cursor; use the byte range as `ident_range`.
  - ropey (from MT-001): apply edits with `TextBuffer::delete(range)` + `TextBuffer::insert(offset, new_text)`; ALWAYS apply edits in descending start-offset order within a file so earlier offsets are not invalidated.
  - egui: inline input via `egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut state.draft).id(egui::Id::new("code_editor_rename_input"))`; position with `egui::Area::new(...).fixed_pos(ident_screen_pos)`; request focus once via `response.request_focus()` guarded by a `focus_requested` flag; select-all by setting the cursor range on first open through `egui::text_edit::TextEditState`.
  - egui preview: `egui::Window::new("Rename Preview").collapsible(false)` or an inline panel listing `FileEditPreview` rows with before/after hunk text.
  - AccessKit: set `author_id` on each interactive node exactly as listed above so swarm agents can drive rename without keystrokes: `code_editor_rename_input` (TextInput), `code_editor_rename_apply` (Button), `code_editor_rename_cancel` (Button), `code_editor_rename_no_lsp_banner` (Label), `code_editor_ctx_rename_symbol` (MenuItem).
  - Reuse WP-011 shell primitives: register the rename input/preview/apply via the existing pane_registry.rs and the AccessKit id registry in accessibility/registry.rs from WP-011; route the 'Rename Symbol' command and the apply/cancel actions through the WP-011 command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) rather than ad-hoc state. Do not invent a parallel registry.

Exact handshake_core API bound (single-file fallback): `GET /knowledge/code/symbols/{entity_id}/references` returns the references of the symbol within the current file (and others, but the fallback only renames same-file occurrences). Use the returned reference byte/char ranges that fall inside the current file's uri to build a single-file WorkspaceEditPreview; render the 'LSP-required for cross-file rename' banner so the operator knows cross-file occurrences were NOT touched. Bind only this existing API; do NOT add or rewrite any backend endpoint — if the references API lacks a needed field (e.g. precise byte ranges), record it as a typed blocker in the validator notes, do not patch the backend.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Wire `CodeEditorAction::RenameSymbol` (F2) into the MT-010 keymap dispatch; on dispatch call `rename::begin_rename(buffer, primary_cursor_byte)`.
  2. `begin_rename`: resolve identifier via tree-sitter; if `None`, do nothing (no rename popup on non-identifiers). Else set `RenameState::Editing` with `draft = original` and request input focus + select-all next frame.
  3. On Enter in the inline input: if `draft == original` or `draft` is empty/whitespace -> cancel (no-op). Else call `confirm_rename`.
  4. If LSP connected: send `lsp_client.rename(uri, position, draft)`; on `Ok(workspace_edit)` build the preview; on `Err` set `RenameState::Error` and show the message (do not panic). If the WorkspaceEdit is empty -> show 'no changes' and return to Idle.
  5. If LSP NOT connected: call `GET /knowledge/code/symbols/{entity_id}/references`, filter to current-file references, build a single-file preview, and set a flag so `render_no_lsp_banner` is shown in the preview.
  6. Preview render lists each file (open vs to-disk noted) with before/after hunks; 'Apply' calls `apply_preview`; 'Cancel' returns to Idle.
  7. `apply_preview`: for open buffers apply edits to the in-memory `TextBuffer` in descending offset order; for unopened files perform atomic disk writes (temp file + rename); never leave a file half-written. Return `RenameApplyReport`. On any per-file failure, stop and report which files were already applied (best-effort rollback is out of scope but the report must be accurate).
  8. After apply, re-highlight affected open buffers (tree-sitter incremental re-parse) and clear `RenameState` to Idle.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement code actions / quick fixes for the native code editor so an operator can act on a diagnostic instead of merely reading it. When the cursor rests on (or selects a range overlapping) a diagnostic line, the editor requests `textDocument/codeAction` from the attached language server for that range, surfaces a gutter lightbulb glyph on the affected line, and on click (or on `Ctrl+.`) shows a popup menu of available actions. Choosing an action applies its `WorkspaceEdit` to the buffer by reusing the apply path built in MT-048. This MT also wires the existing Editor Body Context Menu's quick-fix entry to the same request+apply flow. When no language server is attached (or the server returns no actions) the feature degrades silently: empty action list, no lightbulb, no menu, no error.

Expected diff shape: one new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/code_actions.rs` (~300-450 lines) that owns the code-action request lifecycle, action-list state, lightbulb decision, and the apply call; edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/lsp_client.rs` to add a `code_action(uri, range, context)` request method returning `Vec<CodeActionItem>`; and edits to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/pane.rs` to draw the gutter lightbulb, render the popup menu, bind the `Ctrl+.` shortcut, and route the Editor Body Context Menu quick-fix entry.

Exact files to CREATE:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/code_actions.rs` — defines `CodeActionItem { title: String, kind: Option<String>, edit: Option<WorkspaceEdit>, command: Option<LspCommand>, is_preferred: bool, diagnostics: Vec<LspDiagnostic> }`; defines `CodeActionState { line: usize, actions: Vec<CodeActionItem>, menu_open: bool, selected_index: usize, request_in_flight: bool }`; defines `CodeActionController` holding `Option<CodeActionState>` and the inbound result channel `std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<(usize, Vec<CodeActionItem>)>`. Exact handshake_core API bound: NONE directly. Code actions come from the LSP server over stdio (the same transport MT-008 established). There is no new handshake_core HTTP/Tauri endpoint for this MT. If a future server-side code-action source is desired it is a separate typed blocker, not in scope here.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Add `CodeActionItem`, `CodeActionContext`, `CodeActionParams`, and `LspCommand` types (lsp-types already provides `CodeAction`, `Command`, `CodeActionContext`, `CodeActionParams`, `CodeActionOrCommand` from MT-008's `lsp-types` dependency — prefer reusing those over redefining).
2. In `lsp_client.rs`, implement `code_action` mirroring the existing `completion`/`hover` request pattern from MT-008: build params, send JSON-RPC, await the oneshot, deserialize into `Vec<CodeActionOrCommand>`, normalize to `Vec<CodeActionItem>`. Bare `Command` -> item with `command: Some(..)`, `edit: None`. Full `CodeAction` -> item carrying `edit`, `command`, `is_preferred`, `diagnostics`.
3. The cursor-rest trigger must read diagnostics from the MT-007 gutter diagnostic store (the same store `push_diagnostics` writes to). Only request code actions when the rested line has >=1 diagnostic, to avoid spamming the server on every idle frame.
4. `request_for_cursor` runs the async LSP call off the egui frame thread (tokio spawn) and returns results via the controller's mpsc channel; `poll_results` drains the channel each frame (same non-blocking pattern MT-008 uses for completion).
5. `apply_selected`: take the chosen `CodeActionItem.edit` (a `WorkspaceEdit`), convert each `TextEdit` into the buffer-edit primitive MT-048 already applies, and call the MT-048 apply function. If the item has only a `command` and no `edit`, send `workspace/executeCommand` via the LSP client (server then pushes a `workspace/applyEdit` which the MT-048 apply path also handles) — if `workspace/executeCommand` is unavailable, no-op gracefully.
6. Lightbulb visibility: draw only when `has_actions_on_line(line)` is true AND the menu is closed; while the menu is open, keep the lightbulb highlighted.
7. Degradation: if `lsp_client` is `None`, `request_for_cursor` short-circuits to an empty action list, `has_actions_on_line` returns false, no lightbulb is drawn, `Ctrl+.` opens an empty menu that immediately reports 'No quick fixes available' and closes — never panics, never errors.
8. Wire the existing Editor Body Context Menu quick-fix entry: locate the context-menu builder in `pane.rs` (the menu already lists Cut/Copy/Paste etc.), add/route the 'Quick Fix...' item to call the same request_for_cursor + open_menu flow scoped to the clicked line.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
- MT-007 (gutter diagnostics + `push_diagnostics` store) must be merged — the cursor-rest trigger and lightbulb depend on knowing which lines carry diagnostics.
- MT-008 (LSP client over stdio with JSON-RPC plumbing and lsp-types) must be merged — `code_action` reuses that transport.
- MT-048 (WorkspaceEdit / multi-edit apply path) must be merged — `apply_selected` reuses its apply function and must NOT re-implement it.
- Blocks MT-044 (which depends on quick-fix being available as part of the act-on-error workflow).

HARD constraints: PostgreSQL/EventLedger only (no SQLite anywhere); no backend rewrite — bind existing handshake_core APIs only and treat gaps as typed blockers (this MT binds NONE and that is correct); egui + AccessKit native (no React, no webview); reuse WP-011 shell primitives (pane registry `pane_registry.rs`, command bus `command_registry.rs` + `event_bus.rs`, AccessKit id registry `accessibility/registry.rs`).

Risk if missed: The quick-fix lightbulb is absent, diagnostics remain read-only, and the act-on-error workflow is broken versus VS Code — operators see errors but cannot apply the server's suggested fix from the editor, forcing manual edits and breaking the parity goal.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement VS Code parity 'Format Document' (Alt+Shift+F) and 'Format Selection' for the native egui code editor. Both actions request edits from the language server over the existing stdio LSP client (textDocument/formatting for the whole document, textDocument/rangeFormatting for the active selection), then apply the returned LSP TextEdit array to the ropey buffer as a SINGLE undo step so one Ctrl+Z reverts the entire format. This wires three existing surfaces created by earlier MTs: the EDIT menu 'Format Document' entry, the Editor Body Context Menu 'Format Selection' and 'Format Document' entries, and the MT-010 keymap (Alt+Shift+F). When no language server is attached for the buffer's language, the actions are disabled (greyed) with a hover tooltip 'No formatter available for this language'. The expected diff shape is: (a) one new Rust module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/formatting.rs (~250-400 lines) holding the request builders, the LSP-TextEdit-to-buffer applier, the single-undo grouping, and the no-LSP capability check; (b) edits to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/lsp_client.rs adding the two typed request methods (format_document, format_range) and their response deserialization; (c) edits to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap.rs adding two new CodeEditorAction enum variants (FormatDocument, FormatSelection) with the Alt+Shift+F default binding for FormatDocument.

Exact files to CREATE:
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/formatting.rs — public surface: `pub fn format_document(editor: &mut CodeEditor, lsp: &mut LspClient) -> FormatOutcome`, `pub fn format_selection(editor: &mut CodeEditor, lsp: &mut LspClient) -> FormatOutcome`, `pub fn formatter_available(lsp: &LspClient, language_id: &str) -> bool`, and `fn apply_text_edits(buffer: &mut TextBuffer, edits: &[LspTextEdit], undo: &mut UndoStack) -> usize`. `FormatOutcome` is an enum: `Applied { edit_count: usize }` | `NoChange` | `NoFormatter` | `LspError(String)`.

Exact files to EDIT:
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/lsp_client.rs — add `pub fn format_document(&mut self, uri: &str, options: FormattingOptions) -> Result<Vec<LspTextEdit>, LspError>` issuing a 'textDocument/formatting' request, and `pub fn format_range(&mut self, uri: &str, range: LspRange, options: FormattingOptions) -> Result<Vec<LspTextEdit>, LspError>` issuing a 'textDocument/rangeFormatting' request. Add serde structs `FormattingOptions { tab_size: u32, insert_spaces: bool }`, `LspTextEdit { range: LspRange, new_text: String }`, `LspRange { start: LspPosition, end: LspPosition }`, `LspPosition { line: u32, character: u32 }` if not already present from MT-008. Read the server's documentFormattingProvider / documentRangeFormattingProvider capability flags from the initialize result so `formatter_available` can consult them.
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap.rs — add `FormatDocument` and `FormatSelection` to the `CodeEditorAction` enum; in the default keymap table bind `FormatDocument` to KeyboardShortcut { modifiers: ALT | SHIFT, key: F }. `FormatSelection` has no default binding (menu/context-menu invoked) unless the React reference defines one. Ensure the keymap dispatch routes these actions to the formatting.rs entry points.
- (MENU WIRING) The EDIT menu and Editor Body Context Menu builders (created in earlier E1 menu MTs) must call `format_document` / `format_selection`; locate the existing menu builder where the EDIT menu items are constructed (the EDIT menu lives in the WP-011 top_menu_bar.rs surface; the editor body context menu reuses the WP-011 context_menu.rs / context_menu_surfaces.rs surfaces — search for the EDIT menu label / existing 'Undo'/'Redo' entries) and add 'Format Document' to the EDIT menu and 'Format Selection' + 'Format Document' to the editor body context menu. Each menu item must reflect enabled/disabled state from `formatter_available`. If the menu builder file is outside the allowed_paths of this MT, do the minimal wiring inside formatting.rs by exposing a `menu_descriptors()` helper that the menu builder already consumes; do NOT modify menu files not listed in allowed_paths — instead expose the helper and record a typed blocker if the menu builder cannot consume it.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. FormattingOptions: derive tab_size and insert_spaces from the editor's current indent settings (default tab_size=4, insert_spaces=true if the editor has no per-language override). Do NOT hardcode; read from the editor config struct established in MT-001/MT-010.
  2. format_document flow: (i) check formatter_available; if false return FormatOutcome::NoFormatter. (ii) build the document URI (file:// path the buffer was opened from; if untitled, use the in-memory uri scheme already used by MT-008's LSP didOpen). (iii) call lsp.format_document(uri, options). (iv) on Ok(edits): apply_text_edits as one undo group; return Applied { edit_count } or NoChange if edits is empty. (v) on Err: return LspError(msg) and surface a non-blocking toast; never panic.
  3. format_selection flow: identical but compute LspRange from the editor's current primary selection (start..end). If selection is empty/collapsed, fall back to formatting the whole document is WRONG — instead VS Code formats the current line/empty selection per server behavior; keep it simple: if selection is empty, send the cursor line's range (start of line .. end of line). Convert buffer byte offsets to LSP line/character positions using the TextBuffer byte_to_line + UTF-16 column math (LSP positions are UTF-16 code units by default; convert via the buffer's char/utf16 helpers — do NOT assume bytes == columns).
  4. apply_text_edits MUST sort the incoming TextEdits in descending order of start position before applying, so earlier edits do not invalidate the offsets of later ones. Open ONE undo transaction (UndoStack::begin_group / end_group, or the equivalent batch API from MT-010), apply every edit inside it, then commit so a single Ctrl+Z reverts all. Return the number of edits applied. Re-establish a sensible cursor/selection after formatting (clamp old cursor to new buffer length).
  5. formatter_available: return true only if an LSP client is attached for the buffer's language_id AND the server advertised documentFormattingProvider (for format_document) / documentRangeFormattingProvider (for format_selection) in its capabilities. If no LSP at all, return false -> menu/keymap action disabled.
  6. No-LSP path: the EDIT menu item and context-menu items render disabled (egui add_enabled(false, ...)) with hover tooltip 'No formatter available for this language'. The keymap Alt+Shift+F, when fired with no formatter, must be a no-op (optionally a brief status-bar note) and must NOT panic or block the frame.
  7. AccessKit: the menu items and context-menu items already carry AccessKit metadata from their owning MTs; for any new enabled/disabled state, ensure the disabled state is reflected in the AccessKit node (set the node as disabled / not focusable) so swarm agents observe the same gating the human sees.

React reference: app/src/lib/monaco/* — Monaco wired Format Document via editor.getAction('editor.action.formatDocument').run() and Format Selection via 'editor.action.formatSelection'; Monaco handled the LSP round-trip internally. Here we replace Monaco's internal action with an explicit LSP textDocument/formatting + rangeFormatting call and an explicit single-undo TextEdit applier. Port the action IDs, the EDIT-menu / context-menu placement, and the disabled-when-no-formatter UX from the Monaco wiring; do NOT port Monaco runtime code.

Backend binding: bind the EXISTING stdio LSP transport stood up in MT-008 (textDocument/formatting, textDocument/rangeFormatting). No backend rewrite. If MT-008's LspClient does not yet expose a generic request/response round-trip these methods can build on, record a typed blocker (do not rewrite the transport). PostgreSQL/EventLedger only for any persisted state; this MT persists nothing new (formatting is buffer-local), so no datastore work is expected — if any persistence is implied, it MUST go through the EventLedger/Postgres path, never SQLite.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-008 (LSP client + stdio transport, didOpen URI scheme, capabilities parsing) must be merged first — this MT binds its request plumbing.
  - MT-010 (keymap + CodeEditorAction enum + UndoStack batch/group API) must be merged first — this MT adds two action variants and relies on single-undo grouping.

Risk if missed: the EDIT menu 'Format Document' entry and the editor body context-menu 'Format Selection' / 'Format Document' entries are dead (clickable but inert), and LSP formatting parity with VS Code is unmet, blocking MT-044.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: format_document applies the LSP-returned TextEdit array to the buffer as a SINGLE undo step — proven by a test that mocks the LSP client to return multiple TextEdits, calls format_document, asserts the buffer matches the expected formatted text, then asserts exactly ONE UndoStack entry was created and a single undo reverts the entire format.

AC-002: format_selection edits only the selected range — proven by a test that selects a sub-range, mocks rangeFormatting to return an edit, calls format_selection, and asserts text OUTSIDE the selected range is byte-for-byte unchanged.

AC-003: With no LSP attached (or server lacking documentFormattingProvider), formatter_available returns false, the EDIT menu and context-menu items render disabled, and firing Alt+Shift+F is a no-op that does not panic — proven by the format_no_lsp test.

AC-004: Alt+Shift+F is bound to CodeEditorAction::FormatDocument in the default keymap and routes to formatting.rs — proven by a keymap dispatch test and by an egui_kittest harness that presses Alt+Shift+F and observes the buffer reflow.

AC-005: TextEdits are applied in descending-start order so overlapping/sequential edits do not corrupt offsets — proven by a test feeding two non-trivial edits whose naive ascending application would mis-align, asserting the correct final text.
AC-006: cargo test -p handshake-native passes with no failures across all formatting tests; no unwrap()/panic on the LSP-error path (LspError(String) returned and surfaced as a non-blocking toast).

AC-007: LSP positions are converted using UTF-16 column semantics (not raw byte offsets), proven by a test with a non-ASCII line where byte offset != UTF-16 column and the applied edit lands at the correct character.
proof_targets: PT-001: cargo test -p handshake-native format_document -- --nocapture  =>  mock LSP TextEdits applied, single undo entry created, all GREEN
PT-002: cargo test -p handshake-native format_selection -- --nocapture  =>  only the selected range edited, text outside unchanged, GREEN
PT-003: cargo test -p handshake-native format_no_lsp -- --nocapture  =>  action disabled, no panic, GREEN
PT-004: egui_kittest harness: press Alt+Shift+F, assert FormatDocument fires and the buffer reflows to the mocked formatted text
implementation_notes: Apply TextEdits sorted descending by start position; open one UndoStack group (MT-010 batch API) around the whole apply so a single Ctrl+Z reverts the entire format.
FormattingOptions { tab_size, insert_spaces } must read the editor's current indent config (MT-001/MT-010), defaulting tab_size=4 / insert_spaces=true; do not hardcode.
LSP positions are UTF-16 code units by default — convert buffer byte offsets via the TextBuffer char/utf16 helpers; never assume bytes == columns.

FormatOutcome enum (Applied { edit_count } | NoChange | NoFormatter | LspError(String)) keeps the no-formatter and error paths typed and panic-free; surface LspError as a non-blocking toast, not a frame-blocking dialog.

Disabled menu/context-menu items use egui add_enabled(false, ...) with hover tooltip 'No formatter available for this language' and must set the AccessKit node disabled so swarm agents observe the gating.
Empty/collapsed selection in format_selection sends the current line's range (line start .. line end), matching VS Code behavior; do NOT silently fall back to whole-document formatting.
Re-clamp cursor/selection to the new buffer length after applying edits so the caret does not point past end-of-buffer.
If MT-008's LspClient lacks a generic request round-trip to build format_document/format_range on, record a typed blocker — do NOT rewrite the stdio transport.

PATH + DISPATCH SCOPE (KERNEL_BUILDER gate 2026-06-24): the contract's allowed_paths omit the DISPATCH site + test. The format actions are DEAD without panel.rs wiring (the keymap FormatDocument/FormatSelection dispatch -> formatting::format_document/selection with the CodeEditorPanel's TextBuffer + lsp). allowed_paths corrected: formatting.rs (new) + lsp_client.rs (additive format_document/format_range + capability flags, no 2nd transport) + keymap.rs (FormatDocument+Alt+Shift+F, FormatSelection) + panel.rs (the CodeEditorPanel dispatch arms - the real type is CodeEditorPanel NOT 'CodeEditor'; formatting.rs operates on it/TextBuffer) + mod.rs (pub mod) + tests/test_formatting.rs. EDIT-menu Format Document: top_menu_bar.rs is in allowed_paths for MINIMAL ADDITIVE wiring of the EDIT-menu 'Format Document' entry (reflecting formatter_available enabled/disabled); the editor-body context-menu entries route through the same path. If a needed menu file is genuinely not editable, expose menu_descriptors() from formatting.rs + typed blocker (no scope-bleed beyond allowed_paths, RISK-007).

DATA-INTEGRITY: SINGLE-UNDO + DESCENDING-OFFSET + UTF-16 (KERNEL_BUILDER gate): apply the LSP TextEdit array in DESCENDING start-offset order (reuse MT-048's rename::apply_text_edits_to_buffer / the same descending applier - RISK-001/MC-004, AC-005: ascending corrupts offsets) wrapped in ONE undo GROUP so a single Ctrl+Z reverts the WHOLE format (RISK-002/MC-001, AC-001 - use the existing code-editor undo group/batch API; if MT-010's UndoStack lacks a group API, use the same single-transaction approach MT-048 used). LSP POSITIONS ARE UTF-16 CODE UNITS (RISK-003/MC-005, AC-007 - the load-bearing i18n correctness gate): convert buffer byte offsets <-> LSP line/character via the TextBuffer's char/utf16 helpers, NEVER assume bytes==columns; TEST a non-ASCII line where byte offset != UTF-16 column + assert the edit lands at the correct character. After apply, CLAMP cursor/selection to the new buffer length (RISK-006 - no out-of-range slice panic). format_selection: empty/collapsed selection -> the current LINE's range (line-start..line-end), NOT whole-doc (RISK per VS Code behavior); text OUTSIDE the selected range byte-for-byte unchanged (AC-002).

GATING + HYGIENE (KERNEL_BUILDER gate): formatter_available = LSP attached for the buffer's language_id AND the server advertised documentFormattingProvider (format_document) / documentRangeFormattingProvider (format_selection) in initialize capabilities (RISK-004/MC-003). NO-FORMATTER: EDIT-menu + context-menu items render DISABLED (egui add_enabled(false,...)) with hover 'No formatter available for this language' + the AccessKit node set DISABLED (swarm observes the gating); Alt+Shift+F with no formatter is a NO-OP, no panic, no frame block (AC-003). FormatOutcome enum (Applied{edit_count}|NoChange|NoFormatter|LspError(String)) - NO unwrap()/panic on any path; LspError surfaced as a NON-BLOCKING toast (AC-006/MC-006). FormattingOptions{tab_size,insert_spaces} read from the editor's indent config (MT-001/010, default 4/true - do NOT hardcode). Off-thread LSP request (don't block the frame, RISK-005, MT-008 pattern). FULLY provable WITHOUT live PG (mock LSP returning TextEdits; in-memory buffer; the single-undo + descending + UTF-16 + no-formatter all standalone). Screenshot (if any) EXTERNAL not test_output/. Full suite green (use cargo test -j 2 - ~90 bins OOM at default -j); clippy clean; no SQLite (MC-007 - nothing persisted).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement the buffer-transform handlers behind the MT-010 keymap line-edit actions that currently resolve to actions whose handler bodies do not exist. MT-010 (`src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap.rs`) already declares the `CodeEditorAction` variants `ToggleComment`, `DuplicateLine`, `MoveLineUp`, `MoveLineDown`, `DeleteLine`, `IndentLine`, `DedentLine`, and `InsertTab`, and binds them to VS Code parity chords (Ctrl+/, Ctrl+Shift+K, Alt+Up, Alt+Down, Tab, etc.). When `Keymap::resolve` returns one of these actions and `mod.rs` dispatches it, the handler is currently a stub / unimplemented branch. This MT supplies the real buffer transforms so those chords actually edit the document. Without it, Toggle Comment (Ctrl+/) and the line-edit chords are dead keys.

Expected diff shape: (a) one new module `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/line_ops.rs` (~300-450 lines) that defines pure functions operating on `TextBuffer` (MT-001) and `CursorSet` (MT-003); (b) a small edit to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap.rs` ONLY if a comment-token / tab-policy lookup helper needs to live next to the action enum (prefer adding the lookup to line_ops.rs to keep keymap.rs binding-only — see notes); (c) the dispatch wiring edit in `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs`'s `process_keymap`-driven match so the eight actions call into `line_ops`; (d) a `cursor.rs` touch ONLY if `CursorSet` lacks a helper this MT needs (e.g. a `lines_touched()` accessor) — keep this minimal and additive, do not refactor the cursor model. There is NO backend involvement: `binds_backend_api = ["NONE"]`.

Exact files to CREATE/EDIT:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/line_ops.rs` — the transform library. Define these public functions, each taking `&mut TextBuffer`, `&mut CursorSet`, and a `&LineEditContext` (language + tab settings), and each producing exactly ONE coalesced undo entry (see undo note below):
  * `toggle_comment(buf, cursors, ctx)` — language-aware line-comment toggle.
  * `duplicate_line(buf, cursors, ctx)` — duplicate the line (or each selected line) below.
  * `move_line_up(buf, cursors, ctx)` and `move_line_down(buf, cursors, ctx)` — swap the cursor's line with the line above/below, moving cursors with the text.
  * `delete_line(buf, cursors, ctx)` — delete the whole row including its trailing newline; place the cursor at the start of the next row (or end of buffer).
  * `indent_line(buf, cursors, ctx)` and `dedent_line(buf, cursors, ctx)` — add/remove one indent unit at line start.
  * `insert_tab(buf, cursors, ctx)` — insert a tab character OR `tab_size` spaces depending on `ctx.insert_spaces`; when a selection spans multiple lines, Tab indents the block and Shift+Tab (routed to `dedent_line`) dedents it (VS Code parity).
  Define `LineEditContext { language: EditorLanguage, tab_size: usize, insert_spaces: bool }` and `EditorLanguage` (reuse / re-export the language enum already used by the MT-001 `LanguageRegistry`; do NOT define a second competing language enum — import it). Define `fn line_comment_token(language: EditorLanguage) -> Option<&'static str>` returning `"//"` for Rust/JS/TS/C/C++/Java/Go, `"#"` for Python/Shell/TOML/YAML, `"--"` for SQL/Lua, and `None` for languages with no line comment (those become a no-op for ToggleComment).
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs` — in the action dispatch (the `match action { ... }` fed by `process_keymap` from MT-010), wire the eight variants to the corresponding `line_ops` calls, passing a `LineEditContext` built from the panel's current language and the operator's tab settings. Remove any prior placeholder/`todo!()`/no-op arms for these eight actions. Build the `LineEditContext` once per dispatch batch.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/cursor.rs` — ONLY IF needed: add an additive helper such as `CursorSet::distinct_lines(buf: &TextBuffer) -> Vec<usize>` (sorted, de-duplicated set of line indices any cursor touches) used to apply a transform once per affected line. Do not change existing `Cursor`/`CursorSet` semantics.

Grounded API facts (verified against MT-001 and MT-003 contracts, do not re-derive):
- `TextBuffer` (MT-001, `buffer.rs`) exposes: `insert(byte_offset: usize, text: &str)`, `delete(byte_range: Range<usize>)`, `slice_to_string(line_range: Range<usize>) -> String`, `len_bytes() -> usize`, `len_lines() -> usize`, `line_to_byte(line_idx: usize) -> usize`, `byte_to_line(byte_offset: usize) -> usize`. Range ops are clamp/Result-safe (no panic on out-of-range). Use `line_to_byte`/`byte_to_line` for all row math; never hand-scan for newlines.
- `CursorSet` (MT-003, `cursor.rs`): `Cursor { anchor: usize, head: usize }` (byte offsets), `CursorSet { cursors: Vec<Cursor> }`, methods `add_cursor`, `remove_overlap()`, `move_all`, `insert_at_all`, `delete_at_all`. Cursors are kept sorted by `head`; after any mutation call `remove_overlap()` then re-sort.
- `CodeEditorAction` variants this MT implements are already declared in MT-010 `keymap.rs`: `ToggleComment`, `DuplicateLine`, `MoveLineUp`, `MoveLineDown`, `DeleteLine`, `IndentLine`, `DedentLine`, `InsertTab`. Do NOT add new enum variants; only implement handlers.

Step-by-step implementation notes (multi-cursor + undo are the two cross-cutting requirements):
1. MULTI-CURSOR MODEL: every transform must apply per affected line, derived from the cursor set, not just the primary cursor. Compute the distinct, sorted set of line indices touched by all cursors (each cursor's selection may span multiple lines — include every line from `byte_to_line(min(anchor,head))` to `byte_to_line(max(anchor,head))`). De-duplicate so two cursors on the same line transform it once.
2. APPLY BOTTOM-UP: when a transform changes byte lengths (comment insert/remove, duplicate, move, delete, indent), process the affected lines in DESCENDING line order so earlier (lower-offset) line positions stay valid while later lines are mutated. After all edits, recompute/adjust every cursor's `anchor`/`head` so the cursor stays on the same logical line/column it started on (e.g. after ToggleComment that added `// `, shift heads on that line right by the inserted byte count; after MoveLineUp, move the head's byte offset by the delta of the swapped line lengths). Then call `cursors.remove_overlap()` and re-sort.
3. TOGGLE COMMENT: resolve `token = line_comment_token(ctx.language)`; if `None`, no-op. For each affected line, read the line text via `slice_to_string(line..line+1)`. Determine the line's first non-whitespace column. VS Code semantics: if EVERY affected non-blank line is already commented (first non-ws chars == token), then UNCOMMENT all (remove the token plus one optional following space); otherwise COMMENT all (insert `token + " "` at the first non-whitespace column, or at column 0 for a blank line per VS Code, keeping a consistent insert column across the block = the minimum first-non-ws column of the block). Use `line_to_byte` + the column offset to compute the exact byte position for `insert`/`delete`.
4. DUPLICATE LINE: for each affected line (descending), read its full text including no trailing newline via slice, then `insert` a copy plus a leading/trailing newline immediately after the line's end byte (`line_to_byte(line+1)` is the start of the next line / insertion point; for the last line with no trailing newline, prepend a `\n`). Cursor stays on the original line (VS Code keeps the cursor on the lower/new copy — match VS Code: cursor moves to the duplicated line, i.e. head shifts down by one line's byte length).
5. MOVE LINE UP/DOWN: swap line L with L-1 (up) or L+1 (down). Read both line texts, delete the two-line span, re-insert in swapped order via a single `delete` + `insert` pair (so it coalesces). Clamp: MoveLineUp on line 0 is a no-op; MoveLineDown on the last line is a no-op. Move the cursor with its line (head byte offset adjusted by the neighbor line's length delta).
6. DELETE LINE: for each affected line (descending), delete the byte range `[line_to_byte(line) .. line_to_byte(line+1)]` (this includes the trailing newline). For the last line, delete `[line_to_byte(line)-1 .. len_bytes()]` to also drop the preceding newline so no empty trailing line remains. After deletion, set the affected cursor head to `line_to_byte(min(line, len_lines().saturating_sub(1)))`.
7. INDENT / DEDENT: one indent unit = a literal tab `\t` if `ctx.insert_spaces == false`, else `ctx.tab_size` spaces. INDENT inserts the unit at the start byte (`line_to_byte(line)`) of each affected line. DEDENT removes up to one leading indent unit: if the line starts with `\t` remove it; else remove up to `tab_size` leading spaces (fewer if the line has fewer). Multi-line selection + Tab = indent block (call indent on each affected line); Shift+Tab = dedent block.
8. INSERT TAB (single/collapsed cursor case): if there is NO multi-line selection, insert one indent unit (tab or `tab_size` spaces per `ctx.insert_spaces`) at each cursor head via the cursor set, then advance heads by the inserted byte length. If ANY cursor has a multi-line selection, route to `indent_line` block-indent instead (VS Code behavior: Tab with a block selection indents the block rather than replacing it).
9. UNDO COALESCING: each public `line_ops` function must group all of its sub-edits (across all affected lines and all cursors) into exactly ONE undo entry. The undo stack lives in the editor (introduced by the buffer/edit layer; if a `begin_undo_group()`/`end_undo_group()` or transaction API exists on `TextBuffer`/the panel, wrap the whole transform in it; if no such API exists yet, that is a TYPED BLOCKER — record it as `proof_targets`/`implementation_notes` blocker `BLOCKER-UNDO-API` and implement against the agreed shim rather than inventing a parallel undo stack). Do not emit one undo entry per line.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
- MT-001 DONE (TextBuffer byte-offset API exists).
- MT-003 DONE (CursorSet multi-cursor model exists).
- MT-010 DONE (keymap.rs declares the eight CodeEditorAction variants and dispatches them through mod.rs).
- No new crates required: tabs/spaces/comment tokens are plain string ops on the rope. Do NOT add a dependency for this.
