original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement the four GO-menu navigation behaviors for the native code editor: (1) Go to Next Diagnostic (F8), (2) Go to Previous Diagnostic (Shift+F8), (3) Navigate Back (Alt+Left), (4) Navigate Forward (Alt+Right). Items (1)/(2) traverse the ordered diagnostic markers produced by MT-007's gutter (errors/warnings/info pushed from the MT-008 LSP client via push_diagnostics) with wraparound at the ends. Items (3)/(4) walk an editor jump-history stack that records cursor positions across files whenever the user performs a navigation jump (go-to-definition, find-references result open, symbol/outline jump, and goto-line). This MT also wires the four items into the GO menu (the editor menu bar built in the WP-011 shell, reusing top_menu_bar.rs and pane_registry.rs) and adds the matching CodeEditorAction enum variants into the canonical keymap owned by MT-010.

Files to CREATE:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/navigation.rs` — the diagnostic-traversal logic. Define `pub struct DiagnosticNavigator;` (stateless; it reads live state from the gutter/diagnostic store). Expose `pub fn next_diagnostic(markers: &[DiagnosticMarker], cursor: BufferPosition) -> Option<BufferPosition>` and `pub fn prev_diagnostic(markers: &[DiagnosticMarker], cursor: BufferPosition) -> Option<BufferPosition>`. `DiagnosticMarker` is the marker type already defined by MT-007 (re-use it; do NOT redefine it — import via `handshake_native::code_editor::gutter::DiagnosticMarker`). `BufferPosition { line: usize, column: usize }` is the editor's existing cursor type (re-use the type MT-001/MT-003 established for the cursor; if a shared `Position`/`Caret` type exists, import it rather than create a parallel one). Ordering rule: markers are sorted by (line, column) ascending. `next_diagnostic` returns the first marker strictly after the cursor; if none, wrap to the first marker (index 0). `prev_diagnostic` returns the last marker strictly before the cursor; if none, wrap to the last marker. Return `None` only when the marker list is empty.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/jump_history.rs` — the back/forward jump stack. Define `pub struct JumpEntry { pub file_path: PathBuf, pub position: BufferPosition }` and `pub struct JumpHistory { entries: Vec<JumpEntry>, cursor: usize }`. Expose: `JumpHistory::new() -> Self`, `record(&mut self, entry: JumpEntry)` (push: if the user previously navigated back and then makes a NEW jump, truncate the forward tail before pushing — VS Code semantics; coalesce consecutive entries that point at the same file+position within a small line tolerance so trivial cursor moves do not flood the stack), `back(&mut self, current: JumpEntry) -> Option<JumpEntry>` (move the cursor one entry toward the past and return the prior location, recording `current` so Forward can return to it), `forward(&mut self) -> Option<JumpEntry>` (move toward the future), `can_back(&self) -> bool`, `can_forward(&self) -> bool`. The stack must be cross-file: each entry carries its own `file_path` so Navigate Back can restore a position in a different file than the one currently focused. Cap the stack at a fixed size (e.g. 50 entries) by dropping the oldest.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/keymap.rs` (owned by MT-010 — extend, do NOT rewrite its existing dispatch table) — add four `CodeEditorAction` enum variants: `GoToNextDiagnostic`, `GoToPrevDiagnostic`, `NavigateBack`, `NavigateForward`. Register default bindings in the canonical keymap table: F8 -> GoToNextDiagnostic, Shift+F8 -> GoToPrevDiagnostic, Alt+ArrowLeft -> NavigateBack, Alt+ArrowRight -> NavigateForward, using `egui::KeyboardShortcut { modifiers, key }` consistent with the existing MT-010 entries. Wire the dispatch arms: GoToNextDiagnostic/GoToPrevDiagnostic call `navigation::next_diagnostic`/`prev_diagnostic` with the current marker list + cursor and, on `Some(pos)`, move the editor caret to `pos` AND push the pre-jump location into the JumpHistory; NavigateBack/NavigateForward call `JumpHistory::back`/`forward` and, on `Some(entry)`, open `entry.file_path` (if different from the active file) and move the caret to `entry.position`.

GO-menu wiring: the editor menu bar lives in the WP-011 shell (top_menu_bar.rs). Add four GO-menu items (labels: "Go to Next Problem", "Go to Previous Problem", "Back", "Forward") that each dispatch the matching CodeEditorAction through the WP-011 command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs), so menu click and keybinding share one code path. Reuse the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs) to resolve the currently focused code-editor pane, and reuse the WP-011 command bus rather than calling editor methods directly. Forward/Back menu items should be disabled (greyed) when `can_forward()`/`can_back()` are false.

React reference: `app/src/components/operator/ProblemsView.tsx` — port its diagnostic ORDERING only (how problems are sorted by file then line then column then severity). The native ordering in `navigation.rs` must match ProblemsView so that F8 traversal order equals the Problems-list order a user would see. Do not port React rendering; ordering semantics only.

Backend API binding: NONE. This MT is pure frontend. Diagnostic markers come from MT-007's in-process gutter store (which MT-008 already populated from the LSP client). Jump positions come from in-process editor cursor state. No new handshake_core API call is introduced. (PostgreSQL/EventLedger is irrelevant here — no persistence; the jump stack is in-memory session state.)

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Confirm the MT-007 `DiagnosticMarker` type and the editor's cursor `BufferPosition` type names by reading `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/gutter.rs` and the cursor module; import them — never redefine.
2. Implement `navigation.rs` pure functions first; they are trivially unit-testable without egui.
3. Implement `jump_history.rs` with VS Code back/forward truncation semantics; unit-test push/back/forward and the cross-file path retention.
4. Extend `keymap.rs`: add the four variants, the four default shortcuts, and the four dispatch arms. Keep the existing MT-010 entries intact.
5. Add the four GO-menu items in the WP-011 shell menu bar (top_menu_bar.rs), each dispatching via the command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs); gate Back/Forward enabled-state on can_back/can_forward.
6. AccessKit: give each GO-menu item a stable AccessKit author_id reusing the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) — `menu-go-next-diagnostic`, `menu-go-prev-diagnostic`, `menu-go-back`, `menu-go-forward`, role=MenuItem — so swarm agents can invoke navigation deterministically.
7. When a goto-def / find-references / outline-jump / goto-line jump occurs (MT-006, MT-008 dispatch sites), call `JumpHistory::record` with the PRE-jump location so Navigate Back can return there. This means MT-006/MT-008 dispatch arms must call into the shared JumpHistory; add the record() call at those dispatch sites in keymap.rs without altering their existing jump behavior.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
- MT-006 (goto-line) merged — provides one jump source and the editor caret-move primitive.
- MT-007 (gutter diagnostics) merged — provides the `DiagnosticMarker` list traversed by F8/Shift+F8.
- MT-008 (LSP client) merged — provides goto-def / find-references jump sources and the diagnostics feed.
- MT-010 (unified keymap) merged — provides the `CodeEditorAction` enum and dispatch table this MT extends.
- Cross-WP: WP-011 (native shell) provides the menu bar (top_menu_bar.rs), pane registry (pane_registry.rs), command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs), and AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) reused for GO-menu wiring; these are already-shipped WP-011 modules under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/.

Risk if missed: the four GO menu items are dead/non-functional; diagnostic traversal (F8/Shift+F8) and back/forward navigation (Alt+Left/Right) parity with VS Code is unmet, and the MT-044 Parity Proof Suite cannot prove the navigation feature row.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: deliver two reuse-heavy editor-chrome wayfinding features over the existing tree-sitter scope data already produced by earlier E1 MTs, closing the modern VS Code navigation parity gap inside the native egui code editor. Feature (1) is 'Go to Symbol in file' (Ctrl+Shift+O): a fuzzy command palette scoped to the symbols of the CURRENTLY ACTIVE file only — this is explicitly DISTINCT from the global cross-file quick-switcher delivered by MT-030. Feature (2) is 'Sticky scroll': pinned enclosing-scope header lines rendered at the top of the editor viewport while the user scrolls inside a function, class, impl block, or other nested scope, so the signature/declaration lines of every enclosing scope remain visible (matching VS Code's `editor.stickyScroll`).

This MT is a pure reuse layer. It MUST NOT re-parse source or build its own symbol model. Feature (1) reuses the MT-006 OutlineProvider (the in-file symbol/outline tree built from tree-sitter), and feature (2) reuses the MT-005 fold regions plus the MT-006 outline to compute enclosing scopes. There is NO backend dependency; binds_backend_api is NONE. All scope/symbol data already lives in-process from MT-002 (virtualized text model / viewport), MT-005 (fold regions), and MT-006 (outline). MT-010 supplies the GO menu surface this MT wires the 'Go to Symbol...' item into.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/symbol_palette.rs (~250-350 lines) — the in-file Go to Symbol palette. Defines `SymbolPalette` (egui modal state + fuzzy matcher) and a `FileSymbol { name: String, kind: SymbolKind, byte_range: Range<usize>, line: usize, container: Option<String> }` view-model adapted FROM the MT-006 OutlineProvider's outline nodes (do not redefine the outline data model; map from it). Exposes `SymbolPalette::open(outline: &OutlineProvider)`, `SymbolPalette::filter(query: &str) -> &[FileSymbol]`, and `SymbolPalette::show(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui) -> Option<SymbolPaletteAction>` where the action is `JumpTo { line, byte_range }` on confirm.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/sticky_scroll.rs (~200-300 lines) — computes the set of enclosing-scope header lines for a given viewport top line. Defines `StickyScroll` with `compute(&self, viewport_top_line: usize, fold_regions: &[FoldRegion], outline: &OutlineProvider) -> Vec<StickyHeader>` where `StickyHeader { line: usize, text: String, depth: usize }`. Walks the fold regions / outline nodes whose start line is at or above viewport_top_line and whose end line is at or below it (i.e. scopes that strictly enclose the first visible line) and returns their header (declaration) lines ordered outermost-first. Caps the number of pinned headers (config `max_sticky_lines`, default 5, matching VS Code) to bound viewport consumption.

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/viewport.rs — render the sticky headers as a pinned overlay band at the top of the scroll viewport BEFORE the scrolled content (a fixed `egui::Area`/top strip inside the editor frame, not part of the scrolled galley). Reserve vertical space equal to `headers.len() * line_height` so the first scrolled line is not occluded. Clicking a sticky header scrolls the viewport to that header's line. Also: drive the symbol palette modal from this module — when `SymbolPaletteAction::JumpTo` fires, set the viewport scroll offset to the target line and place the caret/selection at the target byte_range (reusing the existing MT-002 viewport scroll-to-line and MT-010 caret APIs; do NOT introduce a new scroll mechanism).
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/mod.rs — declare `pub mod symbol_palette;` and `pub mod sticky_scroll;` if not already declared.

Menu / command wiring:
  - Wire the GO menu 'Go to Symbol...' item (the menu surface comes from MT-010, built on the WP-011 top_menu_bar.rs) to open the in-file `SymbolPalette`. Also register the Ctrl+Shift+O keyboard shortcut via `egui::KeyboardShortcut { modifiers: Modifiers::COMMAND | Modifiers::SHIFT, key: Key::O }`. Both the menu item and the shortcut call the same `open_symbol_palette()` entry point. Keep this distinct from MT-030's global quick-switcher binding (Ctrl+P / Ctrl+T).

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. In symbol_palette.rs, adapt MT-006 outline nodes into a flat `Vec<FileSymbol>` (flatten the outline tree depth-first; carry the parent name into `container` so the palette can show 'method — in ClassName'). Do not re-walk tree-sitter directly; the outline already encodes kind + range.
  2. Reuse the SAME fuzzy matcher / palette interaction used by the MT-030 quick-switcher and MT-031 command palette, which are built on the WP-011 command_palette.rs (palette UI/fuzzy-filter) and command_registry.rs (command bus), rather than writing a second fuzzy algorithm; if no reusable fuzzy filter helper is exposed by command_palette.rs yet, implement a small subsequence-with-gap-penalty matcher and note it for later extraction into command_palette.rs.
  3. Render the palette as an `egui::Window` anchored CENTER_TOP, opened only when `symbol_palette.open` is true; arrow keys move selection, Enter confirms (emit JumpTo), Escape closes. Mirror the keyboard-nav and overlay-modal pattern already established by MT-030/MT-031 (command_palette.rs).
  4. In sticky_scroll.rs, compute enclosing scopes for the viewport top line by intersecting fold regions (MT-005) with outline nodes (MT-006): a scope is 'sticky' when region.start_line <= viewport_top_line < region.end_line. Order outermost (smallest start_line) first, truncate to `max_sticky_lines`. The header text is the source declaration line for region.start_line (slice it from the buffer via the MT-002 viewport/buffer API).
  5. In viewport.rs, paint the sticky band: a top strip rendered with the editor's gutter/background color, each header a clickable row; clicking calls the same scroll-to-line path used by JumpTo. Recompute headers each frame from the current scroll offset (cheap; bounded by max_sticky_lines).
  6. AccessKit: the symbol palette list container uses author_id='code_editor_symbol_palette' (Role::List); each result row uses author_id='symbol-{index}' (Role::ListItem); the search input uses author_id='code_editor_symbol_palette_search' (Role::TextInput). The sticky band container uses author_id='code_editor_sticky_scroll' (Role::GenericContainer) and each pinned header uses author_id='sticky-header-{depth}' (Role::Button) so swarm agents can address and click headers.

Reuse / shell primitives (WP-011): reuse the WP-011 shell modules — register the Ctrl+Shift+O command and the GO menu item through the existing command_registry.rs command bus (with event_bus.rs for the resulting action events) rather than an ad-hoc keybind table, route menu wiring through top_menu_bar.rs, and allocate all AccessKit author_ids through the shared accessibility/registry.rs id registry to avoid collisions.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-002 (virtualized viewport + scroll-to-line + buffer slice API) merged.
  - MT-005 (fold regions) merged — supplies enclosing-scope ranges for sticky scroll.
  - MT-006 (OutlineProvider / in-file symbols) merged — supplies the symbol model for the palette AND the scope headers.
  - MT-010 (GO menu + caret/selection API) merged — supplies the menu surface to wire and the caret placement used by JumpTo.

(2) FOLD-MAPPING OMISSION: decoration layer assumes contiguous buffer lines (indent-guide loop enumerates buffer lines as consecutive row offsets - its comment is wrong; decoration_xy has no fold mapping and no upper bound; bracket byte window includes hidden folded lines) while the row painter maps through FoldSet -> hidden-line decorations leak onto visible rows and post-fold decorations land N rows too low. (3) FAKE PROOF: AC-006/PT-004 claim pixel sampling; the test saves the PNG and asserts only non-emptiness; the artifact itself falsifies the visually-verified claim. original_scope.summary:
Goal: complete the VS Code editor-chrome rendering layer that sits on top of the MT-002 virtualized line renderer. Three render-only features are added in this MT: (1) matching-bracket highlight driven by cursor adjacency plus bracket-pair colorization across nesting depth, (2) vertical indent guides with an active-guide highlight for the block enclosing the cursor, and (3) a word-wrap mode toggled by Alt+Z that rewrites the visible-row layout math so a single logical buffer line can occupy multiple visual rows. This is strictly a render-layer / decoration addition: the underlying text buffer model (ropey Rope from MT-001) and the highlight span model are NOT changed; no buffer edit, no cursor-model change, no tree-sitter grammar change. The work hangs entirely off the existing viewport / line-painting code created in MT-002.

Exact files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/render_decorations.rs  — bracket matching + bracket-pair colorization. Defines: `struct BracketMatch { open_byte: usize, close_byte: usize }`, `fn find_matching_bracket(buffer: &TextBuffer, cursor_byte: usize) -> Option<BracketMatch>` (scans left/right of the cursor for one of `()[]{}`, then walks the buffer with a depth counter to find the partner, honoring the same bracket family only), and `fn bracket_pair_colors(buffer: &TextBuffer, visible_byte_range: Range<usize>, palette: &[egui::Color32]) -> Vec<(Range<usize>, egui::Color32)>` (assigns each bracket a color by its nesting depth modulo palette length, matching VS Code's bracketPairColorization). Both functions are pure over a borrowed buffer slice; no mutation.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/word_wrap.rs  — visible-row layout math for wrap mode. Defines: `struct WrapConfig { enabled: bool, wrap_column: Option<usize>, viewport_width_px: f32 }`, `struct VisualRow { logical_line: usize, byte_start: usize, byte_end: usize, wrap_index: usize }`, and `fn layout_visual_rows(buffer: &TextBuffer, line_range: Range<usize>, cfg: &WrapConfig, char_width_px: f32) -> Vec<VisualRow>`. When `cfg.enabled` is false, each logical line maps to exactly one VisualRow (wrap_index=0) so existing behavior is preserved. When enabled, a logical line wider than the wrap width is split at the last soft break (whitespace) before the width limit, falling back to a hard character break when no whitespace exists; each fragment becomes its own VisualRow.

Exact files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/viewport.rs  — the MT-002 virtualization module. Today it computes which logical lines are visible and paints them. Change it to: (a) call `word_wrap::layout_visual_rows` to translate the visible logical-line range into a list of VisualRow entries and drive painting + scroll math off visual rows instead of raw logical lines (so the vertical scrollbar, first-visible-row and row-count computations all account for wrapped rows); (b) after painting each line's text + syntax spans, overlay the bracket-match highlight (a rounded rect or underline behind the two matched brackets returned by `find_matching_bracket`) and the bracket-pair colors from `bracket_pair_colors`; (c) paint vertical indent guides — for each visible row compute its leading-whitespace indent level (spaces / tab_width), draw a 1px vertical line via `ui.painter().vline` at x = gutter_right + indent_level * char_width_px * tab_width for each level, and draw the guide that encloses the cursor's block in the active-guide color (theme `visuals.indent_guide_active`) while the rest use `visuals.indent_guide`; (d) register the Alt+Z shortcut (egui::KeyboardShortcut { modifiers: Modifiers::ALT, key: Key::Z }) consumed via ui.input_mut(|i| i.consume_shortcut(..)) to flip `WrapConfig.enabled`, persisted on the editor state struct.

Exact crates / egui / AccessKit patterns:
  - egui only (no new crate). Lines/guides drawn with `ui.painter().vline(x, y_range, egui::Stroke::new(1.0, color))`; bracket highlight rect with `ui.painter().rect_stroke(rect, rounding, stroke)` or `rect_filled` with a low-alpha fill; colored bracket glyphs by painting the bracket character galley with the depth color via `ui.painter().galley` rather than mutating the buffer text.
  - Reuse the existing per-character / per-span layout produced in MT-002 to get glyph x-offsets; do not recompute font metrics independently — pull `char_width_px` and `row_height_px` from the same monospace `egui::FontId` the renderer already uses (`ui.fonts(|f| f.glyph_width(&font_id, ' '))`).
  - AccessKit: word-wrap is a render-mode toggle; expose it as a togglable command. Reuse the existing AccessKit integration in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/ (mod.rs, live.rs, registry.rs, snapshot.rs). If MT-002 already attaches an AccessKit node for the editor surface, add the wrap state as an AccessKit `Toggled` property on a child node with author_id="editor-wrap-toggle" (Role::Button, actions=[Press]) registered through the accessibility/registry.rs node registry so swarm agents can flip wrap deterministically. Do not invent a second editor root node; attach under the MT-002 editor container.
  - Theme tokens: add `indent_guide`, `indent_guide_active`, and a `bracket_pair_palette: Vec<Color32>` to the editor visuals struct if not already present (theme-aware, no hardcoded hex in the paint path). Source the palette/colors through the existing theme layer in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/theme/ (mod.rs, palette.rs, syntax.rs, egui_apply.rs).

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Implement and unit-test `find_matching_bracket` first against the in-process TextBuffer (no egui). Cover: cursor immediately before an opening bracket, cursor immediately after a closing bracket (VS Code adjacency rule), nested pairs, unbalanced input returns None, and brackets inside strings/comments are still matched at the syntactic level for v1 (string-awareness is out of scope; note it as a limitation).
  2. Implement and unit-test `bracket_pair_colors` — walk the visible range maintaining a depth counter per bracket family; map depth to `palette[depth % palette.len()]`.
  3. Implement and unit-test `layout_visual_rows` with wrap disabled (1:1 mapping) and enabled (a 200-char line at wrap width ~80 produces ceil-style multiple VisualRows; assert byte ranges are contiguous and non-overlapping and cover the whole logical line).
  4. Edit viewport.rs to consume VisualRows for paint + scroll math; verify the existing MT-002 non-wrap screenshot is unchanged when wrap is off (regression guard).
  5. Overlay bracket-match highlight + bracket-pair colors + indent guides in the paint pass, in that z-order (text first, then decorations on top).
  6. Wire the Alt+Z toggle and persist `WrapConfig.enabled` on the editor state.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-001 (TextBuffer in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/buffer.rs) must be merged — bracket scanning and indent computation read the buffer.
  - MT-002 (virtualized line renderer / src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/viewport.rs) must be merged — all three features attach to its paint + visible-row math; without it there is no row layout to extend.
  - Cross-WP reuse: the AccessKit integration (accessibility/*) and theme layer (theme/*) reused here are existing WP-011 modules already present under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/.

Risk if missed: bracket matching, bracket-pair colorization, indent guides, and word wrap are absent, leaving the editor chrome visibly below modern VS Code parity (MT-045, the parity proof, is blocked).

implementation_notes: VS Code cursor adjacency rule: a bracket is considered 'active' when the cursor is immediately before an opening bracket OR immediately after a closing bracket. Implement both directions in find_matching_bracket.

Bracket-pair colorization in VS Code is per-family depth-based; maintain one depth counter shared across families for the color index (VS Code increments depth on any open bracket), but match partners only within the same family — keep these two concerns separate in code.
When wrap is disabled, layout_visual_rows must be a strict 1:1 identity mapping so the MT-002 baseline screenshot does not regress; add a fast path that skips the wrap computation entirely.

Pull char_width_px and row_height_px from the SAME egui::FontId the MT-002 renderer uses (ui.fonts(|f| f.glyph_width(&font_id, ' '))); do not hardcode metrics — proportional drift breaks indent-guide x-positions and wrap break points.

Indent level = leading whitespace columns / tab_width (expand tabs to tab_width columns); active guide = the guide enclosing the cursor's current block. Draw guides with ui.painter().vline, theme tokens visuals.indent_guide and visuals.indent_guide_active sourced from the theme/ layer.
Alt+Z shortcut: egui::KeyboardShortcut { modifiers: egui::Modifiers::ALT, key: egui::Key::Z }; consume via ui.input_mut(|i| i.consume_shortcut(&sc)) before default handling to avoid inserting 'z'.

Bracket-pair colors are painted by re-drawing the bracket glyph in the depth color over the syntax-highlighted text (z-order: text, then bracket-pair color, then bracket-match highlight, then indent guides under text); do not mutate buffer text or the HighlightSpan list.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Add a per-document reading/preview mode to the native rich-text editor so any note can be flipped between an editable WYSIWYG view and a clean, read-only rendered presentation. This is the Obsidian 'reading view' parity item and the native equivalent of the React ViewModeToggle: the GUI look-and-behavior doc merges the toggle into the native editor chrome rather than exposing a separate floating control. The chosen mode is persisted per document_id so reopening a note restores its last view. This MT does NOT introduce a new rendering path — it reuses the MT-011 DocModel as the single source of truth and the MT-012 renderer pipeline, switching only the interaction/chrome behavior between Edit and Reading.

Expected diff shape: (a) one new Rust module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/reading_mode.rs (~180–300 lines) defining the ViewMode enum, a per-document mode store keyed on document_id, and the toggle widget; (b) edits to the existing renderer widget at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/renderer/rich_editor_widget.rs to honor a read_only flag (suppress caret, suppress editable TextEdit runs, apply reading margins/typography, keep links and embeds interactive); (c) a one-line registration in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/mod.rs (pub mod reading_mode;) if the module is not already declared; (d) kittest + cargo unit tests under src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_*.rs (flat test files, e.g. src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_reading_mode.rs).

Files to CREATE:
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/reading_mode.rs — defines:
    * `pub enum ViewMode { Edit, Reading }` deriving Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize.
    * `pub struct ReadingModeStore { modes: std::collections::HashMap<String, ViewMode> }` keyed on document_id (String). Methods: `get(&self, document_id: &str) -> ViewMode` (default ViewMode::Edit when absent), `set(&mut self, document_id: &str, mode: ViewMode)`, `toggle(&mut self, document_id: &str) -> ViewMode`.
    * `pub fn reading_mode_store(ctx: &egui::Context) -> ReadingModeStore` / a persisted accessor: store the ReadingModeStore in egui Context data via `ctx.data_mut(|d| d.get_persisted_mut_or_default::<ReadingModeStore>(egui::Id::new("handshake_rich_reading_modes")))` so the per-document choice survives re-render and (via egui persistence) app restart. ReadingModeStore must derive Clone, Default, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize so egui's persistence layer can round-trip it.
    * `pub fn view_mode_toggle(ui: &mut egui::Ui, document_id: &str, store: &mut ReadingModeStore) -> ViewMode` — renders an Edit|Reading segmented toggle inside the native editor chrome and returns the active mode after handling clicks. AccessKit: the toggle container author_id="rich-reading-mode-toggle" role=Group; the Edit segment author_id="rich-reading-mode-edit" role=Button (or ToggleButton) actions=[Press]; the Reading segment author_id="rich-reading-mode-reading" role=Button actions=[Press]; mark the active segment selected/toggled in the AccessKit node so swarm agents and screen readers can read current mode. Use the existing WP-011 accessibility/* helpers (accessibility/mod.rs, accessibility/registry.rs) to register author_ids and toggled state rather than emitting AccessKit nodes inline.

Files to EDIT:
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/renderer/rich_editor_widget.rs — the MT-012 WYSIWYG widget. Add a `read_only: bool` input (or accept a ViewMode) on the show/render entry point. When read_only is true: (1) do NOT instantiate the editable caret/selection state and do NOT emit egui TextEdit widgets for runs — render runs as immutable galleys/labels via the MT-012 block renderer in a non-editable code path; (2) widen the content margins to reading width (e.g. clamp the text column to ~700–760 logical px centered, larger vertical paragraph spacing) using the existing WP-011 theme tokens (theme/mod.rs, theme/palette.rs), not hardcoded hex; (3) keep wikilink chips (MT-015) and embeds/node-views (MT-014) interactive — their click/hover handlers must still fire and route through the shared navigation/command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs); (4) skip input-handler edit dispatch (typing, formatting shortcuts) so the document cannot be mutated while in Reading mode. When read_only is false, behavior is exactly the MT-012 editable path (no regression).
- src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/mod.rs — add `pub mod reading_mode;` if absent.
- src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml — only if serde derive on ViewMode/ReadingModeStore requires enabling the serde feature; reuse the workspace serde already used by MT-011 DocModel, do not add a new dependency if serde is already present.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
1. Define ViewMode + ReadingModeStore in reading_mode.rs. Keep the store pure data; the egui-context accessor lives in the same module but the store type itself must be testable without egui (so the persistence unit test can construct a ReadingModeStore directly).
2. In the rich editor host (the same call site that already builds the MT-012 widget), read the active mode: `let mode = store.get(document_id);` then render the view_mode_toggle in the chrome and pass `read_only = mode == ViewMode::Reading` into rich_editor_widget.
3. In rich_editor_widget.rs, branch on read_only at the top of the per-block render loop. Reuse the MT-012 block renderer for the actual glyph/galley layout — do NOT fork a second renderer; the only difference between Edit and Reading is: caret/selection state allocation, TextEdit emission, input dispatch, and margin/typography. This keeps the DocModel as the single source of truth (MT-011) and guarantees Reading shows exactly what Edit shows, minus editing affordances.
4. Caret suppression: in Reading mode, do not allocate the caret blink state and do not call the input handler that advances caret position; the AccessKit tree for the rendered region must NOT contain an editable TextField/TextInput node for the document body (the test asserts this).
5. Interactivity preservation: wikilink chips and embeds register their own egui responses; ensure the Reading code path still calls their response builders so clicks route to the shared navigation/command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs). Do not gate link/embed click handling behind the editable branch.
6. Persistence: every toggle calls store.set(document_id, new_mode) and writes back to ctx.data_mut so the choice is keyed per document_id and survives re-render; egui's persisted storage carries it across app restart. On render, always read store.get(document_id) so switching documents shows each document's own remembered mode.
7. Tests (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_*.rs flat files, e.g. tests/test_reading_mode.rs):
   - cargo unit test: construct ReadingModeStore, toggle for document_id "doc-A", assert returned mode flips Edit->Reading->Edit; assert get("doc-B") still defaults to Edit (per-document isolation).
   - cargo unit test: toggling to Reading yields read_only=true; assert the widget input the host passes (read_only flag) is true and that no caret/selection state is constructed in that path (e.g. via a test-visible flag or by asserting the render config).
   - kittest harness: seed a DocModel with a heading, a bullet list, a quote, and a wikilink; render in Reading mode; dump the AccessKit tree and assert the heading/list/quote nodes are present AND that no editable TextEdit/TextInput node exists for the document body.
   - kittest screenshot: capture mt055_reading_mode.png of the rendered read-only document and assert it renders (non-empty, headings/list visible) — store under the WP test_output convention.
   - cargo test: persistence across re-render — set mode=Reading for document_id, simulate a second render frame reading from the same store, assert mode is still Reading (choice persists per document_id across re-render).

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
- MT-011 (BlockDocumentModel / DocModel) must be merged — reading mode renders the same DocModel.
- MT-012 (WYSIWYG rendering) must be merged — reading mode reuses its block renderer in a read-only branch.
- MT-013 (formatting blocks) must be merged — headings/lists/quotes/formatting must already exist so reading view can render them.
- MT-014 (embeds/node-views) and MT-015 (wikilinks) are not hard dependencies for this MT to compile, but the interop edge requires their click handlers remain wired in the read-only path when they are present; guard the calls so MT-055 does not break if a build predates them.
- WP-011 dependency (cross-WP, prose only): reuses existing WP-011 modules in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/ — accessibility/* (author_id registration + toggled state), theme/* (reading typography tokens), and the command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs pair as the shared navigation/command bus. These are already merged from WP-011 and are not WP-012 microtask dependencies.

Backend: NONE. This MT is pure frontend view-state; it binds no handshake_core API. Mode persistence uses egui's local context persistence, not the EventLedger. PostgreSQL/EventLedger only applies to backend state and is not touched here.

Risk if missed: Obsidian core 'reading view' is absent; long notes have no distraction-free rendered presentation and the parity proof suite (MT-044) cannot assert Edit|Reading parity.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: implement a heading Outline / Table-of-Contents navigator panel for the native rich-text editor (E2), giving long documents the same wayfinding surface as the Obsidian Outline core plugin and Notion's table-of-contents block. This is the rich-text analog of the MT-006 code-editor outline; the two are distinct surfaces and must not be merged — MT-006 walks code symbols from tree-sitter, MT-056 walks the MT-011 block DocModel for Heading nodes. The panel walks the in-memory DocModel, collects all Heading blocks at levels 1 through 3, and renders an indented, clickable, collapsible tree. Clicking an entry scrolls the rich-text editor viewport to the target heading block and selects that block's range via the MT-012 caret/selection model. The tree live-updates on the next frame whenever headings are added, removed, retitled, or re-leveled.

The expected diff shape is: (a) one new Rust module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/outline_panel.rs (~300-450 lines) defining the OutlinePanel egui widget, the OutlineNode tree type, the build_outline() pure function over the DocModel, and the AccessKit registration; (b) a small wiring edit inside src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/renderer/rich_editor_widget.rs so the widget exposes a scroll-to-block + select-block entry point the outline can call, and so the outline panel is mounted as a side tile next to the editor; (c) a kittest + unit test set proving outline construction, click-to-scroll-and-select, live update, and AccessKit node presence.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/outline_panel.rs
      * Define OutlineNode { block_id: String, level: u8, text: String, byte_offset: usize, children: Vec<OutlineNode>, collapsed: bool }.
      * Define pub fn build_outline(doc: &DocModel) -> Vec<OutlineNode>. This is a PURE function (no egui, no IO) so it is directly unit-testable. Iterate the DocModel block list in document order; for each block whose kind is Heading with level in 1..=3, record (block_id, level, plain_text(block), byte_offset_of_block). Then fold the flat ordered list into a nested tree by level: a heading of level N becomes a child of the most recent heading of level < N still on the stack (standard heading-stack algorithm). Headings that appear before any higher-level heading attach at the root. Byte offsets come from the DocModel block index (the same offset basis MT-012 uses for caret positioning) so the outline and the caret model agree on a single coordinate space.
      * Define pub struct OutlinePanel { roots: Vec<OutlineNode>, doc_revision: u64 } and pub fn OutlinePanel::show(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, doc: &DocModel, editor: &mut RichEditorWidget). On show(): if doc.revision() != self.doc_revision, rebuild self.roots via build_outline(doc) and store the new revision (live update path — rebuild only when the DocModel revision counter advanced, so steady-state frames are cheap). Render the tree inside an egui::ScrollArea::vertical(); each node renders at horizontal indent = (level-1) * INDENT_PX with a collapse caret (egui::collapsing or a manual triangle toggle) for nodes that have children, followed by a selectable_label showing the heading text. On click of a node label, call editor.scroll_to_block(&node.block_id) and editor.select_block(&node.block_id).
      * AccessKit: the panel container registers author_id="rich-editor-outline", role=Tree. Each rendered entry registers author_id=format!("outline.heading.{}", node.block_id), role=TreeItem, with the heading text as the accessible name and an actions=[Press] so swarm agents and accessibility tooling can invoke scroll-to-heading deterministically. The Press action handler runs the same scroll_to_block + select_block path as a mouse click.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_outline.rs (or an inline #[cfg(test)] mod in outline_panel.rs if that is the crate's existing test convention) — unit + kittest coverage listed in proof_targets.

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/renderer/rich_editor_widget.rs
      * Add (or reuse if MT-012/MT-013 already exposed it) pub fn scroll_to_block(&mut self, block_id: &str) that sets the pending scroll target so the next layout pass brings that block into view (egui ScrollArea scroll_to_rect or a stored target offset resolved during render).
      * Add (or reuse) pub fn select_block(&mut self, block_id: &str) that delegates to the MT-012 caret/selection model to place an anchored selection across the target heading block's range — do NOT implement a second independent selection mechanism; route through the existing caret model so cross-pane selection (E5) stays consistent.
      * Mount OutlinePanel as a side tile (left or right) of the editor in whatever tile/dock surface the rich editor uses — reuse the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs): register the outline as its own pane so it is addressable by the swarm pane registry, not an ad-hoc child.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/mod.rs (or the module's existing mod-declaration file) — add `pub mod outline_panel;`.

Exact crates / egui / AccessKit patterns to use:
  - egui::ScrollArea::vertical().auto_shrink([false, false]) for the panel body.
  - egui::SelectableLabel / ui.selectable_label(false, text) for clickable entries; indent via ui.horizontal(|ui| { ui.add_space(indent_px); ... }).
  - Collapse toggle: store collapsed on OutlineNode and toggle on caret click; or use egui::CollapsingHeader for nodes with children. Keep collapse state across rebuilds keyed by block_id so a live update does not reset the user's expand/collapse choices (carry forward collapsed flags by block_id when rebuilding).
  - Scroll-to: prefer egui::Ui::scroll_to_rect / Response::scroll_to_me on the target block's response in the editor, recorded by the editor's render pass when it sees a pending scroll target matching the block_id.
  - AccessKit: use the project's existing AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) for author_id + role registration — the same pattern WP-011 and the other E2 MTs use (egui's accesskit integration via Response or the project's AccessKit id registry under accessibility/). Register role=Tree on the container and role=TreeItem per entry; attach an Action::Default / Press handler that fires the scroll+select.
  - Reuse the WP-011 shell primitives: register the outline as a pane in the pane registry (pane_registry.rs); route any command (e.g. a future "Go to heading" command) through the WP-011 command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) rather than a private dispatch; allocate AccessKit ids through the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) so ids are unique and addressable.

Exact handshake_core / backend API bound: NONE. This MT is pure frontend. The outline is derived entirely from the in-memory MT-011 DocModel that already lives in the rich-text editor; there is no persistence, no document load, and no code-nav call. No PostgreSQL / EventLedger access in this MT (and there is no SQLite anywhere in the project — do not introduce any local store). If a needed DocModel accessor (block iteration order, block kind, heading level, plain-text extraction, per-block byte offset, or a document revision counter) is missing from the MT-011/MT-012/MT-013 surface, treat the gap as a TYPED BLOCKER: stop, name the exact missing accessor and the module that should own it, and escalate rather than reaching into DocModel internals or duplicating block-walk logic.

  1. Confirm the DocModel (MT-011) exposes: an ordered block iterator, per-block kind discriminant with Heading level (1..=3 minimum; ignore deeper levels for this MT), a stable block_id per block, a plain-text extractor for a block's inline content, a per-block byte_offset, and a revision/dirty counter. If any is absent, raise a typed blocker (see above) before writing outline logic.
  2. Implement build_outline() as a pure function and test it in isolation first (no egui needed).
  3. Implement OutlinePanel::show with the revision-gated rebuild and the collapse-state carry-forward.
  4. Add scroll_to_block + select_block to rich_editor_widget.rs, routing selection through the MT-012 caret model.
  5. Register AccessKit Tree / TreeItem nodes and wire the Press action to the same scroll+select path as click.
  6. Mount the panel as a WP-011-registered pane (pane_registry.rs) beside the editor.
  7. Add the test module covering the four proof targets.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: MT-011 (block DocModel) provides the heading blocks; MT-012 (caret/selection model) provides select_block and the shared coordinate/selection space; MT-013 provides the renderer surface that scroll_to_block drives. All three must be merged first. This MT blocks MT-044 (the parity + interconnection proof suite), which asserts heading-navigation parity against Obsidian/Notion.

Risk if missed: long rich-text documents have no heading-level navigation; a primary Obsidian/Notion wayfinding surface (the Outline core plugin / TOC block) is absent, and the MT-044 parity proof cannot pass.

implementation_notes: build_outline() must be a pure function over &DocModel with no egui or IO so it can be unit-tested without a render harness.

Use a heading-stack fold to build nesting: maintain a stack of (level, &mut node); for each heading, pop while stack top level >= current level, then attach under the new top (or root if empty), then push.
Gate rebuilds on a DocModel revision/dirty counter (the same counter MT-012/MT-013 use for re-layout); never rebuild the tree on every frame.

Reuse the WP-011 command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) for any outline command dispatch rather than a private dispatch path.
This is the rich-text outline; keep it distinct from the MT-006 code-editor outline — different source (DocModel headings vs tree-sitter symbols), different module, different AccessKit ids.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Add two Obsidian-core wikilink behaviors on top of the MT-015 wikilink/transclusion engine in the native (egui) rich-text editor: (1) CREATE-FROM-UNRESOLVED — clicking an unresolved `[[Title]]` link offers a 'Create note "Title"' affordance that POSTs a new knowledge document via the MT-037 backend binding and then rewrites the in-document mark from unresolved to resolved; and (2) ALIAS RESOLUTION — resolve a wikilink target not only by exact title/ref but also against a per-document `aliases` list, and surface alias matches in the MT-015 autocomplete dropdown alongside exact-title matches. This MT is pure frontend logic layered on existing panes and existing backend APIs — NO backend rewrite. Backend gaps are TYPED BLOCKERS, not new endpoints.

This MT does NOT re-implement the wikilink mark, the `[[...]]` parser, or the autocomplete UI shell — those already exist from MT-015 (E2-MT015-WikilinksTransclusion). This MT adds: a richer resolver (resolver.rs) and the alias-aware autocomplete data path (autocomplete.rs) feeding the existing MT-015 dropdown widget.

Files to CREATE (new modules under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/):
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/wikilinks/resolver.rs  — the resolution engine. Define:
      * enum WikilinkResolution { Resolved { document_id: String, matched_by: MatchKind }, Unresolved { title: String } }
      * enum MatchKind { ExactRef, ExactTitle, Alias { alias: String } }
      * struct ResolverIndex { by_title: HashMap<String, String /*doc_id*/>, by_alias: HashMap<String, String /*doc_id*/>, aliases_supported: bool }
      * fn resolve_wikilink(index: &ResolverIndex, target: &str) -> WikilinkResolution — normalize target (trim, case-insensitive per Obsidian default), check exact ref/title first, then alias map; if no match return Unresolved.
      * fn create_note_intent(title: &str) -> EditorIntent::CreateNote { title } — emit a command-bus intent (reuse the WP-011 command bus via command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) rather than calling the network inline from the click handler.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/wikilinks/autocomplete.rs  — alias-aware candidate provider. Define:
      * struct WikilinkCandidate { document_id: String, display_title: String, matched_alias: Option<String>, score: i64 }
      * fn candidates_for_query(index: &ResolverIndex, query: &str) -> Vec<WikilinkCandidate> — fuzzy-match query against both titles and aliases, dedupe by document_id (prefer the higher score; if matched by alias, set matched_alias so the dropdown can render 'Title (alias: "foo")'), sort by score desc.
      This module feeds the EXISTING MT-015 autocomplete dropdown — do not build a new dropdown widget; produce the candidate list the MT-015 widget consumes.

Files to EDIT (extend, do not rewrite):

After a successful create, mutate the mark to Resolved { document_id } so it re-renders as a live link without a full document reload.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Build ResolverIndex from data already available via the MT-038 Loom search binding. Call GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/search to enumerate candidate documents (title + id). Populate by_title. For aliases: read a per-document `aliases` field if the search/document payload exposes one (it is set via the MT-017 PropertiesPanel). If the field is ABSENT from the backend payload, set ResolverIndex.aliases_supported = false and raise the typed blocker (see step 7).
  2. Resolution order in resolve_wikilink: (a) exact ref/id match, (b) exact title match (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized), (c) alias match against by_alias. First hit wins; record MatchKind accordingly. No match => Unresolved { title }.
  3. Click activation: when the user clicks a wikilink mark, call resolve_wikilink. If Resolved, route the open through the existing MT-015 link-open path (navigate to document_id). If Unresolved, show a small inline affordance (egui button or popup) labeled 'Create note "{title}"'.
  4. Create-from-unresolved: when the operator confirms, emit EditorIntent::CreateNote { title }. The intent handler calls POST /knowledge/documents (MT-037 binding) with the title and an empty body, receives the new document_id, inserts it into ResolverIndex.by_title, and rewrites the originating mark to Resolved { document_id }. The link must become live immediately (no manual refresh).
  5. Alias autocomplete: while the user types `[[query`, the MT-015 autocomplete trigger calls candidates_for_query. Candidates matched by alias render with a secondary label (e.g. `Project Atlas — alias: "atlas"`). Selecting an alias candidate inserts the canonical `[[Title]]` (or `[[Title|displayed]]` if Obsidian alias-display syntax is in scope per MT-015) that resolves to document_id.
  6. AccessKit: the 'Create note' affordance must register an AccessKit node with a STABLE author_id of the form `wikilink-create-{hash}` where {hash} is a short stable hash of the unresolved title (so swarm agents and kittest can address it deterministically), Role::Button, actions=[Press]. Reuse the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) rather than minting ids ad hoc. Each alias autocomplete row should also carry a stable author_id (e.g. `wikilink-candidate-{document_id}`).
  7. TYPED BLOCKER (aliases gap): if the backend Loom search / knowledge document payload does NOT expose an `aliases` field, do NOT silently no-op. (a) Raise a typed blocker record in the standard WP-012 blocker channel (the packet's typed-gap mechanism) naming the missing field and the two affected APIs; (b) stub alias resolution LOCAL-ONLY: keep a process-local alias map (empty unless populated by the MT-017 PropertiesPanel in-session) so the code path is exercised and testable; (c) render a VISIBLE banner in the rich editor stating alias resolution is running local-only / backend aliases unavailable, so the operator is never misled into thinking aliases are persisted. The CREATE-FROM-UNRESOLVED half is independent of aliases and MUST still proceed fully.
  8. Reuse only — do NOT add SQLite or any local DB. All persistence is PostgreSQL/EventLedger through the existing handshake_core HTTP APIs. The local alias stub in step 7 is in-memory only and is explicitly NOT a persistence layer.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: bring Obsidian/Notion-style inline #tag authoring into the body of the native rich-text editor. Today a tag can only be assigned through the properties panel (MT-017); this MT lets the user type '#' inside prose to detect, autocomplete, insert, and render a tag inline, render it as a clickable chip that navigates to the tag hub, and converge inline tags with property tags on save so the whole product uses ONE tag identity (one tag, one hub).

Expected diff shape: (a) one new parser module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/inline_tags/parser.rs (~250-400 lines) that scans rich-text inline runs for '#tag' patterns at word boundaries and produces typed Tag tokens / Tag marks; (b) one new render+widget module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/inline_tags/inline_chip.rs (~250-350 lines) that draws a Tag mark as an inline egui chip with AccessKit metadata and emits a navigation event on click; (c) edits to the existing input handler src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/renderer/input_handler.rs that detect the '#' trigger at a word boundary, open the autocomplete menu (reusing the MT-016 slash/menu pattern, itself built on command_palette.rs + command_registry.rs), and commit the chosen tag as a Tag mark. There is also a small mod wiring file edit (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/inline_tags/mod.rs — create) and the rich_text module declaration (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/mod.rs — add `pub mod inline_tags;` if not already present).

Exact files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/inline_tags/mod.rs  -- declares `pub mod parser;` and `pub mod inline_chip;`; re-exports the public types (Tag, TagToken, parse_inline_tags, InlineTagChip, TagActivated).
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/inline_tags/parser.rs  -- pure parsing/detection logic, NO egui dependency so it is cheaply unit-testable.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/inline_tags/inline_chip.rs  -- egui widget for rendering one Tag mark as a chip + AccessKit + click->TagActivated.

Exact files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/renderer/input_handler.rs  -- add the '#' trigger detection + autocomplete + commit path.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/mod.rs  -- add `pub mod inline_tags;` (only if the submodule is not already declared).

Parser design (parser.rs):
  1. Define `Tag { name: String }` where `name` is the normalized tag string WITHOUT the leading '#' (e.g. '#rust' -> name='rust'). Normalize: trim, lowercase is NOT applied automatically (preserve author casing for display) but the canonical key used for edge identity and convergence MUST match MT-017 property-tag normalization exactly -- reuse the existing normalization fn from the MT-017 tag model rather than re-implementing it; if MT-017 exposes `normalize_tag(&str) -> String`, call it. If no such fn is exported, that is a typed blocker (see binds_backend_api / implementation_notes).
  2. Define `TagToken { byte_range: Range<usize>, tag: Tag }` -- the span in the source paragraph text covered by the '#tag' literal (INCLUDING the leading '#').
  3. Implement `parse_inline_tags(text: &str) -> Vec<TagToken>`: scan the text; a tag begins only at a WORD BOUNDARY -- i.e. the '#' is at byte offset 0 OR the byte immediately before it is whitespace or a non-word punctuation boundary. Reject mid-word '#': e.g. 'C#' must NOT produce a tag because '#' is preceded by a word char 'C'. The tag body after '#' matches the Obsidian tag charset: ASCII letters, digits, '_', '-', and '/' (for nested tags like #area/sub); the tag ends at the first char not in that set. A bare '#' with no valid body char following is NOT a tag. Empty body ('# foo') is NOT a tag.
  4. Keep parser.rs free of egui/AccessKit imports so its tests are fast and headless.

Inline chip widget (inline_chip.rs):
  5. Define `InlineTagChip<'a> { tag: &'a Tag }` implementing an egui draw fn `show(self, ui: &mut egui::Ui) -> InlineTagResponse` (do NOT implement egui::Widget if the editor renders inline runs manually -- match the inline-run rendering approach already used by the rich-text renderer; follow MT-012's inline mark rendering pattern). Render the chip as a rounded, tinted background pill containing the text '#'+tag.name, sized to fit the inline text run baseline so it flows with surrounding prose.
  6. The chip is clickable: on click (primary button release inside the chip rect), return/emit `TagActivated { tag: Tag }`. Define `TagActivated { tag: Tag }` as the navigation event. The editor forwards TagActivated onto the WP-011 navigation/command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) so the tag hub opens -- DO NOT open a window directly from the chip; emit the event and let the host route it (mirrors how wikilinks emit a navigation request rather than navigating themselves).
  7. AccessKit: every rendered chip MUST register an AccessKit node with author_id = format!("inline-tag-{}", tag.name), role = Role::Link, and an action that triggers TagActivated so swarm agents can click it deterministically. Use the WP-011 AccessKit id registry helper from the accessibility module (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/registry.rs) to register the id (do not hand-roll an AccessKit tree).

Input handler / autocomplete (input_handler.rs):
  8. On every text-input frame, after the existing key handling, inspect the text immediately left of the caret. If the user just typed '#' AND that '#' is at a word boundary (offset 0 or preceded by whitespace), open the tag autocomplete menu. Reuse the MT-016 menu component (the same popup the slash command / wikilink autocomplete uses) -- pass it the tag list as its item source. Do NOT build a second bespoke popup.
  9. Tag list source: load existing tags via the MT-023 tag-hub view source: GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/views/all?content_type=tag_hub. Map each returned tag_hub row to an autocomplete item (display '#'+name). Cache the list for the open session; refresh on menu open. Filter the list live as the user types the body after '#'. Always allow committing a NEW tag that is not yet in the list (free-typed tag), because authoring a tag in the body is a valid create path.
 10. Commit: when the user selects an item or types a valid tag body and presses the menu's confirm key (Enter/Tab, matching MT-016), replace the '#'+typed-body literal in the buffer with a committed Tag mark spanning that range, then close the menu and place the caret after the chip. The Tag mark carries the normalized tag identity from step 1.
 11. Convergence (one tag, one hub): inline Tag marks and MT-017 property-panel tags MUST resolve to the same tag identity and the same hub. On document COMMIT/save, the set of distinct inline tag identities is unioned with the property-panel tag set and persisted as loom edges of edge_type='tag' via POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/edges (one edge per distinct tag, deduped by normalized identity). A tag that already exists as a property tag MUST NOT create a duplicate edge. This is what makes inline #tags index into the SAME tag system as property tags so clicking either lands on the same tag hub (MT-023).

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-011 (rich-text editor pane exists) merged.
  - MT-012 (inline marks / inline run rendering model) merged -- the Tag mark is a new inline mark variant that reuses MT-012's mark rendering pipeline.
  - MT-015 (caret / text-input + buffer mutation surface) merged -- needed for caret-relative trigger detection and range replacement.
  - MT-023 (tag hub + tag_hub loom view + navigation to hub) merged -- supplies the tag list source and the hub the chip navigates to.
  - WP-011 shell primitives reused (real modules under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/): pane registry (pane_registry.rs), command/navigation bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs), AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs), tag-hub navigation surface (loom_graph.rs). PostgreSQL/EventLedger only -- no SQLite anywhere. No backend rewrite: bind the existing handshake_core loom view + edges APIs; any missing endpoint or missing normalize_tag export is a TYPED BLOCKER, not a backend change made here.

Risk if missed: inline #tag authoring and inline tag navigation are absent; users can only set tags from the properties panel, never from the note body, breaking Obsidian/Notion parity and fragmenting tag identity (body tags vs property tags) so MT-044 parity proof cannot pass.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: replace the raw-text wiki projection rendering that was explicitly DEFERRED in MT-025 with proper markdown rendering. MT-025 (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/wiki_page_panel.rs, implementation_notes line: 'Rendered content is plain text for now — do not implement markdown rendering in this MT. Use egui::Label with wrap=true inside a ScrollArea') shipped the read-only wiki view as a single raw egui::Label that prints the LoomWikiProjection.rendered_content string verbatim, so a page whose content is '# Title\n- item' shows the literal hash and dash characters instead of a formatted heading and bullet. This MT resolves that deferral: the read-only view must parse rendered_content as CommonMark and render headings, lists, tables, blockquotes, fenced code blocks, and links using the SAME egui primitives as the MT-012 block renderer, by extracting a SHARED markdown-to-blocks adapter that both surfaces call. The edit overlay is unchanged — it still binds the raw markdown string into the multiline TextEdit (wiki.edit-area.{projection_id}); only the read-only (edit_mode=false) view becomes formatted. This is a read-side-only change: NO backend change, NO new endpoint, NO write-path change. It binds the SAME existing GET endpoint MT-025 already calls and renders the rendered_content field it already returns.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/markdown_render.rs — a SHARED markdown-to-blocks adapter. This is the single rendering path that wiki pages, reading mode (MT-055), and the rich editor all reuse (see interop_edge). It exposes two layers:
      (1) a parse layer: `pub fn parse_markdown(src: &str) -> Vec<MdBlock>` that runs CommonMark over `src` and returns a flat-ish block sequence. Use the `pulldown-cmark` crate (^0.11, pure Rust, MIT/Apache-2.0, the de-facto Rust CommonMark parser; enable the `tables` GFM extension via `pulldown_cmark::Options::ENABLE_TABLES`, and ENABLE_STRIKETHROUGH). Iterate `pulldown_cmark::Parser::new_ext(src, opts)` events (Start(Tag)/End(TagEnd)/Text/Code/SoftBreak/HardBreak/Rule) and fold them into `MdBlock` values. `MdBlock` is an enum: Heading { level: u8, spans: Vec<MdSpan> } | Paragraph { spans: Vec<MdSpan> } | BulletList { items: Vec<Vec<MdBlock>> } | OrderedList { start: u64, items: Vec<Vec<MdBlock>> } | Quote { children: Vec<MdBlock> } | CodeBlock { lang: Option<String>, code: String } | Table { headers: Vec<Vec<MdSpan>>, rows: Vec<Vec<Vec<MdSpan>>> } | Rule. `MdSpan` is { text: String, bold: bool, italic: bool, code: bool, strikethrough: bool, link: Option<String> }.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Extend the existing MT-021 Loom graph view (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs, the LoomGraphView widget) with an Obsidian-class control panel so the graph becomes usable at scale and reaches Obsidian graph parity. Today only Local/Global mode toggle plus pan/zoom exist (delivered by MT-021); there is no filtering, no grouping, no depth control, no orphan handling, and no degree-based sizing. This MT adds all of those as a dedicated, collapsible side control panel rendered alongside the canvas, plus the wiring inside the existing widget to apply those controls to the loaded node/edge set. The expected diff shape is: (a) ONE NEW file src/frontend/handshake_native/src/graph/graph_controls.rs containing a GraphControls state struct and its egui panel renderer plus the pure filter/group/sizing functions that operate over the in-memory graph; (b) EDITS to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs to own a GraphControls field, call the control panel each frame, apply the computed visibility/color/size results in the existing painter pass, and re-fire the backend graph-search query when the link-depth slider changes in Local mode; (c) EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs to add `pub mod graph;` (and the graph module's own mod.rs / `pub mod graph_controls;`) and re-export GraphControls.

Scope boundary: this MT does NOT add any new backend endpoint. It reuses the SINGLE existing endpoint already bound by MT-021: GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/graph-search?q=&limit=&backlink_depth= . The depth slider changes only the backlink_depth query parameter and re-fires that same endpoint; every other control (text/search filter, group color, orphan toggle, degree sizing) operates purely client-side over the already-loaded Vec<GraphNode>/Vec<GraphEdge> and fires no network call. All persistent graph data continues to come from the real PostgreSQL/EventLedger backend via handshake_core; node positions remain ephemeral UI state per MT-021.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: extend the native egui Loom canvas built in MT-026 to full Obsidian-Canvas card parity. MT-026 delivered a draggable/zoomable canvas surface (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/canvas_board.rs) that renders placement cards over an infinite pan/zoom viewport, mutates state through the handshake_core canvas API, and refreshes via the mutate-then-getCanvasBoard cycle. This MT adds the three Obsidian-Canvas features still missing: (1) drag-resize handles on placement cards that persist a new width/height; (2) labeled section/group FRAMES rendered as titled rounded-rectangle containers that cards can be dropped into, promoting the abstract group_id into a visible named frame; (3) in-place editing of free-text card title/body directly on the canvas, persisted through the text-card endpoint. Reference (not copy) semantics for block-backed cards are preserved throughout: resizing, sectioning, or moving a block card NEVER duplicates the underlying loom block; it only mutates the placement record.

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/canvas_board.rs  — the MT-026 canvas. Add the resize-handle interaction layer and the in-place text-card editor. Wire both into the existing mutate-then-getCanvasBoard refresh cycle. Add the AccessKit registrations for resize handles and for section frames.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/canvas_sections.rs  — new module that owns section/group frame rendering and hit-testing. Defines SectionFrame { id: String, label: String, rect: egui::Rect, color: egui::Color32 }; a SectionLayer that derives frames from the placements' group_id values returned by getCanvasBoard (one frame per distinct group_id, with the group label and bounding rect computed from member cards or from a stored frame geometry if the board payload carries one); and hit-testing helpers (which_section(pos) -> Option<group_id>) used during drag-drop to assign a dropped card to a section. Add `pub mod canvas_sections;` to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs (the crate module-declaration file; there is no loom/ subdir — canvas modules are flat under handshake_native::).

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. RESIZE HANDLES (canvas_board.rs):
     a. For each rendered placement card, after drawing the card body, draw a small grab handle in the bottom-right corner (an egui::Rect of ~12x12 logical px, scaled by the current canvas zoom). Use ui.interact(handle_rect, handle_id, egui::Sense::drag()) to get a Response.
     b. handle_id = egui::Id::new(("canvas.placement.resize", &placement.id)) so it is stable per placement.
     c. On response.dragged(): accumulate response.drag_delta() into the card's in-flight width/height (convert screen delta to canvas-space delta by dividing by zoom). Clamp to a minimum card size (e.g. 80x48 canvas units). Render the card live at the in-flight size so the resize is visually immediate.
     d. On response.drag_stopped(): commit by calling updateCanvasPlacement (PATCH endpoint, see binds_backend_api) with the final {w, h}. Debounce: only one PATCH per drag-stop (do not PATCH every frame during the drag). After the PATCH resolves, run the standard getCanvasBoard refresh so server-truth geometry replaces the optimistic local value.
     e. Mouse cursor: set ui.output_mut(|o| o.cursor_icon = egui::CursorIcon::ResizeNwSe) while hovering the handle.
  2. SECTION / GROUP FRAMES (canvas_sections.rs + canvas_board.rs):
     a. After fetching the board, build the SectionLayer: group placements by their group_id; for each distinct non-null group_id, compute the frame rect (union of member card rects, padded; or use frame geometry if the payload provides it) and read the section label (from the board payload's section/group metadata; if absent, fall back to the group_id string).
     b. Render section frames BEHIND the cards (draw frames first, then cards on top) as titled rounded rectangles: ui.painter().rect_filled with a translucent fill, ui.painter().rect_stroke for the border, and a title label painted at the top-left of the frame. Use a per-section color.
     c. Register an AccessKit node per frame with author_id format "canvas.section.{id}" (id = group_id), role = egui's container/group role, and the section label as the accessible name.
     d. Drag-drop assignment: during a card-move drag (the existing MT-026 move interaction), on drag_stopped call SectionLayer::which_section(drop_pos). If the drop falls inside a section frame, include that section/group_id in the updateCanvasPlacement PATCH (section/group assignment field). If the drop is outside all frames, send a null/clear group assignment. This reuses the SAME PATCH endpoint as resize.
     e. Editing a section's title is OUT OF SCOPE for this MT unless trivially free; the focus is creating/assigning frames from existing group_id, not a section-CRUD UI.
  3. IN-PLACE TEXT-CARD EDITING (canvas_board.rs):
     a. Free-text cards (cards whose backing is a text card, NOT a block reference) get an inline editor. On double-click of a text card (response.double_clicked()), switch that card into edit mode: render an egui::TextEdit::multiline bound to a local editing buffer instead of the static label, sized to the card rect.
     b. Track editing state per card: editing_card_id: Option<String> on the canvas struct. Only one card edits at a time.
     c. On commit (focus lost OR Ctrl+Enter), call the text-card create/edit endpoint (POST .../cards, see binds_backend_api) with the new title/body, then refresh via getCanvasBoard. On Escape, discard the buffer and exit edit mode without a server call.
     d. Block-backed cards are NOT inline-editable on the canvas (editing the block content happens in its own editor pane); double-clicking a block card opens/navigates to the block, it does not turn into a text editor. Guard the inline editor strictly to text cards to preserve reference semantics.
  4. REFERENCE-NOT-COPY INVARIANT: none of the three features may duplicate a loom block. Resize and section-assignment only mutate the placement record; text editing only mutates the text card's own content. Add a debug assertion / test that resizing or sectioning a block-backed card does not change the set of underlying block_ids on the board.
  5. AccessKit ids to register this MT: "canvas.section.{id}" for each section frame, and "canvas.placement.{id}.resize" for each card's resize handle. These extend (do not replace) the MT-026 canvas AccessKit ids (e.g. "canvas.placement.{id}").

React reference: app/src/components/LoomCanvasBoard.tsx — port the card geometry model (x/y/w/h placement record), the group/section concept, and the free-text card body editing. The React board persisted resize and section changes through the same canvas placement update path; mirror that contract in Rust against handshake_core.

Backend binding: bind the EXISTING handshake_core canvas APIs only — do NOT add or rewrite backend endpoints. Use PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/canvas/placements/{placement_id} for both resize (w/h) and section/group assignment, and POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/canvas/{canvas_block_id}/cards for text-card create/edit. If either endpoint lacks a field this MT needs (e.g. the PATCH body has no w/h or no group_id field, or the cards endpoint cannot edit an existing card), STOP and emit a typed blocker describing the exact missing field/route rather than rewriting the backend. PostgreSQL/EventLedger is the only persistence path — no SQLite anywhere. Reuse the WP-011 shell primitives: the command bus is command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs and the AccessKit id registry is accessibility/registry.rs (with accessibility/snapshot.rs and accessibility/live.rs); pane integration uses pane_registry.rs. Do not invent parallel infrastructure.

Dependencies/unblock conditions: MT-026 (native canvas board: draggable cards, pan/zoom, mutate-then-getCanvasBoard refresh, AccessKit "canvas.placement.{id}") must be merged first — this MT extends that module in place.
Risk if missed: the canvas falls short of Obsidian Canvas parity — cards stay fixed-size, groups remain invisible abstractions, and free-text cards cannot be edited on the canvas. This also blocks MT-044, which depends on the resize/section/inline-edit surface being present.
acceptance_criteria: AC-061-1: Dragging a card's bottom-right resize handle changes the card's rendered width/height live, and on drag-stop issues exactly one debounced updateCanvasPlacement (PATCH) carrying the final {w, h}; after the PATCH the board re-fetches via getCanvasBoard so server geometry is authoritative — proven by cargo test asserting the queued PATCH count == 1 per drag and the body carries the resized w/h.

AC-061-2: Distinct non-null group_id values from the board render as titled section/group FRAMES (translucent rounded rectangles with a visible label) drawn behind the cards — proven by kittest screenshot/AccessKit dump showing a 'canvas.section.{id}' node with the section label.
