original_scope.summary:
Goal: Add an 'Outgoing Links' pane (egui + AccessKit, native) for the currently active rich document / loom block. The pane lists every link emanating FROM the active document — both wikilinks (`[[target]]` / `[[target|alias]]`) and transclusions (`![[target]]` embeds) — parsed from the document's DocModel / `content_json`. Entries are split into two buckets, Resolved and Unresolved (dangling), and every entry is clickable: clicking navigates to the link target via the shell navigation seam (the MT-030 navigation bus reused through the WP-011 command/event bus: command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs). This completes the Obsidian 'links triad' for the native knowledge surface: backlinks (MT-015 — links INTO this doc) + unlinked mentions (MT-024 — text mentions not yet linked) + outgoing links (this MT — links OUT of this doc).

File to CREATE:
  - `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph/outgoing_links_panel.rs` (~250-400 lines) — defines `OutgoingLinksPanel` egui widget struct plus the pure link-extraction function and the resolved/unresolved bucketing. This is the only new source file. It is created as a new module under the existing loom surface (`src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs`, promoted to the `loom_graph/` subdir module form) so it can reuse the same backend-client wiring (backend_client.rs) and pane-registry registration patterns (pane_registry.rs) the loom surface already uses.

File to EDIT:
  - `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom_graph.rs` — declare the new submodule (`pub mod outgoing_links_panel;`) and export `OutgoingLinksPanel`; register the pane into the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs) under a stable pane id (e.g. `"loom.outgoing_links"`) so the shell can dock/show it.

State / data model:
  - `OutgoingLinksPanel { active_document_id: Option<String>, active_block_id: Option<String>, resolved: Vec<OutgoingLink>, unresolved: Vec<OutgoingLink>, loading: bool, error: Option<String> }`.
  - `OutgoingLink { raw: String, target_value: String, alias: Option<String>, kind: LinkKind, resolved_target_id: Option<String> }` where `LinkKind = Wikilink | Transclusion`.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Link extraction is a PURE function: `pub fn extract_outgoing_links(content_json: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<OutgoingLink>`. Walk the `content_json` DocModel tree (the same prosemirror-style JSON the rich editor stores). Reuse the MT-015 wikilink parser — DO NOT re-implement regex parsing here. Import the parser exposed by the MT-015 wikilinks module (the WP-012 rich-text wikilinks module created by MT-015 at `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/wikilinks/**`); call its parse entrypoint over text nodes and any dedicated wikilink/transclusion mark or node types. Port the React extraction logic from `app/src/components/RichDocumentView.tsx` (which collects links during render) and the parse semantics from `app/src/lib/editor/wikilink.ts` (`[[ ]]` vs `![[ ]]`, alias split on `|`, target normalization). De-duplicate identical (kind, target_value) pairs but keep first occurrence's alias.
  2. Resolution: for each extracted link, resolve `target_value` to a real id. Use the bound backend APIs (NONE new — reuse via MT-037 knowledge_documents binding and the loom block API): call `GET /knowledge/documents/{document_id}` to read the active document's `content_json` (source of links), and resolve each wikilink/transclusion target against the loom block / document namespace via `GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id}` (resolve targets) — i.e. look up whether the target name maps to a live block/document. If resolution returns a live id, push to `resolved` with `resolved_target_id = Some(id)`; otherwise push to `unresolved` with `resolved_target_id = None`. Batch resolution where the loom search/lookup API allows; never block the egui frame — do resolution off the render path and store results in the panel struct (set `loading=true` while in flight).
  3. Rendering: `impl OutgoingLinksPanel { pub fn show(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, on_open: &mut dyn FnMut(NavTarget)) }`. Header label 'Outgoing Links'. If `loading`, show a spinner; if `error.is_some()`, show the error text. Render two collapsible sections: 'Resolved (N)' and 'Unresolved (N)'. Each resolved entry is an `egui` selectable/button row showing the alias-or-target text plus a small kind glyph (link vs embed); on click, invoke `on_open(NavTarget::block(resolved_target_id))` which routes through the shell navigation seam. Each unresolved entry renders dimmed (non-navigable target, but still clickable to offer 'create note' future hook — for THIS MT just fire `on_open(NavTarget::unresolved(target_value))` so the bus decides). If both buckets are empty, render the exact text 'No outgoing links' (no panic, no spinner).
  4. Navigation bus: do NOT create a new navigation channel. Reuse the MT-030 navigation seam wired over the WP-011 command/event bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs). The `on_open` closure passed into `show` is the seam the shell wires to the navigation bus so an outgoing-link click lands in the correct editor/pane (MT-030 interop edge). Keep `OutgoingLinksPanel` decoupled from the bus concrete type via the `FnMut(NavTarget)` callback.
  5. AccessKit: every resolved entry node gets `author_id = "outgoing.resolved.{resolved_target_id}"`, role = ListItem (or Button), action Press. Every unresolved entry gets `author_id = "outgoing.unresolved.{target_value}"`, role = ListItem. The two section containers get stable container ids (e.g. `"outgoing.section.resolved"`, `"outgoing.section.unresolved"`). Register all ids through the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs), never ad-hoc, so swarm agents can address rows deterministically.
  6. Reuse WP-011 shell primitives: pane registry (pane_registry.rs — register `loom.outgoing_links`), command/event bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs — the navigation seam), and the AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs — entry ids). Do not duplicate any of those substrates.

Backend API bound (REUSE ONLY — no new endpoints, no backend rewrite): `GET /knowledge/documents/{document_id}` (read `content_json` — the source of outgoing links) and `GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/loom/blocks/{block_id}` (resolve link targets to live block ids). Both are existing handshake_core APIs already bound by MT-037 (knowledge documents) and the loom block client used by MT-024, both reached through the native `backend_client.rs`. If a needed resolution capability is genuinely absent from the existing API surface, STOP and raise a typed blocker (do not add or rewrite backend endpoints; PostgreSQL/EventLedger only, no SQLite anywhere).

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-015 (wikilinks + transclusion parser) MUST be merged — this MT imports its parser (`src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/wikilinks/**`); re-implementing parsing is forbidden.
  - MT-024 (loom sidebar pins/favorites/backlinks/unlinked) MUST be merged — establishes the loom-surface backend-client wiring (backend_client.rs) and pane patterns this pane reuses on the `loom_graph` surface.
  - MT-037 (knowledge documents API binding) MUST be merged — provides the typed `GET /knowledge/documents/{document_id}` client (over backend_client.rs) used to read `content_json`.
  - MT-030 navigation bus must exist (transitively via MT-024 / WP-011 shell command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) for the `on_open` seam.

Risk if missed: The Obsidian links triad (backlinks + outgoing + unlinked mentions) stays incomplete — users can see what links INTO a note (backlinks) and unlinked text mentions, but cannot see what a note links OUT to. This blocks MT-044 (the triad integration / parity proof) and breaks Obsidian navigation parity.

Keep `extract_outgoing_links` pure and side-effect-free (no I/O, no async) so it is trivially unit-testable; resolution (which needs backend lookups) is a separate step that consumes the pure extraction output.
De-duplicate on (kind, normalized target_value) but preserve the first alias seen; Obsidian shows each distinct outgoing target once.

Resolution must run off the egui render path: set `loading=true`, perform the lookups async (or via the existing loom backend-client request mechanism in backend_client.rs used by MT-024), then store `resolved`/`unresolved` on the struct; never block the frame thread.

Pass navigation out via a `&mut dyn FnMut(NavTarget)` closure so the panel is decoupled from the concrete MT-030 navigation bus type; the shell wires the closure to the command/event bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs).

Unresolved (dangling) entries render dimmed but remain present and addressable; clicking them still fires `on_open` so the bus can decide a fallback (e.g. future create-note flow) — do not silently drop dangling links.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: make the native editors CONSUME the FEMS retrieval capsule (the MemoryPack from Pillar 12) so that relevant project memory surfaces inline while a model or operator is editing a document. This MT is read-only consumption: it adds (a) a typed Rust client to the EXISTING handshake_core FEMS read API and (b) a 'Relevant Memory' side panel that requests a MemoryPack keyed on the active document/selection context and renders provenance-first items, each of which links back to its source through the E5 shared navigation bus. There is NO backend build in this MT — bind the existing handshake_core FEMS read endpoint; if no FEMS read endpoint exists, raise a TYPED BLOCKER and render an empty-state banner. PostgreSQL/EventLedger is the only backing store on the backend side (no SQLite anywhere); this MT does not touch the store directly — it only consumes via the API.

What a MemoryPack is (Pillar 12 contract the client must model): a retrieval capsule bounded to <=500 tokens total and <=24 items, where each item is one of three kinds — episodic (what happened: events, prior sessions, edits), semantic (durable facts/concepts), or procedural (how-to steps, recipes, workflows). Each item is provenance-first: it carries a human-readable summary AND a machine source reference (e.g. a loom:// or atelier:// URI, a document id + range, or an event id) that the navigation bus can resolve to a concrete editor target. The client MUST enforce the <=24-item cap defensively even if the server returns more (truncate + log), and MUST treat the token budget as advisory metadata it surfaces, not something it recomputes.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/memory_client.rs  (~250-350 lines) — defines the typed read client and the deserialized MemoryPack model. Define:
      * enum MemoryKind { Episodic, Semantic, Procedural } (derive Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Deserialize with #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]).
      * struct MemorySource { uri: Option<String>, document_id: Option<String>, byte_range: Option<(usize, usize)>, event_id: Option<String> } — the provenance reference; at least one field must be present for an item to be navigable (enforce in a validate() method; non-navigable items render but disable the source link).
      * struct MemoryItem { id: String, kind: MemoryKind, summary: String, source: MemorySource, score: Option<f32> }.
      * struct MemoryPack { items: Vec<MemoryItem>, token_estimate: Option<u32>, truncated: bool, context_key: String }.
      * struct MemoryClient { base: ApiClient } where ApiClient is the EXISTING shared backend HTTP/core client already used by other E* MTs — the real module is src/frontend/handshake_native/src/backend_client.rs (reuse it; do NOT create a second HTTP stack). Add async fn fetch_pack(&self, workspace_id: &str, context: &MemoryContext) -> Result<MemoryPack, MemoryClientError>.
      * struct MemoryContext { workspace_id: String, document_id: Option<String>, selection_text: Option<String>, cursor_byte: Option<usize> } — built from the active editor pane's focus + SharedSelection (from the MT-031 shared interaction bus — provided by the real WP-011 modules src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs).
      * enum MemoryClientError { EndpointMissing, Http(StatusCode-or-equivalent), Decode(String), OverCap { returned: usize } } — EndpointMissing is the TYPED BLOCKER variant: it is returned when the FEMS read route is absent (404 on the documented path, or feature-not-present sentinel). The panel maps EndpointMissing to the empty-state banner; it must NOT panic and must NOT silently no-op.
      * fetch_pack MUST clamp items to 24 after decode (truncate, set truncated=true, log a warning) so the <=24 cap holds regardless of server behavior.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/relevant_memory_panel.rs  (~250-350 lines) — defines RelevantMemoryPanel, an egui side panel widget. Define:
      * struct RelevantMemoryPanel { client: MemoryClient, last_context: Option<MemoryContext>, current: Option<MemoryPack>, in_flight: bool, blocker: Option<MemoryClientError> }.
      * fn show(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, nav_bus: &NavigationBus) — renders the panel.
      * fn refresh_for_context(&mut self, ctx: MemoryContext) — debounced trigger that requests a new pack when the active document/selection context changes (compare against last_context; skip if unchanged).
      * Rendering: group items by MemoryKind (Episodic / Semantic / Procedural section headers), and within each section render each item as a row: the summary text, a small kind badge, and a 'Go to source' link button. Provenance-first means the source affordance is always visible; clicking it builds a navigation target from MemorySource and calls nav_bus.navigate_to(target) (the E5 shared navigation bus from MT-037, built on the real WP-011 shared bus modules src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs).
      * Empty-state / blocker: when blocker == Some(EndpointMissing), render a calm empty-state banner ('Relevant Memory unavailable — FEMS read endpoint not present in this build') instead of the list, and surface the typed blocker upward so the WP validator sees it. When the pack is present but items is empty, render a neutral 'No relevant memory for this context' state.

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/mod.rs  — add `pub mod memory_client;` and `pub mod relevant_memory_panel;` (create the mod.rs / fems dir if E* prior MTs have not; if the fems module does not yet exist, create src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/mod.rs declaring both submodules and re-exporting the public types).
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs — add `pub mod fems;` so the new module is part of the handshake_native crate.
  - pane-registry wiring (reuse the WP-011 pane registry from src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs and the shared command bus from src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs, wired in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs): register RelevantMemoryPanel as a dockable pane so it can be opened alongside the active editor. Use the existing pane registry API; do NOT invent a new docking system. Subscribe the panel to focus/selection changes via the MT-031 interaction bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) so refresh_for_context fires on context change.

Exact crates / egui / AccessKit patterns:
  - Reuse the existing async runtime + HTTP/core client the other E* MTs already bind (do not add a second client). Deserialize with serde / serde_json into MemoryPack.
  - egui: render the panel inside the host pane area (the pane registry supplies the egui::Ui); group sections with egui::CollapsingHeader per MemoryKind; render each source link as egui::Button or egui::Link; show in_flight with a egui::Spinner.
  - AccessKit (reuse the WP-011 AccessKit id registry at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/registry.rs, part of the accessibility/ module): register stable author_ids so swarm agents can drive the panel — author_id="relevant-memory-panel" Role::GenericContainer on the outer frame; author_id="relevant-memory-list" Role::List on the items container; each item row author_id="mem-item-{item.id}" Role::ListItem; each source link author_id="mem-source-{item.id}" Role::Button. Pull ids through the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/registry.rs) rather than hardcoding to avoid collisions.

Exact handshake_core API bound: GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/memory/pack?context=... (the EXISTING FEMS read endpoint that returns the MemoryPack/retrieval capsule). The client serializes MemoryContext into the query (document_id, selection_text, cursor_byte) and deserializes the MemoryPack response. If this route is ABSENT in the current handshake_core build, fetch_pack returns MemoryClientError::EndpointMissing (the TYPED BLOCKER) — do NOT add the route, do NOT rewrite the backend; record the blocker and ship the empty-state path so the editor remains usable.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Confirm whether the FEMS read endpoint exists in handshake_core (search the existing API surface / route table the other E* MTs already call). If present, bind it; if absent, implement the EndpointMissing typed-blocker path and the empty-state banner, and record the blocker in the handoff.
  2. Define the MemoryPack model in memory_client.rs exactly to the Pillar 12 shape above (3 kinds, provenance-first source, <=24 items, token estimate as advisory metadata).
  3. Implement fetch_pack: build the request from MemoryContext, call the existing ApiClient, decode, then defensively clamp to 24 items (truncate + truncated=true + log).
  4. Implement RelevantMemoryPanel rendering + the navigation hand-off: build a navigation target from MemorySource (prefer uri, else document_id+byte_range, else event_id) and call the MT-037 navigation bus.
  5. Wire focus/selection -> refresh_for_context through the MT-031 interaction bus; debounce so rapid cursor moves do not spam the endpoint.
  6. Register the panel in the WP-011 pane registry (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs) + AccessKit id registry (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/registry.rs).
  7. Tests as in proof_targets — including the missing-endpoint path producing the typed blocker + banner with no panic and no silent no-op.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-011 (rich-text / document editor pane providing the active-document context) must be merged.
  - MT-031 (shared selection/clipboard/command interaction bus) must be merged — supplies the focus + SharedSelection that builds MemoryContext.
  - MT-037 (shared navigation bus) must be merged — supplies nav_bus.navigate_to for provenance source links.
  - The existing shared ApiClient / async runtime used by other E* MTs must be available to reuse.

Risk if missed: the editors would ignore the typed memory pillar (Pillar 12) entirely, and a no-context model would lose the provenance-first memory FEMS is meant to provide inline while editing — defeating the 'relevant memory surfaces where you work' invariant and blocking MT-065 and MT-074 which build on the consumed capsule.

Model the MemoryPack to Pillar 12: <=500 token budget (advisory metadata the client surfaces, never recomputes) and <=24 items (hard cap enforced client-side via defensive truncate).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: turn editor context into FEMS (Pillar 12 typed-memory system, Pillar 12) memory-write PROPOSALS that are always review-gated and NEVER directly committed by the editor. Add a 'Propose to Memory' command that operates on the current SharedSelection (any editor pane: code, rich-text, loom block, canvas). When invoked, the command builds a typed memory-write proposal carrying full source provenance, submits it to the EXISTING review-gated FEMS write path (the proposal endpoint), and emits an FR-EVT-MEM-001 (memory_write_proposed) Flight Recorder event through the MT-036 NativeEditorEventEmitter. The commit step stays operator/review-gated downstream; this MT only creates the PROPOSAL and the observability event. This is the editor entry point into the FEMS proposal->review->commit loop.

This MT is PURE FRONTEND. No backend build, no schema changes, no SQLite anywhere. It binds the EXISTING handshake_core FEMS proposal API. If the proposal endpoint does not exist on the current API surface, STOP and raise a TYPED BLOCKER (do not invent, add, or rewrite a backend endpoint; do not fall back to a direct memory commit).

File to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/memory_proposal.rs (~300-450 lines) — defines the proposal data model, the pure proposal-builder function, the typed blocker, and the egui command/dialog wiring. Lives under a new (or existing) src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/ module so all Pillar-12 editor integration is colocated. If src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/mod.rs does not yet exist, create it and add `pub mod memory_proposal;`; otherwise edit the existing src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/mod.rs to add the module declaration. Also register the module in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs (`pub mod fems;`) if fems is not already declared there.

File to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs — register the 'Propose to Memory' command into the WP-011 command registry / command bus (command_registry.rs) so it appears in the command palette and can be keybound. The command reads the live SharedSelection from the WP-011 selection/event substrate (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs), builds the proposal, and dispatches submission. Do NOT duplicate the registry/bus; reuse the existing command_registry.rs registration API and the SharedSelection that the WP-011 command/event substrate already owns. Wire the MT-036 NativeEditorEventEmitter (already wired through event_bus.rs per MT-036) to emit the FR event after a successful proposal submission.

Proposal data model (in memory_proposal.rs):
  pub enum MemoryClass { Episodic, Semantic, Procedural }
  pub struct MemorySourceProvenance { document_id: String, selection_start: usize, selection_end: usize, content_hash: String, pane_id: String, workspace_id: String }
  pub struct MemoryWriteProposal { class: MemoryClass, content: String, source: MemorySourceProvenance, review_gated: bool, actor_id: String }
  pub enum MemoryProposalError { MissingEndpoint, NoSelection, SubmitFailed(String) }  // MissingEndpoint == the TYPED BLOCKER

Pure proposal-builder (trivially unit-testable, no I/O):
  pub fn build_proposal(sel: &SharedSelection, class: MemoryClass, workspace_id: &str, actor_id: &str) -> Result<MemoryWriteProposal, MemoryProposalError>
  - Reads document_id, selection start/end byte offsets, pane_id, and the selected text from the SharedSelection variant (TextRange { pane_id, start, end, text } per MT-031; BlockRef / NodeRef variants resolve their document_id and use a whole-block/whole-node range). Returns MemoryProposalError::NoSelection if SharedSelection is None.
  - content_hash: compute a stable SHA-256 (or the same hashing primitive MT-032 / the loom content_hash uses — reuse the loom_graph.rs content-hash primitive, do not introduce a second hashing scheme) over the exact selected content; store as lowercase hex in MemorySourceProvenance.content_hash.
  - review_gated: ALWAYS true for Procedural class (spec requires procedural-class proposals to be review-gated); for Episodic/Semantic default to true as well (commit is never editor-direct). Never set review_gated=false from the editor.

Submission (off the egui frame thread, same pattern as MT-036 emit):
  pub async fn submit_proposal(proposal: &MemoryWriteProposal, client: &HandshakeCoreClient) -> Result<ProposalAck, MemoryProposalError>
  - POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/memory/proposals with the typed proposal body (existing review-gated FEMS write path). On 404 / route-absent / capability-missing, return MemoryProposalError::MissingEndpoint — this is the TYPED BLOCKER the coder surfaces; do NOT silently commit or fall back to any direct memory-write route.
  - On success, parse ProposalAck { proposal_id, status } and trigger the FR event emit.

FR event (reuse MT-036 emitter; do NOT build a new emitter):
  - After a successful submit, emit a NativeEditorEvent through the MT-036 NativeEditorEventEmitter (wired via event_bus.rs) whose action maps to FR-EVT-MEM-001 (memory_write_proposed). The payload carries: { action: 'memory_write_proposed', proposal_id, class, document_id, selection_start, selection_end, content_hash, review_gated, pane_id }. The event_type stays 'system' and schema stays the closed FR schema per MT-036 (do NOT invent a new event_type; embed the native_editor payload as MT-036 specifies). FR-EVT-MEM-001 is the stable event-name marker carried in the payload action, not a new ledger schema.

egui command / dialog wiring:
  - Register CommandDescriptor { id: 'fems.propose_to_memory', label: 'Propose to Memory', keybind: None (palette-driven; do not steal a VS Code binding), handler } into the WP-011 command registry via command_registry.rs (the same registration API that backs command_palette.rs).
  - The handler reads the live SharedSelection from the WP-011 command/event substrate (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs), opens a small egui confirmation dialog letting the operator pick MemoryClass (Episodic/Semantic/Procedural radio) and preview the selected content + computed content_hash, then on confirm fires submit_proposal off-thread.
  - AccessKit: command palette entry already covered by MT-031 (author_id 'cmd-fems.propose_to_memory' via the cmd-{id} convention). The dialog gets author_id 'fems-propose-dialog' role Dialog; the class radios get author_id 'fems-class-{episodic|semantic|procedural}' role RadioButton; the confirm button gets author_id 'fems-propose-confirm' role Button. Register all ids through the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs), never ad-hoc.

Reuse WP-011 shell primitives: command registry / command palette (command_registry.rs + command_palette.rs — register the command), the WP-011 command/event substrate that owns SharedSelection (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs), and the AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs for the dialog + radio + button ids). Reuse the MT-036 NativeEditorEventEmitter (wired via event_bus.rs) for the FR event. Reuse the MT-037 knowledge_documents client wiring / HandshakeCoreClient (built on backend_client.rs) for the HTTP call. Do not duplicate any of those substrates.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Create src/frontend/handshake_native/src/fems/memory_proposal.rs with the data model, build_proposal (pure), submit_proposal (async), and the dialog/command wiring.
  2. Make build_proposal pure and side-effect-free so it is trivially unit-testable; submission and FR emit are separate steps that consume its output.
  3. content_hash MUST reuse the loom/MT-032 content-hash primitive in loom_graph.rs (same algorithm, same hex encoding) so a proposal's hash matches the document's block hash for the same content; do not introduce a second hashing scheme.
  4. review_gated is hard-set true for Procedural and never settable to false from the editor; assert this in a unit test.
  5. submit_proposal runs off the egui frame thread (tokio::spawn or the same async mechanism MT-036 uses); never block the frame.
  6. On MissingEndpoint, surface the typed blocker to the coder/validator (return the typed error, log to the MT-036 in-memory error ring, and do NOT commit anything). The absence of the proposal endpoint is a BLOCKER, not a reason to write memory directly.
  7. After a successful ack, emit FR-EVT-MEM-001 via the MT-036 emitter; if the emit fails it must not crash the frame (MT-036 error-ring behavior).
  8. Tests: (a) unit build_proposal sets class + full source provenance (document_id, selection_start/end, content_hash, pane_id) correctly from a TextRange selection; (b) unit Procedural-class proposal has review_gated=true and is never auto-committed (no direct-commit code path exists); (c) integration (real PG): invoking 'Propose to Memory' on a selection creates a proposal record via the FEMS proposal endpoint AND an FR-EVT-MEM-001 (memory_write_proposed) event appears in the flight-recorder ledger; (d) unit missing-endpoint path returns MemoryProposalError::MissingEndpoint (the typed blocker) and performs no commit and no silent fallback.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - WP-011 command/event substrate (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs, owning the command bus + SharedSelection) MUST be present — the command registers into command_registry.rs and reads SharedSelection from the WP-011 substrate. This is a cross-WP dependency on the WP-011 native shell, not an intra-WP MT dependency.
  - MT-031 (CommandBus + SharedSelection editor binding) MUST be merged — the command registers into the command registry and reads SharedSelection. (MT-031 is delivered against the WP-011 substrate; see implementation_notes for the cross-WP relationship.)
  - MT-036 (NativeEditorEventEmitter + FR runtime_chat_event wiring through event_bus.rs) MUST be merged — the FR-EVT-MEM-001 emit reuses this emitter; do not build a new one.
  - MT-037 (knowledge documents API binding / HandshakeCoreClient on backend_client.rs) MUST be merged — provides the typed HTTP client used for the proposal POST.
  - MT-063 MUST be merged — provides the preceding FEMS editor-integration surface this MT builds on.
  - The FEMS proposal endpoint (POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/memory/proposals) must exist on the current handshake_core API surface; if absent, raise the typed blocker.

Risk if missed: Editing work cannot feed the memory pillar; FEMS loses its richest provenance source (operator/model selections in real documents with exact document_id + range + content hash) and the proposal->review->commit loop has no editor entry point. Without it, Pillar 12 memory is fed only by non-editor sources and the native editors fail the FEMS interop edge.

review_gated is a hard invariant: always true for Procedural per spec, and never settable to false from the editor for any class; the commit step is downstream and review-gated, never editor-direct.
submit_proposal must run off the egui frame thread (tokio::spawn or the MT-036 async mechanism); on failure log to the MT-036 in-memory error ring, never block or crash the frame.

original_scope.summary:
PROOF MT (no app code changes; proof only). GOAL: deliver a runtime proof suite that proves the native editor <-> FEMS (Pillar 12 typed-memory system, the project's typed-memory edge described as Pillar 12) interop works end-to-end against a REAL PostgreSQL database and the REAL EventLedger — no mocks, no stubs, no in-memory fakes, no SQLite. The suite proves three load-bearing interop claims: (1) a MemoryPack request issued from a document/editor context returns provenance-linked memory items that the native 'Relevant Memory' panel actually renders; (2) a 'Propose to Memory' action from the editor creates a review-gated proposal row in PostgreSQL AND emits an FR-EVT-MEM-001 event into the live EventLedger; (3) every FEMS editor action (open the Relevant Memory panel, trigger a MemoryPack refresh, invoke 'Propose to Memory', confirm/cancel the proposal) is reachable purely via AccessKit ids so an out-of-process swarm agent can drive the entire flow without screen-scraping or synthetic key events.

WHAT THIS MT IS NOT: it does NOT implement the FEMS panel, the MemoryPack client, the proposal action, or the AccessKit registration — those are delivered by MT-063 (FEMS Relevant Memory panel + MemoryPack client), MT-064 ('Propose to Memory' action + proposal lifecycle), and MT-041 (editor actions exposed through AccessKit). This MT ONLY writes the runtime proof suite that exercises and asserts that already-built behavior. Do not add features. Do not edit any non-test source file. If a needed behavior or backend API is missing, do NOT implement it here — record it as a typed blocker (see implementation_notes) and fail the affected proof with a descriptive message, never a silent skip.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: a single new test file:
  CREATE  src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_fems_interop_proofs.rs  (~350-550 lines)
    - one Rust integration-test module that boots the native editor shell in an egui_kittest harness (the in-process UI test harness from the WP-011 toolkit), connected to a REAL handshake_core backend talking to a REAL PostgreSQL instance and the REAL EventLedger.
    - four #[test] (or #[tokio::test] if the harness is async) proof functions: proof_fems_01_memorypack_render, proof_fems_02_propose_creates_proposal_and_event, proof_fems_03_swarm_drives_fems_via_accesskit, proof_fems_04_procedural_proposal_stays_review_gated.
    - shared test fixtures at the top of the file: a fn that resolves the live PostgreSQL DSN and EventLedger endpoint from the standard test-config surface (env vars / workspace test config — see implementation_notes), a fn that creates a throwaway workspace_id + a seed document with known content, and a teardown that removes only the rows this test created (never TRUNCATE shared tables).

HOW TO BUILD THE SUITE (step-by-step, no-context implementable):
  1. Reuse WP-011 shell primitives — do NOT re-create them. Get the pane registry (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs), the command bus (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs + src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_bus.rs), and the AccessKit id registry (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/registry.rs) from the WP-011 shell (the same surfaces MT-031 wired the editor panes into and MT-041 registered actions into). Construct the kittest app exactly the way MT-041's harness (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_e7_editor_action_accesskit.rs) constructs it, then additionally mount the FEMS Relevant Memory panel from MT-063 and enable the 'Propose to Memory' action from MT-064. Treat MT-041's harness as the canonical pattern for: building the egui_kittest app, advancing frames, querying the AccessKit tree by author_id, and dispatching AccessKit actions (ctx.perform_accesskit_action(node_id, action_id)).
  2. Real PostgreSQL only (HARD CONSTRAINT). The backend under test MUST be configured to use PostgreSQL + the EventLedger. There must be NO SQLite anywhere in this suite or its configuration. Resolve the live DSN from the project's standard integration-test config (env var such as HANDSHAKE_TEST_PG_DSN or the workspace test config file — confirm the exact key against the E6/backend-wiring MTs and existing integration tests before hardcoding). If the DSN is absent, the proof MUST fail with a clear 'live PostgreSQL DSN not configured' message — never silently fall back to an in-memory or SQLite store, and never pass green on an absent backend.
  3. proof_fems_01_memorypack_render: create a throwaway workspace and a seed document whose content deterministically matches at least one memory item already present (or seeded by the fixture) so a MemoryPack request returns at least one hit. Open the editor on that document, open the FEMS Relevant Memory panel via its AccessKit action, trigger the MemoryPack request (the panel issues GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/memory/pack against the live backend), advance frames until the response renders, then ASSERT: (a) the HTTP/IPC call hit the real backend (observable via the returned payload referencing real PG row ids, not a fixture constant), (b) the panel's AccessKit subtree contains >= 1 rendered memory item node, and (c) each rendered item carries provenance linkage (source id / origin reference) — assert the provenance field is present and non-empty on at least one item. No mocked response.
  4. proof_fems_02_propose_creates_proposal_and_event: with the same live workspace, select editor content and invoke the 'Propose to Memory' action (MT-064) via its AccessKit id. After the action completes, ASSERT against the LIVE backend, not the UI alone: (a) a new proposal row exists in PostgreSQL for this workspace_id (query via the backend's proposals read API — GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/memory/proposals — and assert the new proposal id is present), and (b) an FR-EVT-MEM-001 event was emitted into the live EventLedger (query GET /api/flight_recorder, filter for event type FR-EVT-MEM-001 correlated to this workspace_id / proposal id, assert exactly the expected event appears). Both the proposal row and the ledger event must reference the same proposal identity so the proof shows the write and the event are correlated, not coincidental.
  5. proof_fems_03_swarm_drives_fems_via_accesskit: prove the swarm path. Drive the ENTIRE FEMS flow purely through AccessKit ids as an out-of-process agent would: discover the FEMS panel-open action, the MemoryPack-refresh action, the 'Propose to Memory' action, and the proposal confirm/cancel actions by author_id only (no direct Rust calls into the panel, no synthetic key events, no screen-scraping). For each step, look up the node by its stable author_id (per MT-041's 'editor.<pane>.<action>' convention extended for FEMS, e.g. editor.fems.panel-open, editor.fems.memorypack-refresh, editor.fems.propose, editor.fems.proposal-confirm), dispatch the AccessKit activate action, advance a frame, and assert the resulting state. ASSERT that the full sequence (open panel -> refresh MemoryPack -> propose -> reach review-gated proposal) is completable using only AccessKit ids, and that every targeted id is stable (deterministic, no random segments) so a stored swarm reference stays valid across frames.
  6. proof_fems_04_procedural_proposal_stays_review_gated: prove the safety invariant. A 'Propose to Memory' action — even one triggered procedurally / by an agent in proof_fems_03 — must create a REVIEW-GATED proposal and must NOT auto-commit into memory. After triggering the propose action end-to-end, ASSERT against the live backend that: (a) the proposal's status is the review-gated/pending state (not committed/applied), (b) no corresponding committed memory item was created as a side effect (query the live memory store and assert the proposed content did NOT appear as an active memory item without an explicit review/confirm), and (c) the FR-EVT-MEM-001 event records the proposal as pending review, not as an applied write. This proof is the regression guard for the typed-memory edge: it must fail loudly if any path lets a procedural proposal bypass the human/agent review gate.

DEPENDENCIES / UNBLOCK CONDITIONS:
  - MT-063 COMPLETE: the native FEMS 'Relevant Memory' panel and the MemoryPack client (GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/memory/pack) exist and render provenance-linked items.
  - MT-064 COMPLETE: the 'Propose to Memory' editor action exists, creates a review-gated proposal via POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/memory/proposals, and emits FR-EVT-MEM-001.
  - MT-041 COMPLETE: editor actions (and, by extension, the FEMS actions) are exposed through the WP-011 AccessKit surface with stable author_ids; this MT reuses MT-041's kittest harness pattern and AccessKit id/action conventions.
  - A live PostgreSQL + EventLedger backend reachable from the test environment, configured via the project's standard integration-test config. No SQLite.

RISK IF MISSED: FEMS interop is asserted but never proven; the typed-memory edge (Pillar 12) could regress silently — a broken MemoryPack render, a proposal that auto-commits past the review gate, a missing FR-EVT-MEM-001 event, or an AccessKit id drift that breaks the swarm path — all without any failing test. This MT is the E9 cluster's end-to-end interop guarantee for the editor<->FEMS edge.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: implement the bidirectional editors <-> Stage (Pillar 17) interop edge. Today MT-033 only routes a Common Knowledge Component (CKC) reference one way (editors -> Stage). This MT proves a full Stage round-trip: (1) a 'Route to Stage' command that sends a note, a text selection, or a canvas node from any editor pane to a Stage pane via the EXISTING handshake_core Stage route API, and (2) an embed-back path that takes a Stage capture artifact — together with its SHA-256 manifest provenance — and inserts it into a note or canvas as an MT-014 embed NodeView. There is NO backend build in this MT: bind only existing handshake_core endpoints; if the Stage embed-back retrieval endpoint is absent, raise a typed blocker (do not stub, do not add a backend route).

The expected diff shape is: (a) one new Rust module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/stage_interop.rs (~300-450 lines) defining the route-to-Stage payload builders, the Stage round-trip client wrappers over the existing handshake_core HTTP API, and the embed-back -> NodeView conversion; (b) a new pane module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/stage_pane.rs (~200-350 lines) that hosts the Stage surface inside the egui shell, registers into the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs), receives routed content, and exposes a 'Capture -> Embed back' action; (c) integration tests proving the payload shape, the FR event emission, the round-trip against a REAL PostgreSQL/EventLedger, and the typed-blocker path.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/stage_interop.rs
      * StageRouteSource enum: NoteRef { workspace_id, note_id } | Selection { workspace_id, source_pane_id, text, source_ref } | CanvasNode { workspace_id, canvas_id, node_id, node_kind }.
      * struct StageRoutePayload { workspace_id: String, source: StageRouteSource, target_stage_pane: Option<PaneId>, correlation_id: String } with fn build_from_selection(sel: &SharedSelection) -> Result<StageRoutePayload, StageInteropError> and fn build_from_canvas_node(node: &CanvasNodeRef) -> Result<StageRoutePayload, StageInteropError>. These build the payload deterministically; build_from_selection reads the shared selection state published on the WP-011 shared command/event bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) (TextRange / BlockRef / NodeRef variants).
      * fn route_to_stage(client: &HandshakeClient, payload: &StageRoutePayload) -> Result<RouteAck, StageInteropError> that POSTs to the EXISTING endpoint POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/stage/route and, on success, emits the route_to_stage Flight-Recorder (FR) event defined in MT-036 via the FR event bus (do NOT invent a new event name; reuse MT-036's route_to_stage emitter).
      * struct StageArtifactRef { artifact_id: String, workspace_id: String, sha256: String, manifest: StageManifest } and fn fetch_stage_artifact(client: &HandshakeClient, workspace_id: &str, artifact_id: &str) -> Result<StageArtifactRef, StageInteropError> that GETs the EXISTING endpoint GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/stage/artifacts/{id}. If the client returns 404 / 501 / not-implemented OR the route is not registered in the bound handshake_core API surface, return StageInteropError::EmbedBackEndpointAbsent (the typed blocker) — do not fabricate the artifact.
      * fn embed_artifact_as_nodeview(artifact: &StageArtifactRef) -> Result<EmbedNodeView, StageInteropError> that converts a fetched Stage artifact into an MT-014 embed NodeView (reuse MT-014's EmbedNodeView / embed-block type; do not define a parallel embed type). The NodeView MUST carry the artifact's SHA-256 and a provenance descriptor { source: "stage_capture", artifact_id, sha256, manifest_ref } so evidence-grade provenance survives the embed.
      * StageInteropError enum: BadSelection | EmptyPayload | RouteRejected { status: u16 } | EmbedBackEndpointAbsent | ProvenanceMissing | Transport(String).
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/stage_pane.rs
      * struct StagePane { pane_id: PaneId, workspace_id: String, ... } implementing the WP-011 pane trait; registers into the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs) and the AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) with stable author_id "stage-pane" (Role::GenericContainer) and child action button author_id "stage-capture-embed-back" (Role::Button, actions=[Press]).
      * fn receive_routed_content(&mut self, payload: &StageRoutePayload): renders the routed note/selection/canvas-node inside the Stage surface (port the visual surface from the React Stage components + MediaDownloaderView capture/import reference).
      * fn capture_and_embed_back(&mut self, client: &HandshakeClient, target: EmbedTarget) -> Result<(), StageInteropError>: calls fetch_stage_artifact then embed_artifact_as_nodeview then inserts the EmbedNodeView into the target note or canvas (target = note pane or canvas pane resolved via the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs) / shared bus focus owner (event_bus.rs)).

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs  — add `pub mod stage_pane;` and `pub mod interop;` (and, inside interop, `pub mod stage_interop;`); if interop/ does not yet exist, create src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/mod.rs declaring `pub mod stage_interop;`.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs  — register StagePane in the pane factory.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs  — register the 'Route to Stage' command (id "route-to-stage", label "Route to Stage", default keybind Ctrl+Shift+S or OS-appropriate) whose handler calls stage_interop::route_to_stage on the current shared selection / focused canvas node, and register the 'Embed Stage Capture' command (id "embed-stage-capture") on the Stage pane. Do NOT duplicate MT-033's existing CKC route-to-Stage command; this MT EXTENDS it into a proven round-trip (reuse MT-033's command surface and add the embed-back leg).

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Reuse, do not reinvent: the route-to-Stage one-way path already exists from MT-033 (CKC route-to-Stage). Wire route_to_stage() to the SAME existing POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/stage/route endpoint MT-033 uses; this MT adds (a) selection + canvas-node payload builders and (b) the embed-back return leg.
  2. Payload builders read selection state from the WP-011 shared command/event bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) (depends_on is satisfied transitively through MT-033 which depends on MT-031); build_from_selection maps SharedSelection::TextRange -> Selection source, ::BlockRef -> NoteRef, ::NodeRef -> CanvasNode.
  3. On a successful POST, emit MT-036's route_to_stage FR event via the existing FR event bus so the round-trip is observable in the Flight-Recorder timeline. Use MT-036's emitter signature exactly; do not add a new event kind.
  4. The embed-back leg: GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/stage/artifacts/{id}. Bind via the existing HandshakeClient (backend_client.rs). If the endpoint is missing from the bound handshake_core surface (route absent, 404/501, or client method does not exist), return StageInteropError::EmbedBackEndpointAbsent and surface it to the operator as a typed blocker — this is the HARD no-backend-rewrite rule: gaps are typed blockers, never new backend routes.
  5. Convert the fetched artifact to an MT-014 embed NodeView (reuse MT-014's embed-block / NodeView type). The NodeView MUST preserve SHA-256 manifest provenance; if the fetched artifact has no sha256 or manifest, return StageInteropError::ProvenanceMissing rather than embedding an unverifiable artifact.
  6. Insert the EmbedNodeView into the target note (rich-text pane document model) or canvas (canvas pane node graph, canvas_board.rs) resolved through the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs) and the shared bus focus owner (event_bus.rs).
  7. AccessKit: register "stage-pane" (GenericContainer), "stage-capture-embed-back" (Button), and the routed-content region "stage-routed-content" (GenericContainer) into the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) so swarm agents can drive the round-trip.
  8. HARD constraints: PostgreSQL/EventLedger only — no SQLite anywhere; no backend rewrite (bind existing handshake_core APIs via backend_client.rs, gaps are typed blockers); egui+AccessKit native; reuse WP-011 shell primitives (pane_registry.rs, command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs, accessibility/registry.rs).

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-014 (embed NodeView / embed-block type) must be merged — embed-back reuses its NodeView.
  - MT-033 (CKC route-to-Stage one-way command) must be merged — this MT extends it.
  - MT-036 (Flight-Recorder route_to_stage event) must be merged — route_to_stage() emits its event.
  - Cross-WP: the WP-011 shell primitives (pane_registry.rs, command_registry.rs, event_bus.rs, accessibility/registry.rs, backend_client.rs) must already exist in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/; this MT reuses them and does not recreate them.

Risk if missed: the Stage creative-capture edge stays one-directional (CKC -> Stage only); evidence-grade captures (with SHA-256 manifest provenance) cannot flow back into notes or canvas, breaking the closed-loop creative+evidence workflow that Pillar 17 promises.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: build the editors <-> Calendar (Pillar 2) interop edge. This MT melts the daily-note system from MT-019 together with the EXISTING Calendar canonical backend so that (a) selecting a date in the calendar opens-or-creates that date's daily note idempotently, (b) an open daily note resolves and links its CalendarEvent window for that date, and (c) the panel surfaces a read-only ActivitySpan correlation showing which documents were edited during a calendar block. This is pure frontend wiring plus binding to already-shipped handshake_core REST endpoints — NO backend build, NO schema change, NO new SQL. If the ActivitySpan join endpoint is not exposed by the backend, this MT must raise a TYPED BLOCKER (do not stub a fake join, do not query the DB directly), keep the daily-note <-> CalendarEvent binding working, and render an empty-state for the correlation strip.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/calendar_interop.rs (~300-450 lines) — the interop layer. Defines: CalendarInteropService { http: Arc<dyn HttpClient>, workspace_id: WorkspaceId }; the domain types CalendarEvent { id: String, title: String, start_utc: DateTime<Utc>, end_utc: DateTime<Utc>, daily_note_doc_id: Option<DocId> }, ActivitySpan { span_id: String, calendar_event_id: Option<String>, started_utc: DateTime<Utc>, ended_utc: DateTime<Utc>, edited_doc_ids: Vec<DocId> }, and DailyNoteBinding { date: NaiveDate, doc_id: DocId, calendar_event_id: Option<String> }. Methods: events_for_range(from: NaiveDate, to: NaiveDate) -> Result<Vec<CalendarEvent>, InteropError>; activity_spans_for_event(event_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<ActivitySpan>, InteropError> (returns Err(InteropError::EndpointUnavailable) -> the typed blocker path when the activity-span route 404s / is absent); open_or_create_daily_note(date: NaiveDate) -> Result<DailyNoteBinding, InteropError> (MUST delegate to the MT-019 daily-note service rather than re-implement creation — see implementation_notes); resolve_event_for_daily_note(date: NaiveDate) -> Result<Option<CalendarEvent>, InteropError>.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/daily_journal_panel.rs (~250-400 lines) — the egui panel that hosts the daily note view ported from the React LoomDailyJournalPanel.tsx. Renders: a date header with prev/next day nav (reuse MT-019 date navigation, do NOT build a second calendar widget), the linked CalendarEvent chip (clickable -> emits a command-bus event to focus/open the calendar event window for that date), and a read-only 'Edited during this block' correlation strip listing the ActivitySpan.edited_doc_ids as document chips. The correlation strip is strictly read-only: clicking a doc chip navigates to that document but the panel never writes ActivitySpan data.

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/mod.rs — add `pub mod calendar_interop;` (create the interop module dir + mod.rs under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/ if it does not yet exist; interop is a NEW WP-012 module subdir).
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/loom/mod.rs — add `pub mod daily_journal_panel;` and export DailyJournalPanel into the loom panel registry (create the loom module dir + mod.rs under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/ if it does not yet exist; this new loom panel work reuses the existing graph view in loom_graph.rs as its host module, it does not fork a second loom surface).
  - Register the DailyJournalPanel as a pane in the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs), and register its commands (open-daily-note-for-date, link-calendar-event, focus-calendar-event) on the WP-011 command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs). Register AccessKit author_ids (see implementation_notes) using the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs). Do NOT fork new shell primitives — reuse pane_registry.rs, command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs, and accessibility/* shipped by WP-011.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Date -> daily note (idempotent open-or-create). open_or_create_daily_note(date) MUST call the MT-019 daily-note service entrypoint (the same path MT-019 exposes as openDailyJournal / open_daily_note) so a given date always maps to exactly ONE doc; calling it twice for the same date returns the same DocId without creating a duplicate. Do not re-derive the daily-note path or template here — that ownership belongs to MT-019; this MT only orchestrates the call and stores the returned DailyNoteBinding.
  2. Date -> CalendarEvent window. When a date is selected in the calendar (the calendar widget itself is MT-030's territory — the React reference is a dumb view backed by React Big Calendar; here the native calendar emits a date-selected signal on the command bus / event_bus.rs), calendar_interop calls events_for_range(date, date), picks the event whose window contains the date (or the all-day event for that date), opens-or-creates the daily note, and writes daily_note_doc_id back into the in-memory CalendarEvent binding so the linkage is bidirectional in the session. Persisting the link back to the backend is OUT OF SCOPE unless the existing events endpoint already accepts a daily_note_doc_id field — if it does not, keep the link session-local and note it.
  3. Daily note -> CalendarEvent. resolve_event_for_daily_note(date) calls events_for_range(date, date) and returns the matching event so the daily_journal_panel can render the clickable CalendarEvent chip. Clicking the chip emits a focus-calendar-event command on the WP-011 command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs) targeting MT-030's calendar pane (do not import calendar-pane internals; communicate via the command bus only).
  4. ActivitySpan correlation (read-only). activity_spans_for_event(event_id) GETs the existing /calendar/activity-spans route filtered to the event. The panel renders ActivitySpan.edited_doc_ids as read-only document chips under an 'Edited during this block' heading. If the route is absent (404 / not registered / feature-not-enabled), the method returns Err(InteropError::EndpointUnavailable) and the panel shows a typed empty-state ('Activity correlation not available — backend endpoint not exposed') instead of failing the whole panel. This is the typed-blocker contract: surface the blocker, keep the rest of the panel alive, never fabricate spans, never hit the DB.
  5. Backend binding (existing endpoints only). events_for_range -> GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/calendar/events?from={from}&to={to} (existing). activity_spans_for_event -> GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/calendar/activity-spans (read-only correlation; typed blocker if absent). All persistence is PostgreSQL/EventLedger via handshake_core — this MT NEVER opens a DB connection, NEVER touches SQLite (there is none in this product), and NEVER writes a new endpoint. Gaps in the backend surface are typed blockers, not backend work.
  6. egui + AccessKit. The panel is native egui (no web view). Register AccessKit nodes: daily-journal-panel (GenericContainer), daily-journal-date-header (Label/Heading), daily-journal-prev-day (Button), daily-journal-next-day (Button), daily-journal-calendar-event-chip (Button, present only when an event resolves), daily-journal-activity-strip (List), and per item daily-journal-activity-item-{doc_id} (ListItem/Button). Use the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) to allocate these stable ids so swarm agents can address them.
  7. Command bus wiring. Register on the WP-011 command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs): 'loom.daily-note.open-for-date' (payload: NaiveDate), 'loom.daily-note.focus-calendar-event' (payload: event_id), 'loom.activity.open-document' (payload: DocId). The calendar pane (MT-030) and the daily journal panel communicate only through these bus commands.
  8. Error model. Define InteropError enum: Http(reqwest-style status), Decode(serde error), EndpointUnavailable (the typed blocker for the missing activity-span join), DailyNoteServiceError (propagated from MT-019), NotFound. EndpointUnavailable MUST be distinguishable from a generic HTTP error so the panel renders the correct empty-state and the validator can prove the typed-blocker path.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-019 (daily notes + date navigation) must be merged: this MT delegates open-or-create to MT-019's daily-note service and reuses its date nav rather than rebuilding either.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: implement the editors <-> Locus (Pillar 6, structured work tracking) interop edge. Locus is the project's structured work-tracking pillar: it holds Work Packet (WP) and Microtask (MT) records (e.g. WP-KERNEL-012, MT-034). This MT lets code comments and rich notes cross-reference those governed work units through a `locus://` addressing scheme that sits ALONGSIDE the existing addressing already built in this WP: the MT-032 loom/everything-is-a-block scheme (`loom://` / block addressing) and the MT-034 code<->note cross-ref node pattern (`code:` chips + the CrossRef node + resolution service). Concretely: (A) a note or code comment can write `locus://wp/WP-KERNEL-012` or `locus://mt/MT-034`, the editor renders it as a clickable Locus chip, and clicking navigates to that WP/MT record through the shell navigation bus (the MT-030 navigation bus reused via the WP-011 command bus); (B) a reverse-lookup surface answers 'which documents/code reference this WP/MT?' so a Locus panel can list referencing documents for a given work unit. This edge is READ + REFERENCE ONLY: the editors never create, mutate, transition, or delete Locus WP/MT records; they only resolve a `locus://` ref to a record title/summary and navigate to it, and enumerate inbound references.

This MT is a parallel sibling of MT-034 (code<->note cross-refs). It REUSES, does not re-invent: (1) the MT-032 addressing/normalization scheme (the everything-is-a-block URI form and its parse/normalize helpers) — extend it with a `locus://` scheme variant rather than building a new parser; (2) the MT-034 cross-reference node + resolution-service pattern (the CrossRef inline node rendered as a chip, plus the MT-034 cross-ref resolution service in `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/cross_refs.rs` and the `dispatch_command` open-* seam routed through the WP-011 `command_registry.rs` + `event_bus.rs` command bus) — add a Locus variant to that same machinery instead of a parallel one; (3) the MT-030 navigation bus / WP-011 command bus (`command_registry.rs` + `event_bus.rs`) for navigation; (4) the WP-011 shell primitives: the pane registry (`pane_registry.rs`), the command bus (`command_registry.rs` + `event_bus.rs`), and the AccessKit id registry (`accessibility/registry.rs`). Do not duplicate any of those substrates.

Files to CREATE:
  - `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/locus_interop.rs` (~250-400 lines) — the Locus interop module. Defines: `LocusRefKind = WorkPacket | Microtask`; `LocusRef { kind: LocusRefKind, raw: String, id: String, normalized: String }` (e.g. id="WP-KERNEL-012" or "MT-034"); `LocusRecord { kind: LocusRefKind, id: String, title: String, summary: Option<String>, status: Option<String> }` (the resolved, display-facing projection of a WP/MT). Provides a PURE parser `pub fn parse_locus_ref(raw: &str) -> Option<LocusRef>` that recognizes `locus://wp/{id}` and `locus://mt/{id}` (and the bare-id shorthand the MT-032 scheme already normalizes, kept consistent with that scheme). Provides the resolution service: `pub async fn resolve_locus_ref(client: &..., workspace_id: &str, r: &LocusRef) -> Result<LocusRecord, LocusInteropError>` which calls the bound READ APIs (WP -> GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/locus/work-packets/{id}, MT -> GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/locus/microtasks/{id}). Provides the reverse lookup `pub async fn find_documents_referencing(client: &..., workspace_id: &str, r: &LocusRef) -> Result<Vec<DocumentRef>, LocusInteropError>` that returns the documents/code blocks whose content carries a `locus://` ref to the given WP/MT (reuse the same backlink/search mechanism MT-034's `find_notes_referencing_symbol` uses, keyed on the normalized `locus://` ref value rather than re-implementing a scan). `LocusInteropError` MUST carry a distinct, typed `LocusReadApiUnavailable` variant for the typed-blocker path (see below). `DocumentRef { document_id: String, document_title: String, block_id: Option<String>, excerpt: String }` (match the MT-034 NoteRef shape so the two cross-ref surfaces stay symmetric).

Files to EDIT:
  - `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/interop/mod.rs` — add `pub mod locus_interop;` and export the public types (create the `interop` module dir + `mod.rs` if it does not yet exist; if the WP shell already roots interop modules elsewhere, place `locus_interop.rs` under that existing root and adjust the path accordingly rather than forking a new tree — record the chosen path in a code comment).
  - `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_text/cross_refs.rs` — extend the MT-034 cross-ref node machinery with a Locus variant: add a `locus_ref` inline node (attrs { kind: "wp"|"mt", id, normalized }) handled by the SAME CrossRef rendering/resolution path as the MT-034 code_ref node, rendered as a Locus chip (a rounded `egui::Frame` chip showing the short id, e.g. `WP-KERNEL-012` or `MT-034`, plus a small work-unit glyph). On click the chip fires `bus.dispatch_command("open-locus-ref", CommandArgs::LocusRef{ kind, id })` through the reused command bus; register `open-locus-ref` on the bus so the shell routes it to the Locus pane / record view via the MT-030 navigation bus (NavTarget for the WP/MT record). If the resolution returns the typed `LocusReadApiUnavailable`, render the chip in an 'unresolved' (greyed) state with a tooltip naming the missing endpoint, and do NOT panic. Reuse the MT-034 chip rendering and AccessKit registration helpers; add only the Locus-specific attrs and command id.

State / data model:
  - The `locus_ref` rich-text node persists attrs { kind, id, normalized } and MUST survive the rich-document save+reload round-trip exactly like the MT-034 code_ref node (declare `locus_ref` as an allowed node type; if the backend node-type validation rejects it, raise a typed blocker — do not silently strip).
  - Resolution results (`LocusRecord`) and reverse-lookup results (`Vec<DocumentRef>`) are cached on the owning panel/struct; resolution and reverse lookup run OFF the egui render path (async / via the existing client request mechanism) — never block the frame thread.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Parsing: `parse_locus_ref` is a PURE, side-effect-free function. Recognize `locus://wp/{id}` -> LocusRef{ kind: WorkPacket, id }, `locus://mt/{id}` -> LocusRef{ kind: Microtask, id }. Normalize the id form consistently with the MT-032 scheme's normalization (trim, case, separator rules); store the canonical form in `normalized` and use it as the single key for both resolution and reverse lookup so the two directions never disagree. Reuse MT-032 normalization helpers; do NOT add a second normalizer.
  2. Resolution: `resolve_locus_ref` dispatches on kind -> the matching bound READ endpoint. WorkPacket -> GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/locus/work-packets/{id}; Microtask -> GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/locus/microtasks/{id}. Map the response into `LocusRecord { title, summary, status }`. A 404 from a live endpoint means 'record not found' -> return an `Unresolved`/NotFound result (greyed chip), NOT the typed-blocker variant. The typed-blocker variant is reserved for the endpoint not existing on the frontend-reachable API surface at all (see step 7).
  3. Chip rendering: reuse the MT-034 CrossRef chip path. The Locus chip shows the short id text and a work-unit glyph; entire chip is a Button; click fires `open-locus-ref`. A resolved chip may show the resolved title on hover (tooltip) when `LocusRecord.title` is available. An unresolved/NotFound chip renders greyed with an 'unresolved' label. The 'API unavailable' chip renders greyed with a tooltip naming the missing endpoint.
  4. Navigation: register `open-locus-ref` on the InteractionBus (MT-031) and route it through the MT-030 navigation bus to the Locus record view / pane. Do NOT create a new navigation channel; pass navigation out via the same `FnMut(NavTarget)` / command-dispatch seam the WP shell already uses. The NavTarget identifies the WP/MT record so the shell can focus or open the Locus pane on that record.
  5. Reverse lookup (Locus panel inbound references): `find_documents_referencing` returns the documents/code blocks whose stored content carries a `locus://` ref to the given WP/MT. Reuse the MT-034 `find_notes_referencing_symbol` mechanism (backlink filter on ref_value, or knowledge search) keyed on the normalized `locus://` ref value. Provide this as a callable service so a Locus panel can render 'Referenced by N documents' for a selected WP/MT; the panel itself (full Locus pane UI) is downstream (MT-073) — THIS MT delivers the parser, resolution, reverse-lookup service, the `locus_ref` node + chip, and the navigation seam. De-duplicate results on (document_id, block_id).
  6. AccessKit: register every Locus chip and reverse-lookup row through the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (never ad-hoc). Chip author_id = `locus-ref-chip-{kind}-{id}` (e.g. `locus-ref-chip-wp-WP-KERNEL-012`), role = Button, action Press. Reverse-lookup rows (when surfaced) get author_id = `locus-refby-{document_id}`, role = ListItem. Ids must be stable across frames so swarm agents can address them deterministically; de-duplicate so no two nodes share an author_id.
  7. TYPED BLOCKER (hard requirement): if the Locus READ API is NOT exposed to the frontend-reachable surface (the work-packets / microtasks GET endpoints are absent from the bound handshake_core API surface, not merely returning 404 for a missing id), STOP and raise the typed `LocusInteropError::LocusReadApiUnavailable` blocker naming the exact missing endpoint(s). Do NOT add, scaffold, stub, or rewrite any backend endpoint; do NOT introduce a local SQLite cache or any non-Postgres store; do NOT mutate Locus state. Backend access is READ ONLY via existing handshake_core APIs; gaps are typed blockers. PostgreSQL/EventLedger only — no SQLite anywhere.
  8. Reuse, do not fork: extend the MT-032 addressing scheme and the MT-034 cross-ref node/resolution machinery; reuse the MT-030 navigation bus and WP-011 shell primitives (pane registry, command bus, AccessKit id registry). A grep gate should show the Locus path importing the MT-032 normalizer and the MT-034 CrossRef node/chip helpers rather than defining duplicates.

Backend API bound (REUSE ONLY — no new endpoints, no backend rewrite): GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/locus/work-packets/{id} (read a WP record; typed blocker `LocusReadApiUnavailable` if absent from the frontend-reachable surface) and GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/locus/microtasks/{id} (read an MT record). Reverse lookup reuses the MT-034 backlink/knowledge-search mechanism keyed on the normalized `locus://` ref value. If any required read capability is genuinely absent, raise the typed blocker — do not add or rewrite backend endpoints.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-030 (navigation bus) MUST exist — this MT routes `open-locus-ref` through it; no new navigation channel.
  - MT-032 (loom block addressing / everything-is-a-block scheme + normalization) MUST be merged — the `locus://` scheme extends it and reuses its normalizer.
  - MT-034 (code<->note cross-refs: CrossRef node + chip + resolution service + reverse-lookup mechanism) MUST be merged — this MT adds a Locus variant to that same machinery.
  - Backend: GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/locus/work-packets/{id} and GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/locus/microtasks/{id} must be reachable on the frontend API surface; if not, the typed blocker is the correct outcome.

Risk if missed: Notes and code cannot link to governed work units; the structured-work force-multiplier edge is missing. Code/notes stay disconnected from Locus WP/MT records, so a reader cannot jump from a comment to the work unit that governs it, and Locus cannot show which documents reference a given WP/MT. The 'melt-together' / cross-pillar interconnection claim is unproven for the editors<->Locus pair, and MT-073 (which builds the Locus panel UI on top of this service) is blocked.
