original_scope.summary:
Goal: complete the wire-up of the WP-011 native shell menu bar and command palette so that every menu item and palette entry that WP-011 authored as an honestly-DISABLED editor placeholder now dispatches the REAL WP-012 native editor command. WP-011 deliberately shipped these editor-facing menu/palette entries greyed-out (disabled) rather than fake-enabled, and routed all shell state mutation through a single substrate: the MT-031 shared command bus (the `CommandBus` / `CommandDescriptor` registry stored in egui Context data under egui::Id::new("handshake_interaction_bus")) and the MT-035 unified undo scope. This MT does NOT build any new menu infrastructure, new command bus, or new undo stack. It binds the existing, already-rendered menu items to the now-real editor command handlers through those same shared paths, and flips the previously-disabled entries to enabled once a target editor pane is focusable/available.

The diff shape is intentionally thin and additive: (a) EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/top_menu_bar.rs to replace the WP-011 `.add_enabled(false, ...)` placeholder calls for editor actions with `.add_enabled(<is_editor_available>, ...)` plus a dispatch into the command bus; (b) EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs to register/enable the editor command descriptors (and remove the `disabled: true` flag on the previously-stubbed command-palette editor entries) so the palette surfaces them and dispatches real handlers. No editor logic moves into the shell; the shell only routes by command id.

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/top_menu_bar.rs  — the WP-011 native egui menu bar. Locate every editor-facing item that WP-011 left disabled and convert it to a live dispatch. Required FILE menu items: New Document, Save, Save All, Save As, Export Document (HTML / MD / TXT / JSON). Required EDIT menu items: Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, Find, Replace (Find/Replace in current doc), Find in Files, Replace in Files, Toggle Comment, Format Document, Command Palette, Quick Switcher. Required GO menu items: the code-navigation entries (Go to Definition, Go to References, Go to Symbol, Go to Line) that WP-011 stubbed for the editor. Each item, when clicked, must call the shared dispatch helper (e.g. `command_bus.dispatch_command(<cmd_id>, ctx, ui)`), NOT call editor functions directly.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs  — the WP-011 registry that feeds both the menu bar and the MT-031 command palette (command_palette.rs) / MT-031 Quick Switcher (quick_switcher.rs). Register (or un-stub) the editor `CommandDescriptor` entries for every action above, mapping each menu item to a stable command id (e.g. "editor.file.new", "editor.file.save", "editor.file.saveAll", "editor.file.saveAs", "editor.file.export.html|md|txt|json", "editor.edit.undo", "editor.edit.redo", "editor.edit.cut", "editor.edit.copy", "editor.edit.paste", "editor.edit.selectAll", "editor.find.find", "editor.find.replace", "editor.find.findInFiles", "editor.find.replaceInFiles", "editor.edit.toggleComment", "editor.edit.formatDocument", "workbench.action.showCommands", "workbench.action.quickOpen", "editor.go.toDefinition", "editor.go.toReferences", "editor.go.toSymbol", "editor.go.toLine"). Set `disabled: false` (or remove the WP-011 placeholder disabled flag) on the editor palette entries so they are now actionable.

Exact routing the handlers MUST reuse (no forks):
  - Command dispatch: the MT-031 command bus implemented in command_registry.rs (with cross-pane signalling via event_bus.rs). Retrieve the bus via egui Context data with egui::Id::new("handshake_interaction_bus"); call its registered `CommandHandler` by id. Do NOT create a second command registry — reuse command_registry.rs.
  - Save / Save All / Save As / Export: route to the editor save path delivered by MT-020 (rich-text/document persistence) — the menu handler invokes the editor's own save/export command, which owns the handshake_core backend call. The shell passes only the active document target.
  - Undo / Redo: route through the MT-035 unified undo scope. The menu Undo/Redo must call the SAME `undo()` / `redo()` entry point the editors use, so menu-driven undo and keyboard-driven undo share one stack. Never dispatch a per-pane ad-hoc undo.
  - Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All: route through the MT-031 shared clipboard + selection paths (the same `clipboard_write` / `clipboard_read` / selection helpers registered in command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs that the WP-012 editors registered).
  - Find / Replace (in-doc): route to the focused editor's find/replace command (MT-010 code-editor find/replace family). Find in Files / Replace in Files: route to the MT-029 FindInFiles surface command.
  - Toggle Comment / Format Document: route to MT-051 line-edit operations and MT-050 FormatDocumentAndSelection respectively.
  - Go-menu code-nav items: route to the editor code-navigation commands (MT-010 family / code-nav). If a specific target command id is not yet registered by its owning MT, the handler must dispatch a typed, logged "command not yet available" no-op that keeps the item disabled rather than calling todo!()/unimplemented!() — see acceptance criteria.

Enable logic: an editor menu/palette item is enabled only when (a) its command id is registered in the command bus AND (b) the action's preconditions hold (e.g. Save enabled only when an editor pane is the active/dirty target; Undo enabled only when the MT-035 undo scope reports `can_undo()`; Paste enabled only when the clipboard has a consumable payload). Use the existing WP-011 enable-predicate hook; this MT supplies real predicates instead of the hardcoded `false`.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Read the WP-011 top_menu_bar.rs and command_registry.rs to enumerate every item currently rendered with a disabled/`false` placeholder for editor actions. Build the one-to-one map item -> command id from the list above. Do not invent new menu items; only wire existing ones.
  2. In command_registry.rs, for each editor command id, register a `CommandDescriptor` whose handler is a thin closure that looks up the live editor/active pane via the WP-011 pane registry (pane_registry.rs) and calls the editor's already-existing command function (save -> MT-020 path, undo -> MT-035 scope, etc.). The descriptor's `disabled`/enable-predicate must be a real function, not a constant.
  3. In top_menu_bar.rs, replace each `.add_enabled(false, egui::Button::new(label))` (or equivalent disabled placeholder) with `if ui.add_enabled(predicate(), egui::Button::new(label).shortcut_text(shortcut)).clicked() { command_bus.dispatch_command(cmd_id, ctx, ui); ui.close_menu(); }`. Reuse the WP-011 shortcut-text rendering; do not change keybind ownership (keybinds remain owned by the MT-031 bus dispatch).
  4. Command Palette + Quick Switcher: in command_registry.rs remove the WP-011 `disabled: true` on the editor entries so the MT-031 palette (command_palette.rs) shows and dispatches them. The palette already iterates the registry; once the entries are enabled and have real handlers, no palette code changes are needed beyond un-stubbing.
  5. AccessKit: each newly-enabled menu item must keep/receive its WP-011 stable AccessKit author_id (reuse the WP-011 AccessKit id registry under accessibility/ — accessibility/registry.rs — do NOT mint new ids if WP-011 already assigned them to the placeholder item). Enabled state must be reflected in the AccessKit node (an enabled Button, not a disabled one) so swarm agents can press it.
  6. Add an integration test module (kittest) under the flat test surface (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_menu_wireup.rs) that drives the live HandshakeApp tree: open the menu, click each formerly-disabled editor item, and assert the corresponding editor command fired (observe the editor state mutation or a recorded dispatch). Add the no-todo!() static assertion test (see proof targets).

Backend binding: NONE for this MT. The shell only routes to editor command paths; each editor command owns its own handshake_core backend call (PostgreSQL/EventLedger via the existing handshake_core APIs). This MT introduces no new backend call and no new persistence.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: requires MT-010 (code-editor command family incl. find/replace + code-nav), MT-020 (document save/export path), MT-029 (FindInFiles surface), MT-031 (command bus + palette + Quick Switcher + clipboard/selection substrate), MT-035 (unified undo scope), MT-050 (FormatDocument), MT-051 (line-edit/toggle-comment transforms). Cross-WP dependency: also requires the WP-011 native shell modules to be present and reused — the top menu bar (top_menu_bar.rs), pane registry (pane_registry.rs), command registry (command_registry.rs), command palette (command_palette.rs), quick switcher (quick_switcher.rs), and AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs); reuse, do not rebuild.

Risk if missed: the WP-011 shell menus stay half-dead for editor actions; operators and parallel swarm agents cannot drive the native editors from the menu bar or command palette, breaking the WP-012 'melt-together' parity proof and leaving honestly-disabled placeholders permanently inert.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: Every editor-facing FILE menu item (New Document, Save, Save All, Save As, Export Document HTML/MD/TXT/JSON) that WP-011 left disabled now dispatches the real editor command via the MT-031 command bus when clicked against the live HandshakeApp tree — proven by egui_kittest.

AC-002: Every editor-facing EDIT menu item (Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, Find, Replace, Find in Files, Replace in Files, Toggle Comment, Format Document, Command Palette, Quick Switcher) now dispatches its real handler via the command bus — proven by egui_kittest.

AC-003: The GO menu code-navigation items (Go to Definition, Go to References, Go to Symbol, Go to Line) dispatch the real editor code-nav commands or, where the owning command id is not yet registered, keep the item disabled with a typed logged no-op (never a panic) — proven by egui_kittest + static check.

AC-004: Save and Save All route through the MT-020 editor save path (not a shell-local save); Undo and Redo route through the MT-035 unified undo scope (menu undo and keyboard undo share one stack) — proven by cargo test asserting the dispatch reaches the MT-020 save entry and the MT-035 undo entry.

AC-005: The previously-disabled command-palette editor entries are now enabled and dispatch real handlers via the MT-031 palette; the Quick Switcher entry is likewise enabled — proven by egui_kittest opening the palette and confirming the editor entries are actionable.

AC-006: No menu item or palette entry dispatches a todo!() / unimplemented!() / panic!() on the required path — proven by a static source assertion test over the wired handlers plus a runtime kittest that exercises each item without panic.

AC-007: No new menu infrastructure, no second command bus, and no second undo stack are introduced; only src/frontend/handshake_native/src/top_menu_bar.rs and src/frontend/handshake_native/src/command_registry.rs are modified, and they reuse the WP-011 pane registry, MT-031 command bus, and MT-035 undo scope — proven by diff review and grep of dispatch call sites.
AC-008: Each newly-enabled menu item retains/receives its WP-011 AccessKit author_id and renders as an enabled (pressable) AccessKit Button node — proven by an AccessKit tree dump in kittest.
AC-009: cargo test for the native frontend shell passes with no failures across the new menu wire-up tests.
proof_targets: PT-001: cargo test -p handshake-native menu_wireup -- --nocapture => all tests PASS, no panics.

PT-002: egui_kittest harness: for each formerly-disabled editor menu item, click it on the live HandshakeApp tree and assert the editor command fired (observed editor-state mutation or recorded command-bus dispatch id).
PT-003: cargo test asserting Save / Save All dispatch reaches the MT-020 save path and Undo / Redo dispatch reaches the MT-035 unified undo scope (single shared stack).
PT-004: egui_kittest harness: open the command palette (and Quick Switcher), assert the editor entries are enabled and dispatch real handlers.
PT-005: Static assertion test: grep/AST-scan the wired handler bodies in top_menu_bar.rs and command_registry.rs prove zero todo!()/unimplemented!()/panic!() on the required editor dispatch paths.
PT-006: AccessKit tree snapshot: assert at least one formerly-disabled item (e.g. 'editor.file.save') now appears as an enabled Button node with its WP-011 author_id.
implementation_notes: Retrieve the MT-031 command bus (implemented in command_registry.rs) from egui Context data via egui::Id::new("handshake_interaction_bus"); call dispatch_command(cmd_id, ctx, ui). Do not instantiate a new bus in the shell.

Menu item pattern: `if ui.add_enabled(predicate(state), egui::Button::new(label).shortcut_text(shortcut)).clicked() { bus.dispatch_command(cmd_id, ctx, ui); ui.close_menu(); }` — reuse WP-011 shortcut_text and close_menu conventions from top_menu_bar.rs.

Enable predicates must be real: Save enabled only when an editor pane is the active/dirty target; Undo enabled only when MT-035 reports can_undo(); Paste enabled only when MT-031 clipboard has a consumable payload; mirror VS Code enable semantics.
Keybind ownership stays with the MT-031 bus dispatch — this MT does NOT add a parallel keybind table; the menu only adds a click entry point that calls the same command id.

For Go-menu code-nav ids not yet registered by their owning MT, register a typed disabled descriptor in command_registry.rs that logs 'command <id> not yet available' rather than emitting todo!(); keep the item disabled until its owner lands.

Reuse the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs): if WP-011 already assigned an author_id to the disabled placeholder item, keep that id and flip the node to enabled; do not mint a new id.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Bring VS Code-class file-metadata segments to the existing WP-011 status/menu bar so the native code editor reaches VS Code parity on the language/EOL/indent/encoding/whitespace controls. The WP-011 top menu/status bar today (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/top_menu_bar.rs) already renders a fixed set of segments: layout name, active pane-type, line:column cursor position, swarm status, and theme. This MT ADDS five new interactive, editor-aware segments to the RIGHT cluster of that same bar — language mode, EOL, indent, file encoding, and a render-whitespace toggle — and the supporting detection logic. It MUST reuse the WP-011 status/menu-bar segment primitive in top_menu_bar.rs and the WP-011 right-click segment context-menu infrastructure in context_menu.rs / context_menu_surfaces.rs; it MUST NOT introduce a second status bar or new status-bar infra.

This MT builds on MT-001 (the code editor text buffer + extension-only language detection that already exists) and MT-010 (the editor document/model surface that owns per-document state). MT-001 today derives language only from the file extension; this MT upgrades that to content/shebang detection AND adds a user override that sticks per document. MT-010 is the document state owner, so the new metadata (language override, EOL, indent prefs, encoding, whitespace toggle) hangs off the document model MT-010 owns — do not invent a parallel document store.

Exact files to CREATE/EDIT (all under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/**):
- EDIT src/frontend/handshake_native/src/top_menu_bar.rs — add five new segment render functions to the existing right cluster, each built with the WP-011 status/menu-bar segment primitive (reuse the same StatusBarSegment / segment builder helper already in this file; do NOT define a new segment type). Each new segment: (1) renders a compact label reflecting the active editor document's metadata, (2) is interactive on left-click (opens its picker/menu), (3) wires a right-click context menu via the existing WP-011 segment context-menu helper in context_menu.rs / context_menu_surfaces.rs. The segments, left-to-right in the right cluster, are: LanguageMode, Eol, Indent, Encoding, RenderWhitespaceToggle. When no code-editor document is active (e.g. a non-code pane is focused), these five segments hide (return early) rather than render stale data.
- CREATE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/language_mode.rs — the language-mode detection + override model. Defines: `LanguageId` (reuse the LanguageRegistry id type from MT-001 if already defined there; otherwise a thin newtype String), `LanguageDetection { detected: LanguageId, source: DetectionSource }` where `DetectionSource` is an enum `Extension | Shebang | Content | UserOverride`. Functions: `detect_language(path: Option<&str>, first_bytes: &[u8], full_text: &str) -> LanguageDetection` — first checks a user override on the document (highest precedence), then shebang (`#!` first line, e.g. `#!/usr/bin/env python` -> python, `#!/bin/bash` -> shell), then a small content heuristic table (e.g. leading `<?php`, `<!DOCTYPE html`, `{`/JSON shape, `package main` -> go) layered ABOVE the MT-001 extension-only path, then falls back to MT-001 extension detection. `available_languages() -> Vec<LanguageId>` returns the picker list (reuse MT-001 LanguageRegistry so the set matches the highlighter). `set_override(doc, lang)` records a per-document override on the MT-010 document model that survives re-render and re-focus.
- CREATE src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/file_meta.rs — the EOL / indent / encoding model. Defines: `Eol` enum `Lf | Crlf` with `detect(text: &str) -> Eol` (count `\r\n` vs lone `\n`; majority wins, default Lf) and `convert(buffer, target: Eol)` which rewrites all line endings in the document buffer as ONE undo step (use the MT-001/MT-010 buffer edit transaction API so a single Ctrl+Z reverts the whole conversion — do NOT emit per-line edits). `IndentStyle { kind: IndentKind, size: usize }` where `IndentKind` is `Tabs | Spaces`; `detect_indent(text: &str) -> IndentStyle` samples leading whitespace across lines (tabs present in leading indent -> Tabs; otherwise infer space size from the most common positive leading-space delta, default 4); `set_indent(doc, style)` updates the document's active editing indent behavior (Tab key inserts tab vs N spaces accordingly) on the MT-010 model. `Encoding` enum (at minimum `Utf8 | Utf8Bom | Utf16Le | Utf16Be`, default `Utf8`) with a display label and a `reopen_with(doc, encoding)` action that re-decodes the on-disk bytes (via the MT-010 document load path) under the chosen encoding — encoding detection on load reads a BOM if present, else assumes Utf8. `RenderWhitespace` is a bool toggle stored on the document/editor view state; when on, the code editor renders middots for spaces and arrows for tabs (the actual glyph rendering lives in the MT-001 editor draw path — this MT only owns the toggle state + status-bar control; flip the flag the MT-001 draw path reads).

Exact crates / egui / AccessKit patterns:
- Segment rendering reuses the existing WP-011 status/menu-bar segment helper in top_menu_bar.rs (whatever it is named there — e.g. `fn segment(ui, label, on_click) -> Response`); call it five more times, do not re-implement hover/padding/separator styling.
- Pickers: the language-mode picker and encoding picker open as a small egui popup anchored to the clicked segment using `egui::popup::popup_below_widget` (or the WP-011 segment popup helper if one exists), listing options as selectable rows; EOL and Indent use the same popup pattern (EOL: two rows LF/CRLF; Indent: rows for Tabs and Spaces 2/4/8). RenderWhitespace is a direct toggle on click (no popup) plus a checkbox in its right-click menu.
- Right-click context menus reuse the WP-011 segment context-menu infrastructure in context_menu.rs / context_menu_surfaces.rs: attach via the same helper WP-011 segments already use (e.g. `response.context_menu(|ui| { ... })`), exposing quick actions (e.g. on the EOL segment: 'Convert to LF', 'Convert to CRLF'; on Indent: 'Convert indentation to tabs/spaces', 'Change tab size'; on Encoding: 'Reopen with Encoding', 'Save with Encoding' if MT-010 exposes a save path, else only Reopen).
- AccessKit: give each new segment a stable author_id so swarm agents can address it — `status-bar-language-mode`, `status-bar-eol`, `status-bar-indent`, `status-bar-encoding`, `status-bar-render-whitespace`, each role=Button; each popup list item author_id `status-bar-{segment}-item-{value}` role=ListItem; reuse the WP-011 AccessKit id-registry helper in accessibility/ (accessibility/registry.rs / accessibility/mod.rs) (do NOT hand-roll a new registry). Picker popups expose role=List on the container.

Exact handshake-native API bound: NONE backend. This MT is pure frontend status/menu-bar + editor-state work. Language/EOL/indent detection are in-process string analysis; encoding reopen routes through the EXISTING MT-010 document load path (frontend), not a new backend call. If a needed document-model field (override slot, indent prefs, whitespace flag, encoding) does not yet exist on the MT-010 model, extend the MT-010 frontend model struct (allowed under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/**); do NOT add a backend API or a backend rewrite — any genuine backend gap is a typed blocker, not an implementation here.

Step-by-step:
1. In file_meta.rs implement `Eol`, `IndentStyle`, `Encoding`, `RenderWhitespace` plus their detect/convert/set functions; unit-test detection and the single-undo EOL convert in isolation.
2. In language_mode.rs implement `DetectionSource`, `detect_language` (override -> shebang -> content -> extension fallback), `available_languages`, `set_override`; unit-test that shebang/content beat extension and that a user override sticks per document.
3. In top_menu_bar.rs, locate the existing right-cluster render block; add the five segments using the existing segment helper, each reading the active editor document's metadata via MT-010, each with left-click picker/toggle and right-click context menu via the WP-011 context_menu helpers, each with the AccessKit author_id above; hide all five when no code-editor document is active.
4. Wire the language-mode override and indent/EOL/encoding/whitespace mutations back onto the MT-010 document model so they persist across re-render and re-focus and so the MT-001 editor draw + Tab-key behavior reads the updated state.
5. Add the egui_kittest test that the status/menu bar shows the language/EOL/indent/encoding segments with working right-click menus.

Dependencies / unblock conditions: MT-001 (text buffer + extension-only language detection + editor draw path) and MT-010 (document/model surface) must be merged first. Blocks MT-072.
Risk if missed: Language mode, EOL, indent, and encoding controls are absent from the status bar; the native editor has a VS Code parity gap on file metadata (users cannot see or change line endings, indent style, encoding, or override the detected language).
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: Language detection by shebang and content overrides MT-001 extension-only detection — proven by `cargo test -p handshake-native`: a file whose extension says one language but whose shebang/content says another resolves to the shebang/content language (DetectionSource = Shebang or Content), and a user override (DetectionSource = UserOverride) beats all auto-detection and sticks per document across re-render.

AC-002: EOL convert rewrites line endings LF<->CRLF as exactly one undo step — proven by `cargo test -p handshake-native`: convert a multi-line buffer, assert all endings changed, then a single undo restores the original buffer exactly.

AC-003: Indent detection picks tabs vs spaces and infers size — proven by `cargo test -p handshake-native`: tab-indented sample yields IndentKind::Tabs; 4-space sample yields Spaces size=4; a set_indent override updates the document's Tab-key editing behavior.

AC-004: The status/menu bar renders five editor segments (language mode, EOL, indent, encoding, render-whitespace) reflecting the active document, each with a working right-click context menu — proven by egui_kittest; segments are built with the WP-011 segment primitive in top_menu_bar.rs (no new status-bar infra).
AC-005: All five segments hide when no code-editor document is active and re-appear with correct metadata when a code document is focused — proven by egui_kittest.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: add the editor-specific Settings sections that the Handshake GUI look-and-behavior doc defines and that WP-KERNEL-011 only stubbed, into the EXISTING WP-011 settings dialog. WP-011 already ships a native egui Settings dialog that loads with GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/settings and persists with PUT /workspaces/{workspace_id}/settings (PostgreSQL/EventLedger-backed workspace settings — there is NO SQLite anywhere and NO new settings persistence in this MT). This MT only adds three editor-focused sections to that dialog and wires their values into the editors built earlier in this WP. It does NOT build a new settings system, a new persistence layer, or a new dialog shell.

Three concrete deliverables inside the existing dialog:
  (1) EDITOR section — user-configurable editor preferences distinct from UI chrome:
      - editor_font_size (f32, point size used ONLY by editor text surfaces; MUST be a separate field from the UI/chrome font size that WP-011 already manages — do not reuse the chrome font field).
      - tab_size (u8, columns per tab; default 4).
      - insert_spaces (bool, tabs-vs-spaces; true = insert spaces, false = keep hard tabs; default true).
      - word_wrap (enum: Off | On | BoundedColumn(u16); the editor default wrap mode; default Off).
      - render_whitespace (enum: None | Boundary | All; whether the code editor draws whitespace glyphs; default None).
      - auto_save_interval is ALREADY present in WP-011 settings — do NOT re-add it; only surface/label it inside this Editor section so all editor prefs read together (reference the existing field, do not duplicate it).
  (2) SYNTAX color scheme palette editor — a Muted | Standard | Custom selector that feeds the MT-001 HighlightScope -> Color32 mapping:
      - syntax_palette_mode (enum: Muted | Standard | Custom; default Standard).
      - When Custom is selected, expose one color swatch per MT-001 HighlightScope variant (Keyword, String, Comment, Number, Function, Type, Operator, Other) using egui::color_picker so the user can edit each scope color.
      - The palette must feed MT-001's scope_to_color path LIVE: changing a swatch updates the code editor highlight colors in the same frame (no app restart, no reload).
  (3) KEYBINDINGS section extension — extend the existing WP-011 keybindings table to include ALL editor-specific actions: the MT-010 code-editor chords (multi-cursor, find/replace, fold, comment-toggle, etc.) AND the rich-editor commands, sourced from the workspaceSettings.keybindings store. Each action row shows action id, label, current binding, and a default; a custom binding overrides the default for that action.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/settings_editor_section.rs (~300-500 lines) — defines the EditorSettingsSection widget: a struct holding a mutable view over the deserialized workspace settings struct, plus three render fns: render_editor_prefs(&mut self, ui), render_syntax_palette(&mut self, ui), and render_editor_keybindings(&mut self, ui). Also defines the serde types EditorPrefs { editor_font_size, tab_size, insert_spaces, word_wrap, render_whitespace }, WordWrapMode enum, RenderWhitespaceMode enum, SyntaxPaletteMode enum, and SyntaxPalette { mode, custom: HashMap<HighlightScope, [u8;4]> } that round-trip cleanly through the existing settings JSON the PUT/GET endpoint already stores. Do NOT invent a new top-level settings document — these types are nested fields appended into the SAME workspace-settings struct WP-011 serializes (the type defined in workspace_settings.rs that settings_dialog.rs deserializes GET into).

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/settings_dialog.rs — mount the three new sections into the existing dialog. Call into settings_editor_section.rs render fns inside the existing dialog body (egui::Window / side panel the dialog already uses). Do NOT change the dialog's load/save plumbing: it already calls GET on open and PUT on apply/close; the new fields ride along because they are part of the same serialized settings struct. Register AccessKit author_ids on the new controls (see notes). Reuse the WP-011 shell primitives: the pane registry (pane_registry.rs), the command bus (command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs), and the AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) — do not stand up parallel infrastructure.

Exact crates / egui / AccessKit patterns to use:
  - egui::DragValue for editor_font_size, tab_size, and BoundedColumn width.
  - egui::ComboBox for word_wrap mode, render_whitespace mode, and syntax_palette_mode selectors.
  - egui::Checkbox for insert_spaces (tabs-vs-spaces) toggle.
  - egui::color_picker::color_edit_button_srgba (or egui::widgets::color_picker) for each Custom syntax swatch; store as [u8;4] sRGBA, convert to egui::Color32 via Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied for live use.
  - AccessKit: register each control via the WP-011 AccessKit id registry with stable author_ids: 'settings-editor-font-size', 'settings-editor-tab-size', 'settings-editor-insert-spaces', 'settings-editor-word-wrap', 'settings-editor-render-whitespace', 'settings-syntax-palette-mode', 'settings-syntax-swatch-{scope}' (one per HighlightScope), and 'settings-keybind-row-{action_id}' for each keybinding row. Roles: DragValue/ComboBox -> appropriate input role, swatches -> ColorWell/Button, keybind rows -> ListItem/Row.
  - Serde: derive Serialize/Deserialize on every new type; use #[serde(default)] on each new field so OLDER stored settings docs (without these fields) still deserialize (forward/backward compatibility with WP-011-era rows in PostgreSQL).

Exact handshake_core / backend API bound (REUSE ONLY — no backend rewrite, no new endpoint):
  - GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/settings  — existing WP-011 read path; returns the workspace settings JSON. The new editor fields are read from this same payload.
  - PUT /workspaces/{workspace_id}/settings  — existing WP-011 write path; persists the workspace settings JSON to PostgreSQL/EventLedger. The new editor fields are written through this same payload. If the existing settings struct on the backend is strongly typed and would REJECT unknown fields (rather than passing them through as an opaque JSON blob), that is a typed blocker: STOP and record it as a blocker (do NOT rewrite or extend the backend in this MT). If the backend stores settings as an opaque/extensible JSON document, no backend change is needed and this MT is pure frontend.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. Read MT-069 and MT-071 outputs first: MT-069/MT-071 are dependencies that establish the editor-settings groundwork this MT builds the UI sections on; align field names and the settings struct shape with whatever they introduced rather than inventing parallel fields.
  2. Locate the WP-011 workspace-settings serde struct (the type the dialog deserializes GET into and serializes back for PUT) — it lives in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/workspace_settings.rs and is consumed by settings_dialog.rs. Add the new EditorPrefs and SyntaxPalette nested fields to it with #[serde(default)]. Edit workspace_settings.rs minimally; if the struct is locked behind a backend typed-contract and is not extensible, treat as the typed blocker above.
  3. Implement EditorSettingsSection in settings_editor_section.rs operating on a &mut reference to the deserialized settings struct so edits mutate in place and the existing PUT-on-apply path picks them up with no new save code.
  4. render_editor_prefs: DragValue for editor_font_size (clamp 6.0..=48.0), DragValue for tab_size (clamp 1..=16), Checkbox for insert_spaces, ComboBox for word_wrap, ComboBox for render_whitespace; show (read-only label + existing control) for the already-present auto_save_interval so the section reads as a complete editor-prefs group without duplicating the field.
  5. render_syntax_palette: ComboBox for Muted|Standard|Custom. For Muted and Standard, apply a built-in palette table mapping each HighlightScope to a Color32 (define two const tables). For Custom, render one color_edit_button per HighlightScope writing into SyntaxPalette.custom. Expose a fn resolve_scope_color(scope, &SyntaxPalette, visuals) that MT-001's scope_to_color delegates to, so the editor picks up palette changes live in the same frame.
  6. render_editor_keybindings: read the editor-specific action list from the workspaceSettings.keybindings source (the same source the WP-011 keybindings table already reads). Filter/extend so the table includes the MT-010 code chords and the rich-editor commands. Each row: action id, label, an editable binding capture control, and the default. A captured custom binding overrides the default for that action; persist into the same keybindings map the existing table writes.
  7. Wire the three render fns into settings_dialog.rs in section order: Editor, Syntax, Keybindings (extend the existing Keybindings section in place rather than adding a second one).
  8. AccessKit: register every new control's author_id through the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs, with live/snapshot support in accessibility/live.rs and accessibility/snapshot.rs) so swarm agents and egui_kittest can address them.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-001 (code editor buffer + HighlightScope enum + scope_to_color) must exist — the syntax palette feeds its highlight scopes.
  - MT-010 (code editor chords/keybindings) must exist — its action ids populate the editor keybindings table.
  - MT-069 and MT-071 (editor-settings groundwork) must be merged — this MT adds the UI sections on top; align field names with them.
  - The WP-011 settings dialog + GET/PUT /workspaces/{workspace_id}/settings persistence must be present and the settings struct must be extensible (else typed blocker).

Risk if missed: editors have no user-configurable preferences surface; the editor font size, tab size, tabs-vs-spaces, word-wrap, render-whitespace, syntax color scheme, and editor keybindings that the GUI look-and-behavior doc requires are all unreachable, leaving the WP-011 settings stubs permanently incomplete and breaking Obsidian/VS Code parity.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001 [RECONCILED 2026-08-05 to Master Spec v02.203 section 10.17]: Editor preferences persist through the GOVERNED TYPED PreferenceRecord path, not an opaque settings document. Setting editor_font_size, tab_size, insert_spaces, word_wrap, and render_whitespace then applying MUST write typed PreferenceRecords to PostgreSQL (SET-STORE-001), each validated against its registry schema entry (SET-REC-002), carrying a monotonically increasing revision (SET-REC-001), emitting a PreferenceChangedEvent to the EventLedger (SET-EVT-001), a Flight Recorder event (SET-EVT-003), and a recoverable receipt (SET-EVT-002). Reopening the dialog in a fresh client MUST reload the same effective values by the SET-REC-001 resolution order (surface over workspace over global over default). Proven by a live-PostgreSQL cargo test, not StubPreferenceTransport.

AC-002: editor_font_size is a SEPARATE field from the UI/chrome font size — changing the editor font size does not change chrome font size and vice versa. Proven by test asserting the two fields are distinct in the serialized settings payload.

AC-003: Syntax palette edit updates MT-001 highlight scopes live — selecting Custom and changing the Keyword swatch changes the color MT-001 scope_to_color/resolve_scope_color returns for HighlightScope::Keyword in the same frame (no restart). Proven by cargo test.

AC-004: Muted, Standard, and Custom palette modes each yield a complete HighlightScope->Color32 mapping with no missing scope. Proven by cargo test iterating all HighlightScope variants for each mode.

AC-005 [RECONCILED 2026-08-05, PARTIALLY BLOCKED - see packet reconciliation_debt RD-MT072-EDITOR-KEYBINDING-SPEC-AUTHORITY]: The Keybindings section MUST list ALL editor-specific actions (MT-010 code chords + rich-editor commands) and a custom binding MUST override the default for that action IN THE MOUNTED RICH EDITOR, resolving custom-if-present-else-default from the canonical persisted override source before dispatch, with reset removing only the selected override. The mounted rich-editor override consumption is the REAL product gap the V4 validator identified and is spec-neutral, so it MUST be implemented and proven regardless. BLOCKED SUB-QUESTION: the phrase sourced from workspaceSettings.keybindings is stale and has NO current spec authority - Master Spec v02.203 FEAT-SETTINGS-PREFERENCES (anchor 10.17, SET-SCOPE-001) defines exactly four namespaces (data-roots, view-defaults, retention, feature-toggles) and no editor-keybinding namespace exists anywhere in the bundle. The storage shape for keybinding overrides therefore awaits an Operator decision: (A) authorize the existing separate namespaced editor-keybinding preference/list as the current design, or (B) approve a governed copy-first Master Spec enrichment adding that authority. KERNEL_BUILDER MUST NOT invent the namespace (CX-032, CX-105A, CX-405/406).

AC-006: New settings fields use #[serde(default)] so a stored WP-011-era settings document without these fields still deserializes without error. Proven by cargo test deserializing a legacy JSON fixture.

AC-007: AccessKit nodes present for all new controls — 'settings-editor-font-size', 'settings-editor-tab-size', 'settings-editor-insert-spaces', 'settings-editor-word-wrap', 'settings-editor-render-whitespace', 'settings-syntax-palette-mode', at least one 'settings-syntax-swatch-{scope}', and at least one 'settings-keybind-row-{action_id}'. Proven by AccessKit tree dump in egui_kittest.

AC-008: An egui_kittest test renders the Editor settings section against the live settings surface, edits a field, applies, and confirms persistence — section renders without overlap and the control values reflect the stored state.

AC-009 [RECONCILED 2026-08-05 to Master Spec v02.203 section 10.17]: No SECOND settings authority and no embedded-file authority is introduced. All preference writes MUST flow through the single governed typed PreferenceRecord path with PostgreSQL as the sole authoritative store (SET-INV-001); SQLite is forbidden in runtime, tests, fixtures, mocks, examples, fallbacks, cache, compatibility adapters, harnesses, imports, and exports (SET-STORE-002 / CX-503R). The original wording - that the only write path is the pre-existing opaque PUT /workspaces/{workspace_id}/settings and that no new endpoint may exist - is SUPERSEDED: the typed per-preference routes ARE the current-spec design, and regressing the product back to the opaque document write path to satisfy the stale text would violate current Master Spec authority. Proven by grep showing no SQLite and no competing persistence path.
proof_targets: PT-001 [RECONCILED 2026-08-05]: cargo test -p handshake-native editor_preference_records -- --nocapture against REAL PostgreSQL => every editor scalar preference (not font size alone), each palette mode plus at least one custom swatch, and the code and rich keybinding overrides each prove typed projection, set, fresh-process/client reopen, exact revision, receipt, EventLedger reference, reset, and history WITHOUT StubPreferenceTransport. Must also cover the adversarial cases: numeric bounds, invalid enums/colors/chords, unknown preference ids, stale revision and concurrent writes, workspace isolation, backend loss/retry without edit loss, duplicate chord collision, reset idempotence, and legacy/default hydration - with rejected writes proven not to mutate revision, history, or mounted editor state.

acceptance_and_requirement_map.original: AC-001 [RECONCILED 2026-08-05 to Master Spec v02.203 section 10.17]: Editor preferences persist through the GOVERNED TYPED PreferenceRecord path, not an opaque settings document. Setting editor_font_size, tab_size, insert_spaces, word_wrap, and render_whitespace then applying MUST write typed PreferenceRecords to PostgreSQL (SET-STORE-001), each validated against its registry schema entry (SET-REC-002), carrying a monotonically increasing revision (SET-REC-001), emitting a PreferenceChangedEvent to the EventLedger (SET-EVT-001), a Flight Recorder event (SET-EVT-003), and a recoverable receipt (SET-EVT-002). Reopening the dialog in a fresh client MUST reload the same effective values by the SET-REC-001 resolution order (surface over workspace over global over default). Proven by a live-PostgreSQL cargo test, not StubPreferenceTransport.

AC-002: editor_font_size is a SEPARATE field from the UI/chrome font size — changing the editor font size does not change chrome font size and vice versa. Proven by test asserting the two fields are distinct in the serialized settings payload.

AC-004: Muted, Standard, and Custom palette modes each yield a complete HighlightScope->Color32 mapping with no missing scope. Proven by cargo test iterating all HighlightScope variants for each mode.

AC-005 [RECONCILED 2026-08-05, PARTIALLY BLOCKED - see packet reconciliation_debt RD-MT072-EDITOR-KEYBINDING-SPEC-AUTHORITY]: The Keybindings section MUST list ALL editor-specific actions (MT-010 code chords + rich-editor commands) and a custom binding MUST override the default for that action IN THE MOUNTED RICH EDITOR, resolving custom-if-present-else-default from the canonical persisted override source before dispatch, with reset removing only the selected override. The mounted rich-editor override consumption is the REAL product gap the V4 validator identified and is spec-neutral, so it MUST be implemented and proven regardless. BLOCKED SUB-QUESTION: the phrase sourced from workspaceSettings.keybindings is stale and has NO current spec authority - Master Spec v02.203 FEAT-SETTINGS-PREFERENCES (anchor 10.17, SET-SCOPE-001) defines exactly four namespaces (data-roots, view-defaults, retention, feature-toggles) and no editor-keybinding namespace exists anywhere in the bundle. The storage shape for keybinding overrides therefore awaits an Operator decision: (A) authorize the existing separate namespaced editor-keybinding preference/list as the current design, or (B) approve a governed copy-first Master Spec enrichment adding that authority. KERNEL_BUILDER MUST NOT invent the namespace (CX-032, CX-105A, CX-405/406).

All preference writes MUST flow through the single governed typed PreferenceRecord path with PostgreSQL as the sole authoritative store (SET-INV-001); SQLite is forbidden in runtime, tests, fixtures, mocks, examples, fallbacks, cache, compatibility adapters, harnesses, imports, and exports (SET-STORE-002 / CX-503R). original_scope.summary:
Goal: Author the built-in User Manual content for the native editors (code, rich-text/knowledge, graph, canvas, FEMS) and their interop, and wire that content into the EXISTING WP-011 manual pane (HBR-MAN obligation). This is content + pane-wiring only: it does NOT build a new manual subsystem. It reuses (a) the WP-011 manual pane shell primitive and (b) the WP-011 AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs). The deliverable is a no-context manual that lets a fresh model with zero chat history operate every native editor, plus an agent-vision/steering reference that maps every editor/knowledge/FEMS/interop action to its stable AccessKit author_id and the MCP swarm tool that drives it. Note: this MT carries NO React port (manual content is freshly authored) and binds NO backend API (it is pure frontend content + registry read).

Expected diff shape: (a) one new content module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/manual_content_editors.rs (~400-700 lines) that returns the editors manual as a structured in-Rust data model (sections -> topics -> body + optional agent-tool rows), and (b) a thin edit to the existing src/frontend/handshake_native/src/manual_pane.rs to register/load the editors section produced by manual_content_editors.rs into the already-existing manual pane content registry. Do NOT re-implement the manual pane container, its search box, its navigation tree, or its AccessKit scaffolding — those exist from the prior manual/registry surface (manual_pane.rs, established by MT-072 on top of the WP-011 shell and accessibility/registry.rs); this MT only supplies content and the one registration call.

Files to CREATE:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/manual_content_editors.rs — defines `pub fn editors_manual_section() -> ManualSection` (ManualSection is the existing manual data type from manual_pane.rs; if manual_pane.rs exposes a different constructor name, match it exactly — read manual_pane.rs first to learn the real type/fn names before authoring). The section contains: (1) one GLOBAL-BUILD-MANUAL topic per required heading (see below), and (2) an `agent_tool_reference` topic that holds one row per addressable editor/knowledge/FEMS/interop action: { author_id: &'static str, surface: enum(Code|RichText|Graph|Canvas|FEMS|Knowledge|Interop), action_label: String, mcp_tool: &'static str, description: String }.

Files to EDIT:
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/manual_pane.rs — add a single registration call so the editors section appears in the manual pane's section list/navigation. Match the existing registration mechanism (e.g. push into the manual registry Vec, or call manual.register_section(...)); read the file to find the exact API. Do not change the pane container, search logic, or AccessKit ids of the pane itself.
  - src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs — add the `mod manual_content_editors;` declaration so the new flat module is part of the crate (modules in this crate are declared flat at the crate root, not under a shell/ directory).

Required GLOBAL-BUILD-MANUAL headings (each MUST be present as its own topic so the heading-presence test passes): 'Purpose', 'Core Workflows', 'Startup and Run', 'Inputs and Outputs', 'Navigation Paths', 'Safety Constraints', 'Common Failure Modes', 'Recovery Steps'. Each topic body must be written for a no-context model: concrete commands, concrete pane names, concrete AccessKit ids, concrete keybinds, no hand-waving.

Manual content requirements per topic:
  - Purpose: explain that the native editors replace the legacy React/Monaco/Excalidraw/graph surfaces with egui+AccessKit panes that share one selection/clipboard/command bus (the WP-012 melt-together substrate, built on command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs); explain that all panes are addressable by stable AccessKit author_id and steerable by MCP swarm tools.
  - Core Workflows: open a file in the code editor; edit rich-text/knowledge notes; build a graph; sketch on the canvas; drive FEMS; move a selection between panes (copy in code -> paste in rich-text) via the shared command/event bus; jump from a knowledge backlink to its target; open the command palette and run a command.
  - Startup and Run: how the editor panes mount inside the WP-011 shell (named tiles in the docking layout managed by split_layout.rs + pane_registry.rs + layout_persistence.rs), and the run command for the native frontend (state it as `cargo run -p handshake-native`; if the exact binary target name differs, write the cargo run invocation and mark the exact target name as a typed lookup against src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml rather than inventing one).
  - Inputs and Outputs: inputs = file paths / loom:// block refs / atelier refs / graph node ids; outputs = edited buffers persisted via existing handshake_core APIs (PostgreSQL/EventLedger only), clipboard payloads, command-bus events.
  - Navigation Paths: keyboard and AccessKit navigation between panes; command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P, command_palette.rs + command_registry.rs); manual search box; backlink/graph jump.
  - Safety Constraints: editors never write to .GOV/**; never touch legacy app/src/** except as read-only reference; persistence goes through handshake_core (no direct DB writes, no SQLite anywhere); destructive actions are bounded and quiet (HBR-QUIET, quiet_mode/focus_guard.rs) — no focus-stealing popups while a swarm agent is driving.
  - Common Failure Modes: pane fails to mount; clipboard daemon missing on headless CI; stale pane_id after a closed pane; AccessKit node not found by an agent; backend persistence API returns a typed error.
  - Recovery Steps: re-mount the pane from the docking menu; re-run with a present display/clipboard; re-query the AccessKit registry (accessibility/registry.rs) for the live author_id; retry persistence after the typed backend error clears; where a step needs a backend capability that does not yet exist, the manual states it as a typed blocker rather than fabricating behavior.

Agent-vision / steering reference (HBR-VIS + HBR-SWARM): produce one row for EVERY addressable editor, knowledge, FEMS, and interop action. Each row pairs the stable AccessKit author_id with the MCP swarm tool that drives it (the same tool surface other E12 MTs expose via mcp/tools.rs + mcp/action.rs, e.g. an MCP 'gui.invoke_action' / 'gui.read_state' family keyed on author_id — match the actual tool names defined by the depended-on MTs; read their contracts/code to get the real tool names rather than inventing them). Cover at minimum: code-editor actions, rich-text/knowledge actions, graph actions, canvas actions, FEMS actions, and the interop edges (FEMS, Stage, Calendar, Locus). The interop edge documentation MUST name the FEMS, Stage, Calendar, and Locus interop edges and describe, for each, the AccessKit author_id(s) and the MCP tool an agent uses to cross that edge — all in this one no-context manual.

Step-by-step implementation notes:
  1. FIRST read src/frontend/handshake_native/src/manual_pane.rs to learn the real manual data types (ManualSection / ManualTopic or whatever they were named), the real registration API, and how search indexes topic text. Author manual_content_editors.rs against those real types — do not invent a parallel type system.
  2. Build the editors_manual_section() returning the eight GLOBAL-BUILD-MANUAL topics + the agent_tool_reference topic. Keep all author_id and mcp_tool strings as &'static str literals so the id-audit test can compare them against the live AccessKit registry (accessibility/registry.rs) and the MCP tool table (mcp/tools.rs).
  3. Source every documented author_id from the LIVE AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) and from the depended-on E12 MT surfaces (MT-041, MT-042, MT-063, MT-066, MT-067, MT-068, MT-072). Do NOT hardcode an author_id that no live pane registers; the id-audit test will fail if a documented id is absent from the registry.
  4. Register the section into the manual pane in manual_pane.rs with the single existing registration call. Confirm the manual pane's existing search box indexes the new topic bodies (it should automatically if registered sections are indexed; if registration alone is insufficient, add only the minimum to include the new section in the search index).
  5. Add tests in the handshake-native crate flat tests directory (src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_manual_pane_editors.rs, following the crate's flat tests/test_*.rs convention): (a) the manual pane loads the editors section and all eight GLOBAL-BUILD-MANUAL headings are present; (b) the agent-tool reference lists every editor/knowledge/FEMS/interop author_id with a non-empty mcp_tool; (c) an egui_kittest 'Search Manual' interaction finds an editor topic by keyword; (d) an id-audit test asserts no documented author_id is missing from the live AccessKit registry.

Dependencies / unblock conditions:
  - MT-041, MT-042 (interop/melt-together surfaces) provide the interop author_ids and tools to document.
  - MT-063, MT-066, MT-067, MT-068 (editor/knowledge/FEMS surfaces) provide the per-surface author_ids and MCP tools to document.
  - MT-072 (prior E12 manual/registry surface) provides the registry/section primitives this MT documents and registers against (manual_pane.rs).
  - WP-011 cross-WP reuse: the manual pane shell, the docking layout (split_layout.rs, pane_registry.rs, layout_persistence.rs), the command/event bus (command_registry.rs, event_bus.rs), the command palette (command_palette.rs), and the AccessKit id registry (accessibility/registry.rs) must exist (reuse, do not rebuild).

Risk if missed: no-context models and swarm agents cannot learn to operate the editors; GLOBAL-BUILD-MANUAL and HBR-MAN remain unmet for the editor surfaces, and the agent-vision/steering surface (HBR-VIS, HBR-SWARM) has no human/agent-readable index mapping author_id -> MCP tool.

original_scope.summary:
PROOF MT (no app code changes; proof only). GOAL: author and execute a runtime scenario suite that proves the three 'other-pillar' interop edges of the native editors — Stage (Pillar 17), Calendar (Pillar 2), and Locus (Pillar 6) — actually work end-to-end against a REAL PostgreSQL database and the REAL EventLedger / Flight Recorder (NO mocks, NO SQLite, NO in-memory substitute for the persistence layer). This MT mirrors the MT-046 InterconnectionScenarioProofs pattern exactly: each scenario crosses a surface boundary, drives real state through existing handshake_core HTTP APIs, and is additionally reachable purely via AccessKit ids so an out-of-process swarm agent can drive it without screen-reading. The MT proves these force-multiplier edges instead of merely asserting them; if any backend API or AccessKit id needed by a scenario does not yet exist, the scenario is recorded as a TYPED BLOCKER in the manifest (status='BLOCKED', blocker='<reason>') rather than mocked, stubbed, or silently skipped.

WHY THIS IS A PROOF-ONLY MT: This task creates NO new product/app code under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/**. It exercises surfaces, panes, commands, and AccessKit ids that earlier MTs already built (Stage pane = MT-068, Calendar binding = MT-067, Locus cross-reference = MT-066, EditorActions AccessKit registry = MT-041, KnowledgeGraph AccessKit = MT-042). The only files created are test files plus a manifest under src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/. If a needed pane/command/AccessKit id is missing because an upstream MT did not register it, the correct outcome is a typed blocker, not new app code (a backend rewrite is also forbidden — bind existing handshake_core APIs only).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: Creates src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_other_pillar_interop_proofs.rs — a single Rust integration test file (harness = true) containing the four proof scenarios OP-01..OP-04 below, plus a sibling manifest src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/other_pillar_interop_manifest.json with one entry per scenario. Registers the suite under [[test]] in src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml ( name = 'test_other_pillar_interop_proofs', harness = true ). No other files change.

PERSISTENCE INVARIANT (HARD): Every scenario must run against a real PostgreSQL instance provisioned by the same workspace/PG fixture builder used in MT-044/MT-045/MT-046 (reuse it; do not invent a parallel fixture). The EventLedger / Flight Recorder assertions must read the real ledger via GET /api/flight_recorder (or GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/events, whichever route exists in src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/mod.rs — verify the route name before authoring; if neither exists the FR assertions become typed blockers). SQLite, mock connections, and stubbed repositories are explicitly forbidden anywhere in this suite.

SWARM/AccessKit INVARIANT (HARD): Each interop edge must be reachable purely via AccessKit author_ids registered by MT-041 (EditorActions) and MT-042 (KnowledgeGraph), plus the pane-specific ids registered by MT-066/067/068. OP-04 specifically proves an out-of-process agent path: it builds the egui widget tree with egui_kittest, looks up each target by author_id only (never by coordinates or label-scraping), simulates the AccessKit Activate/Press/SetValue action, and calls handshake_native::accessibility::flush_pending_updates() before asserting the resulting label/focus/value state.

FR-EVENT INVARIANT (HARD): Each scenario must, after driving its edge, assert that the EXPECTED Flight Recorder / EventLedger event(s) were emitted, by reading GET /api/flight_recorder and filtering for the edge's event kind (e.g. STAGE_ROUTE, STAGE_EMBED_BACK, CALENDAR_EVENT_BOUND, ACTIVITY_SPAN_CORRELATED, LOCUS_REF_RESOLVED, LOCUS_REVERSE_LOOKUP — verify the exact emitted kind strings against the upstream MT implementations; if a kind is not emitted, surface a typed blocker, do not weaken the assertion).

=== SCENARIO OP-01 — Stage interop (Pillar 17): route-to-Stage then embed-back round-trip ===
Proves the Stage edge end-to-end. Steps: (1) using the real PG fixture, create a workspace and a rich-text note with a known text range; (2) drive the 'route-to-stage' command via the shared command bus (the same command_registry.rs + event_bus.rs dispatch path MT-031/MT-046 use) so the selected range is routed to the Stage pane (Pillar 17) — reach the command via AccessKit author_id (EditorActions registry, MT-041) NOT by label; (3) assert the Stage pane received the routed selection (AccessKit author_id 'stage.selection.preview' label matches the routed text, after flush_pending_updates()); (4) drive 'embed-back': the Stage pane produces an embed that is inserted back into the originating note as an MT-014-style embed node carrying SHA-256 provenance of the routed payload; (5) save the note via the existing PUT /workspaces/{id}/knowledge/documents/{doc_id}, reload via GET, and assert the block tree contains the embed node with a non-empty sha256 provenance field that matches the SHA-256 of the original routed bytes; (6) assert GET /api/flight_recorder contains a STAGE_ROUTE event followed by a STAGE_EMBED_BACK event for this workspace/doc, in order. Real PG only; no mocks.

=== SCENARIO OP-02 — Calendar interop (Pillar 2): daily-note <-> CalendarEvent binding + ActivitySpan correlation ===
Proves the Calendar edge end-to-end. Steps: (1) create a daily note for a fixed date via the existing knowledge-documents API; (2) drive the daily-note<->CalendarEvent binding (MT-067) so the daily note is bound to a real CalendarEvent row in PG (create the event via the existing calendar API or the binding command, NOT a direct mock); (3) assert the binding persists: reload the daily note and assert it carries the CalendarEvent id, and GET the CalendarEvent and assert it back-references the daily note doc_id; (4) generate an ActivitySpan correlated to that day (edits to documents on that date should correlate to an ActivitySpan); query the correlation and assert it returns the set of edited documents for the bound day (i.e. ActivitySpan correlation returns the edited documents); (5) assert GET /api/flight_recorder contains CALENDAR_EVENT_BOUND and ACTIVITY_SPAN_CORRELATED events for the workspace/day. Reach the binding command via AccessKit id (swarm path). Real PG / real EventLedger only.

=== SCENARIO OP-03 — Locus interop (Pillar 6): locus:// cross-reference resolve + reverse lookup ===
Proves the Locus edge end-to-end. Steps: (1) create a WP/MT-style governed entity addressable by a locus:// URI (reuse the Locus cross-reference layer from MT-066; if Locus addressing requires a seeded governance entity, seed it via the existing API, not a mock); (2) in a note, insert a locus:// reference (e.g. locus://wp/WP-KERNEL-012/mt/MT-066) as a cross-reference node; save the note; (3) resolve the reference: drive the resolve path (via AccessKit id for the swarm path) and assert it resolves to the correct WP/MT target (returns the target's stable id and a resolvable title/anchor); (4) reverse lookup: query the Locus reverse-index for that WP/MT and assert it lists the referencing document(s) — i.e. the note created in step 2 appears in the reverse lookup result; (5) assert GET /api/flight_recorder contains LOCUS_REF_RESOLVED and LOCUS_REVERSE_LOOKUP events for the workspace. Real PG only; the reverse index must be the real persisted index, not an in-memory map built by the test.

=== SCENARIO OP-04 — Swarm path: out-of-process agent drives each interop edge purely via AccessKit ids ===
Proves all three edges (Stage, Calendar, Locus) are addressable by an out-of-process agent with zero screen-reading. original_scope.summary:
Goal: give the native editors full Unicode glyph coverage by replacing the Latin-only font set with an ORDERED FONT FALLBACK CHAIN in egui, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean (CJK), Cyrillic, Greek, math/currency/arrow symbols, box-drawing, and emoji all render real glyphs instead of tofu boxes. This is the FOUNDATIONAL i18n MT - MT-076 (IME input), MT-077 (segmentation/line-break), and MT-078 (RTL) all depend on the glyphs existing first. EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: edit the existing font installer src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs::install_fonts (app.rs:3626) to register additional faces and build the fallback chain; add the font assets under src/frontend/handshake_native/assets/fonts/; add a font-coverage test.

ROOT CAUSE (verified by KERNEL_BUILDER code inspection 2026-06-22): install_fonts currently does FontDefinitions::default() then inserts ONLY INTER_REGULAR (app.rs:654) + INTER_BOLD (app.rs:656). egui's default fonts contain NO CJK and only partial symbol coverage; Inter covers Latin + Cyrillic + Greek but no CJK. Any codepoint with no glyph in any registered font renders as the tofu/notdef box.

EXACT APPROACH (egui-native font fallback, NO cosmic-text):
1. egui FontDefinitions has `font_data: BTreeMap<String, FontData>` and `families: BTreeMap<FontFamily, Vec<String>>` where each family is an ORDERED fallback list - egui falls through to the next font when a glyph is missing in the current one. Build the chain by inserting each face into font_data and APPENDING its name to the Proportional and Monospace family vecs (Inter first, then CJK, then broad-Unicode, then emoji).
2. Register, in fallback order after Inter: a CJK face (Noto Sans CJK - see size decision below), a broad-Unicode face for symbols/math/currency/arrows (Noto Sans + Noto Sans Symbols / Noto Sans Math as needed), and keep an emoji face (egui default ships NotoEmoji - retain it). The Monospace family (code editor) gets the same fallbacks appended after the existing monospace face so code with CJK comments / box-drawing / symbols renders.
3. Verify Inter's bundled .ttf actually contains Cyrillic + Greek (the standard Inter build does); if the bundled face was Latin-subsetted, add Noto Sans (covers Latin-Extended + Cyrillic + Greek) as the fallback so those scripts never tofu.

CJK FONT SIZE DECISION (the implementing coder MUST choose + document one, grounded in research): (a) bundle a single Noto Sans CJK weight via include_bytes! (full pan-CJK Regular is ~16MB; acceptable for a desktop binary but heavy), OR (b) bundle a per-region subset (e.g. Noto Sans SC Regular covers most Simplified Han + common Kana/Hangul punctuation, smaller), OR (c) load a CJK font from the OS font directory at startup via a font-discovery path (no binary bloat, but OS-dependent - must fail-soft to a documented 'install a CJK font' empty-state, never panic). Prefer (a) or (b) for determinism; if (c), gate behind graceful fallback. Whatever is chosen, the CJK font file(s) live under assets/fonts/ (when bundled) and the choice + size is documented in a code comment + the validator handoff.
forbidden_paths: src/backend/** (no backend involvement - fonts are pure frontend)
acceptance_criteria: AC1: install_fonts builds an ordered fallback chain - the Proportional AND Monospace egui families each list Inter (or the primary) FIRST, then the CJK face, then the broad-Unicode/symbol face, then the emoji face; a unit test asserts each family vec contains the expected font names in fallback order.

AC2: A kittest screenshot of a doc containing 'English 中文 日本語 한국어 Русский Ελληνικά ∑∫∞ →€✓ 😀' renders REAL glyphs for every run with NO tofu/notdef boxes - verified by pixel/visual inspection of the PNG (no repeated identical notdef-box glyph).
AC3: CJK renders in BOTH the rich-text editor (proportional) and the code editor (monospace) - a code block / file containing a CJK comment shows real CJK glyphs in the monospace family.
AC4: Cyrillic and Greek render (verified against the actual bundled Inter face; if Inter lacks them, the Noto Sans fallback supplies them) - no tofu for 'Привет' / 'Καλημέρα'.
AC5: Common symbol/math/currency/arrow codepoints (∑ ∫ ∞ → € £ ✓ ✗ — box-drawing │─┌) render real glyphs.

AC6: A codepoint with NO glyph in ANY registered font (e.g. a Plane-15 private-use char) degrades gracefully to the single notdef box without panic and without breaking layout of surrounding text (graceful-degradation test).

AC7: The CJK font size decision (bundle-full / bundle-subset / OS-load) is documented in a code comment + handoff; if OS-load is chosen, a missing-font path fails soft to a visible 'CJK font not found - install one' state, never a panic.
AC8: No regression - the full crate test suite (every bin) stays green; existing Latin-only screenshots (MT-012/013/etc.) are unaffected by the added fallbacks.
proof_targets: PROOF1: cargo test -p handshake-native font_coverage -- --nocapture passes: family-fallback-order unit test + a glyph-presence assertion (for each target script, the chain resolves a representative codepoint to a non-notdef glyph via egui's font lookup).

PROOF2: egui_kittest screenshot tests/screenshots -> EXTERNAL Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp-kernel-012-mt-075/mt075_unicode_coverage.png rendering the multi-script string; pixel-asserted no-tofu (the notdef box glyph does not repeat across distinct scripts) + visually inspected.
PROOF3: cargo test -p handshake-native (FULL suite, every bin) = 0 failures (no regression from the font change - this touches the shared install_fonts used by every kittest).
PROOF4: cargo tree -d shows no new duplicate core crates from any added font crate; binary-size delta from bundled fonts is reported in the handoff.
implementation_notes: RESEARCH BASIS (field-standard, coder must verify current versions): Noto (“No Tofu”) is Google's pan-Unicode font family and the de-facto standard for broad coverage - Noto Sans CJK (SC/TC/JP/KR or the unified OTC), Noto Sans (Latin/Cyrillic/Greek/Latin-Extended), Noto Sans Symbols / Noto Sans Math, Noto Color/Emoji. egui's own CJK story is exactly this: users register a Noto/Source-Han face and append it to the family fallback vec (egui FAQ + egui examples). Source Han Sans is the Adobe equivalent. Reject: shipping a single mega-font, or relying on egui defaults (no CJK). Reject cosmic-text here - egui's built-in font_data + families fallback is sufficient for COVERAGE (shaping for complex scripts is MT-078's concern).

egui API: ctx.set_fonts(FontDefinitions) - mutate fonts.font_data.insert(name, FontData::from_static(bytes)) then fonts.families.get_mut(&FontFamily::Proportional).unwrap().push(name) and the same for FontFamily::Monospace. Order matters: primary face first, broad fallbacks after. This is the SAME install_fonts already in app.rs - extend it, do not fork.

LICENSING: Noto + Source Han are SIL OFL 1.1 (bundling allowed with the license file). If bundling, add the OFL license text under assets/fonts/ and note attribution. (Operator owns final licensing per GLOBAL-PRODUCTION - this note is engineering hygiene, not a legal gate.)

DO NOT stack the whole pan-CJK OTC if a regional subset suffices for the target market; document the size/coverage trade-off. CJK fonts dwarf the binary - a full Noto Sans CJK Regular is ~16MB; reported in PROOF4.

ARTIFACT HYGIENE (CX-212E): the screenshot goes to the EXTERNAL Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp-kernel-012-mt-075/ root via the external_artifact_dir() pattern (see tests/test_code_editor_panel.rs / test_keymap.rs) + assert_no_local_artifact_dir(); NEVER repo-local tests/screenshots/. A tracked font asset under assets/fonts/ is INTENTIONAL product content (not a test artifact) and is allowed; a tracked PNG under src/ is a hygiene failure.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: make text segmentation Unicode-correct across the rich-text and code editors for international text - (1) CJK line-breaking (no spaces -> break between ideographs per UAX#14), (2) grapheme-cluster caret movement (arrow keys / backspace move by user-perceived character, not byte/codepoint), and (3) correct word + character counts for CJK and other scripts. EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: line-break logic in rich_editor/renderer/line_layout.rs (+ code_editor virtual_lines/buffer where it wraps), grapheme movement in the cursor layer (rich_editor cursor + code_editor/cursor.rs), and the count fix in daily_notes/journal_panel.rs (footer) + a shared text-metrics helper.

WHAT'S WRONG TODAY (the gaps this closes):
- LINE-BREAK: egui's default line-breaking breaks on whitespace; a long unbroken CJK run (e.g. a Chinese paragraph) has no spaces, so it either overflows the wrap width or never wraps. CJK must break between (almost) any two ideographs, with UAX#14 rules forbidding breaks before closing punctuation / after opening punctuation (kinsoku).
- CARET: caret/backspace by char or byte splits a grapheme cluster - a flag emoji, a family ZWJ emoji (man+woman+girl), a combining-accent sequence, or a Hangul syllable can be torn in half. Movement must be by GRAPHEME CLUSTER (unicode-segmentation).
- COUNTS: MT-019's footer word count splits on whitespace; for CJK ('today I wrote' style) that is meaningless. Word count must use Unicode word boundaries (UAX#29 word segmentation, which handles CJK as per-character/per-run); character count = grapheme clusters (or scalar count, documented).

SCOPE OF CORRECTNESS (honest): this MT handles CJK + grapheme + Latin/Cyrillic/Greek word boundaries. FULL bidirectional reordering and complex-script (Arabic/Indic) shaping are MT-078's concern - this MT must not regress LTR behavior and may leave RTL line-break to MT-078.

AC2: UAX#14 kinsoku basics: a line never breaks BEFORE a closing bracket/period or AFTER an opening bracket - cargo test on the break-opportunity function with mixed CJK + punctuation.

AC3: Caret RIGHT/LEFT over a multi-codepoint grapheme (a family ZWJ emoji, a combining-accent 'e+\u0301', a flag) moves by the WHOLE cluster in one keypress, not into the middle - cargo test (rich + code editor).
AC4: Backspace deletes a whole grapheme cluster (deleting the family emoji removes all its codepoints, not one) - cargo test.

AC5: Word count for a CJK string counts via Unicode word boundaries (not whitespace tokens); a mixed 'Hello 世界 test' counts sensibly (documented rule) - cargo test on the count fn; the MT-019 footer uses it.
AC6: Character count = grapheme clusters (the family emoji counts as 1 character, not 7 codepoints) - cargo test; documented if scalar-count is chosen instead, with rationale.

Goal: support right-to-left (Arabic, Hebrew) and complex scripts (Arabic cursive joining, Indic reordering) as far as the egui layout stack honestly allows, and explicitly SURFACE the limits rather than render broken text. EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: a bidi/shaping layer (reuse the text_intl module from MT-077) feeding the rich + code renderers; a visible 'limited RTL/complex-script support' note where full shaping is unavailable. HONEST PROBLEM STATEMENT (the hard 10%, verified by the earlier egui rich-text research): immediate-mode egui's epaint layout does line-based LTR layout and does NOT natively perform (a) the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (visual reordering of mixed LTR/RTL runs), nor (b) complex-script shaping (Arabic letters change form by position - isolated/initial/medial/final cursive joining; Indic reordering/conjuncts).
