original_scope.summary:
Goal: Build the SHARED-MEMORY RING that is the substrate of the whole three-tier diagnostic decoupling (Master Spec v02.196 §5.8.6 + §6.13.4). This is the ROOT MT of WP-KERNEL-012: internal_diagnostics (Tier 2, written by Handshake) and Palmistry (Tier 3, read by the external watcher) both depend on this one ring protocol, so it MUST be a SHARED crate both binaries link, not a private module inside handshake-native. The ring is a fixed-size, memmap2-mapped, single-producer/single-consumer (SPSC) lock-free ring with a seqlock-versioned header so a frozen/slow reader can NEVER back-pressure or tear the writer (the writer is the Handshake UI thread, which must never block on diagnostics). It also defines the TYPED-ALLOWLIST DiagEvent record schema used by every later MT.

Exact crate to create (NEW workspace member, separate from handshake-native and palmistry):
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/Cargo.toml` — a small standalone library crate named `handshake-diag-ring` (`[package] name = "handshake-diag-ring"`, `edition = "2021"`, `publish = false`, its own `[workspace]` table so it stands alone exactly like handshake-native does — the repo has NO root cargo workspace per the handshake-native Cargo.toml header). Place it as a SIBLING of `src/frontend/handshake_native/` (i.e. `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/`) so both the Handshake crate and the palmistry crate (MT-089) can declare it via a relative `path = ` dependency. Dependencies: `memmap2 = "0.9"` (the OS shared-memory map; the latest 0.9 line is 0.9.11 as of 2026-06-27), `bytemuck = "1"` (zero-copy plain-old-data cast of the header + records into the mapped bytes — derive `Pod`/`Zeroable`), `serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }` (DiagEvent (de)serialization for tests + later survivor-store JSON). NO tokio, NO egui, NO reqwest — this crate is pure substrate.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/.cargo/config.toml` — redirect `[build] target-dir` to the EXTERNAL artifact root so this crate NEVER creates a sibling `target/` folder. Use `target-dir = "../../../../../Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-diag-ring-target"` (count the `../` from the diag_ring crate dir to the `Handshake Worktrees/` parent that holds `Handshake_Artifacts/`; the handshake-native crate one level up uses four `../`, so this nested crate uses five — VERIFY the depth by resolving the path before committing). DO NOT create a repo-local `target/`.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/src/lib.rs` — declares `pub mod ring;` and `pub mod schema;` and re-exports the public types.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/src/ring.rs` — the seqlock SPSC ring.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/src/schema.rs` — the typed-allowlist DiagEvent record.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/tests/test_ring_roundtrip.rs` + `tests/test_seqlock_torn_read.rs` + `tests/test_schema_allowlist.rs`.

Ring design (ring.rs) — research basis: the Linux seqlock pattern (writer bumps a u32 sequence BEFORE and AFTER each write; an odd sequence means a write is in progress, and a changed sequence between the reader's two reads means it raced a write, so the reader RETRIES — this is exactly how the kernel publishes time without locks, and it is the standard lock-free single-writer publish primitive). Layout, all `#[repr(C)]` POD so the memory map is ABI-stable cross-process:
- `RingHeader { magic: u64, version: u32, record_size: u32, capacity: u32, write_index: u32, heartbeat: HeartbeatSlot, _pad: [u8; N] }` — `magic` is a fixed constant (e.g. 0x48534B5F44494147 = "HSK_DIAG") the reader checks to refuse a foreign/garbage map; `version` lets MT-096/WP-016 evolve the layout; `capacity` is the fixed number of record slots (default 1024).
- `HeartbeatSlot { seq: u32, counter: u64, timestamp_nanos: u64, _pad }` — the RESERVED heartbeat slot (a monotonic frame counter + a monotonic timestamp, written by MT-084 every egui frame; read by Palmistry MT-090/MT-091 with zero cooperation). It is its OWN seqlock-protected slot in the header (not a record) so a freeze probe reads ONLY the heartbeat without scanning records.
- Each record slot: `RecordSlot { seq: u32, event: DiagEvent }` (DiagEvent is fixed-size POD from schema.rs). The whole region is `header + capacity * size_of::<RecordSlot>()`.
- `DiagRingWriter` (Handshake side): `create(name: &str, capacity: u32) -> io::Result<Self>` maps a named shared region of the exact computed size and writes the header. `write(event: DiagEvent)` does: pick slot = `write_index % capacity`; bump that slot's `seq` to odd (`fetch_add(1)` semantics via `core::sync::atomic` on the mapped bytes, or a volatile store + `Ordering::Release`); write the record bytes; bump `seq` to even again; then advance `write_index` (Release). NON-BLOCKING + WAIT-FREE: the writer NEVER waits on the reader — overwriting an unread slot is allowed by design (a slow reader loses old records, it never stalls Handshake). `write_heartbeat(counter, timestamp_nanos)` does the same odd/even seq dance on the HeartbeatSlot.
- `DiagRingReader` (Palmistry side): `open(name: &str) -> io::Result<Self>` maps the SAME named region read-only-ish, checks `magic` + `version`. `read_heartbeat() -> Option<Heartbeat>` does the seqlock read: read `seq` (retry if odd), read counter+timestamp, re-read `seq`; if it changed, retry (bounded retry count, e.g. 16, then return the last consistent value or None). `read_last_n(n) -> Vec<DiagEvent>` walks back from `write_index` reading each slot under the same seqlock retry, skipping any slot whose seq is odd or changed (torn) — returns only CONSISTENT records.
- Cross-process named shared memory on Windows: memmap2's `MmapMut` maps a FILE, not a Win32 named section directly. Use a NAMED FILE in the OS temp dir as the backing (e.g. `%TEMP%/handshake-diag-<session-id>.ring`) and `memmap2::MmapMut::map_mut` over it — both processes map the SAME file path and share pages. This is the portable, field-standard memmap2 cross-process pattern (the alternative, raw Win32 `CreateFileMappingW` with a `Global\` name, is NOT portable and not needed). The backing file path (NOT a Win32 object name) is what Handshake passes to Palmistry (MT-089/MT-094). DOCUMENT this choice in the module doc.

DiagEvent typed-allowlist schema (schema.rs) — this is the HARD privacy invariant from §5.8.3 + §6.13.8: NO project content, NO sensitive data, NO free text, NO file contents, NO prompts, NO document bodies. EVERY field is a mechanical primitive. Define:
- `DiagEvent { event_code: u16, phase_marker: u8, severity: u8, thread_id: u64, sequence_id: u64, counter_a: u64, counter_b: u64, metric_micros: u64, timestamp_nanos: u64 }` — all fixed-width integers, `#[repr(C)]`, `Pod + Zeroable`. NO `String`, NO `Vec`, NO `&str`, NO byte blob.
- `event_code: u16` is a value from a CLOSED enum `DiagEventCode` (`#[repr(u16)]`): e.g. `Heartbeat`, `PanicCaught`, `SlowFrame`, `ResourceSample`, `BackendUnreachable`, `BackendRecovered`, `PaneMounted`, `FreezeSuspected`, `CrashDetected`, `PalmistryHandshake`, `Shutdown`, `Other`. Adding a code is a code change reviewed against the allowlist; a caller cannot smuggle arbitrary text because there IS no text field.
- `phase_marker: u8` from a small `DiagPhase` enum (`Start`, `Tick`, `End`, `Recovered`, `Degraded`); `severity: u8` from `DiagSeverity` (`Info`, `Warn`, `Error`).
- Provide `DiagEvent::heartbeat(...)`, `DiagEvent::resource_sample(cpu_milli, rss_kb, ...)`, etc. constructor helpers so call sites cannot hand-roll a malformed event.
- Provide a compile-time + test guarantee that the struct contains NO pointer/heap field: a `const _: () = assert!(size_of::<DiagEvent>() == EXPECTED);` and a test that the type is `Pod` (bytemuck enforces no padding-UB / no non-POD field at the type level — bytemuck's derive FAILS to compile if you add a `String`).

Reuse / placement note: handshake-native is a STANDALONE `[workspace]` crate (no repo root workspace — see its Cargo.toml header). This new crate is ALSO standalone with its own `[workspace]`; handshake-native (MT-082) and palmistry (MT-089) depend on it via `handshake-diag-ring = { path = "diag_ring" }` / `path = "../handshake_native/diag_ring"` relative deps. NO backend involvement: this is pure local shared memory, src/backend is untouched.

Risk if missed: every other MT in WP-KERNEL-012 is blocked. internal_diagnostics (MT-082) has nothing to write to; Palmistry (MT-090/011/012) has nothing to read; the heartbeat (MT-084) has no slot; the typed-allowlist invariant (MT-096) has no schema to enforce. A wrong seqlock here means torn reads of the heartbeat under freeze, which is the single most safety-critical read in the whole watcher.

implementation_notes: Use `core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering}` over the mapped bytes for the seq + write_index + heartbeat fields (cast the mapped &[u8] region to the atomic via bytemuck/pointer with the correct alignment); Release on the writer's post-write seq bump, Acquire on the reader's seq reads — this is what gives the happens-before that prevents torn reads. Document the ordering choice.

The seqlock writer protocol is: store seq (odd) Release; store payload; store seq (even, == old+2) Release. The reader protocol is: load seq Acquire (retry while odd, bounded); load payload; load seq Acquire again; if unchanged accept, else retry (bounded). Bound the retries so a pathologically hot writer cannot livelock the reader — after the bound, return None/last-good.

memmap2 cross-process sharing is via a SHARED BACKING FILE both processes map (not an anonymous map). Create/truncate the file to the exact region size with set_len before map_mut. Put the backing file under the OS temp dir with the session id in the name so parallel Handshake instances do not collide.
Keep capacity + record_size in the header so the reader validates the writer's layout matches its own compiled expectation (refuse on mismatch — forward/backward-compat guard for WP-016).

DiagEvent MUST stay POD: prefer `bytemuck::Pod + Zeroable` derives; bytemuck refuses to derive Pod for a type with any non-POD field, which is a COMPILE-TIME enforcement of the no-free-text allowlist — lean on it.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Build the `internal_diagnostics` MODULE inside handshake-native and its OPEN diagnostic-event API (Master Spec v02.196 §5.8.2 'Open diagnostic-event API' + §5.8.4). This is Tier 2 of the three-tier model. The module owns a process-global diagnostics facade: any feature (backend call site, widget, GUI action, job bridge) calls `diagnostics::record(DiagEvent)` and the event is (a) written to the MT-081 shared-memory ring (so the external Palmistry watcher sees it) AND (b) appended to a small in-process ring buffer the in-app Diagnostics Panel (MT-087) reads. Per §5.8.2 the API is OPEN BY DESIGN so nothing built is left un-instrumented. CRITICAL (no dead code / wire-into-live, HBR-INT + Spec-Realism Gate): this MT MUST wire AT LEAST ONE real, live call site so `record()` is actually CONSUMED by the running app, not scaffolding.

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/mod.rs` — the module root. Declares submodules and exposes the public API. Add `pub mod diagnostics;` to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/lib.rs` (alphabetically near `debug_console`).
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/recorder.rs` — the `DiagnosticsRecorder` struct + the process-global facade.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml` — add the path dependency `handshake-diag-ring = { path = "diag_ring" }` (the crate created in MT-081).
- EDIT one LIVE call site to prove consumption (see step 5).
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_internal_diagnostics.rs`.

API shape (recorder.rs):
- `pub struct DiagnosticsRecorder { writer: Option<DiagRingWriter>, buffer: Mutex<VecDeque<DiagEvent>>, dropped: AtomicU64 }` — `writer` is the MT-081 `handshake_diag_ring::DiagRingWriter` (None in a headless/test shell that did not create a ring — graceful degradation, never a panic); `buffer` is a bounded in-process last-N (cap 512) the panel reads; `dropped` counts events shed when contended (never blocks).
- `pub fn record(event: DiagEvent)` — the OPEN public API. Pushes to the in-process buffer (bounded; drop-oldest, never grow unbounded, never block the caller) AND calls `writer.write(event)` if a writer is installed. MUST be cheap + non-blocking + panic-free: a poisoned mutex is recovered (`into_inner`), a full buffer drops the oldest, a missing writer is a silent no-op on the ring side. The UI thread calls this every frame (MT-084/005) so it cannot allocate-heavy or lock-contend.
- `pub fn record_with(code: DiagEventCode, phase: DiagPhase, severity: DiagSeverity, counters...)` — ergonomic helper that builds a typed DiagEvent and calls `record`; keeps call sites from hand-rolling.
- `pub fn install(writer: DiagRingWriter)` / a `OnceLock<DiagnosticsRecorder>` global so `record()` is callable from ANY module without threading a handle (the spec's 'any feature MAY call' requirement). Before install, `record()` buffers in-process only (no ring) — still works, just not visible to Palmistry yet.
- `pub fn snapshot_last_n(n: usize) -> Vec<DiagEvent>` + `pub fn dropped_count() -> u64` — what the panel (MT-087) reads.
- The recorder NEVER stores anything but DiagEvent (the MT-081 typed allowlist), so the no-sensitive-data invariant is structural: there is no API surface that accepts free text.

Where to install the writer (HandshakeApp::new): in `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs` `HandshakeApp::new(cc)` (line ~1181), after the runtime/clients are set up, create the ring writer (named by a per-session id) and call `diagnostics::install(writer)`. The session id + ring backing-file path are needed by MT-094 (passed to Palmistry), so store them on HandshakeApp (a `diag_session: DiagSession { session_id, ring_path }` field). If ring creation fails (e.g. temp dir unwritable), log a tracing::warn and continue WITHOUT a writer (graceful degradation — the app still runs, diagnostics are in-process-only). This app.rs edit is the install point; the per-frame heartbeat/record calls are MT-084/005 (this MT just installs + proves one consume).

Step 5 — the REQUIRED live call site (proves consumption, not dead code): wire `diagnostics::record_with(DiagEventCode::PaneMounted, ...)` (or a similarly cheap existing lifecycle event) at ONE real runtime point that fires in the normal app run — e.g. in `app.rs` when a pane is first mounted, or a `DiagEventCode::Other`/startup marker recorded once in `HandshakeApp::new` right after install. The point is that a NORMAL launch produces at least one real DiagEvent in the ring + buffer with zero test scaffolding. (MT-084 heartbeat + MT-085 frame-time + MT-086 resource counters + MT-088 backend-unreachable are the fuller instrumentation; this MT proves the pipe is live with one consumer.)

Reuse note: app.rs already owns the tokio runtime handle + per-session state (workspace id, clients) — reuse those, do not mint a second runtime. The in-process buffer mirrors the existing bounded-error-ring pattern event_emitter.rs already uses (cap-20 in-memory error ring) — same shape, cap 512. src/backend untouched.

Risk if missed: nothing can record diagnostics; MT-084/005/006/007/008 all have no API to call; the open-API spec requirement (§5.8.2) is unmet; and a panel with no producer is empty.

Goal: Install a `std::panic::set_hook` PANIC HOOK in the native app that, on any Rust panic, writes a DURABLE LOCAL crash record (thread name/id, panic location file:line:col, a captured backtrace, a monotonic + wall timestamp) to local disk AND signals the MT-081 ring with a typed `DiagEventCode::PanicCaught` event, BEFORE delegating to the default panic behavior. This is the internal_diagnostics (Tier 2) panic-record component named in Master Spec v02.196 §5.8.2 ('durable crash record'). It is the IN-PROCESS crash capture; the out-of-process minidump is Palmistry's job (MT-092) — this MT is the in-process half that records what the process itself can still record on the way down.

TYPED-ALLOWLIST CONSTRAINT (HARD, §5.8.3): the crash record is mechanical only — thread id, panic source LOCATION (the file:line:col of the panic site is allowed; it is code position, not project data), backtrace frames (symbol names / addresses — code structure, not user data), counters, timestamps. The panic MESSAGE string is the ONE risk surface (a panic payload can contain interpolated values). Policy: DO NOT write the raw panic payload string into the ring DiagEvent (the ring is strictly typed integers — there is no string field, so this is structural). For the durable on-disk record, write the panic location + backtrace, and either OMIT the free-form payload message or write it only into a SEPARATE local-only crash file that is clearly marked local-only and never forwarded to the ring or FR without the typed-allowlist filter (MT-093 forwards only the typed fields). original_scope.summary:
Goal: Bump the MT-081 ring HEARTBEAT slot on EVERY egui frame from the UI thread (Master Spec v02.196 §5.8.2 'UI-thread heartbeat -- a frame-loop counter plus a monotonic timestamp, written every frame into a shared-memory ring buffer' + §6.13.4/§6.13.5). This is THE liveness signal Palmistry polls: a stalled UI thread stops advancing the counter, and the staleness is observable out-of-process with zero cooperation. This is the single most important producer in the whole WP — if the heartbeat does not advance every frame, freeze detection (MT-091) is blind.

Exact edit (ONE precise wire-in point):
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs` `impl eframe::App for HandshakeApp` `fn update(&mut self, ctx, _frame)` (currently at line ~6782 — it calls `self.ui(ctx)` then the MCP snapshot block). Add a heartbeat bump at the TOP of `update` (or immediately after `self.ui(ctx)` — top is preferred so the counter advances even if a later panic aborts the frame; a freeze inside ui() then shows as a stale heartbeat, which is exactly what we want). Maintain a `frame_counter: u64` field on HandshakeApp, increment it each `update`, read a monotonic timestamp, and call `diagnostics::heartbeat(frame_counter, timestamp_nanos)` which forwards to `DiagRingWriter::write_heartbeat` (MT-081) via the MT-082 recorder.
- ADD a `frame_counter: u64` field to the HandshakeApp struct (init 0 in `HandshakeApp::new`).
- The timestamp: use a process-start `std::time::Instant` (monotonic, immune to wall-clock changes) for the elapsed-nanos counter the staleness check uses, and optionally a wall `SystemTime` for the human-readable panel. The freeze threshold (MT-091) compares the MONOTONIC value, so the heartbeat MUST write a monotonic source. Store the start Instant on HandshakeApp (or in the recorder).
- Add a thin `pub fn heartbeat(counter: u64, timestamp_nanos: u64)` to `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/recorder.rs` (mod.rs re-export) that writes the heartbeat slot (NOT a record — the heartbeat is its own header slot in MT-081) and is a no-op if no writer is installed (graceful degradation).

CRITICAL — the heartbeat write MUST be wait-free + allocation-free on the frame path (the whole point is it never blocks the UI thread): it is a single seqlock store of two integers into the mapped header (MT-081 write_heartbeat). No lock contention with the record buffer, no format!, no allocation. egui repaints on demand by default; for the heartbeat to advance even when the UI is idle (so an idle app is not mistaken for a frozen one), call `ctx.request_repaint_after(Duration::from_millis(~250))` from update so the frame loop ticks at least ~4 Hz even with no input. This bounds the idle heartbeat cadence ABOVE Palmistry's poll (MT-091 polls ~200-500ms) and well below the ~5s freeze threshold, so an idle (but healthy) app never trips a false freeze. (Verify this does not regress HBR-QUIET/idle-CPU expectations — a 4 Hz wake is cheap; document the tradeoff.)

Reuse note: `fn update` already exists and already calls request_repaint conditionally for the MCP path — extend that pattern. The diagnostics recorder + ring writer are MT-081/MT-082. No backend involvement. egui_kittest can drive frames via `Harness::step()` / `run()` to prove the counter advances.

Risk if missed: Palmistry has no liveness signal; freeze detection (MT-091) cannot work; a healthy-but-idle app could be misread as frozen (if request_repaint cadence is wrong) or a real freeze could go undetected (if the heartbeat is on the wrong thread or written off-frame).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Track per-frame FRAME TIME on the UI thread and emit a typed `internal_diagnostics` event when a frame is SLOW (Master Spec v02.196 §5.8.2 'frame-time and resource counters'). Frame-time is the in-process degradation signal BELOW a full freeze: a frame that takes 250ms is not yet a 5s freeze, but it is a stutter the Diagnostics Panel (MT-087) should surface and the panel's frame-time stats (§5.8.4) need. This is the cheap in-process complement to Palmistry's external freeze detection.

Exact edit (build on MT-084's wire-in point):
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs` `fn update` — alongside the MT-084 heartbeat, measure the wall duration of the frame. Use a `last_frame_instant: Option<Instant>` field on HandshakeApp: at the top of `update`, compute `dt = now - last_frame_instant` (the inter-frame interval) and store `now`; this is the frame period. (Optionally also measure the WORK time inside update by sampling an Instant before `self.ui(ctx)` and after — the period is simplest + sufficient for the slow-frame flag; document which you use.)
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/frame_timing.rs` — a `FrameTimer` helper: rolling stats (last, min, max, and a small ring of the last ~120 frame durations for a p50/p95 the panel reads) + a `record_frame(dt: Duration)` that updates the stats and, when `dt` exceeds a SLOW threshold (default ~100ms => below ~10fps; make it a const, tune so normal 60fps frames never flag), calls `diagnostics::record_with(DiagEventCode::SlowFrame, DiagPhase::Tick, DiagSeverity::Warn, frame_micros, ...)`. Declare `pub mod frame_timing;` in diagnostics/mod.rs.
- Expose `pub fn frame_stats() -> FrameStats` (last/min/max/p50/p95 in micros) for the panel (MT-087). All typed integers (micros) — no content.
- DEBOUNCE the SlowFrame event so a sustained slow period does not flood the ring (e.g. emit at most one SlowFrame per ~1s window, or only on the rising edge into a slow streak + a count) — the ring is bounded (MT-081) and flooding it with SlowFrame would evict useful events. Use a simple last-emit Instant gate.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_frame_timing.rs`.

Why the threshold matters (no false flags): the SlowFrame threshold (~100ms) sits ABOVE a normal 16ms (60fps) / 33ms (30fps) frame and the ~250ms idle-repaint cadence from MT-084 — BUT the idle 250ms repaint period would itself look like a slow frame if you measure the PERIOD. AVOID THIS: either measure WORK time inside update (before/after self.ui), OR exclude the idle path (only flag when the app was actively repainting due to input/animation, not the idle keep-alive). Document the chosen approach so the idle keep-alive heartbeat (MT-084) does not generate spurious SlowFrame spam. Measuring update WORK time (Instant around self.ui(ctx)) is the cleaner choice and is recommended.

No backend. egui_kittest drives frames; a slow frame can be simulated by sleeping inside a test pane or by feeding a known duration to FrameTimer::record_frame directly (unit-level) plus a kittest that a real slow frame flags.

Risk if missed: no frame-time stats for the panel (§5.8.4 unmet); stutters below the freeze threshold are invisible; OR (if done wrong) the idle keep-alive is mis-flagged as slow, flooding the ring and burying real events.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Sample CPU%, resident memory (RSS), and GPU/driver identity as periodic typed `internal_diagnostics` RESOURCE COUNTERS (Master Spec v02.196 §5.8.2 'resource counters'). The §6.13.1 'pinned under heavy CPU' stall mode means CPU% is a first-class signal Palmistry/the panel care about. CPU + RSS are sampled periodically off the hot frame path; GPU adapter info is read ONCE at startup from the already-initialized wgpu render state (it is static identity, not a per-frame counter).

Exact files to create/edit:
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml` — promote `sysinfo` from a [dev-dependencies] entry to a real [dependencies] entry. NOTE (version drift, VERIFY): handshake-native currently has `sysinfo = "0.33"` under [dev-dependencies] (used by the MT-045 perf suite). The current crates.io sysinfo is 0.39.5 (verified 2026-06-27). To avoid a DUPLICATE sysinfo family in the locked graph, pin the new runtime dep to the SAME line already locked (0.33) UNLESS the coder upgrades both the dev-dep and the runtime dep together to 0.39 in one step and re-runs `cargo tree -d` to confirm a single sysinfo core. Pick one and record it; do NOT leave two sysinfo majors in the graph. sysinfo gives cross-platform CPU% (per-process) + RSS (Windows GetProcessMemoryInfo, Linux /proc, macOS task_info) with no per-OS windows-sys feature add.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/resource_counters.rs` — a `ResourceSampler` that holds a `sysinfo::System` (refreshed for THIS process only — refresh_process(Pid::from_u32(std::process::id())) so we never read other processes' data, which would be both wasteful and a privacy concern) and a `sample() -> ResourceSample { cpu_milli: u64, rss_kb: u64 }` (cpu as integer milli-percent, rss in KB — typed integers). `record_sample()` calls `diagnostics::record_with(DiagEventCode::ResourceSample, ...)`.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/gpu_info.rs` — capture the wgpu adapter info ONCE. eframe with the wgpu renderer exposes the render state via `eframe::CreationContext::wgpu_render_state` (a `RenderState` with the `wgpu::Adapter`). In `HandshakeApp::new(cc)`, read `cc.wgpu_render_state` -> adapter `.get_info()` -> `AdapterInfo { name, vendor, device, device_type, driver, driver_info, backend }`. Map this to a TYPED record: vendor id (u32), device id (u32), device_type (enum -> u8), backend (enum -> u8). The driver NAME/INFO strings are vendor/driver identity (e.g. 'NVIDIA', 'D3D12') — field-standard hardware identity, NOT project data; they are allowed but keep them to a bounded set / store them once for the panel's hardware line, and DO NOT put strings into the typed ring DiagEvent (the ring is integers; emit the vendor/device/backend as integer codes via ResourceSample-adjacent fields, keep the human strings only in an in-process GpuInfo the panel reads). Document this split.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs` — (a) in `HandshakeApp::new`, capture GpuInfo once from cc.wgpu_render_state and store it; (b) drive periodic CPU/RSS sampling: sample at a bounded cadence (~1-2s, NOT every frame — CPU% needs an interval between refreshes to be meaningful and sysinfo refresh is not free) using a `last_sample_instant` gate inside `fn update`, OR a lightweight background timer; emit a ResourceSample event each interval. Sampling inside `fn update` behind a ~1s gate is the simplest correct approach (no extra thread) — but the sysinfo refresh must be cheap enough not to stutter the frame; if it is not, move the refresh to a `spawn_blocking` on the existing tokio runtime and only read the cached result on the frame. Choose + document.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_resource_counters.rs`.

Reuse note: sysinfo is ALREADY a (dev-)dependency — reuse the same crate, just the right scope + version. wgpu is ALREADY the eframe renderer (eframe = { features = ["wgpu", ...] }) and `cc.wgpu_render_state` is the supported eframe seam to reach the adapter — no new wgpu dep, no second device. The tokio runtime + `fn update` are already there. src/backend untouched.

Risk if missed: no CPU/RSS counters means the §6.13.1 heavy-CPU stall mode is invisible in-process and the panel's resource line (§5.8.4) is empty; a wrong sampling cadence either stutters the frame (too frequent sysinfo refresh) or gives meaningless CPU% (no interval between refreshes).
acceptance_criteria: AC-006-1: a test constructs a ResourceSampler, samples CPU% + RSS for THIS process (sysinfo refresh_process on the current pid only), and asserts the sample returns plausible typed integers (rss_kb > 0; cpu_milli is a non-negative integer) — and that the sampler refreshes ONLY the current process (not the whole system process table).
AC-006-2: a ResourceSample DiagEvent reaches the ring/buffer (typed integers only — cpu_milli, rss_kb — no content) via `record_sample`.

AC-006-3: GPU adapter info is captured once from `cc.wgpu_render_state` — a kittest (or the wgpu-screenshot-gated harness) constructs the real HandshakeApp and asserts a non-empty GpuInfo (vendor/device/backend codes set) is stored; the human driver strings are kept in the in-process GpuInfo only, NOT pushed into the typed ring DiagEvent.

AC-006-4: sampling cadence is bounded (~1-2s, not per-frame) and does not stutter the frame — a kittest steps many frames and asserts ResourceSample is emitted at the bounded interval (not every frame) and the frame loop stays responsive (no SlowFrame storm from the sampler).
AC-006-5: NO duplicate sysinfo family in the locked graph — `cargo tree -d -p handshake-native` shows a single sysinfo core (the chosen pin is recorded; the dev-dep + runtime dep agree).
AC-006-6: `cargo build -p handshake-native` (lib + bins) clean; clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean; full suite `-j 2` green; external target dir; no repo-local target/, no tracked artifact.

Goal: FIX THE LATENT BACKEND-DOWN FREEZE — the concrete bug from the 2026-06-26 live session — and enforce the HARD spec requirement that the native app DEGRADES, NOT FREEZES when a backend route is unreachable (Master Spec v02.196 §5.8.5 'Backend-down graceful degradation (HARD)': 'a UI path that can freeze the frame loop on an unreachable backend is a spec defect'). When the backend on 127.0.0.1:37501 is down, a mounted-pane load / backend call that runs `Handle::block_on` (or locks waiting on a backend result) ON THE UI THREAD stalls the egui frame loop — the app stops responding (Responding=false, CPU->0) instead of showing a 'disconnected' state. This MT makes those UI-thread backend interactions NON-BLOCKING (off-thread spawn + poll-if-finished), records a typed `BackendUnreachable` internal_diagnostics event, and RE-PROVES the 2026-06-26 repro: launch with the backend down, the app stays responsive and the heartbeat keeps advancing.

ROOT-CAUSE LOCATION (verified in this codebase — the coder MUST audit + confirm the exact live frame-path offenders, do not assume): `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs` contains BOTH the CORRECT pattern and the buggy one:

This is the off-thread + poll-if-finished pattern the whole fix must follow.
- OFFENDERS (audit + fix the ones reachable on the UI/frame path): `self.runtime.block_on(...)` at app.rs ~lines 979 and 1011 (and any other `block_on` / blocking backend call reachable from `fn update` / `ui()` / a `PaneFactory::render` / a mount path). original_scope.summary:
Goal: Create the NEW separate `palmistry` BINARY crate and implement its LIFECYCLE INVERSION (Master Spec v02.196 §6.13.2 'a separate palmistry executable, distinct from the Handshake process' + §6.13.3 'Lifecycle inversion (HARD)'). Palmistry is the Tier 3 external out-of-process watcher following the Google-Crashpad model: a SIBLING process, NOT a thread, NOT an in-process subsystem. This is the ROOT Palmistry MT — it builds the executable, its argument/env intake, its control socket, and the inverted lifecycle (launched with Handshake, survives parent death, closes ONLY on explicit Shutdown). The ring reader (MT-090), freeze detection (MT-091), crash/minidump (MT-092), survivor store + FR forward (MT-093), and the Handshake-side launch (MT-094) build on this.

LIFECYCLE INVERSION (the HARD §6.13.3 requirement — get this exactly right):
- Launched WITH Handshake at startup (the spawn is MT-094's Handshake-side job; this MT defines the binary + how it is invoked).
- CLOSES ONLY on explicit command — a deliberate Shutdown signal from Handshake or the operator over the control socket. NOT on parent death, NOT on a timer, NOT on EOF.
- SURVIVES parent death — if Handshake freezes or crashes, Palmistry KEEPS RUNNING so it can capture + persist the evidence. It holds the parent's OS process handle and WAITS on it: an unexpected parent exit BEFORE a Shutdown command is RECORDED (it is a crash/abnormal-exit signal for MT-092) and Palmistry continues running (it does NOT die) until either an explicit Shutdown arrives OR a bounded post-death finalize window elapses (capture the evidence, write the survivor record, then it MAY exit after the finalize — but it must NOT die at the instant of parent death).
- MUST NOT be a kill-on-job-close child — it MUST NOT be tied to the parent via a Win32 Job Object / process-group that terminates children when the parent dies (§6.13.3: 'A watcher that dies with its parent cannot record the parent's death'). The Handshake-side spawn (MT-094) must NOT add Palmistry to a kill-on-close job; this MT documents that constraint as a contract on the launcher and the watcher refuses/does-not-assume any job membership.

Exact crate to create (NEW workspace member, separate binary):
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/Cargo.toml` — `[package] name = "palmistry"`, `edition = "2021"`, `publish = false`, its own `[workspace]` table (standalone, like handshake-native + diag_ring). `[[bin]] name = "palmistry" path = "src/main.rs"`. Dependencies: `handshake-diag-ring = { path = "../handshake_native/diag_ring" }` (the MT-081 ring crate — relative path), `interprocess = "2"` (the cross-platform local-socket IPC for the control channel; latest 2.4.2 as of 2026-06-27), `serde`/`serde_json` (control-message + survivor-record JSON), `tracing`/`tracing-subscriber` (its own logging). On Windows for the parent-handle wait: `windows-sys = "0.61"` with `Win32_Foundation` + `Win32_System_Threading` (OpenProcess/WaitForSingleObject/GetExitCodeProcess) — matching the handshake-native windows-sys pin so the family is consistent. (minidumper/minidump-writer/crash-context are added in MT-092, not here.)
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/.cargo/config.toml` — redirect `[build] target-dir` into the EXTERNAL artifact root (`target-dir = "../../../../Handshake_Artifacts/palmistry-target"` — VERIFY the `../` depth resolves to the Handshake_Artifacts sibling before committing). NO repo-local target/.
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/main.rs` — arg/env intake + the lifecycle state machine + the control-socket server loop.
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/cli.rs` — parse the inputs: Handshake PID, session-id, ring backing-file path/name, control-socket name. Accept via CLI args AND/OR env vars (document which; env is often cleaner for a spawned sibling). Validate all are present; refuse to run partially-configured.
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/lifecycle.rs` — the parent-handle wait + the Shutdown-only exit logic + the post-death bounded finalize.
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/control.rs` — the interprocess `LocalSocketListener` server; the typed control protocol (a `ControlMessage` enum: `Shutdown`, `Ping`, `CrashContext{...}` (the MT-092 hand-off), and a `HandshakeHello{...}` startup handshake ack). Newline-delimited JSON over the local socket is fine.
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/tests/test_lifecycle.rs`.

Parent-handle wait (lifecycle.rs): on Windows, `OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, false, pid)` to get a handle to the parent, then `WaitForSingleObject(handle, timeout)` in a loop / on a dedicated thread; when it signals, the parent has EXITED. Read `GetExitCodeProcess` to distinguish a clean exit code from a crash code (corroborated by whether a Shutdown was received first). If the parent exited and NO Shutdown was received => abnormal exit (crash/kill) => record it (the typed signal MT-092 consumes) and ENTER the bounded post-death finalize, do NOT exit immediately. If a Shutdown WAS received first => clean shutdown => Palmistry may exit normally (and MUST NOT record a crash, §6.13 clean-shutdown rule). Provide a cross-platform-shaped abstraction (a `ParentWatch` trait) so the Windows impl is behind a seam; the proof runs on Windows.

THE LIFECYCLE PROOFS (the deliverable, §6.13.3): (1) launches with valid inputs and stays running (does not exit) with no Shutdown; (2) exits promptly + cleanly ONLY when a Shutdown control message arrives; (3) SURVIVES a HARD-KILL of the parent (spawn a dummy parent process, give Palmistry its PID, TerminateProcess/kill the dummy parent, assert Palmistry is STILL RUNNING after the parent is dead and that it RECORDED the abnormal parent exit) — then on a subsequent Shutdown (or the bounded finalize) it exits. This is the inversion: a normal child would die with its parent; Palmistry must outlive it and record its death.

Reuse note: the diag_ring crate (MT-081) is the shared dep. interprocess is the field-standard cross-platform local-socket crate (Unix domain sockets / Windows named pipes behind one API). windows-sys is already the handshake-native Windows dep family (match the pin). No backend involvement — Palmistry never talks to src/backend; it talks to Handshake via the ring (read) + the control socket, and to the FR only at recovery via Handshake's existing HTTP route (MT-093, from the Handshake side or a documented reuse).

Risk if missed: the entire Tier 3 watcher has no host process; the inversion done wrong (kill-on-job-close, or dying on parent death) makes the watcher useless precisely when it is needed (it cannot record the parent's death) — §6.13.3 calls that a spec defect.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/** (MT-081-owned; reuse via the path dep + public API)
src/frontend/handshake_native/** (the Handshake-side launch is MT-094; this MT builds the watcher only)
src/backend/** (Palmistry never touches the backend directly)
acceptance_criteria: AC-009-1: the `palmistry` binary builds (`cargo build -p palmistry`, external target dir) and runs; given valid inputs (parent PID, session-id, ring path, control-socket name via args/env) it starts, completes its startup, and STAYS RUNNING with no Shutdown (it does not exit on its own).
AC-009-2: it refuses to run partially-configured — missing any required input (PID / ring path / socket name) exits with a clear non-zero error, not a silent half-start.

AC-009-3 (CLOSES ONLY ON SHUTDOWN): with a connected control socket, sending a `Shutdown` control message causes Palmistry to exit promptly + cleanly (bounded exit time); WITHOUT a Shutdown it keeps running (a Ping does NOT cause exit). Proven by a test that pings, asserts still-alive, then shuts down and asserts exit.

AC-009-4 (SURVIVES PARENT DEATH — the inversion): a test spawns a DUMMY parent process, launches Palmistry with the dummy's PID, HARD-KILLS the dummy parent (TerminateProcess/kill), and asserts Palmistry is STILL RUNNING after the parent is dead AND that it RECORDED the abnormal parent exit (a typed parent-died signal in its state/log). It then exits on a subsequent Shutdown or the bounded post-death finalize — NOT at the instant of parent death.

AC-009-5 (NOT kill-on-job-close): the design + a documented contract on the MT-094 launcher ensures Palmistry is NOT added to a Win32 Job Object / process-group that terminates it on parent death; the survives-parent-death test (AC-009-4) is the behavioral proof, and a code/doc review confirms no job-membership assumption.

implementation_notes: The inversion is the whole point: a normal child dies with its parent; Palmistry must SURVIVE and RECORD the parent's death. Hold the parent handle (OpenProcess + WaitForSingleObject) and treat the signal as 'parent exited' — distinguish clean (Shutdown-received-first) from abnormal (no Shutdown) via GetExitCodeProcess + the Shutdown flag.

Do NOT add Palmistry to a Win32 Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (§6.13.3 spec defect). Document this as a hard contract on the MT-094 launcher; the watcher itself assumes no job membership.

interprocess 2.x LocalSocketListener gives a cross-platform local socket (Unix domain socket / Windows named pipe). Use newline-delimited JSON ControlMessage framing (Shutdown/Ping/CrashContext/HandshakeHello). The control socket is request-response for CONTROL only — liveness is observed PASSIVELY from the ring (MT-090), never requested over the socket (a frozen Handshake could not answer — §6.13.4).
Inputs via env vars are often cleaner for a spawned sibling (no quoting issues); CLI args are also fine. Validate all required inputs are present; refuse a partial start (AC-009-2).
Provide a ParentWatch seam so the Windows OpenProcess/WaitForSingleObject impl is behind a trait; the proof runs on Windows. Match the handshake-native windows-sys 0.61 pin + features family.

The post-death bounded finalize: on abnormal parent exit, capture/persist (MT-092/013 fill the capture), then either wait for Shutdown or exit after a bounded window — NEVER exit at the instant of death (that would lose the capture).
Read the KERNEL_BUILDER coder protocol under .GOV/ first; the survives-parent-death proof must HARD-KILL a real dummy parent and assert Palmistry is still alive — not a simulated/mocked parent exit.
ports_from_react: NONE (new native watcher binary; the Google-Crashpad architecture is the reference, §6.13.2)
binds_backend_api: NONE. Palmistry talks to Handshake via the shared ring (read, MT-090) + the control socket; it never calls src/backend directly. FR forwarding at recovery is MT-093 (via Handshake's existing HTTP route).

acceptance_and_requirement_map.original: AC-009-1: the `palmistry` binary builds (`cargo build -p palmistry`, external target dir) and runs; given valid inputs (parent PID, session-id, ring path, control-socket name via args/env) it starts, completes its startup, and STAYS RUNNING with no Shutdown (it does not exit on its own).
AC-009-2: it refuses to run partially-configured — missing any required input (PID / ring path / socket name) exits with a clear non-zero error, not a silent half-start.

AC-009-3 (CLOSES ONLY ON SHUTDOWN): with a connected control socket, sending a `Shutdown` control message causes Palmistry to exit promptly + cleanly (bounded exit time); WITHOUT a Shutdown it keeps running (a Ping does NOT cause exit). original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement Palmistry FREEZE DETECTION (Master Spec v02.196 §6.13.5): poll the ring heartbeat (~200-500ms); when it goes STALE (the frame-loop counter / monotonic timestamp stops advancing for longer than a threshold, default ~5s) AND the OS hung-window probe corroborates, declare a FREEZE. The double-signal (stale heartbeat + hung-window probe) avoids false positives during a legitimate long frame (§6.13.5: 'Staleness alone is corroborated by an OS hung-window probe ... before Palmistry declares a freeze'). A healthy, advancing heartbeat must NEVER trip a freeze.

Exact files to create/edit (inside the palmistry crate):
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/freeze_detect.rs` — a `FreezeDetector` that, on a poll tick (~200-500ms, between the MT-084 ~250ms idle heartbeat cadence and the ~5s threshold), reads the heartbeat via the MT-090 reader, tracks the last-seen counter + the wall time it was last observed to ADVANCE, and computes staleness = now - last_advance_time. When staleness > the threshold (~5s, a named const), it runs the hung-window probe; if the probe also says not-responding, it declares `FreezeState::Frozen` (with the stale duration + last heartbeat snapshot, typed integers). If the heartbeat advances again, it clears back to `Healthy` (a freeze can recover — the app may unfreeze).
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/hung_window_probe.rs` — the Windows hung-window probe. Use `SendMessageTimeoutW(hwnd, WM_NULL, 0, 0, SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG|SMTO_BLOCK, timeout_ms, &result)`: if it TIMES OUT, the window's message pump is not pumping => not responding (the standard Win32 hung-window check; it is what Task Manager uses for 'Not responding'). Resolve Handshake's top-level HWND from the parent PID (enumerate top-level windows via EnumWindows + GetWindowThreadProcessId, match the PID; pass the resolved HWND in or resolve once at startup). windows-sys features needed: `Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging` (SendMessageTimeoutW, EnumWindows, WM_NULL, the SMTO_ flags) + `Win32_Foundation` — add these to the palmistry Cargo.toml windows-sys features (matching the handshake-native family; Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging is already enabled there). Provide a `HungWindowProbe` trait so a headless/non-Windows test can inject a fake probe result.
- EDIT `src/frontend/palmistry/src/main.rs` — run the FreezeDetector poll in the watch loop (a dedicated poll thread / loop at the ~200-500ms cadence). On a Frozen transition, hand off to MT-093 (survivor store) — for THIS MT, record the freeze state + a typed `DiagEventCode::FreezeSuspected`-style marker in Palmistry's own state/log (the durable survivor record is MT-093).
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/tests/test_freeze_detect.rs`.

NO-FALSE-POSITIVE PROOF (the deliverable, §6.13.5): (1) HEALTHY: a test where the heartbeat keeps advancing (a writer bumps it faster than the threshold) and the FreezeDetector NEVER declares a freeze — even across many poll ticks, even past the ~5s threshold in wall time, because the counter keeps advancing. (2) FREEZE: a test where the writer STOPS bumping the heartbeat (simulated freeze), staleness crosses the threshold, the (injected/fake) hung-window probe returns not-responding, and the detector declares Frozen with the correct stale duration. (3) CORROBORATION: a test where the heartbeat is stale BUT the hung-window probe says responding (a borderline long frame) and the detector does NOT yet declare a hard freeze (or declares only a 'suspected' state, not a confirmed freeze) — proving the double-signal gate. (4) RECOVERY: after a freeze, the heartbeat resumes and the detector clears to Healthy.

THRESHOLD TUNING (no false positive on a healthy heartbeat — AC-011-1 is the gate): the poll cadence (~200-500ms) is BELOW the MT-084 idle heartbeat cadence (~250ms) — verify the chosen poll + threshold do not flag a healthy IDLE app (whose heartbeat advances every ~250ms via request_repaint_after). The ~5s threshold is >> the ~250ms idle cadence, so a healthy idle app never goes stale. Document the relationship between MT-084's idle cadence, this poll interval, and the freeze threshold so they are provably consistent.

Reuse note: the heartbeat read is the MT-090 reader; the parent PID + HWND resolution uses the MT-089 inputs + windows-sys (already the handshake-native Windows family). No backend. The hung-window probe is the standard Win32 SendMessageTimeout WM_NULL technique (Task Manager's 'Not responding' check).

Risk if missed: Palmistry cannot detect freezes (its primary §6.13.1 job); OR (false positives) it declares freezes on healthy long frames / idle apps, crying wolf and producing noise; OR (false negatives) a wrong staleness reference (e.g. comparing wall timestamps that jumped, or never resetting last_advance on a counter bump) misses real freezes or fires spuriously.
acceptance_criteria: AC-011-1 (NO FALSE POSITIVE — the gate): a test where the heartbeat keeps ADVANCING (a writer bumps it faster than the threshold, including at the ~250ms idle cadence) and the FreezeDetector NEVER declares a freeze across many poll ticks and past the ~5s wall-time threshold — a healthy/idle heartbeat must not trip a freeze.

AC-011-2 (FREEZE DETECTED): a test where the writer STOPS bumping the heartbeat, staleness crosses the ~5s threshold, the hung-window probe (injected fake = not-responding) corroborates, and the detector declares Frozen with the correct stale duration + last-heartbeat snapshot (typed integers).

AC-011-3 (CORROBORATION / double-signal): a test where the heartbeat is stale BUT the hung-window probe says responding (borderline long frame) and the detector does NOT declare a confirmed hard freeze (suspected-only, not confirmed) — proving the §6.13.5 double-signal gate prevents false positives on legitimate long frames.
AC-011-4 (RECOVERY): after a declared freeze, the heartbeat resumes advancing and the detector clears back to Healthy (a freeze can recover).

AC-011-5: the poll cadence (~200-500ms) + threshold (~5s) are named consts and provably consistent with MT-084's ~250ms idle heartbeat cadence (documented relationship); staleness is measured against a MONOTONIC reference (the heartbeat's monotonic timestamp + Palmistry's own monotonic clock), never a wall clock that can jump.

AC-011-6: the hung-window probe is the real Win32 SendMessageTimeoutW(WM_NULL, SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG) on Handshake's resolved top-level HWND (Windows); a `HungWindowProbe` trait allows a fake in headless tests. `cargo build -p palmistry` clean; clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean; external target dir; no repo-local target/.

PT-011-B: stale-heartbeat + corroborating probe => Frozen declared with correct duration; recovery clears to Healthy.
PT-011-C: corroboration test GREEN — stale-but-responding does not confirm a hard freeze (double-signal gate).

implementation_notes: Track last-SEEN heartbeat counter + the Palmistry monotonic time it was last observed to ADVANCE. staleness = now - last_advance_time. Reset last_advance_time every time the counter changes. NEVER compare wall clocks that can jump — use Palmistry's own Instant + the heartbeat's monotonic nanos (MT-084).

Double-signal (§6.13.5): stale heartbeat ALONE => suspected; stale heartbeat AND hung-window-probe-not-responding => confirmed Frozen. A legitimate long frame (stale but the window still pumps messages) must NOT confirm a hard freeze.

Hung-window probe: SendMessageTimeoutW(hwnd, WM_NULL, 0, 0, SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG|SMTO_BLOCK, timeout_ms, &result) — a TIMEOUT means the message pump is stuck (not responding). Use a HungWindowProbe trait so headless/CI tests inject a fake probe result (Windows GUI message-pump probing is awkward in CI); the real Win32 impl is behind the seam.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Implement Palmistry CRASH DETECTION + OUT-OF-PROCESS MINIDUMP capture (Master Spec v02.196 §6.13.6). Crash is detected two ways: (a) the PROCESS-HANDLE WAIT (MT-089's parent-handle wait signals on Handshake exit; an unexpected exit — no prior Shutdown — is a crash) and (b) Handshake's crash-handler `UnhandledExceptionFilter` hands a `CrashContext` to Palmistry over the control socket at the moment of an unhandled exception. On crash, Palmistry writes a MINIDUMP using an OUT-OF-PROCESS minidump writer (§6.13.6: 'the crashing process cannot reliably dump itself; the external writer captures the dump from outside'). A CLEAN Shutdown must NOT produce a crash record (§6.13 clean-shutdown rule + the MT-089 distinction).

FIELD CRATE STACK (the Embark/Rust-minidump out-of-process model — verified 2026-06-27): the canonical Rust out-of-process crash pipeline is `crash-handler` (installs the in-process exception handler in the CLIENT — here Handshake), `crash-context` (the typed CrashContext: exception pointers, thread id, process id — passed across the process boundary), `minidumper` (the client/server IPC pair: the crashing client signals the server, which writes the dump out-of-process), and `minidump-writer` (the actual out-of-process dump writer the server uses). This MT builds the Palmistry/SERVER side (the dump writer). The Handshake/CLIENT side (installing crash-handler + sending the CrashContext to Palmistry) is a small EDIT in handshake-native main.rs that is part of THIS MT's wiring but lives in the MT-094 launch path — coordinate: the client install can be done here (in handshake-native main.rs, within this MT's allowed_paths) OR deferred to MT-094; this contract puts the CLIENT install here so crash detection is end-to-end in one MT, and MT-094 only owns the process spawn + handshake.

Exact files to create/edit:
- EDIT `src/frontend/palmistry/Cargo.toml` — add `minidumper = "0.10"` (latest 0.10.1, 2026-06-27), `minidump-writer = "0.12"` (latest 0.12.0), `crash-context = "0.7"` (latest 0.7.0 — NOTE: the field research said 0.6; crates.io shows 0.7.0, a drift UP — pin 0.7 and record the correction), and `minidump = "0.26"` (latest 0.26.1, the reader, used in tests to VALIDATE the written dump parses). All from the Embark/rust-minidump ecosystem; verify they resolve to a single consistent set (cargo tree -d).
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/crash_capture.rs` — the Palmistry-side crash capture: (a) a `minidumper::Server` listening on the same control transport (or a dedicated minidumper socket name passed from Handshake) that, on a client crash signal carrying the CrashContext, writes a minidump out-of-process via `minidump-writer` to a local file; (b) the process-handle-wait crash path (from MT-089): when the parent exits unexpectedly (no prior Shutdown), record a crash even if no CrashContext arrived (a hard kill / abrupt exit may not deliver one) — in that case write at least a crash RECORD with the exit code + last heartbeat/events (a full minidump may not be possible post-mortem without the client's cooperation, so a best-effort record is the floor; document the distinction between a CrashContext-driven minidump and a post-mortem record). Declare the module in main.rs.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/main.rs` (CLIENT side) — install `crash-handler`'s exception handler early in main(); in its on-crash callback, build the `crash-context::CrashContext` and send it to Palmistry via the minidumper client (so Palmistry, the server, writes the dump out-of-process). Keep the callback minimal + async-signal-safe-ish (do the minimum: signal the server with the context, let the EXTERNAL writer do the heavy dump). This complements the MT-083 in-process panic hook (panic = Rust panic; this = a hard unhandled OS exception / SEH on Windows). Document that the two cover different death modes.
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/tests/test_crash_capture.rs` + `src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_crash_client_install.rs`.

CLEAN-SHUTDOWN-IS-NOT-A-CRASH (§6.13, HARD): if a Shutdown control message was received before the parent exit, Palmistry writes NO crash record + NO minidump. Proven by a test: clean Shutdown then parent exit => no crash artifact. Only an UNEXPECTED exit (no Shutdown) or a delivered CrashContext produces a crash record/minidump.

TYPED-ALLOWLIST + LOCAL-ONLY (§6.13.8): the minidump itself contains thread stacks/registers/loaded modules (the OS process image — field-standard crash data, local-only by default, §6.13.8: 'Minidumps are local-only by default; any upload ... is consent-gated and never happens automatically'). Palmistry's own crash RECORD metadata (the JSON the survivor store reads, MT-093) is TYPED ALLOWLIST only: exit code, crash event code, thread id, timestamps, minidump file path — NO project content, NO free text. Do NOT auto-upload the minidump anywhere; write it local-only.

Reuse note: the parent-handle wait is MT-089 (reuse it as a crash signal). The control socket is MT-089. The minidumper/minidump-writer/crash-context/minidump crates are the field-standard Rust out-of-process crash stack. No backend.

Risk if missed: §6.13.6 crash capture is the other half of Palmistry's job (freeze=MT-091, crash=this); a self-dump (in-process) would be unreliable (the crashing process cannot dump itself — the whole point of out-of-process); a clean shutdown producing a false crash would flood the survivor store; an auto-uploaded minidump would violate §6.13.8 local-only/consent-gated.

implementation_notes: The Embark out-of-process crash model: crash-handler (client exception handler) -> crash-context (the typed context across the boundary) -> minidumper (client signals server) -> minidump-writer (server writes the dump out-of-process). Palmistry is the SERVER (writer); Handshake is the CLIENT.

The client on-crash callback must be minimal (signal the server with the CrashContext; the EXTERNAL writer does the dump). Do not do heavy work in the crashing process — that is the whole out-of-process point.

Two crash paths: (1) CrashContext-driven => a full minidump (the rich case). (2) process-handle-wait unexpected exit with no CrashContext (hard kill) => a best-effort crash RECORD (exit code + last heartbeat/events) — a full minidump may be impossible without the client's cooperation. Document the floor vs rich case.
CLEAN SHUTDOWN must produce NO crash artifact (§6.13). The Shutdown-flag-before-exit distinction is from MT-089; reuse it. AC-012-2 is the gate.

LOCAL-ONLY (§6.13.8): write the minidump to a local path; NEVER auto-upload. Any upload is consent-gated (out of scope here). The crash RECORD metadata is typed-allowlist integers + the local file path only.
This complements the MT-083 panic hook (different death mode). Document both so coverage is explicit (AC-012-7).

Goal: Implement Palmistry's DURABLE SURVIVOR STORE + recovery-time FLIGHT-RECORDER FORWARDING (Master Spec v02.196 §6.13.7). On a detected freeze (MT-091) or crash (MT-092), Palmistry persists a durable LOCAL survivor record (the freeze/crash timeline: last heartbeat snapshot, last-N events, OS hung-window probe result, minidump file path) that outlives the Handshake process. When Handshake RECOVERS (restarts after a crash, or unfreezes), Palmistry FORWARDS the captured freeze/crash records into the Flight Recorder (Tier 1) via the EXISTING FR HTTP route (reuse-via-API) so the out-of-process evidence rejoins the governed business-event ledger + shows up in the Diagnostics Panel (MT-087). CRITICAL HONESTY GATE (§6.13.7 + the FR-kept-as-is constraint): if the existing FR ingestion route CANNOT accept the forwarded record, surface a TYPED BLOCKER (honest) — do NOT fake the forward, do NOT edit the FR, do NOT invent a new FR route (the FR is forbidden_paths).

Exact files to create/edit (inside the palmistry crate + a thin reuse seam):
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/survivor_store.rs` — the durable local store. A `SurvivorRecord` (typed allowlist: record kind = Freeze|Crash, session-id, timestamps, stale-duration, last-heartbeat counter/timestamp, last-N DiagEvents (typed), hung-window-probe result, minidump path, exit code — NO project content / free text) serialized as JSON to a durable local dir (reuse the same portable per-user data dir convention as MT-083's crash dir, e.g. dirs-resolved `data_local_dir()/handshake/palmistry/survivors/`). ATOMIC writes (temp+rename) so a record survives a Palmistry restart. The store outlives both Handshake AND a Palmistry restart (read existing records on Palmistry startup).
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/fr_forward.rs` — the recovery-time forwarder. It REUSES the EXISTING Flight Recorder HTTP route. VERIFIED ROUTE (do not invent): `POST http://127.0.0.1:37501/api/flight_recorder/runtime_chat_event` is the verified FR ingestion endpoint (confirmed in the Handshake-side event_emitter.rs which posts exactly there, building a `RuntimeChatEventV0_1` body; the route requires an `actor_id` and a non-nil session UUID). The forwarder builds a FR event body carrying ONLY the typed survivor fields (event code, timestamps, counters, minidump path string as a local reference — NO project content), posts it to the FR route via reqwest, and on success marks the survivor record forwarded (idempotent — do not double-forward). HONESTY: if the FR route does NOT accept the survivor shape (e.g. runtime_chat_event's schema cannot represent a freeze/crash record, or it rejects the actor_id, or the route is absent), the forwarder returns a TYPED BLOCKER (`FrForwardBlocker::SchemaIncompatible` / `RouteAbsent` / `Rejected{status}`) and the survivor record stays local + flagged 'forward pending — typed blocker', surfaced honestly; it MUST NOT fabricate a success and MUST NOT edit the FR. The coder VERIFIES against the running FR whether runtime_chat_event can carry the survivor payload; if it cannot, the typed blocker is the correct, honest outcome (and a follow-on/WP-016 item to add a proper FR ingestion shape — without touching the FR here).
- WHO forwards (recovery detection): Palmistry detects Handshake recovery either (a) the heartbeat resumes advancing after a freeze (MT-091 recovery), or (b) a NEW Handshake instance reconnects to Palmistry's control socket / starts a new session (after a crash-restart). On either, drain the unforwarded survivor records and forward them. Forwarding can ALSO be initiated from the Handshake side on recovery (Handshake reads Palmistry's survivor store + posts to its own FR) — choose the simpler reliable path and document it; the constraint is the same: reuse the existing route, honest blocker if incompatible.
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/tests/test_survivor_store.rs` + `src/frontend/palmistry/tests/test_fr_forward.rs`.

TYPED-ALLOWLIST (§6.13.8): the survivor record + the forwarded FR body carry NO project content, NO free text — only typed integers, enums, timestamps, and local file-path references (the minidump path is a local path string, not project data). A test asserts the survivor record + the forward body contain no free-text/content field.

Risk if missed: §6.13.7 unmet (out-of-process evidence never rejoins the ledger; the Diagnostics Panel Tier-3 section stays empty); OR (the dishonest failure) a faked forward that claims success when the FR cannot actually accept the record — which would hide the real integration gap and violate the no-fake-runtime + FR-kept-as-is constraints.

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Make HANDSHAKE LAUNCH palmistry.exe at startup and complete the startup IPC HANDSHAKE (Master Spec v02.196 §6.13.3 'launched WITH Handshake at startup' + §6.13.2). At Handshake startup, the native app spawns the sibling `palmistry` process, passes it the Handshake PID + session-id + ring backing-file path + control-socket name (the MT-089 inputs), and completes a startup handshake (Palmistry acks it is watching). This MUST honor HBR-QUIET (§6.13 cross-ref HBR-QUIET-003): the spawned Palmistry process must NOT steal foreground / pop a window / hijack input — it is a headless background watcher.

LIFECYCLE-INVERSION LAUNCH CONSTRAINT (the HARD §6.13.3 contract on the launcher, from MT-089): the spawn MUST NOT add Palmistry to a Win32 Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (and must not put it in a process group that dies with the parent). A normal `std::process::Command::spawn` on Windows does NOT add the child to the parent's job by default, BUT eframe/winit or a wrapping launcher might; the spawn must explicitly ensure Palmistry is a free-standing process that survives parent death (MT-089 AC-009-4 is the behavioral proof; this MT must spawn it in a way that preserves that). Document the spawn flags used (e.g. on Windows, DETACHED_PROCESS / CREATE_NO_WINDOW for quiet headless, and NOT adding it to a kill-on-close job).

Exact files to create/edit:
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/palmistry_launch.rs` — `pub fn launch_palmistry(session: &DiagSession, ring_path: &Path, control_socket: &str) -> io::Result<PalmistryHandle>`. It resolves the palmistry.exe path RELATIVE to the running Handshake exe (`std::env::current_exe()` -> sibling `palmistry.exe`) — portable, no hardcoded path (the installer ships both binaries side by side; install_payload in handshake-native Cargo.toml already lists a two-binary layout — add palmistry.exe to that payload). Spawns it via `std::process::Command` with: the PID/session/ring/socket passed as env vars or args (matching MT-089's cli.rs intake), CREATE_NO_WINDOW + a detached/quiet flag (HBR-QUIET — no console window, no focus steal), stdout/stderr piped or to a log file (not inherited to steal the console). Returns a handle holding the child + the control-socket client for sending Shutdown later.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/main.rs` (or `app.rs` HandshakeApp::new) — call `launch_palmistry(...)` AFTER the ring writer is created (MT-082 install) + the session id is minted, EARLY in startup so the watcher is up before the app can freeze. Store the PalmistryHandle on HandshakeApp so a clean app shutdown sends the Shutdown control message (the §6.13.3 'closes only on explicit command' path — on a normal Handshake exit, send Shutdown so Palmistry exits cleanly + records NO crash). Graceful degradation: if palmistry.exe is missing or the spawn fails, log a tracing::warn + a typed BackendUnreachable-style diagnostic and CONTINUE (Handshake must run even without the watcher — the watcher is supplementary; never block startup on it).
- The IPC HANDSHAKE: after spawn, Handshake connects to Palmistry's control socket (MT-089 control.rs) and exchanges a `HandshakeHello{ pid, session_id, ring_path }` / ack so both sides confirm the channel + the ring binding before the app proceeds. Bounded: if Palmistry does not ack within a short deadline, log + continue degraded (do not hang startup waiting on the watcher).

original_scope.summary:
Goal: Define the HBR-INT-009 THREE-TIER DIAGNOSTIC EVIDENCE FORMAT — the `test_run_with_three_tier_diagnostic_wiring_record` evidence a WP emits to prove its FR / internal_diagnostics / Palmistry wiring per tier — plus a VALIDATOR-SIDE check that reads it and marks the acceptance rows. This is the GATE INFRA that WP-KERNEL-016 (the retrofit) and ALL future WPs use to satisfy HBR-INT-009 (Master Spec v02.196 §5.8/§6.13 + the CODER_PROTOCOL HBR-INT-009 duty + CX-981). Per the CODER_PROTOCOL, every observable runtime behavior an MT touches must record each of the three tiers as WIRED, NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason, or DEFERRED-with-reason. THIS MT makes that recording machine-readable + validator-checkable instead of prose-only.

IMPORTANT BOUNDARY (repo-gov vs product split): the EVIDENCE FORMAT + the validator check are GATE INFRA. Where they live depends on whether they are product code or governance tooling. Decompose:
- (A) The MACHINE-READABLE EVIDENCE SCHEMA (the JSON a WP/MT emits): this is a small typed schema + emitter usable by product test runs. Build it as a tiny product-side helper crate/module so a Rust test can EMIT a `ThreeTierDiagnosticWiringRecord` JSON artifact to the external artifact root during a WP's test run. Place under the palmistry/diag-ring shared area OR a small `diag_evidence` module — RECOMMEND: a module in the diag_ring crate (MT-081) since it is the shared substrate both binaries already depend on, OR a standalone tiny `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/three_tier_evidence.rs` if it is handshake-native-only. The schema mirrors the `hbr_int_009_tier_obligations` array shape already used in these MT contracts: an array of `{ tier: FLIGHT_RECORDER|INTERNAL_DIAGNOSTICS|PALMISTRY, status: WIRED|NOT_APPLICABLE|DEFERRED, reason: string, proof_ref: string }` plus run metadata (wp_id, mt_id, run timestamp, the observable behavior covered).
- (B) The VALIDATOR-SIDE CHECK (reads the emitted record, marks acceptance rows): this is GOVERNANCE tooling (it gates WP acceptance), so it belongs under .GOV/ governance scripts — BUT .GOV/ is forbidden_paths for the product-code coder lane. RESOLUTION: this MT builds the PRODUCT-SIDE half (the schema + emitter + a self-validating test that asserts a record is well-formed + every tier is accounted for), and SPECIFIES the governance-side validator as a typed HANDOFF to the validator/governance lane (an RGF item or a validator-protocol check), NOT a product-code edit to .GOV/. The coder must NOT write into .GOV/; instead emit the schema + a documented contract for what the validator check must assert, and raise it as the governance-side follow-on. (If the operator/orchestrator wants the validator check authored in .GOV/ in this MT, that is a governance-lane RGF, not this product MT.)

Exact files to create/edit (PRODUCT side only):
- CREATE the schema + emitter module (RECOMMENDED: `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/src/three_tier_evidence.rs`, re-exported from the diag_ring crate so both handshake-native + palmistry + any future WP can emit it; OR `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/three_tier_evidence.rs` if handshake-native-scoped — choose + document). Define `ThreeTierDiagnosticWiringRecord { wp_id, mt_id, observable_behavior, run_at, tiers: Vec<TierWiring> }`, `TierWiring { tier: DiagTier, status: WiringStatus, reason: String, proof_ref: String }`, `DiagTier { FlightRecorder, InternalDiagnostics, Palmistry }`, `WiringStatus { Wired, NotApplicable, Deferred }` — serde-serializable. Provide `emit(record, out_dir)` that writes `test_run_with_three_tier_diagnostic_wiring_record.json` to the external artifact root atomically. Provide a `validate(record) -> Result<(), Vec<ValidationError>>` that enforces: all THREE tiers present (no tier silently omitted — the CODER_PROTOCOL 'never silently skip it' rule), every NOT_APPLICABLE/DEFERRED carries a non-empty reason, every WIRED carries a non-empty proof_ref.
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/tests/test_three_tier_evidence.rs` (or the handshake-native tests dir if scoped there).
- Produce a DOCUMENTED CONTRACT (in the module doc + the MT implementation_result handoff) for the governance-side validator: what the validator must read (the emitted JSON), what it asserts (all three tiers accounted for, reasons/proof_refs present), and how it marks the WP acceptance rows. Raise the governance-side authoring as a typed handoff (RGF / validator-protocol update), NOT a .GOV/ product edit here.

WHY this is the gate WP-016 + future WPs use: WP-KERNEL-016 is the RETROFIT — it goes back over already-shipped features and records their three-tier wiring. This evidence format is what it emits per retrofitted surface, and the validator check is what marks those rows. Future WPs emit a `ThreeTierDiagnosticWiringRecord` per observable runtime behavior they touch (the CODER_PROTOCOL HBR-INT-009 duty), and the validator gate reads them. Reuse note: the `hbr_int_009_tier_obligations` array shape already used in every MT contract in THIS WP is the human/contract-side mirror of this machine record — keep them congruent (same tier names, same status vocabulary WIRED/NOT_APPLICABLE/DEFERRED) so a model reading either understands the other. serde/serde_json are available (diag_ring has serde; handshake-native has serde_json). The external artifact root is the standard Handshake_Artifacts target.

Goal: CAPSTONE end-to-end proof that the whole three-tier diagnostic system works as an integrated system on the real binaries (Master Spec v02.196 §5.8 + §6.13 + §10.12.5; HBR-INT-009). This MT runs the full system — real HandshakeApp + the real spawned palmistry.exe + the real shared-memory ring — through the four scenarios the WP exists to handle, proves each, asserts the typed-allowlist privacy invariant holds across EVERY artifact, and writes a proof manifest. It is integration-level: it WIRES the pieces from MT-081..015 together and proves them as a whole; it does not re-implement them.

THE FOUR END-TO-END SCENARIOS (each a real run, no mocks for the spec-required runtime):
- (1) FORCE A FREEZE: launch the real HandshakeApp (which spawns palmistry.exe, MT-094), then STALL the UI thread (e.g. a test seam / a test-only pane that blocks the egui frame loop past the ~5s threshold). Assert: the heartbeat goes stale (MT-084), Palmistry detects the freeze via stale-heartbeat + hung-window probe (MT-091), Palmistry CAPTURES + SURVIVES (it is still running while Handshake is frozen, MT-089/010), and RECORDS the last state into the survivor store (MT-093). Palmistry read what Handshake wrote even while Handshake was stalled (zero cooperation, MT-090).
- (2) FORCE A CRASH: launch the real app + Palmistry, then force a CRASH (a hard unhandled exception / abort on a test seam — NOT a clean shutdown). Assert: Palmistry writes a MINIDUMP out-of-process (MT-092), SURVIVES the parent death (MT-089), records the crash into the survivor store (MT-093), and the minidump validates with the minidump reader. A CLEAN shutdown in the same harness produces NO crash record (the §6.13 clean-shutdown gate).
- (3) RE-RUN THE BACKEND-DOWN REPRO (MT-088): launch the real app with the backend (127.0.0.1:37501) DOWN; assert the app stays RESPONSIVE (frames complete within a tight bound, the heartbeat keeps advancing, a BackendUnreachable event recorded, a degraded UI shown) — the 2026-06-26 freeze does NOT recur. (This re-proves MT-088 at the integrated level.)
- (4) TYPED-ALLOWLIST PRIVACY PROOF: across ALL artifacts produced by scenarios 1-3 — every ring record, the heartbeat, the survivor store records, the minidump METADATA (the typed crash record, not the dump's OS image bytes), and the FR-forward body — assert NO project content / NO sensitive data / NO free text appears: only typed event codes, ids, counters, phase markers, thread ids, resource metrics, timestamps, and local path references. A scan of the emitted artifacts confirms the typed-allowlist invariant (§5.8.3 + §6.13.8) holds system-wide.
