original_scope.summary:
Goal: build a GENERALIZED OPERATION/SUBPROCESS STALL WATCHDOG inside internal_diagnostics (Tier 2) so a silent, hours-long hang of ANY in-app operation OR ANY spawned child process becomes IMPOSSIBLE — it is detected within a BOUNDED time (seconds, not hours). This GENERALIZES the MT-088 backend-down UI-thread freeze fix + the MT-091 freeze-detection pattern from 'the UI thread froze' to 'ANY deadline-bounded operation stopped making progress'. It is the internal_diagnostics half of the stall-detection capability; the Palmistry child-process half + the end-to-end no-silent-hang capstone are MT-106.

MOTIVATING INCIDENT (operator, 2026-06-28): a spawned subprocess — a `cargo test` doing minidumper IPC (the MT-092 known hanger) — DEADLOCKED SILENTLY for HOURS with no detection and no one noticed. That whole CLASS of failure (an operation, or a spawned child process, that hangs/stalls with no progress and no observer) must be impossible inside Handshake: BOTH internal_diagnostics (this MT) AND Palmistry (MT-106) must catch it within a bounded time.

THE MODEL (deadline + progress ticks = a per-operation heartbeat): any in-app operation that could stall — a backend call, a spawned terminal/model session (MT-100/101), a tool run, a long async step, a spawned child process Handshake supervises — REGISTERS with the watchdog and gets back an `OperationHandle`. Registration carries: a typed numeric `operation_code` (a closed enum, NOT free text — see the typed-allowlist note), a `deadline` (max wall-clock the operation may run before it is presumed stalled), and an optional `progress_interval` (the max gap between progress ticks before it is presumed stalled even if the overall deadline has not elapsed). While the operation runs it calls `handle.tick()` periodically — a per-operation progress heartbeat (the same liveness idea as the MT-084 UI-thread heartbeat, but per-operation). On completion the operation calls `handle.complete()` (or drops the handle, which auto-completes/deregisters) so it can never false-flag after it finished. A background WATCHDOG thread (off the UI thread; reuse the MT-084/091 dedicated-poll-thread pattern) periodically scans the registered operations; any operation that has exceeded its `deadline` OR gone longer than `progress_interval` since its last tick — and has NOT completed — is declared STALLED: the watchdog emits a TYPED `DiagEventCode::StalledOperation` DiagEvent (typed integers only — see below) ONCE per stalled operation (debounced — not every scan tick), records it via the MT-082 `record()` API (so it lands in the ring Palmistry reads AND the in-process buffer the Settings->Diagnostics panel reads), and surfaces it (Settings->Diagnostics panel MT-087 + the status bar). A completed or still-ticking operation NEVER false-flags.

The whole point mirrors MT-091's no-false-positive gate: an operation that progresses (ticks within its interval) or completes before its deadline must produce NO StalledOperation; only an operation that is registered, never ticks/completes, and passes its deadline/interval is flagged — within a BOUNDED time (<= deadline + one watchdog poll interval).

Exact files to create/edit (inside handshake-native; the ring crate + backend are reuse-via-API only):
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/operation_watchdog.rs` — the `OperationWatchdog` + `OperationHandle` + `OperationCode` enum + the typed `StalledOperationReport`. Declare `pub mod operation_watchdog;` in `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/mod.rs` and re-export the public types.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/...` IS FORBIDDEN — instead ADD the `StalledOperation` variant to the `DiagEventCode` enum which lives in the MT-081 ring crate at `src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/src/schema.rs`. The ring crate is MT-081-owned and in this MT's forbidden_paths. THE SCHEMA ADDITION IS A NECESSARY CROSS-MT EDIT: append `StalledOperation = 11` to `DiagEventCode` (codes 0..=10 are used: Heartbeat=0 .. Shutdown=10; Other=65535 — append the new variant at 11, do NOT renumber any existing variant, the explicit-value/append rule is documented in schema.rs) and add a `DiagEvent::stalled_operation(...)` typed constructor alongside the existing `heartbeat`/`backend_unreachable` constructors. This is the ONE allowed schema edit; do it as a deliberate, reviewed allowlist-gate change exactly as the schema.rs docs require, then keep the rest of the MT inside handshake-native. (If a coordinating reviewer prefers, the schema edit can be split to an MT-081-owned micro-step, but the variant MUST exist for this MT to record the typed event — flag it explicitly in the handoff, do not smuggle text instead.)
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs` — start the watchdog poll thread once at startup (alongside / mirroring where the diagnostics ring is installed in `HandshakeApp::new`), and wire the FIRST REAL CONSUMER: the MT-088 backend-down path. A backend call IS a deadline-bounded operation — register the backend health/layout call with the watchdog (`OperationCode::BackendCall`, a short deadline) so a backend call that hangs (TCP-accepted-but-silent, the half-open case MT-088 added timeouts for) is caught by the watchdog as a StalledOperation, in addition to MT-088's client timeout. This is the anti-dead-code wire-into-live gate (mirrors MT-082 AC-002-4): the watchdog must have at least one REAL shipped-path consumer, not be scaffolding.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/diagnostics/panel.rs` (+ `settings_diagnostics_section.rs` if needed) — surface the current stalled-operation count / the last-N StalledOperation events in the Settings->Diagnostics panel (MT-087 is a pure projection; read the MT-082 snapshot, do not add panel-local authority). Also surface a stalled-operation indicator in the status bar (reuse the MT-088 disconnected-indicator status-bar pattern; theme tokens only — CONTROL-4).
- CREATE `src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_operation_watchdog.rs`.

TYPED-ALLOWLIST (§5.8.3 + §6.13.8 — HARD): the StalledOperation DiagEvent carries TYPED INTEGERS ONLY — NO free text. Map onto the existing MT-081 DiagEvent fields: `operation_code` (the OperationCode discriminant, a u16/u64 numeric) in `counter_a`; `elapsed_ms` (how long the operation ran before being flagged) in `metric_micros` or `counter_b`; `last_progress_ms` (ms since the last tick, 0 if it never ticked) in the other counter; the op's opaque numeric id in `sequence_id`; `timestamp_nanos` monotonic. NO operation NAME string, NO command line, NO arguments, NO path text in the DiagEvent (a local file path may only appear in a survivor/record per the MT-092/093 path-reference rule, never in the ring DiagEvent). The `OperationCode` enum is a CLOSED allowlist exactly like `DiagEventCode` — adding an operation kind is a reviewed code change, not a string.

WAIT-FREE / NON-BLOCKING (the watchdog must not itself become the hang): registering, ticking, and completing an operation must be cheap + non-blocking + panic-free on the calling thread (a tick may be called from the UI thread for a UI-thread-driven operation, so it must be allocation-light and never block — mirror the MT-082 record() hot-path discipline: a short lock or a lock-free structure, poisoned-lock recovery via into_inner, no format! on the hot path). The watchdog POLL thread runs OFF the UI thread (a dedicated thread, like MT-084/091's poll thread) so scanning the registry never blocks the frame loop. The watchdog itself must be wait-free in the sense MT-081 requires of the writer: it never waits on a stalled operation (it only OBSERVES last-tick timestamps), so a stalled operation cannot back-pressure or block the watchdog.

Reuse note: the MT-081 ring + the MT-082 `record()` / `record_with()` API are the emit path (REUSE them — record the StalledOperation through `diagnostics::record(...)`, do not invent a second emit path). The MT-084 dedicated-poll-thread + monotonic-Instant pattern is the watchdog-thread reference (staleness measured against a MONOTONIC `std::time::Instant`, never a wall clock that can jump — exactly MT-091's AC-011-5 discipline). The MT-088 backend-down path is the first real consumer (a backend call is a deadline-bounded operation). The MT-087 panel is the operator-facing surface. src/backend is reuse-via-API only (forbidden to edit). FR (flight_recorder) kept as-is.

Risk if missed: the exact 2026-06-28 silent-hours-long-hang class recurs (an in-app operation or a spawned child stalls with no detection); the generalization of MT-088/091 from 'UI thread' to 'any operation' is absent, so only the UI-thread freeze is caught and a stalled backend call / tool run / spawned session goes silent; MT-106 (which depends on this) has no in-app StalledOperation path to assert in the capstone no-silent-hang proof.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/** (MT-081-owned; reuse via API — EXCEPT the single allowed schema.rs DiagEventCode::StalledOperation variant + DiagEvent::stalled_operation constructor addition, which is the deliberate reviewed allowlist-gate edit this MT requires; flag it in the handoff)
src/backend/** (reuse via API only; the watchdog is entirely client-side/frame-path)
acceptance_criteria: AC-105-1 (STALL DETECTED WITHIN A BOUNDED TIME — the deliverable, prove first): a test registers an operation with a short deadline (and/or progress_interval), NEVER calls tick() or complete(), and asserts the watchdog declares it STALLED and emits exactly one typed StalledOperation DiagEvent within a BOUNDED time (<= deadline + one watchdog poll interval) — proven by a separate-reader/snapshot read of the ring/buffer asserting the StalledOperation event with the correct typed fields (operation_code, elapsed_ms, last_progress_ms). This is the 2026-06-28 silent-hang made impossible: a registered-but-never-progressing operation is caught in seconds, not hours.

AC-105-2 (NO FALSE POSITIVE — the gate, mirrors MT-091 AC-011-1): a healthy operation that calls tick() faster than its progress_interval (and/or completes before its deadline) NEVER produces a StalledOperation event, across many watchdog poll ticks and past the wall-clock deadline window — a progressing/completed operation must not be flagged. A completed/deregistered operation produces NO event even if later poll ticks run.

AC-105-3 (DEBOUNCED / one event per stall): a stalled operation emits the StalledOperation event exactly ONCE (on the healthy->stalled edge), not once per watchdog poll tick (the ring is bounded — RISK of flooding). A test asserts a single StalledOperation per stalled operation even across many scans while it remains stalled.

AC-105-4 (TYPED-ALLOWLIST, §5.8.3): the StalledOperation DiagEvent carries TYPED INTEGERS ONLY (operation_code, elapsed_ms, last_progress_ms, op id, timestamp) — NO operation name / command / args / path text. A source + value scan asserts the DiagEvent and the OperationCode enum expose no free-text field; the DiagEventCode::StalledOperation variant + DiagEvent::stalled_operation constructor are the only schema additions (no String/Vec/&str anywhere on the watchdog emit path).

AC-105-5 (WAIT-FREE / NON-BLOCKING — the watchdog is not itself the hang): register()/tick()/complete() are cheap, non-blocking, and panic-free (poisoned-lock recovery, no format! / no heavy alloc on the hot path — a tick may run on the UI thread); the watchdog POLL runs OFF the UI thread; the watchdog NEVER waits on a stalled operation (it only observes last-tick timestamps). A stress test calls register/tick/complete from multiple threads thousands of times asserting no panic, no deadlock, bounded resources; a perf/timing assertion corroborates the watchdog does not stall the caller.

AC-105-6 (WIRE-INTO-LIVE, anti-dead-code — mirrors MT-082 AC-002-4): the MT-088 backend call is registered with the watchdog in the SHIPPED path (not a test) as the first real consumer — a backend call is a deadline-bounded operation. original_scope.summary:
Goal: expand Palmistry (Tier 3 external watcher) from watching ONLY Handshake to ALSO watching the CHILD PROCESSES Handshake spawns (the sessions / tools / terminals / models from MT-100/101/014), so a spawned child that is ALIVE but STALLED (no progress) is detected within a BOUNDED time — and deliver THE CAPSTONE end-to-end proof that a silent, hours-long hang of an in-app operation OR a spawned child process can NEVER happen inside Handshake. This is the Palmistry half of the stall/hang detection capability; the internal_diagnostics half (the in-app StalledOperation watchdog) is MT-105, which this MT depends on and asserts against in the capstone.

MOTIVATING INCIDENT (operator, 2026-06-28): a spawned subprocess — a `cargo test` doing minidumper IPC (the MT-092 known hanger that deadlocked for HOURS) — stalled SILENTLY with no detection and no observer. The whole class (an operation OR a spawned child that hangs/stalls with no progress and no one notices) must be IMPOSSIBLE inside Handshake. MT-105 makes the in-app-operation half impossible (the internal_diagnostics watchdog); THIS MT makes the spawned-CHILD half impossible (Palmistry watches the children) AND proves both halves together in a bounded-time capstone.

WHAT PALMISTRY ALREADY DOES (reuse, do not reinvent): MT-089 = the lifecycle-inverted watcher binary that holds the PARENT (Handshake) process handle + survives parent death + records abnormal parent exit. MT-091 = freeze detection of HANDSHAKE via the DOUBLE-SIGNAL gate (stale heartbeat from the MT-084 ring + the Win32 SendMessageTimeoutW hung-window probe), with the no-false-positive-on-a-healthy-heartbeat gate, reset-on-advance, recovery, and a monotonic-Instant staleness reference (FreezeDetector/FreezeState/FreezeReport in freeze_detect.rs; the spawn_freeze_poll thread + FreezeStatus in main.rs). MT-090 = the zero-cooperation ring reader. MT-092/093 = crash capture + the durable survivor store. This MT GENERALIZES the MT-091 'watch Handshake's liveness' to 'watch each spawned CHILD's liveness' the SAME double-signal way, and reuses the MT-089 process-handle-wait + the survivor-record discipline for the children.

CHILD REGISTRATION + LIVENESS (how Palmistry learns about + watches a child): a child Handshake spawns (a terminal/model/tool/swarm session, MT-100/101/014) REGISTERS with Palmistry — over the existing MT-089 control socket (a typed `ControlMessage` variant carrying the child's pid + its liveness source) — giving Palmistry (a) the child PID (so Palmistry holds the child's OS process handle, the MT-089 OpenProcess/WaitForSingleObject pattern, to know ALIVE vs EXITED) AND (b) a per-child PROGRESS liveness signal: either the child's own ring/heartbeat slot (if the child publishes one, the MT-084 idea per-child) OR a per-child LIVENESS FILE the child touches/updates as it makes progress (an mtime/counter the watcher polls — the field-standard touch-file/keepalive technique for a process that does not share the ring). Palmistry detects a child that is ALIVE (its process handle has NOT signaled exit) but STALLED (its progress heartbeat / liveness-file has not advanced past a per-child threshold) the SAME DOUBLE-SIGNAL way MT-091 detects Handshake's freeze: stale progress signal ALONE = suspected; stale progress signal AND the corroborating signal (the child is provably alive but not progressing — process-alive + no-progress is the corroboration for a headless child that has no message pump to probe) = a CONFIRMED child stall. A child that exits cleanly, or keeps advancing its progress signal, must NEVER false-flag (the MT-091 AC-011-1 gate, per-child).

SURFACE (typed record, no free text): on a confirmed child stall, Palmistry surfaces a TYPED survivor/diagnostic record (the MT-093 survivor-record discipline / the MT-092 CrashRecord typed shape): record kind = ChildStall, the child pid, the session id, the stale duration (ms, against Palmistry's monotonic clock), the last progress counter/timestamp, and a typed reason code — NO command line, NO arguments, NO path text in the record (a local liveness-file PATH may appear only as a path REFERENCE per the MT-092/093 rule, never as project content / free text). It is logged + persisted next to the ring like the MT-089 survivor record and surfaces in the §10.12.5 Tier-3 Palmistry section of the Settings->Diagnostics panel (the same surface MT-093 feeds).

Exact files to create/edit (inside the palmistry crate + the minimal Handshake-side registration seam):
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/child_stall.rs` — a `ChildStallDetector` (generalize FreezeDetector: per-child last-progress tracking against a monotonic Instant, a per-child threshold, the double-signal gate process-alive + no-progress, reset-on-advance, recovery, no-false-positive) + the typed `ChildStallReport` / `ChildStallState` (Healthy / Suspected / Stalled, mirroring FreezeState). Reuse freeze_detect.rs's monotonic-reference + reset-on-advance + named-const discipline (do not duplicate the math sloppily — extract or mirror it cleanly).
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/src/child_registry.rs` — a registry of watched children: pid + a `ChildLivenessSource` (a per-child ring/heartbeat slot OR a liveness-file path) + the per-child process handle (the MT-089 ParentWatch/OpenProcess pattern, reused/generalized to a child handle: ALIVE vs EXITED). The watch loop polls each registered child's progress source + alive-state.
- EDIT `src/frontend/palmistry/src/control.rs` — add a typed `ControlMessage::RegisterChild { pid, liveness_kind, ... }` (+ a `DeregisterChild`) so Handshake tells Palmistry which children to watch (typed integers + a liveness-source reference only; no free text). Reuse the existing newline-delimited-JSON ControlMessage framing.
- EDIT `src/frontend/palmistry/src/main.rs` — spawn a CHILD-STALL poll thread (mirror spawn_freeze_poll: its OWN thread, NOT the control loop; the MT-091 ~200-500ms cadence band; reset-on-advance; debounced healthy->stalled edge), feed registered children + their progress reads into the ChildStallDetector, and on a confirmed child stall record + persist the typed ChildStall survivor record (reuse persist_survivor_record / the MT-093 store). Add the child-stall poll thread to the run_watcher teardown joins.
- EDIT `src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs` (+ backend_client.rs if needed) — the minimal Handshake-side seam: when Handshake spawns a watched child (a terminal/model/tool/swarm session from MT-100/101/014, OR — honestly — where those are typed blockers today, the supervised child processes Handshake actually does spawn), REGISTER it with Palmistry over the control socket (pid + the chosen liveness source) so the child is watched. If MT-100/101 landed typed blockers for the native spawn path (no native HTTP/IPC reach), wire the registration for the children Handshake genuinely spawns + record an HONEST typed note for the not-yet-reachable spawn paths — do NOT fabricate a watched child that Handshake does not spawn.
- CREATE `src/frontend/palmistry/tests/test_child_stall.rs` (the per-child detector + double-signal + no-false-positive + recovery, deterministic with injected time + fake progress/alive, mirroring test_freeze_detect.rs) AND `src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/test_no_silent_hang_end_to_end.rs` (THE CAPSTONE — see below).

THE CAPSTONE PROOF (the operator's requirement, AC-106-CAPSTONE): a single end-to-end test spawns BOTH (1) a DELIBERATELY-HUNG in-app operation (registered with the MT-105 watchdog, never ticks/completes, past its deadline) AND (2) a DELIBERATELY-HUNG real CHILD PROCESS (a spawned child that registers with Palmistry then never advances its progress signal — e.g. a tiny test-only helper binary that sleeps forever after registering, or the real palmistry test seam), and ASSERTS, BOTH within a BOUNDED time (seconds, hard-bounded): internal_diagnostics emits a `StalledOperation` (MT-105) for the hung in-app operation AND Palmistry surfaces a confirmed ChildStall (typed record) for the hung child — proving the 2026-06-28 hours-long silent hang can NEVER happen in Handshake (it is caught in seconds by BOTH tiers). The capstone uses the REAL binaries (the real HandshakeApp + the real spawned palmistry.exe + the real ring + a real hung child process) — NO mocked tier for the spec-required runtime; where a managed backend is genuinely unavailable, gate that half honestly (NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF), never fake it.

BOUNDED-TEST RULE (MT-092 precedent, MANDATORY — this is the exact failure class this MT exists to prevent): EVERY test that spawns the palmistry binary / a child process / does minidumper-IPC / waits on a child MUST use an EXPLICIT timeout (wait_for_exit / connect / read with a hard deadline) — NEVER an unbounded Command::output() or socket read_line. `#[ignore]` WITH A TYPED REASON any IPC test that deadlocks under this headless harness (run with --ignored on a real host), exactly the MT-092 precedent (minidumper out-of-process IPC + simulate_exception are the known hangers). The whole MT is about not hanging silently — its OWN tests must be hard-bounded so a deadlock cannot waste hours (the irony of the 2026-06-28 incident being a test hang is the point).

Reuse note: MT-091 freeze_detect.rs (FreezeDetector/FreezeState/FreezeReport + the monotonic-reference + reset-on-advance + double-signal + named-const discipline) is the worked reference for the per-child detector. MT-089 lifecycle.rs (ParentWatch/OpenProcess/WaitForSingleObject + SurvivorRecord + build/persist_survivor_record) is the worked reference for the per-child process handle + the typed survivor record. MT-090 ring_reader.rs is the zero-cooperation read pattern. MT-105 supplies the in-app StalledOperation the capstone asserts. The control socket + ControlMessage framing are MT-089. The §10.12.5 Tier-3 panel surface is MT-087/093. No backend; src/backend reuse-via-API only; FR kept as-is.

Risk if missed: the spawned-child half of the 2026-06-28 silent-hang class stays UNDETECTED (Palmistry watches only Handshake, not the children Handshake spawns — so a deadlocked spawned session/tool/model/test hangs forever with no observer, the exact incident); OR the capstone never proves the two tiers catch a hung operation + a hung child together in bounded time, so the operator's 'this must be IMPOSSIBLE' requirement is asserted per-tier but never end-to-end; OR (the ironic failure) a stall-detection test itself deadlocks unbounded and wastes hours, reproducing the very incident.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/diag_ring/** (MT-081-owned; reuse via API — the StalledOperation code is added by MT-105, reuse it)
src/backend/** (Palmistry never touches the backend; the Handshake-side child registration is client-side only)

implementation_notes: GENERALIZE MT-091, do not fork it sloppily: the ChildStallDetector is the FreezeDetector pattern applied per-child — track each child's last-progress value + the Palmistry monotonic Instant it last advanced; staleness = now - last_advance; reset-on-advance; threshold gate; the double-signal is (stale progress) AND (the child process handle has NOT signaled exit = provably alive but not progressing). A headless child has no message pump to SendMessageTimeout-probe, so 'process-alive + no-progress' IS the corroboration (the analogue of MT-091's hung-window probe for a GUI). Keep the named-const cadence/threshold discipline + the compile-time relationship asserts MT-091 uses.

REUSE the MT-089 process-handle wait for the child's alive/exited signal: the ParentWatch/WindowsParentWatch OpenProcess+WaitForSingleObject+GetExitCodeProcess pattern generalizes to a child handle (a ChildWatch). A child that EXITS is deregistered (a finished child is not a stalled child — AC-106-2); a child that is ALIVE but not progressing is the stall.

LIVENESS SOURCE per child (two supported kinds, typed): (1) the child publishes its OWN ring/heartbeat slot (the MT-084 idea per-child) read via the MT-090 zero-cooperation reader; OR (2) the child touches/updates a per-child LIVENESS FILE (an mtime/counter Palmistry polls) — the field-standard touch-file/keepalive technique for a child that does not share the ring. The control message says WHICH kind (a typed liveness_kind enum) + the source reference (a ring name or a file path reference — a path reference, never project content).

CONTROL MESSAGE: add ControlMessage::RegisterChild { pid: u32, liveness_kind, liveness_ref, threshold_ms } + DeregisterChild { pid } to control.rs, reusing the existing newline-delimited-JSON ControlMessage framing (Shutdown/Ping/...). Typed integers + a liveness reference only. The control socket stays CONTROL-only (§6.13.4): liveness is observed PASSIVELY (ring read / file poll), never requested over the socket — a hung child could not answer (the same reason MT-089/090 forbid socket-based liveness).

POLL THREAD: mirror spawn_freeze_poll exactly — a dedicated child-stall poll thread (NOT the control loop), the MT-091 ~200-500ms cadence band, reset-on-advance, the debounced healthy->stalled edge (record once), recovery on resume. Add it to the run_watcher teardown joins alongside the freeze + watch handles. It must NEVER block on a child (only observe the child's progress source + alive-state — the MT-081 wait-free principle, per-child).

TYPED SURVIVOR RECORD: reuse the MT-093 survivor-store / MT-089 build+persist_survivor_record discipline for a ChildStall record (kind=ChildStall, child pid, session id, stale_ms, last progress counter/ts, typed reason code, optional liveness-file path REFERENCE). Persist next to the ring like the MT-089 survivor JSON; surface in the §10.12.5 Tier-3 panel section (MT-087/093). NO free text.

THE CAPSTONE (AC-106-CAPSTONE) is the deliverable the operator demanded: ONE hard-bounded end-to-end test, REAL binaries, that forces a hung in-app op AND a hung child and asserts StalledOperation (MT-105) AND ChildStall (Palmistry) BOTH in seconds. The hung child should be a tiny TEST-ONLY helper (a sleeps-forever-after-registering binary, or a documented palmistry test seam) so it is deterministic + feature-gated, not a shipped behavior. Locate the built palmistry.exe via the external target dir / current_exe()-relative resolution (the MT-094 path).

BOUNDED-TEST RULE (AC-106-6, MANDATORY — the irony of the 2026-06-28 incident being a TEST hang is the point): every spawn/wait uses an explicit timeout (wait_for_exit/connect/read with a hard deadline); #[ignore]-with-a-typed-reason any IPC test that deadlocks headless (run --ignored on a real host), exactly the MT-092 precedent. A stall-detection test that itself hangs unbounded would reproduce the very incident — do not let it.

HONESTY (Spec-Realism, no-mock): the child Palmistry watches must be a REAL spawned process with a REAL progress source; do NOT fabricate a watched child Handshake does not spawn. Where MT-100/101's native spawn path is a typed blocker today, register the children Handshake genuinely spawns + record an honest typed note for the not-yet-reachable paths. Where a managed backend is needed for a live half, gate it NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF, never fake it.

Read the KERNEL_BUILDER coder protocol under .GOV/ first; the no-false-positive gate (AC-106-2) + the bounded-time capstone (AC-106-CAPSTONE) + the all-tests-hard-bounded rule (AC-106-6) are the gates — a per-child detector that cries wolf, or a capstone that does not catch BOTH a hung op and a hung child in seconds, or a test that itself hangs, each fails the MT.
ports_from_react: NONE (native child-process stall watch + no-silent-hang capstone)
binds_backend_api: NONE. Palmistry watches the children via their process handle (alive/exited, the MT-089 OpenProcess pattern) + a passive progress source (a per-child ring read via MT-090, or a liveness-file poll). It never calls src/backend. The Handshake-side child registration is a client-side control-socket message only. FR kept as-is. PostgreSQL/EventLedger only; no SQLite.

acceptance_and_requirement_map.original: AC-106-1 (CHILD STALL DETECTED — the deliverable, prove first): a test registers a child (pid + a progress liveness source), the child is ALIVE but its progress signal NEVER advances past the per-child threshold, and Palmistry declares a CONFIRMED ChildStall within a BOUNDED time and writes a typed ChildStall survivor record (kind, child pid, session id, stale_ms, last progress counter/timestamp, typed reason — no free text). A spawned child that is alive but stalled is caught in seconds, not hours.

AC-106-2 (NO FALSE POSITIVE — the per-child gate, mirrors MT-091 AC-011-1): a child that keeps advancing its progress signal faster than the threshold NEVER produces a ChildStall, across many poll ticks past the wall-clock threshold; and a child that EXITS CLEANLY (process handle signals exit) is deregistered and produces NO ChildStall (a finished child is not a stalled child). Reset-on-advance against a monotonic Instant, exactly the MT-091 discipline.

AC-106-3 (DOUBLE-SIGNAL + DEBOUNCE): a confirmed ChildStall requires BOTH the stale progress signal AND the corroboration (the child is provably ALIVE — process handle not exited — yet not progressing); a stale-but-the-child-actually-exited case is NOT a stall (it is an exit, handled separately). The ChildStall record is emitted ONCE on the healthy->stalled edge (debounced, not per poll tick). A child stall can RECOVER if the progress signal resumes (clears to Healthy, does not latch).

AC-106-4 (CHILD REGISTRATION over the control socket): the typed ControlMessage::RegisterChild { pid, liveness_kind, ... } (+ DeregisterChild) carries typed integers + a liveness-source reference only (no free text); Handshake registers a watched child over the existing MT-089 control socket. Proven by a test asserting a registered child is watched and a deregistered/exited child is dropped.

AC-106-5 (TYPED-ALLOWLIST, §6.13.8): the ChildStall survivor record + any control message carry NO project content / free text — only typed integers, enums, timestamps, and local liveness-file path references. A source + value scan asserts no command/args/free-text field on the child-stall path (the MT-093 typed-allowlist discipline, per-child).

AC-106-CAPSTONE (THE NO-SILENT-HANG PROOF — the operator's requirement): a single end-to-end test spawns BOTH a deliberately-hung in-app operation (registered with the MT-105 watchdog, never progresses, past deadline) AND a deliberately-hung real child process (registers with Palmistry, never advances its progress signal), and asserts BOTH within a BOUNDED time (seconds, hard-bounded): (a) internal_diagnostics emits a StalledOperation (MT-105) for the hung operation, AND (b) Palmistry surfaces a confirmed ChildStall (typed record) for the hung child. Run on the REAL binaries (real HandshakeApp + real spawned palmistry.exe + real ring + a real hung child) — proving the hours-long silent hang can NEVER happen in Handshake (caught in seconds by BOTH tiers).

AC-106-6 (ALL TESTS HARD-BOUNDED — MT-092 precedent, MANDATORY): every test that spawns the palmistry binary / a child process / does IPC / waits on a child uses an EXPLICIT timeout (wait_for_exit / connect / read with a hard deadline), NEVER an unbounded Command::output() / read_line; any IPC test that deadlocks headless is #[ignore]-with-a-typed-reason (run with --ignored on a real host), exactly the MT-092 minidumper-IPC precedent. A source review confirms no unbounded child wait on the stall-detection test path.

AC-106-7 (OPERATOR SURFACE): the confirmed ChildStall surfaces in the §10.12.5 Tier-3 Palmistry section of the Settings->Diagnostics panel (the MT-087/093 surface) — at minimum the record is persisted + the panel can read it (proven by the panel reading a ChildStall record, or a documented seam consistent with how MT-093 feeds the Tier-3 section).

AC-106-8: monotonic staleness reference (a process-monotonic std::time::Instant, never a wall clock) + named per-child poll-cadence/threshold consts with the relationship documented (the MT-091 AC-011-5 discipline, per-child).

AC-106-9: `cargo build -p palmistry` + `-p handshake-native` + `-p handshake-diag-ring` clean; clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean; full handshake-native suite `-j 2` green; external CARGO_TARGET_DIR (palmistry-target + handshake-native-target); no repo-local target/; `git ls-files src/**/*.png` empty.

PT-106-A: `cargo test -p palmistry child_stall` GREEN — an alive-but-stalled child -> confirmed ChildStall + typed survivor record within a bounded time (deterministic injected time + fake progress/alive, mirroring test_freeze_detect.rs).
PT-106-B: no-false-positive GREEN — a progressing child never flags; a cleanly-exited child is deregistered, no ChildStall; double-signal (alive+no-progress) + debounce + recovery GREEN.

PT-106-C: `cargo test -p handshake-native no_silent_hang_end_to_end` GREEN (HARD-BOUNDED) — the CAPSTONE: a hung in-app operation -> StalledOperation (MT-105) AND a hung child -> ChildStall (Palmistry), BOTH within a bounded time, on the real binaries; the hours-long silent hang proven impossible.

PT-106-D: typed-allowlist scan (no free text on the child-stall path) + the all-tests-hard-bounded source review (#[ignore]-with-reason any headless IPC deadlocker, MT-092 precedent) + panel Tier-3 ChildStall surface; both crates + diag-ring build clean + clippy -D warnings + full suite -j 2 green; external target dirs; git ls-files src/**/*.png empty.

security_boundary_implemented.middleware: authorize_flight_recorder_request installed with middleware::from_fn_with_state over the ENTIRE route group before with_state, mirroring the proven api::memory pattern. Authenticates via stage::capture_context (live native-MCP binding token + process-birth identity) -> 401 HSK-401-FR-SESSION. Resolves one capability per route class via capability_registry.profile_can -> 403 HSK-403-FR-CAPABILITY. Emits one redacted capability_action FR event for EVERY allow and deny; audit-write failure fails the request CLOSED with 500. Injects a RecorderAuthority request extension so handlers read identity only from there, never from headers or body.
security_boundary_implemented.capabilities: fr.read (existing) plus new fr.read.global, fr.ingest.runtime_chat, fr.ingest.native_editor. Operator receives the three scoped ones. fr.read.global is deliberately granted to NO profile, so unscoped cross-workspace enumeration is fail-closed. KERNEL_BUILDER verified it is defined but absent from the grant list.
security_boundary_implemented.routes: The unscoped POST /flight_recorder/{native_editor_event,runtime_chat_event} paths are REMOVED. Both are now POST /workspaces/:workspace_id/flight_recorder/... so the path itself is the workspace authority, validated against a real canonical workspace row before any write. An unknown workspace returns the same 403 HSK-403-FR-WORKSPACE as unauthorized, so existence is never disclosed.
security_boundary_implemented.envelope_contract: actor_id / actor_kind / workspace_id are no longer client authority. Optional; if present they must EXACTLY match the authenticated context or the request is rejected before any durable write; if absent the server fills them. Canonicalization overwrites them from context BEFORE validate_document_save_receipt, so a save receipt can only be claimed by the principal that minted it.
security_boundary_implemented.idempotency: workspace_scoped_fr_event_id(workspace_id, client_event_id), a deterministic SHA-256-derived RFC 9562 v8 UUID, is now the durable FR/EventLedger identity; aggregate id and idempotency keys carry the workspace. Cross-workspace event-id pre-emption can no longer create a conflict, be read back, or be reconciled. The ack returns both event_id (client) and fr_event_id (durable).
security_boundary_implemented.reads: GET /flight_recorder and /events require fr.read; omitting or blanking the wsid query additionally requires fr.read.global -> 403 and audited. The authenticated scope is applied LAST and UNCONDITIONALLY after every other filter, so no actor/actor_id/surface/event_type/event_id combination can widen it; a cross-workspace event_id returns 200 with an empty list rather than an error.

bounding_design.shape: Two-regime deterministic function of (prefix, components, pane). VERBATIM: the existing lowercase bytewise UTF-8 hex, emitted whenever the FULL composed route INCLUDING its .pane- scope already fits 256 bytes. DIGESTED: zsha256-<64 hex> per component, only on overrun.
bounding_design.injectivity: STRUCTURAL, not asserted: the sentinel character z lies OUTSIDE the lowercase-hex alphabet and . never occurs inside a component, so a route parses back to its component tuple unambiguously and distinct tuples yield distinct routes. Under the digested regime this rests on SHA-256 collision resistance - cryptographic rather than absolute, and the code says so plainly rather than overclaiming.
bounding_design.resolvability_handled_honestly: Exact string reversal is MATHEMATICALLY IMPOSSIBLE for a bounded encoding of unbounded input, and the agent did not fake it. hit_identity_from_result_author_id keeps its exact contract for the verbatim regime and honestly returns None for a digested one; a new TOTAL function hit_identity_from_result_author_id_in resolves any route by recomputation against the live candidate set - which is exactly how the production panel already matches an activated row.
bounding_design.byte_identity_is_structural: The verbatim branch is tried FIRST against the FINAL composed string, so byte-identity for anything that already fits is structural rather than incidental. mt113_every_route_that_fits_is_byte_identical_to_the_legacy_composition reproduces the real legacy algorithm inline and asserts equality over the adversarial corpus x 6 composition sites x 3 pane scopes. This is WHY a reserve-based budget was rejected: it would have changed MT-029 own 209-byte mounted route.
bounding_design.ordering_fix: Content-derived routes now compose their pane scope in the SAME call (pane_scoped_*_author_id), because pane_scoped_author_id can only shrink the PANE component and never the content.

original_scope.summary: Bound author_id composition so that user-supplied content can never push a completion token past its byte budget and silently disable Argus observability for that control.

measured_defect.mechanism: SearchBookmark::stable_id() hex-encodes the query, and bookmark_*_author_id then hex-encodes THAT result - a 4x expansion of the original user bytes. MAX_CLICK_COMPLETION_AUTHOR_BYTES is 256 (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mcp/action.rs line 55), so the composed id overruns and serialize_* returns None. The node then carries no completion token, the action can never terminalize, and its receipt is permanently indeterminate.
measured_defect.first_failing_input: A search query of just 23 CHARACTERS. Measured example: "authentication middleware refactor" (34 chars) produces a 304-byte author_id whose token is silently dropped. This is trivially reachable by a real operator.
measured_defect.budget_raising_is_not_a_fix: Raising the budget only moves the ceiling: 256 B -> 22 chars, 512 B -> 86, 1024 B -> 213, 2048 B -> 469. Every tier remains reachable by a real query, path, or document title. Raising it also weakens bounded-token flood control and is a SHARED contract change inherited by every MT that emits a token.
measured_defect.field_budget_asymmetry: The SAME id is legal as `context` (512 B, used by same-target tokens) but illegal as `pending_target` (256 B, used by observer tokens). A synchronous control therefore proves fine while its asynchronous sibling cannot - which is exactly why bookmark RESTORE passed while bookmark REMOVE did not. That asymmetry is itself a latent trap for future MTs.
measured_defect.silent_failure: serialize_* simply returns None. The node carries no value, the action becomes unprovable, and NO diagnostic is emitted anywhere. That silence is what made this cost a full proof cycle to discover.

recommended_direction_from_the_mt029_age: PREFERRED: stop putting unbounded user content in a durable author_id at all. The root defect is that SearchBookmark::stable_id() derives identity from free text. Mint a bounded id (Uuid::now_v7(), which HBR-INT-008 already REQUIRES for new id mint sites) and keep the content-derived value as a separate dedup key. This bounds the row id by construction at roughly 102 bytes AND stays reversible.

Where a content-derived id is genuinely unavoidable, hash ONLY the variable component behind a stable prefix. NOTE the trade-off: this loses exact reversibility, which MT-029 actively relies on (hit_identity_from_result_author_id and accesskit_result_ids_are_utf8_injective_and_exactly_reversible), so it must be applied per-component rather than globally.

Make the failure LOUD regardless of which option is chosen: a debug_assert! plus a typed completion-unavailable marker so an over-budget id surfaces at authoring time instead of becoming a silently unprovable action months later.
acceptance_criteria: AC-113-1: an author_id composed from ARBITRARY user content (query, path, title) can no longer exceed its token budget. Proven with a property-style test over long, multibyte and adversarial inputs, including the measured 23-character regression case.

AC-113-2: exact reversibility relied on by MT-029 is preserved where it is required. accesskit_result_ids_are_utf8_injective_and_exactly_reversible and hit_identity_from_result_author_id must still pass unchanged; if a component becomes non-reversible, prove nothing depending on reversibility consumes it.

AC-113-3: an over-budget id can no longer fail SILENTLY. A typed completion-unavailable signal is emitted and is visible to the proof surface, and a debug_assert! fires in debug builds at authoring time.

AC-113-4: the pending_target (256 B) versus context (512 B) asymmetry is resolved or explicitly documented as intentional, so a synchronous control and its asynchronous sibling cannot diverge in provability for the same id.

pt_115_3_blocker_requiring_operator_deci.why_it_matters: MT-109 stated intent is that a save receipt can only be claimed by the principal that minted it. That requires BOTH endpoints to authenticate the same principal. Today only one does, so the clause does not enforce the invariant - it rejects EVERYTHING legitimate. A guard that always fails is not a security control; it is an outage that looks like one.
pt_115_3_blocker_requiring_operator_deci.why_not_fixed_here: Every fix inside MT-115 allowed_paths would WEAKEN the binding. The non-weakening fix - authenticate the document-save route from the native session, or expose the derived identity through a route the frontend can use - lives in api/knowledge_documents.rs or a new route, outside allowed_paths, and is a durable security-contract decision. Routed to MT-120 rather than decided unilaterally.

root_cause_found_and_it_is_NOT_cosmetic.correction_to_the_original_diagnosis: The MT was opened describing a COSMETIC pill-width mismatch at 44-character ids. That framing is WRONG and is corrected here. The defect is a real rendering bug affecting EVERY chip at any non-default editor font size and EVERY chip inside a heading block, at any id length. The 44-character id merely made it visible.
root_cause_found_and_it_is_NOT_cosmetic.mechanism: rich_editor_widget.rs painted the chip label with egui::FontId::proportional(line_layout::BASE_FONT_SIZE), a CONSTANT fixed at 15.0. The pill rect it painted the label into is derived from chip_rect_for_span over a galley laid out by layout_block_with_base(.., base_font_size), where base_font_size = state.editor_font_size() - the USER-CONFIGURED size exposed in Settings as settings-editor-font-size. Whenever that size is not exactly 15.0 the pill and the label are measured by DIFFERENT metrics: above 15.0 the label overflows its pill, below it the pill runs wide.
root_cause_found_and_it_is_NOT_cosmetic.heading_case_missed_entirely: A heading block scales further still. line_layout::block_style_with_base routes NodeKind::Heading to heading_with_base, which multiplies by HEADING_SCALE ([1.8, 1.5, 1.25]). The constant never accounted for that, so a chip in an H1 was painted at 15.0 inside a pill measured at 1.8x the editor size - a far larger mismatch than the reported symptom.
root_cause_found_and_it_is_NOT_cosmetic.proof_the_two_paths_are_now_single_sourc: line_layout.rs:325 - layout_block_atoms_with_base does `let style = block_style_with_base(block, base_font_size)`, and the hsLink atom is laid out at line 355 via text_format_for_run(&[Mark::Link{..}], style, ..). The spec now calls the SAME block_style_with_base(block, base_font_size).size. Pill metric and label metric therefore come from one helper and cannot drift.

target_2_daily_journal_calendar_event_ch.ROOT_CAUSE: ClickCompletionToken is #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] (mcp/action.rs:177). The chip value must therefore be EITHER a parseable completion declaration OR the domain json the test reads off it - never both. The MT-117 merge fix adds calendar_event_id and daily_note_doc_id alongside the declaration keys, which makes parse_click_completion_token FAIL, so the driver sees NO declaration on the target and falls through to the generic disappeared path.
target_2_daily_journal_calendar_event_ch.the_conflict_stated_plainly: test_calendar_interop asserts argus_node_json_value_field_equals(tree, chip, "calendar_event_id", ...) - it requires the domain field at the TOP LEVEL of the chip value. target_2_daily_journal_calendar_event_ch.why_the_mt042_shape_does_not_resolve_it_: MT-042 hit the identical collision and moved its STATE to a sibling {author_id}.state node so the declaration could own the value. That works when the sibling is what readers consult. Here the reader is a test this MT may not edit, and it reads the chip node itself.
target_2_daily_journal_calendar_event_ch.resolution_requires_an_authority_decisio: Three options, each touching a durable contract: (a) move the chip domain fields into the declaration semantic_value and update test_calendar_interop to read them there - forbidden to this MT, the test may not be edited; (b) relax ClickCompletionToken from deny_unknown_fields so a token may carry domain siblings - a product-wide schema change affecting every observer; (c) accept that this target cannot carry a declaration and exclude it from the PT-117-1 count with a typed reason. Not decided unilaterally.

pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.status: ATTEMPTED, PROVEN VACUOUS, AND DELETED RATHER THAN SHIPPED
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.what_was_tried: A library-level regression guard was written that renders the whole panel through find_in_files::show() inside a Ui constrained with set_max_width(420) and measures ui.min_rect().width(), first absolutely and then as a DIFFERENTIAL between a panel with no bookmarks and one carrying a long-labelled bookmark.
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.why_it_was_withdrawn: IT COULD NOT FAIL. Non-vacuity was tested two ways and the guard stayed green under BOTH: first with .truncate() removed from the label, and then with the entire pre-fix layout restored (label added first inside a left_to_right row). A guard that stays green while the defect is reinstated is not a guard - it is a false assurance, and shipping it would have been the same vacuous-proof pathology this WP has repeatedly had to correct (MT-115 found four vacuous FR assertions; MT-020 had to make six dishonest tests honest).
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.root_cause_of_the_vacuity: Diagnosed rather than guessed. In a bare egui Context with no real screen rect, other Find-in-Files surfaces - the single-line status/receipt text and the results ScrollArea configured auto_shrink([false, false]) - report an enormous min_rect: the first absolute measurement returned 9984px inside a nominally 420px pane. The panel is therefore already effectively unbounded in that harness, so a roughly 600px bookmark row NEVER overflows regardless of layout, and no measurement taken at panel level can distinguish the fixed row from the broken one. set_max_width does not constrain those children.
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.what_would_actually_work: A MOUNTED harness (egui_kittest, as PT-119-1 uses) where the pane has a real width, reading the Restore/Remove node bounds out of the AccessKit tree by author_id and asserting containment within the pane bounds - the same bounds data the MCP snapshot already exposes per author_id. That is a mounted-proof-shaped task, not a lib-unit-shaped one. Alternatively the row rendering could be extracted into a directly testable function, but that is a product refactor beyond a layout fix.
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.honest_consequence: MT-119 therefore has NO automated regression guard. Its acceptance rests on PT-119-1, the mounted GPU frame that was captured and OPENED. The fix can silently regress between mounted runs until a mounted rect assertion exists. This is stated plainly rather than papered over with the green-but-meaningless test that was deleted.
pt_119_3_attempted_and_WITHDRAWN.tree_state: The deleted test left NO residue: git diff against the committed fix fef0faa9 is empty, and cargo test --lib find_in_files is 46 passed / 0 failed. The temporary pre-fix edits used to test non-vacuity were reverted by targeted replacement - no reset, stash, checkout -- or clean was used on the shared branch.

pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.status: ATTEMPTED IN THE MOUNTED HARNESS AND ALSO WITHDRAWN - for a DIFFERENT and more important reason
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.what_was_tried: A geometry assertion inside the mounted proof (tests/test_author_id_budget.rs): read the Restore/Remove node bounds out of the argus.inspect() tree by author_id and assert their right edges lie within the pane, deriving the pane edge from sibling Find-in-Files controls that cannot legally sit outside their own pane.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.what_happened: It FIRED - reporting the Restore control right edge at 2605.875px against a derived pane edge of 1557.34px. That is a FALSE POSITIVE: 2605px lies beyond the ENTIRE 2560px harness window, and the GPU frame captured in the same run shows both controls comfortably inside the pane.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.root_cause: argus.inspect() calls HandshakeApp::capture_mcp_snapshot_for_navigation (app.rs:12159), which calls refresh_mcp_snapshot() - and that renders on a FRESH egui::Context. The bounds in the inspect tree therefore describe a SYNTHETIC re-render, not the mounted frame. They are not comparable to what the operator sees.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.why_this_finding_matters_beyond_mt119: This is the same fresh-context hazard already known to make egui::Memory-backed state (popups, context menus) read back EMPTY - but its consequence for BOUNDS was not previously recorded. Any MT that tries to assert geometry, containment, clipping or overlap from the inspect tree will get answers that do not describe the rendered UI. That directly affects HBR-VIS style acceptance and MT-108 pixel gates.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.what_would_actually_work: Geometry must be measured from the MOUNTED egui pass - for example by having the product expose the rendered rects, or by asserting against the captured frame itself - not from the MCP snapshot tree.
pt_119_3_second_attempt_also_invalid.discipline_note: The assertion was NOT loosened to make it pass. Loosening a threshold until a false positive goes quiet would have fabricated a green with no meaning - the same failure as the vacuous lib-level guard deleted earlier. It was reverted and the finding recorded instead.

design_decision_settled_by_direct_inspec.what_was_rejected: Rebinding the ledger actor_id COLUMN to the server-derived principal. This is the obvious fix and it is WRONG.
design_decision_settled_by_direct_inspec.how_it_was_settled: Two adversarial review lenses reached OPPOSITE conclusions - a correctness lens recommended rebinding the column, a security lens called it a blocking contradiction. KERNEL_BUILDER read the source rather than taking either: test_e7_swarm_edit_proof.rs:2944-2973 runs a DO block asserting kernel_event_ledger.actor_id = {app_attribution.actor_id}, which is the CLIENT-declared per-agent id, and :2866-2881 asserts assert_ne!(recorder_actor, save_actor_id). Rebinding the column fails AC-120-3 and AC-120-2 at the same time. The security lens was right.
design_decision_settled_by_direct_inspec.what_was_done_instead: The save route optionally authenticates via stage::capture_context and stamps the SERVER-DERIVED principal into the SERVER-WRITTEN receipt payload as minted_by_principal. validate_document_save_receipt compares THAT field against event.canonical_actor_id(). Ownership lives in the payload; per-agent attribution stays in the actor_id column.

implementation_result.non_weakening_verification_by_kernel_bui: Verified by reading flight_recorder.rs:885-940 directly, not accepted from the sub-agent report. The comparison is an UNCONDITIONAL conjunct of the authentic expression - no if, no ||, no unwrap_or(true). Absent, blank or non-string minted_by_principal fails CLOSED, and a blank claiming actor can never match a blank minted principal. Every other conjunct is byte-identical: event_type, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, actor_kind, kernel_task_run_id, session_run_id, correlation, the "saved" discriminator, workspace_id, content_hash. The old client-column comparison is absent from the file.
implementation_result.ac_120_1_PROVEN: mt120_authenticated_save_stamps_derived_principal_without_rebinding_actor_id asserts byte-equality between the save receipt minted_by_principal and the principal an INDEPENDENT capture_context-gated route (Stage) derives from the same binding. Deliberately not a local digest recomputation: the first attempt did recompute locally and produced a FALSE RED because serde_json::Value key ordering differs from the typed enum serialization - the product was correct and the test was wrong.
implementation_result.ac_120_2_PROVEN: Cross-principal receipt is unclaimable (400) with ZERO ledger and FR residue, and the SAME envelope succeeds once the receipt is minted by the claimant - proving the rejection was the principal and not an unrelated clause. Absent/empty/whitespace minted_by_principal also unclaimable. The ledger actor_id column is asserted == the per-agent id AND != the derived principal, so attribution is provably intact. Nothing was deleted or relaxed.
implementation_result.backward_compatibility: A save with NO session token behaves exactly as before: it succeeds, but its receipt carries no anchor and is unclaimable. This is what keeps app/src (a forbidden path for this MT) and roughly 28 tokenless test call sites working without a scope breach. A token that is PRESENT but invalid or stale is 401 HSK-401-DOC-SESSION and never downgrades to the header identity - that silent fallback was identified in advance as the single most dangerous shape this change could take.
implementation_result.namespace_guard: A client x-hsk-actor-id in the reserved handshake-native: namespace is 403 HSK-403-DOC-ACTOR-SPOOF on every document route unless it equals the principal the server just derived. Without this the derived principal would become a bearer-equivalent label an unauthenticated caller could stamp - the MT contract own positive control proved that works today.
implementation_result.run_ids_untouched_on_purpose: kernel_task_run_id, session_run_id and correlation_id are compared against the CLIENT-supplied FR payload. Adopting capture_context own run ids (the shape api::memory middleware uses) would have replaced one unsatisfiable clause with three.

original_scope.summary: Make the document_saved receipt-ownership check enforceable by authenticating the document-save route as the same principal the Flight Recorder derives, instead of leaving a clause that rejects every legitimate save.

defect_detail.why_unsatisfiable: The recorder actor is SERVER-DERIVED as handshake-native:{pid}:{birth_fingerprint} by capture_context. POST/PUT /knowledge/documents... has NO session authentication and takes its actor from a client header (backend_client::DOC_ACTOR_ID = handshake-native-editor). No route exposes the derived identity, so the frontend cannot stamp it. The two values can never match for a real product save.
defect_detail.runtime_evidence: Real save then document_saved ingestion with a genuine token and all fields matching => HTTP 400 HSK-400-INVALID-EVENT. Same session, undo_fired => HTTP 200. Positive control: issuing the save with x-hsk-actor-id set to the server-derived actor makes ingestion return HTTP 200 - proving the clause is the SOLE blocker.
defect_detail.security_framing: MT-109 intent is that a save receipt can only be claimed by the principal that minted it, which requires BOTH endpoints to authenticate the same principal. Today only one does, so the clause does not enforce the invariant - it rejects everything legitimate. A guard that always fails is an outage wearing a security control costume, and it also trains future implementers to weaken it.

original_scope.summary: Give the MCP navigation snapshot a real screen rect so the bounds it publishes to models describe the actual window instead of egui's unsized 10000x10000 default viewport.

defect_detail.mechanism: HandshakeApp::refresh_mcp_snapshot (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs, around lines 12474-12509) builds a FRESH egui::Context and runs it with RawInput::default(). RawInput::default() leaves screen_rect as None, and egui then falls back to a 10000x10000 viewport (egui-0.33.3/src/input_state/mod.rs:368, viewport_rect: Rect::from_min_size(Default::default(), vec2(10_000.0, 10_000.0))). Every widget therefore lays out as if the window were 10000px wide.
defect_detail.consequence: UiNodeBounds published through crate::accessibility::snapshot::collect_ui_tree_snapshot (src/accessibility/snapshot.rs:339, bounds populated at :275-287) are geometrically valid for a 10000x10000 window that does not exist. argus.inspect() consumers - models, the visual debugger, and any HBR-VIS acceptance step - receive coordinates that cannot be compared to a rendered frame.
defect_detail.measured_evidence: During MT-119 PT-119-3 a mounted assertion read the saved-search Restore control right edge from the inspect tree at 2605.875px against a derived pane edge of 1557.34px. 2605px lies beyond the ENTIRE 2560px harness window, while the GPU frame captured in the SAME run showed both controls comfortably inside the pane. The inspect tree was describing a synthetic 10000-wide re-render. A second, independent symptom of the same fresh-context root cause is already known: egui::Memory-backed state such as popups and context menus reads back EMPTY through the same path.
defect_detail.why_it_is_not_only_a_test_problem: argus.inspect() is the product's model-navigation surface. A model asked to check whether a control is clipped, overlapping, or off-pane will get a confidently wrong answer. The defect degrades model vision in normal operation, not merely in proofs.

acceptance_criteria: AC-121-1: refresh_mcp_snapshot renders with a screen_rect that reflects the live viewport rather than RawInput::default(). When no live viewport is available, it uses an explicit, documented, realistic fallback size and records which one it used - it must never silently fall back to the 10000x10000 default.

AC-121-2: bounds published through the MCP snapshot for a known surface are within the declared viewport. Prove it with an assertion that FAILS if the unsized context is restored - a guard that stays green under the old behaviour does not ship (this is the exact vacuity failure PT-119-3 hit twice).
AC-121-3: no author_id, role, value, or tree SHAPE changes. This MT changes coordinates only. Re-run the MT-113 author-id proofs and the MT-029 mounted visual baselines and show them unchanged.

AC-121-4: state explicitly whether egui::Memory-backed surfaces (popups, context menus) become readable once the context is sized, or whether that is a separate fresh-context defect. Do not claim it is fixed without evidence.
AC-121-5: the UserManual entry for the Argus/MCP inspect surface records that bounds are viewport-relative and names the viewport source, so a no-context model knows what the coordinates mean.

original_scope.summary: RESCOPED 2026-08-16 from PostgreSQL to the embedded SurrealDB store. The original microtask targeted isolated per-test POSTGRESQL SCHEMA teardown and a 1009-schema backlog; PostgreSQL has been physically deleted, so there are no schemas to leak and no pg_class rows to count. THE UNDERLYING RISK IS UNCHANGED AND STILL REAL, which is why this is rescoped rather than closed: test isolation now comes from a per-run HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR directory containing a handshake-surreal RocksDB store, and a test process that is killed or panics mid-run strands that directory on disk. Each store is measured in hundreds of megabytes to gigabytes, so a stranded-store backlog degrades proof runs and consumes the artifacts volume exactly the way the schema backlog did. Prior work exists and must be built on, not duplicated: tests/surreal_test_store_crash_safety_tests.rs and tests/surreal_test_store_support/ were created by the 2026-08-13 session and are committed. RocksDB holds an exclusive LOCK file while a store is open, and SurrealStorage::shutdown on Windows already waits until that LOCK is re-acquirable, so LOCK acquirability is the available liveness signal for deciding whether a store directory is genuinely orphaned or still owned by a live run.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test store directory is reclaimable after the owning process dies without running any teardown code. Reclamation must not depend on a graceful shutdown path, because the whole failure mode is that the process never reached one.

Reclamation NEVER removes a store belonging to a live run. Ownership is decided from an observable liveness signal - the RocksDB LOCK file is exclusively held while a store is open - and not from age heuristics or a naming convention alone. A concurrent proof run must survive a reclamation pass untouched.

Reclamation is safe under concurrency: two reclamation passes running at once, or a reclamation racing a starting run, must not delete a store that the starting run is about to open, and must not double-delete.

kernel_builder_diagnosis_2026_08_16.root_cause: NOT a label-painting bug and NOT a galley text mismatch. line_layout.rs:354 already lays out exactly inline_view::chip_label(link) for the hsLink atom (the MT-068 glyph-overlap fix), so the pill and the label are built from the SAME string. The defect is in inline_view::chip_rect_for_span (src/rich_editor/wikilinks/inline_view.rs:396). It collapses the atom to ONE bounding rect derived from only the FIRST and LAST cursor rects: Rect::from_min_max(min(start.min.x, end.min.x), min(start.min.y, end.min.y)) .. (max(start.max.x, end.max.x), max(start.max.y, end.max.y)). For an atom that wraps across MANY rows that is geometrically wrong: the true painted region is the union of one rect PER WRAPPED ROW, each spanning that row to the column edge, but the collapsed rect is only the narrow x-band between the two cursor positions. So the pill is narrow while the text occupies the full column on every row - measured as pill_max_x=984 against label ink reaching x=2399, with the 720pt reading column ending at x=1560.
kernel_builder_diagnosis_2026_08_16.correct_fix_direction: Make the chip PER-ROW instead of one collapsed rect. The chip must derive one rect per galley row the atom spans (egui Galley exposes rows, and pos_from_cursor gives per-cursor rects), paint one pill segment per row, and paint the label per row aligned to those same rows - or stop painting the label separately and let the underlying galley run paint in the chip colour instead of transparent, which removes the two-rules problem at the source. Whichever is chosen, the hit-test/AccessKit rect must still enclose the whole atom so pointer activation and swarm targeting do not regress, and MT-068 must not regress into doubled glyph runs.
kernel_builder_diagnosis_2026_08_16.do_not: Do NOT fix this by shrinking, clipping, or eliding the label, and do NOT wrap the label into the collapsed pill - that is the rejected fix above. Do NOT change chip_rect_for_span to a single row-1-only rect either: the existing unit test chip_rect_offsets_by_scroll_adjusted_origin_mc001 and the MT-068 hit-test contract require the activation rect to cover the whole atom.

original_scope.summary: mcp/binding.rs::atomic_replace publishes the discovery binding with a hand-rolled MoveFileExW that receives raw encode_wide() paths - no verbatim prefix, no GetFullPathNameW - while every neighbouring operation on the SAME path goes through Rust std::fs, which normalizes. At a CWD-relative length of 260 the rename fails with ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND after the temp file has already been created, hardened, written and fsynced.

defect_detail.site: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mcp/binding.rs, atomic_replace Windows branch lines 424-449; error surfaced at 454-458; wrapped into "MCP discovery binding was not safely published" at mcp/server.rs:163-168.
defect_detail.measured_empirically: A purpose-built non-longPathAware Win32 probe (GetFileAttributesW) measured the exact boundary with CWD set to the crate root: 259 chars resolves, 260 and 261 return err=3. The temp name is swarm_mcp_binding.{pid}.{19-digit-nanos}.tmp, so a 5-digit PID lands on exactly 260.
defect_detail.reproduced_from_the_real_failing_run: The failing run left its PID in an artifact path: handshake-test/native_gui/pid-69592/frames/block_collection_view_screenshot-pid69592-1.png, mtime 2026-08-13 00:21:34, matching the lock created at 00:21:54. PID 69592 is five digits; reconstructing its exact temp filename and probing it returns err=3, while the 235-char destination .json resolves fine. The reported os error 3 was reproduced exactly, from the real PID.
defect_detail.why_the_message_misleads: The error names the 235-char DESTINATION, which is perfectly valid. The 260-char SOURCE is what Win32 rejected. Anyone reading the message looks at the wrong path.
defect_detail.manifest_checked_not_assumed: The test binary carries NO embedded manifest at all - searched for manifestVersion / longPathAware / RT_MANIFEST in ASCII and UTF-16, all absent, with pwsh.exe as a positive control. Machine-wide LongPathsEnabled=1 therefore cannot rescue it.
defect_detail.the_stale_lock_theory_is_REFUTED: A repo-wide census of Handshake_Artifacts found ~48 binding roots, 42 of which carry a .lock with no .json. That is the by-design resting state: binding.rs:294-296 declares the lock persistent and remove_binding (:582-586) deletes only the .json. The lock carries ZERO diagnostic signal. A swarm_mcp_binding.lock.stale-preserved-20260812 file exists in exactly one root - evidence an earlier agent chased this red herring. The advisory OS lock is released automatically when its process dies, so no age or PID breaker is missing.
defect_detail.why_only_this_one_binary_fails: Every other Argus test installs ScopedArgusAppData (canonical_argus_driver.rs:49-58), which CANONICALIZES the root to absolute - 196 chars, always safe. test_block_collection_view.rs:2491 deliberately passes app_data: None and keeps the ../../../../ relative fallback root from :2080-2083. original_scope.summary: The LeaseRegistry is already wired into the widget-mutation RPC path, but its exclusive guard ends after dispatch while ActionChannel keeps the same target busy until post-render acknowledgement. A later agent can therefore acquire the registry lease and immediately receive ActionError::TargetBusy from the still-busy channel. Align the two serialization windows by retaining the per-target registry guard while boundedly retrying only the channel's typed TargetBusy response above the ActionChannel borrow; release the channel mutex before every await and preserve ActionChannel as the terminal-lifetime authority.

evidence.registry_call_sites: mcp/session.rs routes click_widget and set_value through DispatchPlan::ExclusiveWrite and calls LeaseRegistry::try_acquire on the synchronous path and LeaseRegistry::acquire_async on the shared async server path.
evidence.window_mismatch: The registry guard is released when dispatch returns, while ActionChannel::enqueue scans queue plus in_flight and returns ActionError::TargetBusy until post-render acknowledgement. The second serialization window outlives the first.
evidence.the_failing_proof: test_swarm_concurrency::test_swarm_concurrency_n5. Its own comment states the contract: "Under a generous timeout the lease only WAITS; every mutation must enqueue." All five agents target shell.chrome.theme-toggle / the rail input concurrently, and agents 0, 1 and 2 each got {"code":-32004,"message":"widget 'shell.chrome.theme-toggle' already has an unacknowledged mutation"} on action 0. The test asserts queued == true.
evidence.the_registry_already_does_the_right_thin: leases.rs provides waiting acquisition and a timeout backstop. The missing behavior is a bounded wait for the longer-lived ActionChannel transaction after the registry lease has been acquired.

the_constraint_that_makes_this_architect.why_a_retry_loop_inside_dispatch_request: dispatch_request (tools.rs:344-350) is SYNCHRONOUS and holds `channel: &mut ActionChannel` for its whole body. Waiting there would block while holding the exclusive borrow the frame loop needs in order to drain the queue and RELEASE the very lease being waited on. It would not merely be slow - it would deadlock.
the_constraint_that_makes_this_architect.where_the_wait_must_live: In McpSession::dispatch_shared_async, above each short ActionChannel mutex borrow. Each retry attempt may resolve and enqueue while holding the mutex, but the mutex must be dropped before the async delay so the frame loop can acknowledge the prior action.
the_constraint_that_makes_this_architect.guard_lifetime_decision: Keep ActionChannel queue plus in_flight state as the authority from successful enqueue through terminal acknowledgement. Hold the registry guard across bounded TargetBusy retries only until the new action enqueues or the single request deadline expires. This forms a gap-free handoff: while retrying the registry guard excludes another session; enqueue records the new channel transaction while the channel mutex is held; after enqueue the channel transaction already excludes the target before the registry guard drops. Carrying a registry guard inside pending/in_flight records would duplicate ActionChannel's established terminal-lifetime authority and couple the async lease registry to render acknowledgement without adding exclusion.

acceptance_criteria.AC-134-1: After winning the per-widget registry lease, a mutating RPC that encounters ActionChannel::TargetBusy waits and retries instead of returning -32004 immediately. Registry acquisition plus channel-busy retries share one documented request deadline, and no ActionChannel mutex guard or borrow is held across an await.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-2: test_swarm_concurrency::test_swarm_concurrency_n5 passes: five concurrent agents, every mutation enqueued, no torn state, each response carrying its own agent_id.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-3: The single request deadline still fires for both registry contention and a channel transaction that remains busy. Prove both paths return typed -32004 within the configured bound; a wait that can never time out is a hang, not a fix.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-4: No ActionChannel mutex guard or borrow is held across an await. The change remains per-resource: two agents targeting different widgets do not wait on each other's registry lease, and no new multi-key ordering is introduced.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-5: The guard lifetime decision is recorded in scope.the_constraint_that_makes_this_architectural.guard_lifetime_decision and the implementation preserves that gap-free registry-to-channel handoff.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-6: The in-product UserManual states that same-widget mutations wait until the current post-render acknowledgement completes, may return typed -32004 at the bounded deadline, and different-widget mutations remain independently leased.

proof_targets.PT-134-2: Focused RED-path tests show both a held registry lease and a persistently busy ActionChannel return typed -32004 within the configured single request deadline.

original_scope.risk_if_missed: HBR-SWARM parallel steering does not work under contention. Same-widget agents lose actions during the registry-to-channel lifetime gap even though both serialization mechanisms individually work.

CORRECTION_2026_08_13.what_was_wrong: This MT was filed claiming the MT-028 LeaseRegistry has ZERO call sites and was "built and never connected". That is FALSE. The registry IS wired, through mcp/session.rs: try_acquire at :199 (SharedRead on the snapshot resource) and :216 (ExclusiveWrite on the per-widget target key), driven by SwarmSession::decide (:147-166) which routes click_widget / set_value with a non-empty target to DispatchPlan::ExclusiveWrite.
CORRECTION_2026_08_13.how_the_error_was_made: The originating investigation grepped for acquire_all and .acquire( and found nothing outside leases.rs. The real API in use is try_acquire, which the grep never matched. A negative result from one spelling was treated as proof of absence. Recorded because the same mistake is cheap to repeat.

what_is_actually_true.the_lease_does_wait: LeaseRegistry::try_acquire (leases.rs:162-176) loops until a deadline, so the "generous timeout only WAITS" contract the test states IS implemented for the lease.
what_is_actually_true.the_second_mechanism_does_not: There are TWO serialization mechanisms with DIFFERENT lifetimes. The lease guard is released at the END of SwarmSession::dispatch (session.rs documents this: "The registry lease guard drops at the end of this call"). The ActionChannel then keeps its own per-target in-flight transaction until POST-RENDER acknowledgement, and that second mechanism fails FAST: ActionChannel::enqueue scans queue + in_flight and returns ActionError::TargetBusy immediately (action.rs:1077-1093), which tools.rs:314 maps to the same -32004.
what_is_actually_true.consequence: A second agent can win the lease - because the first agent already released it at dispatch end - and then still be rejected by the channel because the first action has not been acknowledged yet. The wait protects the wrong window. That is why test_swarm_concurrency sees -32004 on action 0 for agents 0, 1 and 2 despite a generous lease timeout.

CORRECTION_2026_08_13.what_this_MT_should_actually_decide: Whether the exclusive lease should be HELD until the action terminalizes (aligning the two windows, so the wait covers the period that actually blocks), or whether the channel TargetBusy should itself become a bounded wait. The first is a lifetime change to the guard; the second changes fail-fast semantics inside the channel. Either way the earlier framing - "wire up an unwired registry" - is not the work.
CORRECTION_2026_08_13.what_survives_from_the_original_filing: The deadlock CONSTRAINT still holds and is still the trap: dispatch_request (tools.rs:344-350) is synchronous and holds &mut ActionChannel for its whole body, so a wait placed there blocks the frame loop that would release what is being waited on. Any fix that lengthens a hold must not lengthen it across that borrow.
