original_lifecycle.ready_for_validation_summary: MT-135 implemented. MECHANISM (AC-135-2, generalises without an allowlist): egui 0.33.3 keeps AT MOST ONE open popup per viewport - a single OpenPopup{id,pos} slot in egui::Memory. Top menu-bar dropdowns, pane/tab/tree/editor context menus and any future Popup::menu / Popup::context_menu / Popup::open_memory caller all funnel through that one slot, so copying it projects EVERY memory-backed popup surface, present and future, with no registration step for a new menu. egui exposes no public 'which popup is open' getter (Memory::popups is private), so the new module accessibility/popup_projection.rs composes two public halves: Memory::areas().visible_layer_ids() (an open popup always has a visible layer, because Popup::show renders through Area::new(popup_id)) probed by Popup::is_id_open for exact match. Only one can match, so the unordered HashSet cannot make it nondeterministic. The stored POSITION is load-bearing, not polish: Popup::context_menu uses PopupAnchor::PointerFixed, so re-opening without the position yields anchor.rect == None and egui SILENTLY RENDERS NOTHING - a position-less projection would have looked like a fix while publishing nothing. WHY THE MT-121 COORDINATE CONTRACT SURVIVES (AC-135-3): only egui::Id + Option<Pos2> crosses the context boundary. No focus, no Memory::data (where scroll offsets and widget state live), no area geometry, no interaction state. The blanket Memory clone that the contract's red-team flagged is explicitly rejected in the module docs. Proven rather than asserted: published and rendered bounds for the menu leaf matched with ZERO delta - published=(x=381.000, y=286.000, w=586.000, h=18.000) rendered=(x=381.000, y=286.000, w=586.000, h=18.000) - and the whole-tree viewport guard was re-run WITH a menu projected. The MT-121 theme-toggle proof is unchanged and still exact. PT-135-1 RED (verbatim): 3 tests failed, including the inverted witness - "AC-135-1: 'ctx-menu.pane.pop_out' is open in the live rendered frame, so it MUST appear in the published MCP snapshot". PT-135-1 GREEN (verbatim): 'test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed'. PT-135-3 CLOSED-MENU PROOF (AC-135-5) checks two closed states that fail differently: never-opened (a projection that force-opened menus would publish it) and opened-then-dismissed-with-Escape (a latching or stale projection would keep publishing a menu the operator dismissed). Runtime line: never_opened=false while_open=true after_escape=false. Stale entries cannot leak because Memory::end_pass drops any popup not kept open during the pass and the projection is read fresh per capture, never cached. PT-135-4 REGRESSION: native lib suite 2074 passed / 0 failed (the MT-121 baseline was 2069; +4 are this MT's unit tests and +1 predates it, which the implementer recorded as NOT_INSPECTED rather than guessing). Ten targeted integration binaries green including test_context_menu, test_context_menu_surfaces and test_menu_wireup. Implementer evidence only, not validation.
ready_for_validation_v4_open_items: SUBMENUS NOT_INSPECTED: one-level submenus (ui.menu_button) keep MenuState in Memory::data, which is deliberately not projected, so an open SUBMENU may not render in the capture pass. The parent menu and its items do. No acceptance criterion covers this and it was not proven either way.

Menu-internal keyboard cursor is not projected: render_menu_root stores its highlight index in Memory::data. Item identity, bounds and clickability are correct, but a model reading tree-focus inside an open menu sees the first actionable item rather than the operator's arrowed-to item. Fixing it means copying Memory::data, which is the exact layout risk this MT rejected.

A popup opened in memory but never rendered in a live frame is not in visible_layer_ids() and will not project. Not currently reachable, since context_menu::request_open is followed by a live frame, but it is a real edge; the mcp_open_top_menu forward projection covers the equivalent case for top menus only.

No GPU-pixel proof was run. AC-135-3 is proven against the live AccessKit tree - the same tree the platform UIA adapter receives - with an exact zero-delta match, and the contract's gui_obligation accepts accesskit-tree evidence. The real-GPU path is available on this host if a validator wants pixels.

original_scope.summary: HandshakeApp::refresh_mcp_snapshot builds a BRAND-NEW egui::Context for the model-vision capture pass. That fresh context has an EMPTY egui::Memory, so any surface whose open/closed state lives in egui::Memory is absent from the published MCP snapshot even when it is visibly open in the live window. app.rs already works around this for two surfaces by hand-copying the Reading-mode store and the open top-menu into the capture context, but pointer-opened PANE CONTEXT MENUS have no such projection. Consequence: a model driving Argus cannot see, target, or steer any context menu - it is invisible in argus.inspect while a human sees it on screen. This was proven live during MT-121 by tests/test_mcp_snapshot_viewport.rs::mt121_memory_backed_context_menu_remains_invisible_to_the_sized_capture_pass, which shows author_id 'ctx-menu.pane.pop_out' present in the rendered kittest frame and absent from the published snapshot. MT-121 fixed viewport SIZING only and deliberately did not fix this; the failing condition is asserted as current behaviour there, so that assertion MUST be inverted by this MT.

acceptance_criteria.text: A pane context menu that is open in the live window appears in the published MCP snapshot with its stable author_id, role and bounds, exactly as it appears in the rendered AccessKit tree.

The projection is general, not a hard-coded allowlist of one menu: any egui::Memory-backed surface the shell can open is projected into the capture context by a single documented mechanism, and adding a new menu does not require a new bespoke copy step.
Bounds published for the projected menu lie inside the declared SnapshotViewport and match the rendered frame, preserving the MT-121 coordinate contract.

The MT-121 test mt121_memory_backed_context_menu_remains_invisible_to_the_sized_capture_pass is inverted to assert the menu IS visible, and its comment is updated so it no longer documents the defect as expected behaviour.
A closed context menu is still absent from the snapshot: the fix must not make menus permanently visible, which would be a different falsehood.

landed: process_ledger/writer.rs: PostgresProcessLedgerStore -> SurrealProcessLedgerStore over the kernel_process_lifecycle table. The two ON CONFLICT update lists were reproduced field-for-field in Rust: START coalesces optional identity columns and takes the earliest started_at but never touches stopped_at/exit_code/stop_reason, so a replayed START cannot erase a STOP that already landed; STOP overwrites only the stop triple. Both merges stay idempotent, so the existing retain-and-retry loop re-converges.

session_checkpoint/writer.rs: append-only writes keyed on checkpoint_id. An existing id is skipped and NOT counted in the returned row count, reproducing ON CONFLICT (checkpoint_id) DO NOTHING plus rows_affected, so an idempotent retry neither errors nor double-counts.

flight_recorder/fr_emitter.rs: batch flusher appends kernel_event_ledger through the embedded store. Ledger ordering stays owned by the database via event_sequence DEFAULT sequence::nextval. A real regression was prevented: the old batch was one transaction, so a mid-batch failure rolled back and the retained batch replayed each event exactly once; with per-record commits the flusher now drains the successfully-written prefix before propagating the error, restoring exactly-once.
process_ledger/table.rs: deleted the three PostgreSQL DDL/DML constants as dead residue.
progress_2026_08_16.known_regression_disclosed: Batch atomicity is lost in the process ledger: rows now commit individually rather than as one transaction. The merges are idempotent so recovery still converges, but this is a real semantic change and is recorded rather than hidden.
progress_2026_08_16.deliberate_non_regression: process_ledger/reclaim.rs went 4 -> 5 errors ON PURPOSE. Its store no longer has a PgPool, and reclaim depends on an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE stopped_at IS NULL ... RETURNING whose lock covers the kill-and-STOP decision. Emulating that with read-then-write would be a silent correctness regression, so the honest compile error was left in place.

ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.by: KERNEL_BUILDER-20260903-213930 (orchestrator, on Operator instruction to resolve it on product grounds)
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.question: The implementer refused to claim the tripwire exemption for knowledge_code_index_tests.rs:265, which holds PostgreSQL DDL (BIGSERIAL, public.users), and escalated rather than widening the exemption quietly. Correct call - it is not a tripwire.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.inspected: MIGRATION_SQL sits in a block with PKG_JSON, JSON_SCHEMA and BROKEN_RUST, one fixture per language, consumed by mt097_adapter_parses_each_language_and_versions. It is the code indexer's parser corpus.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.ruling: EXEMPT under a newly named third category, content-as-data. It is neither a tripwire nor a violation. Handshake's code indexer exists to index the user's repository, and real repositories contain SQL. This fixture is how the product proves it can parse a .sql file, exactly as PKG_JSON proves it can parse package.json. The PostgreSQL flavour of the DDL is incidental - it is representative user content, not a statement about Handshake's own storage.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.why_scrubbing_it_would_be_the_wrong_outc: Removing it would not make the product less dependent on PostgreSQL, because it never was here. It would delete the only proof that the indexer handles SQL, degrading a real product capability to satisfy a rule aimed at something else. Governance would be damaging the thing it exists to protect.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.anti_laundering_test: The exemption is deliberately hard to abuse: the tokens must live inside a string literal or fixture file used as parser input, and must not appear in an import, dependency, feature gate, env var, connection string, or any code path. If a token can influence how the process talks to a database, it is a dependency and exemption (b) does not apply. A future reader can apply that test mechanically.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.operator_note: The Operator asked for this to be resolved on product grounds rather than ruling on it themselves. This is that ruling.

These tests compile against the handshake_core lib, so this MT is implementable only after MT-136/137/138 make the lib compile cleanly. Patterns to follow: unit-adjacent storage tests use SurrealStorage opened at a temporary HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR (see tests/surreal_test_store_support/ and storage/surreal/test_inspector.rs behind the surreal-test-support feature); API-level tests exercise the product HTTP surface; migration-corpus assertions (apply_migration, DDL-constant asserts) are retired with the corpus per MT-139's recorded SEVER decision and replaced by the schema.surql coverage proof. acceptance_criteria.text: No file under src/backend/handshake_core/tests/ DEPENDS ON sqlx, PostgreSQL, psql, PG DSN env vars, SQLite, or PL/pgSQL. Two exemptions, both narrow. (a) Deliberate forbidden-technology tripwires whose purpose is detection. (b) Content-as-data fixtures: literal text that exists to be PARSED OR INDEXED as user content, never executed or connected to. Exemption (b) holds only where the tokens appear inside a string literal or fixture file consumed as parser input, and nowhere in an import, dependency, feature gate, env var, connection string, or code path. If a token can influence how the process talks to a database, it is a dependency and not a fixture.
Every retained test compiles and its proof intent is preserved at equivalent strength against the embedded store; every retired test names the superseding proof or the removed behavior it covered.
Durability-class tests (process ledger, session checkpoint, CRDT persistence, EventLedger) prove behavior across a real store close-and-reopen, not against mocks.
The backend test suite runs green on the pinned toolchain with per-run HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR isolation and no shared-store contention between binaries.

decisions_20260910.why_acceptable: These rows are DERIVED: they carry no authority, are never read as the source of truth for document content, permissions or ledger receipts, and are fully rebuilt from the source document's content by the next save (replace_knowledge_document_backlinks is an idempotent content-derived rebuild). decisions_20260910.blast_radius: A dangling derived row pointing at a tombstoned document until the source document is next saved. Visible in backlink panes and Loom edge counts; not visible in document content, versions, drafts, ledger receipts or search authority.
decisions_20260910.what_it_does_NOT_cover: It does NOT cover R1-1-2 (the delete transaction deciding backlink scope from a title-uniqueness read outside its write set, and stamping that decision into a durable tombstone). defect_20260911_retry_budget.summary: guarded_mutation used RetryContext::unbounded(); RetryPolicy::CONTRACT.maximum_elapsed (2000 ms) bounds only SLEEPS (an in-flight attempt is deliberately never raced against the deadline so an acknowledged commit is never dropped); each attempt was bounded by statement_timeout (300 s) and maximum_attempts is 8. One contended mutation could therefore occupy 8 x 300 s = 40 minutes uninterruptibly. A2 s R1-1-2 remediation, which makes every title-mutating transaction write the title anchor, raised same-title contention and turned that latent bound into a real stall.
defect_20260911_retry_budget.contract_violation: AC-142-5 bound requirement and hbr_obligations.STOP (a timeout must be a typed failure, never a silent park); red_team minimum control every retry loop is explicitly bounded
defect_20260911_retry_budget.fix: ONE budget for the whole logical mutation: deadline = now + statement_timeout, used for the keyed-lock wait, set as RetryContext.deadline and enforced around the whole retry via SurrealStorage::with_operation_deadline; with_data_operation clamps each attempt to min(statement_timeout, remaining budget) through an OPERATION_DEADLINE task-local; retry refuses to START an attempt once the deadline has passed (typed Exhausted{MaxElapsed}). New worst case for one mutation: one statement_timeout (300 s default, 30 s if the caller tightens it).

original_scope.summary: Prove and harden the SurrealDB-only storage layer for parallel model swarms. Exercise concurrent point reads, range/search queries, creates, idempotent upserts, optimistic updates, deletes and multi-record projection transactions against a real embedded SurrealDB RocksDB store. Measure conflicts, retries, retry exhaustion, lock wait, operation latency and throughput. Replace the coarse process-global RICH_DOCUMENT_MUTATION_LOCK and KNOWLEDGE_UPSERT_LOCK in storage/surreal/knowledge.rs with record/workspace-keyed contention control where local coordination is useful and with atomic Surreal transactions plus in-transaction guards where correctness must survive independent clients or future remote deployment. A keyed in-process lock is only a local contention-shaping optimization; it MUST NOT be the sole correctness mechanism for uniqueness, compare-and-set, versioning, idempotency, ledger/projection atomicity or lost-update prevention. Preserve SurrealDB as the only database: no PostgreSQL or SQLite driver, fallback, fixture, syntax, environment variable, server spawn or compatibility path may be introduced.

embedded_mode_boundary.supported_topology_to_prove: One embedded SurrealDB engine owns one RocksDB store path and is shared through cloned in-process database/client handles across parallel async tasks.
embedded_mode_boundary.forbidden_claim: Do not claim that multiple processes may open the same embedded RocksDB path concurrently. Do not use a second embedded engine on the same path as a distributed-concurrency test.
embedded_mode_boundary.future_remote_compatibility: All cross-client correctness invariants live in atomic SurrealQL transactions, conditional guards, stable record identities, version checks and idempotency keys. Tests must be able to use independent lock registries over the same database client/context so a process-local lock cannot masquerade as distributed correctness. A remote-server run may be added when a managed endpoint is configured, but an unconfigured remote run is reported as NOT_RUN_UNCONFIGURED and never as PASS.

contention_control_requirements: Eliminate RICH_DOCUMENT_MUTATION_LOCK and KNOWLEDGE_UPSERT_LOCK as coarse process-global serialization points.

Choose the narrowest verified stable key for local coordination: record identity for single-record mutations, normalized workspace-plus-natural-key for uniqueness/upsert races, and workspace identity only for invariants that genuinely span a workspace.
Cross-record operations use deterministic key ordering or one atomic Surreal transaction so nested acquisition cannot deadlock.
The keyed-lock registry has bounded or reclaimable cardinality; completed one-off record keys cannot leak lock entries indefinitely.
No read-only operation waits on an unrelated write lock. Disjoint-record and different-workspace writes must be observably concurrent.

Every invariant formerly protected only by a coarse mutex is revalidated inside the committing Surreal transaction. An independent-client proof must remain correct when the clients do not share a keyed-lock registry.

Inventory other process-global storage mutation locks under storage/surreal/. Retain singleton lifecycle/schema-bootstrap locks only with a written invariant; route product-data global locks to a follow-on MT or harden them in this MT when they share the same proven primitive and test surface.

retry_policy_requirements.algorithm: Bounded exponential backoff with full jitter and a caller-visible deadline/cancellation boundary.
retryable_only: Engine errors proven by pinned-version evidence to represent transient transaction/write conflict or temporary busy conditions
A transaction guard's explicitly typed retryable snapshot-change outcome when the complete operation is idempotent
never_retry: Validation, authorization, not-found, schema, corruption or invariant errors
Expected-version mismatch or stale caller state that requires the caller to merge or refresh
Unknown database errors without a pinned-version classification
Any operation without a stable idempotency key or otherwise proven replay safety
retry_policy_requirements.exhaustion_semantics: Return a typed retry-exhausted error preserving the final cause, attempts and elapsed time; emit the structured diagnostic exactly once; never spin, silently downgrade, fall back to another database or report success after an uncommitted write.
retry_policy_requirements.testability: Jitter randomness and time are injectable or seedable in tests so bounds, cancellation and exhaustion are deterministic without weakening production jitter.

ci_deterministic.workload: Mixed reads, searches, creates, idempotent upserts, optimistic versioned writes, deletes and multi-record projection/ledger transactions over same-record, disjoint-record, same-workspace and different-workspace keys.
ci_deterministic.hard_bound: Every worker and the whole test have explicit timeouts; a timeout is a failure, not an ignored test.

extended_local.workload: Seeded repeatable large-dataset run with configurable dataset size, read/write mix, key skew and contention ratio.
extended_local.gate: Run before READY_FOR_VALIDATION_V4 on the operator-designated machine. The report records machine context and selected numeric budgets; absolute cross-machine latency is not inferred from CI.

acceptance_criteria.text: A current pinned-version research basis is recorded before code changes and distinguishes SurrealDB transaction/isolation guarantees, embedded RocksDB single-owner constraints, retryable error classes and future remote-server behavior from assumptions.

RICH_DOCUMENT_MUTATION_LOCK and KNOWLEDGE_UPSERT_LOCK no longer exist as coarse global locks. Same-record and natural-key contention remains correct through atomic Surreal transactions and guards; disjoint records and different workspaces demonstrate at least two simultaneous in-flight writes rather than global serialization.

The deterministic CI profile runs at least 16 workers and 2,000 operations against a real embedded RocksDB store, covers reads, queries, creates, idempotent upserts, optimistic updates, deletes and multi-record transactions, and finishes with zero lost writes, zero duplicate natural keys/idempotency effects, zero partial projections or ledger receipts, zero dirty reads of uncommitted state, zero hangs and exact final counts/hashes.

Same-record tests prove explicit semantics: an expected-version race produces one committed winner and typed stale/conflict outcomes for losers; identical idempotency-key replays converge to one durable effect; disjoint-record operations all commit without unrelated lock waiting. No test accepts last-writer-wins where the API promises optimistic concurrency.

Retry behavior is bounded, jittered, cancellation-aware and limited to proven retryable/idempotent operations. Tests prove first-attempt success, eventual success after retryable conflicts, terminal-error no-retry, maximum-attempt exhaustion, maximum-elapsed exhaustion and cancellation, with no attempt beyond either configured bound.

The extended local profile runs at least 64 workers and 50,000 operations and emits a versioned machine-readable report containing workload seed/configuration, engine/SDK version, embedded/remote mode, dataset cardinality, attempted/succeeded/failed counts by operation, conflicts, conflict rate, retries, retry rate, retry exhaustion, lock-wait p50/p95/p99, operation-latency p50/p95/p99 by class, throughput, maximum concurrent operations, timeout/cancellation counts and final integrity verdict.

Lifecycle stress races reads and writes with graceful shutdown. Shutdown stops admission, drains or cancels in-flight work within an explicit bound, closes the one owning embedded engine without deadlock, then a real close-and-reopen proves every acknowledged write and no unacknowledged partial transaction is durable.

Correctness remains green for independent clients/SurrealDatabase wrappers that do not share a keyed-lock registry but do share the same owning database context. This proves local locks are optional contention control and database transactions/guards own future remote/distributed correctness.

A repo-wide and dependency scan proves no PostgreSQL or SQLite runtime, driver, fallback, fixture, syntax, environment variable or server-spawn path was introduced. SurrealDB remains the only database.

The keyed-lock registry's entry count returns to its documented idle bound after high-cardinality churn, and deterministic lock ordering plus timeout-backed tests prove no deadlock when multi-record operations overlap in opposite input order.

The built-in UserManual documents the embedded single-owner topology, safe parallel swarm use, retry/exhaustion behavior, how to run both load profiles, how a no-context model reads the structured report, and the distinction between current embedded proof and future configured remote proof.

Two independent adversarial reviewers using different lenses approve the final implementation after all blocker findings are remediated and re-reviewed: one concurrency-correctness/atomicity lens and one load/performance/lifecycle/operability lens.

original_scope.summary: A mounted next-day click on the daily-journal surface must actually navigate while a calendar read for the previous date is still in flight. Today it does not. test_calendar_interop::mounted_navigation_while_old_get_is_in_flight_cancels_without_fr_residue clicks the journal-EDITOR next-day control (author_id `journal-next-day`, JOURNAL_DATE_NAV_AUTHOR_IDS, rendered by rich_editor/daily_notes/journal_panel.rs line 439) and then waits for the MOUNTED graph::daily_journal_panel::DailyJournalState to reach the second date with projection NoEvent. It never does. The mock request log captured at the failure shows only first-date traffic after the click: GET /knowledge/documents, POST /loom/search-v2, PUT /loom/journals/<first_date>, GET /api/flight_recorder, and the /calendar/events GET for <first_date> twice. There is no PUT /loom/journals/<second_date> and no /calendar/events GET for <second_date>. Because the editor's own handler (journal_panel.rs, DateNavOutcome::Navigated -> state.store.open(date)) would itself have issued that PUT, the editor's nav did not advance either. The click is therefore NOT landing on the control at all, rather than landing and being dropped downstream. Two mechanisms remain open and must be distinguished by measurement before any fix: (a) POSITION drift, since egui_kittest dispatches a click at the observed node's rect and the conditional projection labels in graph/daily_journal_panel.rs ('Loading calendar event and activity...', 'Waiting for daily note...', 'Calendar binding paused...') appear and disappear as the transient read settles, moving every widget below them between the inspected frame and the frame that processes the click; (b) IDENTITY drift of an ANCESTOR of the nav row, the same class MT-113 and MT-117 hit. Stabilizing the DateNavWidget row itself was already attempted and did NOT change the outcome, and that attempt was reverted, so the row's own scope is not the cause. This microtask must also decide and record whether the mounted daily-journal panel is expected to follow the EDITOR's date navigation at all: the editor nav writes only the editor's own DateNav and store, while the mounted panel's nav advances only through DailyJournalEvent::DateNavigated emitted by the panel's own widget (author_ids DAILY_JOURNAL_DATE_NAV_AUTHOR_IDS, graph/daily_journal_panel.rs line 563). If no such cross-surface sync is intended, then the product contract is what needs stating and the test must be corrected to the surface that owns the state it asserts on, with the reasoning recorded rather than the assertion weakened.
original_scope.embedded_mode_boundary: Frontend-only. This microtask must not add, restore, or depend on SQLite or PostgreSQL, and must not change backend storage. The Calendar reads under test are served by the test's transient mock server, not by a real backend.

original_scope.summary: Make the in-crate cfg(test) modules in api/flight_recorder.rs and workflows.rs run against a live embedded SurrealDB store instead of a store that has already been shut down, and delete the vestigial skip branches that can no longer be taken. Today both modules build, but their setup_state helpers destroy the store before the first assertion runs.
original_scope.defect: Both helpers are declared to return Result<Option<AppState>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>. Each calls embedded_test_backend, moves the database and storage fields into the AppState, and then lets the partially-moved EmbeddedTestBackend fall out of scope at the end of the function. EmbeddedTestBackend carries a private cleanup field holding an Arc<TestStoreCleanupGuard> whose Drop shuts the store down and removes its data directory, and the Arc strong count is 1 at that point, so the shutdown always runs. Every test that then touches storage gets the embedded-database-is-closed error. This is the exact failure MT-144 diagnosed and fixed in the other five modules by returning the backend alongside the state and binding it so it outlives the test body.
original_scope.secondary_defect: Both helpers still return an Option and always return Some, a shape left over from the PostgreSQL era when the backend could legitimately be absent. 28 call sites in api/flight_recorder.rs and 26 in workflows.rs still open with a let-else that returns Ok early when the state is None, so each of those 54 tests carries a silent-skip branch that can never be taken. The branch is dead today, but it is the same construct that let 17 tests pass while proving nothing before MT-144 removed it.
original_scope.embedded_mode_boundary: SurrealDB and EventLedger only. No SQLite and no PostgreSQL may be added, restored, imported, or referenced as a live backend. Historical mentions in doc comments that explain why a skip branch was removed are permitted, matching the convention already used in storage/tests.rs and accepted for MT-144.
acceptance_criteria: AC-145-1: setup_state in both modules returns the EmbeddedTestBackend alongside the AppState so the store outlives every assertion, using the same tuple shape MT-144 established.

AC-145-2: every let-else skip call site becomes an unconditional binding that also holds the backend for the life of the test. The count is 55, not the 54 this contract first stated: api/flight_recorder.rs has 28 `let Some(state)` plus one `let Some(base_state)` at line 2982, and workflows.rs has 26. No test keeps a branch that can return Ok without asserting anything.

AC-145-3: no assertion is weakened, ignored, or deleted to make a test pass. Every test that fails once the store is live must be either fixed or recorded with a named owner and a stated reason; none may be quietly marked ignore.
AC-145-4: the full api::flight_recorder and workflows in-crate suites are run and their pass and fail counts recorded verbatim, including a per-test attribution for every failure.

AC-145-5: no SQLite or PostgreSQL BACKEND WIRING survives inside the cfg(test) modules this microtask touches - meaning no DSN, connection string, env var, feature gate, import, helper, or code path that would reach either engine. Historical naming in fixture data does not count and must not be rewritten: identifiers, file-path strings, labels, work-packet ids and assertion messages that merely contain the word are out of scope, because rewriting values a test stores and asserts on would risk AC-145-3. Live product references elsewhere in workflows.rs are also out of scope: the error string at line 2909 and the locus::sqlite_store::parse_locus_operation call at line 11034 are working product behaviour, not test-era leftovers.
AC-145-6: the product binary still builds, proving the change stayed inside cfg(test).

original_scope.risk_if_missed: 43 of the 55 in-crate tests in these two modules touch the store after setup_state and therefore fail deterministically with Database("embedded database is closed") the moment they are actually run; they currently compile and are counted as present while proving nothing. premise_correction_2026_09_04.retracted_claim: The original risk_if_missed said 54 in-crate tests 'cannot exercise storage at all'. That is wrong in two separate ways and is retracted here rather than quietly worked around in the implementation.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.error_1_overcounted: 12 of the 55 tests never touch the store after setup_state returns, so the store's lifetime is irrelevant to them and they would pass either way. api::flight_recorder has 11 such tests (its 29 setup_state tests break down as 18 that touch the store — 8 directly and 10 through a helper — and 11 that do not); workflows has 1 (25 of its 26 touch the store directly). The honest number of tests losing real proof is 43, not 54. The fix is still correct for all 55 because it deletes the dead skip branch from every one of them, but those 12 must not be counted as tests whose proof was destroyed.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.error_2_mischaracterised_mechanism: I then hypothesised, from a green RED, that the defect was racy — that the store was mid-teardown and tests passed or failed on timing. The implementer refuted that with measurement and was right. The behaviour is deterministic: the store handle is closed before the test body runs, so the first storage call returns Database("embedded database is closed") every time. What the discriminator actually is: whether the test touches the store after setup_state, not when it does so.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.why_the_first_red_was_green: The implementer's initial RED target, list_events_preserves_model_session_id_filter_and_payload, is one of the 11 flight_recorder tests that never touch the store — it uses only the in-memory DuckDB recorder. It was chosen because it was the first call site in the file. That is a measurement error in target selection, not evidence that the defect is absent, and the implementer identified it as its own error before I did.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.the_30_second_timeout_is_a_different_def: The 'shutdown failed: still draining operations after 30000 ms' line appears in BOTH the passing and the failing run, so it is a constant and not what separates them. Two distinct things are happening: the handle close takes effect immediately, which is what fails the storage-touching tests; the directory REMOVAL separately times out after 30 seconds and leaves the store on disk with os error 32. The latter is the MT-123 teardown defect, already disclosed there, and is unrelated to this microtask. Do not conflate them.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.incidental_cost_finding: TestStoreCleanupGuard::drop spawns a cleanup thread and joins it, so setup_state blocks up to 30 seconds on a shutdown that then times out anyway. Every one of these 55 tests pays that stall, which is roughly half an hour of pure teardown wait across the two modules and partly explains why a single test can run for 417 seconds. Recorded as an observation for whoever owns MT-123; not in scope here.
evidence: Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp-kernel-012-kb-0902-proof-logs/red2-workflows.log - model_run_timeout_ms_fails_before_simulated_runtime_finishes FAILED with Error: Database("embedded database is closed"), 0 passed 1 failed
premise_correction_2026_09_04.method_note: The corrected flight_recorder RED target was selected by a rule fixed in advance — first store-touching test in file order — specifically so the evidence could not be shopped for. The implementer committed to reporting a green result as falsifying the deterministic reading rather than trying another target.

figure_is_a_lower_bound.note: The '12 tests never touch the store after setup_state' figure is a LOWER BOUND on store usage, not a firm count, and should not be quoted as exact. The implementer's classifier matched textual `.storage` and `.surreal` references only, so it missed tests that reach the store indirectly through API handlers such as ingest_native_editor. At least one test I recorded as non-store-touching, native_editor_same_id_mutated_envelope_conflicts, in fact reaches the store that way — which is why it went on to fail on a genuine assertion once the store was live. The direction of the error is safe: more tests were losing proof than the figure implies, not fewer. The implementer identified this itself after the suite results contradicted its own classification.

AC-146-1.evidence: proposal_delete_race_never_leaves_workspace_orphans green. Measured cause, not the contract guesses: surrealdb 3.2.0 on RocksDB uses OptimisticTransactionDB with set_snapshot(true) and WRITE-WRITE conflict detection only; get_for_update is never called anywhere in surrealdb-core, so there is no read-set tracking and no SSI. Insert and delete write disjoint keys so neither aborts: the insert ASSERT record::exists reads a snapshot that still holds the workspace, and REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE is a snapshot-bound scan that cannot see a reference key written by a transaction uncommitted at snapshot time. Both contract candidate mechanisms are facets of that one cause. Fix orders the two snapshots via the existing FEMS mutation lock plus an in-transaction existence guard mapped to 404.

AC-146-2.evidence: list_proposals_is_bounded_deterministic_and_workspace_scoped green, including its bounded-limit and workspace-scoping assertions. Cause code-verified: ORDER BY had no status-priority term. Fixed with a SurrealQL-computed status_rank ordered ahead of created_at DESC, proposal_id ASC, so ORDER BY still precedes LIMIT and no Rust-side sort is used.

AC-146-3.evidence: Fixed and proven twice. In isolation: 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2112 filtered out; finished in 711.45s'. In full-suite context it no longer appears among the failures. Root cause was two compounding defects. (1) list_commit_rows withheld an un-published FR-EVT-MEM-004 until its FR-EVT-MEM-003 sibling was published; the causal rule was moved to dispatch time via commit_event_dispatch_ready so the listing now reports the true durable pending set while a pack-built event still cannot precede its commit event. (2) The test selected pending events on payload proposal_id, which FR-EVT-MEM-004 cannot carry because validate_memory_pack_built_payload enforces a closed key allowlist omitting it. Operator authorised a SELECTOR-ONLY correction (lifecycle.operator_authorisation_2026_09_04). The authorisation named activity_span_id but required verifying first that BOTH events carry it; verification showed only the pack builder sets it and FlightRecorderEvent::new defaults it to None, so selecting on it alone would have dropped FR-EVT-MEM-003 and been wrong in the opposite direction. The selector used is trace_id, which both events genuinely share by construction: the commit event is built with stable_uuid('fems-memory-proposal:{proposal_id}') as its trace_id and the pack event copies that same value. Expected count of 2 and the assertion message are unchanged, and flight_recorder/mod.rs was not touched.

AC-146-4.evidence: No assertion was weakened, reordered, relaxed or deleted. The single test-region edit is the selector correction expressly authorised by the Operator and permitted by the amended AC-146-4; the expected count and the assertion message are byte-identical, verified by grep after the edit. implementation_findings.detail: flight_recorder/mod.rs:4307 require_allowed_keys enforces a closed allowlist. Recommend the test filter on activity_span_id. Operator decision required per AC-146-4.

implementation_findings.summary: A quarantined FR-EVT-MEM-003 could permanently strand its FR-EVT-MEM-004 sibling, invisible to every listing.
implementation_findings.detail: The old list_commit_rows gate hid a pack-built row until its commit row was published, and unlike the lifecycle outbox there is no requeue path for a quarantined commit-outbox row (only requeue_quarantined_memory_lifecycle_event exists). The gate removal in this MT closes that hole while preserving the ordering guarantee at dispatch time. The change is currently proven only by the suite staying otherwise green; the corrected D-146-3 test would prove it directly. The Orchestrator reviewed this and directed that it be kept rather than reverted.

implementation_findings.summary: Changing an outbox event payload is durable-evidence-affecting.
implementation_findings.detail: ensure_commit_outbox compares row.event_hash against a re-derived event_json_hash, so altering the FR-EVT-MEM-004 payload shape would make pre-existing rows conflict on retry with the message about commit outbox identity being bound to different evidence. Any Operator decision to add proposal_id to that payload must account for existing rows; cold-genesis stores are unaffected.

implementation_findings.summary: concurrent_workspace_commits_publish_a_pack_containing_both_items intermittently returns 500 on concurrent commit A under full-suite load.
implementation_findings.detail: Registered as unassigned. Three points stay open. Attribution to MT-146 is neither established nor cleared: the test passed on a binary already containing all three of this MT's product changes, and passed 3/3 in isolation, but no controlled comparison was run. The mechanism by which this MT could widen the window without causing it remains open: reconcile_workspace_memory_commit_events is workspace-scoped, so concurrent commits reconcile the same rows, and the listing-gate removal returns FR-EVT-MEM-004 alongside its FR-EVT-MEM-003 in the same pass rather than deferring it, increasing rows contended per pass; a project_commit_event failure propagates through reconcile(...)? and surfaces as exactly this 500. Nobody has yet read what the 500 actually wrapped: internal_error is the outer wrapper from storage_error, and the inner StorageError is only emitted to tracing as fems_memory_api_internal_error, which the test harness does not capture. Reading that inner error is the highest-value next step. The decisive controlled experiment, not yet run because it costs two recompiles, is to revert this MT's three product files and run the test repeatedly to compare failure rates.

operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.what_was_asked: AC-146-4 forbids the implementer from editing any assertion in the three target tests and routes 'the test asserts the wrong thing' to the Operator. The implementer established by measurement that commit_outbox_recovers_on_restart_and_preserves_original_evidence_across_later_commits filters pending events on event.payload["proposal_id"], while validate_memory_pack_built_payload (flight_recorder/mod.rs:4307) enforces a closed ten-key allowlist with an empty optional list that does not include proposal_id. FR-EVT-MEM-004 therefore cannot carry that key and the filter can never match it, making the assertion pending_outbox == 2 unsatisfiable by construction.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.what_is_authorised: A narrow correction to the SELECTOR ONLY: the test may filter on the field that actually carries the proposal linkage, activity_span_id, in the form fems-memory-proposal:{proposal_id}. The assertion itself is NOT authorised to change - the expected count of 2 and the assertion message stay exactly as written. This is a repair to a filter that cannot match, not a weakening of what the test proves; the assertion's intent, that both the commit and pack-built events survive the crash window un-published and non-quarantined, becomes testable for the first time rather than being quietly impossible.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.what_is_not_authorised: Changing the expected count, changing or softening the assertion message, adding proposal_id to the FR-EVT-MEM-004 payload allowlist, or touching flight_recorder/mod.rs. Nothing else in any of the three tests may be edited.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.why_the_payload_route_was_rejected: The implementer found (F-146-C) that ensure_commit_outbox compares event_hash, so adding proposal_id to the pack event's payload would change that hash and make pre-existing durable rows conflict on retry. The two routes are not equivalent: correcting the selector touches no durable data, while changing the payload is durable-evidence-affecting on a live store. That finding is what settled the choice.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.verification_required: Before choosing the selector, confirm from the source that BOTH FR-EVT-MEM-003 and FR-EVT-MEM-004 carry activity_span_id in the expected form. If the commit event does not, the filter must match both events correctly rather than silently dropping one - a filter that matches only the pack event would make the count wrong in the other direction and would be just as broken as the current one.
operator_authorisation_2026_09_04.effect_on_acceptance: AC-146-3 becomes obtainable and AC-146-5 returns to its original target of 29 passed / 0 failed. If the corrected test still fails, that is a genuine product defect and must be reported as such, not filtered around a second time.

selector_substitution.why: The verification clause in this authorisation required confirming that BOTH FR-EVT-MEM-003 and FR-EVT-MEM-004 carry activity_span_id before the selector was chosen. They do not. build_memory_commit_flight_recorder_event never sets activity_span_id and FlightRecorderEvent::new defaults it to None, so only the pack builder sets it. Filtering on activity_span_id would have matched FR-EVT-MEM-004 alone, dropped FR-EVT-MEM-003, and produced left: 1 again - wrong in the opposite direction. The recommended field was wrong and the mandated check is what caught it.
selector_substitution.substituted_selector_is_correct: trace_id is shared by both events by construction: the commit event is built with stable_uuid("fems-memory-proposal:{proposal_id}") as its trace_id, and the pack event copies commit_event.trace_id. It is scoped to the proposal, and because the listing returns only commit-outbox rows it selects both events of this commit and nothing else. The test derives the same value with its own deterministic_uuid_from_seed.
selector_substitution.independently_verified_by_orchestrator: Checked against the source rather than accepted: zero activity_span_id references in the commit builder at fems_memory.rs:1013-1049; trace_id set from stable_uuid("fems-memory-proposal:{proposal_id}") in that builder; commit_event.trace_id copied at fems_memory.rs:1065; and stable_uuid (fems_memory.rs:1138) and deterministic_uuid_from_seed (api/memory.rs:1659) are byte-identical implementations - SHA256, first 16 bytes, same UUID v4 bit-fixing.
selector_substitution.within_authorisation: Yes. The authorisation text names activity_span_id but its verification clause explicitly contemplates this case: "the filter must match both events correctly rather than silently dropping one". Substituting a field that satisfies that requirement is what the clause directs. Recorded here rather than left silent, because the Operator approved a named field and what shipped is a different one.
selector_substitution.third_route_correctly_refused: The implementer did not add activity_span_id to the commit builder, which would have looked like the obvious fix. That is a product change to a hashed event, and ensure_commit_outbox compares event_hash, so it would have reintroduced the exact durable-evidence hazard (F-146-C) that got the payload route rejected.
selector_substitution.unchanged: Expected count still 2. Assertion message byte-identical. flight_recorder/mod.rs untouched. One line of behaviour changed.

original_scope.summary: Fix three defects in the memory proposal surface that the restored in-crate test layer exposed: workspace deletion leaves an orphan proposal under a concurrent insert, the proposal list does not put approved proposals first, and the commit outbox restart-recovery path does not reach its expected state. All three are pre-existing behaviour, not regressions from the test restoration.
original_scope.embedded_mode_boundary: SurrealDB and EventLedger only. No SQLite and no PostgreSQL may be added, restored, imported, or referenced as a live backend.

defects.observed: panicked at src/api/memory.rs:3931: assertion left == right failed: workspace deletion must cascade proposals. left: 1, right: 0.
defects.what_it_means: The test issues delete_workspace and create_memory_proposal concurrently through tokio::join, then counts fems_memory_proposals rows still pointing at the deleted workspace. One row survives. A memory proposal is left referencing a workspace that no longer exists.
defects.code_context: schema.surql line 4886 already declares the workspace_id field on fems_memory_proposals as record<workspaces> with ASSERT record::exists($value) REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE, and delete_workspace_record in storage/surreal/workspaces.rs runs an explicit transaction that clears the Loom dependants and then deletes the workspace, relying on that cascade for the remaining workspace-owned rows. So the cascade is declared, yet an orphan survives under concurrency.
candidate_mechanisms_not_yet_confirmed: The proposal insert evaluates record::exists in a transaction that began before the delete committed, so the assert passes against a snapshot while the cascade has already run, and the insert lands afterwards with nothing left to cascade it.
The SurrealDB reference cascade only reaches rows whose reference was recorded before the delete transaction took its view, so a row created during the delete is invisible to it.
defects.instruction: Confirm which mechanism is real by measurement before changing anything. Do not implement against the guess.

defects.observed: panicked at src/api/memory.rs:2875: assertion left == right failed: approved proposals must lead the actionable projection for crash-safe commit recovery. Observed order was the newer proposal then the approved one; expected the approved one first.
defects.what_it_means: After one proposal is set to approved, the list route must return it ahead of a newer pending proposal, because the actionable projection is what crash-safe commit recovery walks. It does not.
defects.code_context: list_memory_proposals in storage/fems_memory.rs around line 2114 orders strictly by created_at DESC then proposal_id ASC. There is no status priority term, so an approved proposal can never lead a newer pending one. The defect is in the ordering clause, and the diagnosis is code-verified rather than inferred.
defects.instruction: Add a deterministic status-priority ordering term ahead of the recency term, keeping the tie-break stable so the bounded limit case stays deterministic. Do not reorder in Rust after the fact if that would break the LIMIT semantics the test also asserts.

defects.observed: thread 'api::memory::tests::commit_outbox_recovers_on_restart_and_preserves_original_evidence_across_later_commits' (48040) panicked at src\api\memory.rs:4672:9: assertion `left == right` failed: crash leaves the commit (FR-EVT-MEM-003) and pack-built (FR-EVT-MEM-004) events durably un-published and non-quarantined left: 1 right: 2
defects.result_line: test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2112 filtered out; finished in 247.38s
defects.what_it_means: After the simulated crash the test counts the pending commit-outbox events for proposal A and expects exactly 2: the commit event FR-EVT-MEM-003 and the pack-built event FR-EVT-MEM-004, both left durably un-published and non-quarantined. Only 1 is present. One of the two events is either never written on the commit path, or is already published or quarantined at the point the crash is simulated, so the crash window does not preserve the evidence the recovery path is supposed to replay.
defects.code_context: The assertion is at src/api/memory.rs:4672 and filters list_pending_memory_commit_events on the proposal id. The commit path writes into fems_memory_commit_fr_outbox and fems_memory_lifecycle_fr_outbox, both keyed on the proposal with ON DELETE CASCADE in schema.surql. The count is short by one before the recovery poll is ever reached, so the defect is on the write side of the crash window, not in the startup projector.
defects.instruction: Determine by measurement which of FR-EVT-MEM-003 and FR-EVT-MEM-004 is missing from the pending set and why. Do not assume it is the pack-built event. The later assertions about projector recovery and evidence preservation across a second commit are unreached today, so they must also be proven once the count is right.

defects.observed: ##[error]Unable to locate executable file: pnpm. Please verify either the file path exists or the file can be found within a directory specified by the PATH environment variable.
defects.cause: actions/setup-node was configured with cache: "pnpm", which makes the action shell out to pnpm for its store path during setup. corepack enable ran as the next step, so pnpm was not yet on PATH. The job died about ten seconds in, long before any product step.
defects.fix: Move the corepack enable step ahead of Setup Node.js in both jobs.

defects.observed: error: failed to run custom build command for `libdbus-sys v0.2.7`. The system library `dbus-1` required by crate `libdbus-sys` was not found.
defects.cause: The Ubuntu runner image does not ship the dbus-1 development package, and libdbus-sys is a transitive dependency of the backend, so every job that compiles handshake_core failed at exit 101 in a build script.
defects.fix: Install libdbus-1-dev and pkg-config in each job that compiles the backend, folding it into the existing ripgrep install where one is already present.
defects.attribution_correction: An earlier draft of this contract also listed secret_scan and sbom_generate under this defect. The baseline per-job table shows both of those failed at their go install step, before any cargo invocation, so they were never dbus failures. They are carried separately as D-147-6.

defects.observed: backend-storage runs a [sqlite, postgres] matrix with a postgres:16-alpine service container, setting DATABASE_URL=sqlite::memory: on one leg and POSTGRES_TEST_URL plus DATABASE_URL on the other.
defects.cause: Stale configuration left behind by the storage pivot. Both backends were removed from the product, so even with the dbus fix these legs would test wiring that no longer exists and would keep the pipeline permanently red.
defects.fix: Collapse the matrix to a single embedded run, drop the service container and both env-configuration steps, and keep the storage conformance and MCP e2e invocations unchanged.

defects.observed: Database("HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT must name the absolute _Artifacts root for embedded tests"), reproduced locally at src/storage/tests.rs:48.
jobs: every job that runs an embedded-store test
defects.cause: The embedded test backend resolves its store root only from an explicit absolute HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT, with relative and current-directory fallbacks deliberately forbidden. CI never set it, so any embedded test would fail on startup rather than on its assertion.
defects.fix: Declare HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT once at workflow level beside CARGO_TARGET_DIR.

defects.observed: The only Linux compile of handshake_core sat behind the frontend lint, dependency-cruiser and test steps inside the validate job.
defects.cause: Not a failure of its own, but a structural weakness: any frontend failure hides the cross-platform build result, and RC-004 then has nothing to cite even when the backend compiles cleanly.
defects.fix: Add a small cross-platform-build job that runs cargo check with all targets and all features on Linux and depends on nothing else.

defects.observed: secret_scan fails at the step Install gitleaks (pinned) and sbom_generate fails at the step Install syft (pinned), both in the baseline run 33666580708 and again in the post-repair run 33818193204.
defects.cause: Not yet determined. Both steps go install a pinned tool version under Go 1.22.4 and fail before any cargo invocation, so this is independent of every other defect in this contract. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
defects.fix: Diagnose from the completed run log and either fix in this microtask or hand to a named owner under AC-147-6. Must not be left unattributed.

defects.observed: validate fails at the step Docs check. The step asserts five governance documents directly under .GOV/roles_shared/: START_HERE.md, SPEC_CURRENT.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, RUNBOOK_DEBUG.md and PAST_WORK_INDEX.md.
defects.cause: None of the five lives at that path any more. START_HERE, ARCHITECTURE and RUNBOOK_DEBUG moved to .GOV/roles_shared/docs/, SPEC_CURRENT to .GOV/spec/, and PAST_WORK_INDEX to .GOV/reference/. The step had been unreachable behind the pnpm failure for as long as that failure existed, so the stale paths were never surfaced. Verified against the branch tree, not the working directory, because .GOV is a junction locally.

defects.observed: error: target `mex_tests` in package `handshake_core` requires the features: `duckdb-flight-recorder`, `test-utils`
defects.cause: All four supply-chain jobs invoke the mex_tests target without the features it declares, so cargo refuses before compiling or running anything. In the baseline this was hidden behind the dbus and go install failures in three of the four jobs.
defects.fix: Pass --features duckdb-flight-recorder,test-utils on each of the four invocations.

defects.observed: backend-storage killed by the runner with exit code 143 and the message: The runner has received a shutdown signal. Reproduced in two consecutive runs, 33818193204 and 33819481804, both around thirty minutes into compiling and before any assertion ran.
defects.cause: The invocation is --tests storage_conformance, which builds every integration test binary in the crate and only then filters by name. The crate has 393 integration test targets, so the job was compiling the whole tests/ tree, including targets that do not compile at all, until the runner died. This also explains why the job never reached a test result in any historical run.
defects.fix: Use --test storage_conformance and --test mcp_e2e_tests, singular, so each job builds exactly the one target it needs. The set of tests that actually run is unchanged.

defects.observed: error: target `storage_conformance` in package `handshake_core` requires the features: `test-utils`, exit code 101, in run 33820723714.
defects.cause: Cargo.toml declares required-features for both targets this job runs: storage_conformance needs test-utils, and mcp_e2e_tests needs duckdb-flight-recorder and test-utils. Neither invocation passed them. This was invisible until D-147-9 was fixed, because the job had been dying at the runner before cargo got as far as checking the target's features.
defects.fix: Pass the declared features on both invocations.

ac_148_3_correction_2026_09_05.reason: I wrote AC-148-3 as --all-targets --all-features. The implementer pointed out that llama-cpp-sys-2 is optional behind the llama-cpp-runtime-engine feature, so the literal --all-features form drags a native llama.cpp C++ build into a criterion whose actual purpose is that the tests tree compiles with no E0599. A third-party native build failing is neither proof nor blocker for this microtask. This is the same drafting error I have now made three times in this packet: writing a criterion broader than its intent and having the implementer find it unsatisfiable or irrelevant on the edge.

AC-148-6.review_basis: KERNEL_BUILDER independently re-verified the central claim before accepting it: tempfile resolves to 3.27.0 in Cargo.lock, and `pub fn from_path` does not exist anywhere in the vendored tempfile-3.27.0 source. AC-148-6.summary: create(), close_for_reopen(), shutdown() and the Drop impl behave exactly as the previous tempfile::TempDir-based code did: delete-on-drop unless released first. OwnedTempRoot::drop calls fs::remove_dir_all exactly once per lifecycle. No directory leak is introduced by this fix.
AC-148-6.material_qualification: The old call TempDir::from_path(data_dir) never compiled, because from_path has never existed on TempDir in any tempfile 3.x release (it belongs to TempPath, which is single-file, not a directory). There is therefore no working prior baseline for open_existing to have regressed from. OwnedTempRoot::adopt is the FIRST WORKING IMPLEMENTATION of a contract that close_for_reopen's doc comment already described before the fix.
AC-148-6.consequence_for_proof: Because open_existing never compiled, no close-and-reopen durability proof in this crate has ever executed. PT-148-2b is therefore the first-ever runtime execution of that path, not a confirmatory formality. A compile-only gate is explicitly insufficient for this microtask.
AC-148-6.not_a_silent_fold_in: The intent is stated in-source in OwnedTempRoot's own doc comment within the same diff, and in the commit body of 6d5d705f. AC-148-6's requirement that a behaviour change be stated explicitly rather than folded in silently is satisfied.

contract_defect_20260909.finding: AC-148-3 names `cargo check --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml --all-targets` with no --features. contract_defect_20260909.manifest_observation: Cargo.toml declares 89 [[test]] blocks, 88 carrying required-features, but only 15 mention surreal-test-support while 28 test files consume the gated API. Reconciling that is a Cargo.toml change, which lies outside the allowed_paths of MT-141 (tests/ only), MT-148 (2 files) and MT-149 (src/ plus 1 test file).
contract_defect_20260909.discriminating_run: compile-gate-4 with --features surreal-test-support,test-utils determines whether this is contract wording only or also a manifest defect.

ac_148_3_correction_20260909.precedent: Mirrors ac_148_3_correction_2026_09_05, in which the contract author corrected this same criterion after the implementer showed the literal --all-features form was unsatisfiable for reasons unrelated to this microtask.
ac_148_3_correction_20260909.problem: As written, AC-148-3 is satisfied by `cargo check --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml --all-targets` with no --features. That command cannot compile this tree at any commit, because 28 test files consume APIs gated behind `surreal-test-support` (test_inspector, test_mutator, SurrealTestInspector, RowFilter, ScalarValue, bootstrap_mt137_*) and `test-utils` (InMemoryLlmClient). It is not a statement about whether the tests tree compiles.
ac_148_3_correction_20260909.correction: AC-148-3 is satisfied by the --all-targets run with `--features surreal-test-support,test-utils` completing with no E0599 and no could-not-compile error originating in tests/**. The feature list is not a relaxation: it is the minimum set the crate's own test targets require. The `--all-features` variant remains SECONDARY and best-effort exactly as the original criterion says, because --all-features enables llama-cpp-runtime-engine and drags in the third-party llama-cpp-sys-2 native C++ build, whose failure says nothing about this microtask.

defects.title: Fresh Windows checkouts get CRLF .surql files and cannot bootstrap any embedded test
defects.observed: Every embedded test in a newly created worktree fails at verify_compiled_manifest before any assertion runs. The symptom presents as schema drift, which invites misdiagnosis as a schema or migration bug.
defects.cause: .gitattributes pins .md, .mjs, .json and a long list of governance paths to eol=lf but never *.surql. git check-attr text eol on src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql returns unspecified, so a fresh Windows checkout materialises those files with CRLF. The product include_str!s them in four places and hashes the bytes, so the manifest check fails.
defects.why_it_hides: Long-lived worktrees are unaffected because their files were already LF on disk. The defect is invisible until someone creates a new worktree, which is exactly when it costs the most.
defects.fix: Add *.surql text eol=lf to .gitattributes and renormalise the affected files so the committed bytes match.
defects.care_required: This renormalises every .surql in the tree. Verify afterwards that the compiled-manifest hashes still match and that an embedded test actually bootstraps -- do not assume the attribute alone is sufficient.

defects.title: The integration test tree does not compile on any host
defects.observed: error[E0599]: no associated function or constant named `from_path` found for struct `TempDir` in the current scope --> tests/atelier_surreal_support/mod.rs:124:49, followed by: error: could not compile handshake_core (test "atelier_command_corpus_tests").
defects.cause: Cargo.toml declares tempfile = "3", which resolves to 3.27.0. TempDir::from_path no longer exists in that version and into_path is deprecated in favour of keep(). tests/atelier_surreal_support/mod.rs still calls from_path at line 124 and into_path at lines 41 and 159.
defects.why_it_hides: This is a dependency API change, not a platform difference, so it breaks everywhere. It is why cargo check --all-targets has not passed on any host, and why the MT-147 cross-platform CI job had to be scoped to --lib --bins to avoid reporting another microtask's defect as its own.
defects.fix: Either pin tempfile to a version that still has from_path, or rewrite open_existing so it does not wrap an already-existing directory in a TempDir. The second is likely correct: open_existing takes ownership of a caller-supplied path for a close-and-reopen durability proof, which is not what TempDir is for. Decide by reading the call site, not by taking this note as instruction.

original_lifecycle.fingerprint_defect_fixed: During MT-151 the schema INFO fingerprint briefly had two definitions (schema.rs pin computed with engine table catalog ids stripped; test_inspector.rs computing unstripped), which broke every inspector-backed test at store open. Fixed at the source: one shared schema::canonical_catalog_fingerprint used by bootstrap and the inspector. Why ids are stripped: INFO STRUCTURE tables[].id is the engine allocation counter - a fresh apply numbers tables by script position while an in-place delta DEFINE TABLE takes the next free id (observed 233 vs 300), so no table-adding lineage could match a raw-INFO pin; MT-138's atelier fingerprint already stripped them.

items.title: early-lock-release residual (RESIDUAL-MT142-EARLY-LOCK-RELEASE-ON-STATEMENT-TIMEOUT)
items.detail: The caller-side statement bound in SurrealStorage::with_data_operation now wraps every store, so a 300 s timeout drops the LOOM_/CANVAS_/OVERLAY_/MARKDOWN_IMPORT_/WIKI_COMPILE_/BLOCK_VIEW_/BRIDGE_/DEPENDENCY_ mutex guard while the abandoned statement may still be live. Audit every invariant those mutexes protect (MT-142 recon lock_inventory.json other_global_locks lists them with sites; the recon flagged the Loom journal get-or-create and the Canvas/Wiki identity-choice paths as lock-only candidates). For each invariant that is ALSO enforced database-side (UNIQUE index, THROW guard, CAS) record that and move on. For each invariant that is LOCK-ONLY, add the database-side guard (a UNIQUE index or an in-transaction THROW) so early release is safe, and prove it with a test that races the path with the lock registry disabled. Fallback, only where a guard is not cheap: exclude that specific store from the caller-side bound with a written reason in a doc comment, so it returns to its pre-MT-142 behaviour rather than gaining a new window. Do NOT migrate those stores onto guarded_mutation/keyed locks in this MT (D-142-1 follow-on).

items.title: exercise no_retry_window against a live saturation event
items.detail: MT-142 left HSK-STORAGE-NO-RETRY-WINDOW wired but unexercised (count 0 on every clean run). Add a deterministic test that forces it: open a store, set a small with_statement_timeout so the shared budget is tiny, make the first attempt slow enough to consume it (a SurrealQL SLEEP inside the retried statement, or a held keyed lock released only after the budget), and assert the typed HSK-STORAGE-NO-RETRY-WINDOW outcome with attempts == 1, distinct from HSK-STORAGE-RETRY-EXHAUSTED. Then feed the same outcome through the swarm classifier and assert no_retry_window.count == 1 and that it never lands in expected_stale_or_conflict.

items.title: cover the zero-remaining-budget branch
items.detail: with_data_operation refuses to dispatch when the OPERATION_DEADLINE task-local has already passed and returns SurrealStorageError::StatementBudgetExhausted { budget_ms }. Cover it with a unit test that sets an already-expired deadline and asserts the typed error and that no statement was issued (a resume-path store or the kv-mem dev engine is fine; a fresh cold apply is not required).

items.title: title-anchor reclamation using the anchor row as the conflict key
items.detail: MT-142 rejected reclamation because a naive 'read live count then delete' reintroduces the R1-1-2 window. The safe design uses the MT-142 write-set discipline: every title-mutating transaction already UPSERTs the anchor row, so a reclamation transaction that DELETEs the anchor row writes the same key and collides at commit with any concurrent create/rename/delete on that title - one side loses, its bounded retry re-reads and either recreates the anchor (create path) or sees the new live document and skips (reclaim path). Implement reclamation inside the atomic delete transaction (knowledge.rs delete_knowledge_rich_document_atomic, around :2068 where the anchor is written): after tombstoning, LET $live = count of live documents in the workspace whose title_key equals the anchor's; IF $live = 0 THEN DELETE the anchor row. Also cover rename (the OLD title's anchor may become orphaned, same rule). Prove with a race test in both orders: delete-of-last-holder racing a create of the same title must end with exactly one anchor row and one live document, never zero anchors with a live document. Record the invariant in a doc comment: an anchor row exists for a title iff at least one live document holds it, eventually, with the transient window bounded by a single conflicting transaction.

items.title: migrate the eight remaining product-data locks onto the MT-142 primitives
items.detail: Static mutexes and acquisition sites: LOOM_MUTATION_LOCK (loom_store.rs:51, 15 sites via its guard helper), CANVAS_MUTATION_LOCK (loom_canvas_store.rs:51, 9), OVERLAY_MUTATION_LOCK / MARKDOWN_IMPORT_LOCK / WIKI_COMPILE_LOCK (wiki_store.rs:40-42, 4), BLOCK_VIEW_MUTATION_LOCK (block_view_store.rs:38, 2), BRIDGE_MUTATION_LOCK (bridge_store.rs:23, 1), DEPENDENCY_MUTATION_LOCK (locus_store.rs:37, 1). MT-151 proved every invariant behind them is now database-guarded (its audit table is in MT-151.json lifecycle.i_151_4_audit), so the mutexes are pure contention shaping. Replace each with the knowledge.rs pattern: the per-SurrealDatabase KeyedLockRegistry on the narrowest stable key (LockKey::Record for single-record mutations, NaturalKey for uniqueness/upsert races, Workspace only for invariants that genuinely span a workspace - the MT-142 contract's contention_control_requirements), wrapped in guarded_mutation-style bounded retry with pre-reads inside the closure. Delete the static mutexes (PT: zero occurrences of the ten names in src/). Prove: (a) every existing target that exercises those stores stays green (loom, canvas, wiki, block_view, bridge, locus targets - enumerate them from tests/ and run each once); (b) a new disjoint-record overlap proof per store family in the style of tests/surreal_swarm_semantics_tests.rs::disjoint_records_commit_concurrently_without_unrelated_waiting, asserting engine-window overlap >= 2 for two different Loom blocks, two Canvas boards and two Wiki projections; (c) a same-record race per family asserting one winner and typed losers.

items.title: memory envelope: measure, then bound if the engine allows it
items.detail: The RSS finding (413.9 MB and 433.99 MB of growth on an 18 MB store; 25x operations and 20x store for 1.9x growth against the CI profile) suggests fixed engine overhead. Two steps. MEASURE: run the extended load profile at constant worker count and buffer configuration while varying only operation_count (e.g. 5000, 20000, 50000 at 64 workers, same seed family) and record growth_bytes per run; state whether growth is ingest-proportional or fixed with the three points. BOUND: the research basis records RocksDB defaults of write_buffer_size 128 MiB x max_write_buffer_number 32 on machines with >= 64 GiB RAM (surrealdb-core-3.2.0 cnf.rs:31-50), i.e. up to 4 GiB of write buffers, and that the SDK never passes a ConfigMap. Read cnf.rs and the kvs/rocksdb config path in the pinned crates for ENVIRONMENT-driven knobs (historically SURREAL_ROCKSDB_* variables) and for anything reachable through the SDK's opt::Config or Capabilities; if a supported knob exists, expose it through SurrealStorageConfig with a documented default that bounds the engine's memory to a stated envelope, set it at open, and re-measure at the same workload to show the effect. If no supported knob exists, say so with the file:line evidence and record the envelope as a documented characteristic with the measured curve. Write a memory-envelope section into the manual page.
closes: RSS finding turned into a measured answer

items.title: FEMS_MUTATION_LOCK and STAGE_INSERT_LOCK under the caller-side statement bound
items.detail: Both take their mutex OUTSIDE with_data_operation, but a statement timeout still returns Err through them and drops the guard while the abandoned statement may be live. Then migrate both onto the keyed registry + bounded retry as in I-152-2 and delete the statics.

original_closure.outcome: Every Loom HTTP route listed in scope.routes runs its protected-table reads and writes inside the authenticated account (record-user) session with least-privilege PERMISSIONS, so an owner succeeds, an anonymous caller and another account are denied with no side effect, and no Loom route executes a protected flow as root.

specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings.

**[LM-RLS-002]** Authority tables default to `PERMISSIONS NONE`; every grant is explicit at the database layer and rechecked by ResourceBroker. Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions.

Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary." 02:2773: "- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;" 02:2776: "Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer." LM-RLS-001: "**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings." LM-RLS-002: "**[LM-RLS-002]** Authority tables default to `PERMISSIONS NONE`; every grant is explicit at the database layer and rechecked by ResourceBroker. Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions."

For each of the 68 routes in scope.routes, the handler authenticates the caller with authorize_request (resource kind and action per the route's semantics: reads = ResourceAction::Read + fs.read; creates/updates = Update or Create + fs.write; deletes = Delete + fs.write) BEFORE any protected-table access, and every protected-table read and write of that request executes inside state.surreal.with_record_user_scope(ctx.record_user_scope, ...). No route in scope keeps a root-session read or write of a protected table (including root ensure_workspace_exists lookups that disclose existence: authorize workspace read first, then look up under scope).

Least privilege at the database layer: every Loom table these routes touch has explicit record-user PERMISSIONS in schema.surql that admit exactly the owner's grant for that operation (fn::mt120_loom_block_access / fn::mt109_has_workspace_access with the matching action+capability) and nothing broader; tables currently PERMISSIONS NONE that a scoped route needs (loom_folders, loom_folder_members, knowledge_wiki_projections, loom_wiki_overlays, assets, media_asset_tiers, loom_collections + members, loom_ai_suggestions, knowledge_quick_switcher_recents, loom_block_view_fr_outbox) get per-operation predicates; update NONE on loom_canvas_boards / loom_canvas_placements and create/update NONE on loom_canvas_visual_edges get owner predicates; loom_edges select/create/delete admit user tag edges (not only SYSTEM mention edges) through fn::mt120_loom_block_access. Tables no scoped route needs stay PERMISSIONS NONE (LM-RLS-002 default).

Every kernel_event_ledger receipt appended by a scoped Loom write (KNOWLEDGE_LOOM_BLOCK_MUTATED, KNOWLEDGE_LOOM_TAG_MUTATED, folder/wiki/collection/suggestion/quick-switcher/view-definition/canvas viewport receipts) is accepted by a receipt predicate branch that checks $session = $auth.id, fn::mt109_ledger_access and the matching loom access, and carries the session principal as actor (never a System or header-supplied actor). The owner can read these receipts via GET /kernel/events/aggregates/:type/:id; another account reads 0 of them.

Per route family (blocks+pins+metrics, folders, wiki+overlays+bootstrap/drift/fanout, markdown import + asset import, tags+edges, assets+tiers, collections, views+graph+search+visual-debug, quick-switcher, AI jobs+suggestions, canvas viewport/cards/stage-cards/placements/visual-edges, block-view definitions+results, daily journal): (a) owner positive through the real HTTP route returns the success status and the canonical row reflects the change; (b) anonymous (no session headers) returns the constant denial and the canonical row is unchanged; (c) a second account returns the constant denial (or an empty list for list routes, never the other account's rows) and the canonical row is unchanged; (d) for write routes, a same-account read-only (viewer) principal is denied the write (LM-RLS-001 viewer) - if the grant model cannot express a viewer for a table, record that under residual_risks with the table name instead of inventing sharing.

Content types: owner/admin/member may create every LoomBlockContentType (note, file, annotated_file, tag_hub, journal) plus the existing canvas and view_def types through the scoped routes; the POST /loom/views/definitions and card/journal paths no longer need root to create their block rows.

Stage path of POST /loom/canvas-boards/:block_id/cards and POST .../stage-cards/:placement_id/compensate require an authenticated account session and run their writes under record-user scope (they are unauthenticated root writes today). The spawn_block_view_reconciler loop (api/loom.rs:2041 @2f49f2a6, tokio::spawn) must not perform protected writes as root on behalf of a user: it either re-enters the owning user's scope per work item or is limited to non-protected bookkeeping - record which.

Loom-owned workspace-delete blockers: rows in knowledge_quick_switcher_recents, loom_folders (+members), loom_ai_suggestions, loom_collections and any other Loom table named in fn::mt120_workspace_delete's zero-row checks no longer make an owner's workspace undeletable: the owner workspace delete (DELETE /workspaces/:id) removes them (cascade or predicate-permitted delete) and api::workspaces::tests::owned_workspace_delete_cascades_documents_versions_and_canvas_with_audit stays green with such rows seeded through the scoped routes.
