specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings.

**[LM-RLS-002]** Authority tables default to `PERMISSIONS NONE`; every grant is explicit at the database layer and rechecked by ResourceBroker. Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions.

Deny by default (unconditional, no decision needed): every route in scope.routes rejects a caller without a valid account session + live channel binding with the constant denial BEFORE touching any table, filesystem path, DuckDB store or process. This includes the Atelier routes (api/atelier.rs:300-1104 @2f49f2a6), locus, preferences, calendar, stage, canvases, knowledge CRDT/ingestion/memory/retrieval and GET /kernel/trace_projection.

Workspace-scoped tables (canvases, canvas_nodes, canvas_edges, calendar_sources, calendar_events, calendar_activity_spans, calendar_mutation_outbox, stage_capture_artifacts, knowledge_source_roots and ingestion children, kernel_crdt_updates/snapshots/denial receipts, knowledge memory/retrieval tables, preference_records/receipts with scope_kind='workspace'): the route authorizes against the workspace resource (Read+fs.read for reads, Update/Create+fs.write for writes, Delete+fs.write for deletes; fr.read for Flight Recorder reads) and every read/write runs inside with_record_user_scope; schema.surql gives each table per-operation predicates via fn::mt109_has_workspace_access(record::id(workspace_id), <action>, <cap>) instead of PERMISSIONS NONE. calendar events must no longer read other accounts' loom_blocks (calendar_activity.rs:224 @2f49f2a6).

Account-global surfaces without a workspace or owner column (atelier_* tables, work_packets/micro_tasks, preference_records with scope_kind 'global'/'surface', atelier_stealth_*): AC-154-2 applies now; per-row account isolation is decision-gated by D-154-3 (ownership model). Until decided, these routes must not read or write rows as root on behalf of a user beyond what AC-154-2 already requires, and the residual is recorded in residual_risks with the table list. PUT /atelier/intake/items/:id/loom-projection (atelier/intake.rs:1362 @2f49f2a6) must additionally authorize loom_block read on the target block (it currently lets any account make another account's workspace undeletable).

C2 risk closed: after a preference write, the owner reads the preference_record aggregate via GET /kernel/events/aggregates/preference_record/:id and sees the new receipt; another account sees 0 receipts.

original_closure.outcome: POST /kernel/product_screenshot_capture/execute only runs for an authenticated account session that holds the screenshot-capture capability; everyone else is denied before any process starts, and an authorized run is attributable to the session principal and its child process is always reclaimed.

specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary." 02:2776: "Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer."

Anonymous: a request without a valid account session token + live channel binding returns HTTP 401 (Operator 2026-09-23: 'anonymous -> 401'), and no process is spawned (no `node --version` pre-flight either). This status is route-local: do NOT change api::authority::constant_denial (403) used by every other route.

Authenticated account WITHOUT the capability `kernel.product_screenshot_capture.execute` in the session's delegated_capabilities returns HTTP 403 with the constant body {"error":"HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE"}, and no process is spawned. Deny by default: an absent, empty or unreadable capability list is a denial. Wildcards are not accepted (setup_local_owner already rejects '*' at storage/surreal/local_accounts.rs:374-375 @ab618f46).

Authorized (session holds the capability): the capture runs; the response keeps its current shape (schema_id hsk.kernel.product_screenshot_capture_execute_result@1, artifact, durable_receipt, proof, receipt) and the receipt/proof record the session principal (actor id + session id) as the initiator, not a constant or header value.

Process safety: the request body may no longer choose the executable or script. `node_binary` and `adapter_script_path` in ProductScreenshotCaptureExecuteRequest are ignored or rejected (400) when they differ from the server-side defaults ('node' resolved by the server; app/scripts/handshake-screenshot-capture.mjs); the handler never executes a caller-supplied path. The child process (kernel/product_screenshot_capture.rs:561 pre-flight and :590-606 adapter) runs off the async executor (spawn_blocking or tokio::process), has a wall-clock timeout, is killed and waited on (reaped) on timeout or request cancellation, keeps hide_console_window (no foreground window, Codex CX-SAFE-002), and a timeout returns a typed error, never a hang.

Negative tests exist and pass against the real router and real account-session store: anonymous -> 401 and zero spawns; account without capability -> 403 and zero spawns; authorized -> runs (or returns the typed AdapterDependencyMissing when node/playwright are absent - the test asserts the authorization passed, i.e. the error is not 401/403) and the result/receipt carries the session principal; caller-supplied node_binary/adapter_script_path -> not executed; a hung adapter is killed and reaped within the timeout (use a server-side test hook for the timeout value and a script that sleeps, placed under the owner TMP dir - no network, no foreground).

POST /api/bundles/debug/export (api/bundles.rs export_bundle :134 @ab618f46) requires an authenticated account session; the export scope must resolve to exactly one workspace (scope.wsid for workspace/time_window scopes; the job's workspace entity_ref or job_inputs.wsid for job/problem scopes - see bundles/exporter.rs job_matches_wsid :134-144) and the caller must pass authorize_request(Workspace, wsid, Read, 'fr.read'). A scope that cannot be resolved to one authorized workspace (e.g. time_window without wsid, a job in another account's workspace) is denied with the constant 403 and no job is created.

The export job records the requesting account (account_id, principal_id, session actor) in its job_inputs, and the export work (started via tokio::spawn -> start_workflow_for_job, api/bundles.rs:177-181; executed in workflows.rs:11353/11466 via DefaultDebugBundleExporter) reads SurrealDB (ai_jobs etc.) inside the requesting user's record-user scope (re-enter with_record_user_scope inside the spawned future, F5), never as root. ai_jobs gets a select predicate admitting rows whose workspace entity_ref the caller can read (fn::mt109_has_workspace_access(..., 'read', 'fr.read')); DuckDB Flight Recorder reads are filtered to the authorized wsid (DuckDB has no SurrealDB permissions; same residual as MT-154 D-154-2).

Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions."

POST /api/bundles/debug/export (api/bundles.rs export_bundle :134 @ab618f46) requires an authenticated account session; the export scope must resolve to exactly one workspace (scope.wsid for workspace/time_window scopes; the job's workspace entity_ref or job_inputs.wsid for job/problem scopes - see bundles/exporter.rs job_matches_wsid :134-144) and the caller must pass authorize_request(Workspace, wsid, Read, 'fr.read'). A scope that cannot be resolved to one authorized workspace (e.g. time_window without wsid, a job in another account's workspace) is denied with the constant 403 and no job is created.

The export job records the requesting account (account_id, principal_id, session actor) in its job_inputs, and the export work (started via tokio::spawn -> start_workflow_for_job, api/bundles.rs:177-181; executed in workflows.rs:11353/11466 via DefaultDebugBundleExporter) reads SurrealDB (ai_jobs etc.) inside the requesting user's record-user scope (re-enter with_record_user_scope inside the spawned future, F5), never as root. ai_jobs gets a select predicate admitting rows whose workspace entity_ref the caller can read (fn::mt109_has_workspace_access(..., 'read', 'fr.read')); DuckDB Flight Recorder reads are filtered to the authorized wsid (DuckDB has no SurrealDB permissions; same residual as MT-154 D-154-2).

GET /api/bundles/debug/:bundle_id/download (download_bundle :264) - and the sibling read routes of the same router that expose the same bundle, GET /api/bundles/debug/:bundle_id (bundle_status :192), POST .../validate (validate_bundle :300) and GET /api/bundles/debug/exportable (list_exportable :288) - require an authenticated session and return the bundle only if the job's recorded account equals the caller's account AND the caller still passes Workspace Read fr.read on the bundle's workspace; otherwise the constant 403 (a non-existent bundle id also returns 403, not 404, so existence is not disclosed to other accounts). list_exportable returns only items from workspaces the caller can read.

Cross-account negatives through the real router with two account sessions: account B cannot export account A's workspace (403, no ai_jobs row created), cannot download/status/validate A's bundle (403, bytes never returned), and B's exportable inventory contains none of A's items; anonymous gets 403 on all five routes; A's own export -> status -> download round trip succeeds and the downloaded zip's manifest names only A's workspace.

Bundle path traversal: bundle_id is validated (uuid-shaped) before being joined into a filesystem path (download/status/validate use PathBuf::from("data").join("bundles").join(format!("bundle-{bundle_id}")) today).

Receipt: the PUT's kernel_event_ledger receipt is accepted by a receipt predicate branch (resource rich_document, action update, fs.write, $session = $auth.id) and carries the session principal as actor instead of the constant 'debug-breakpoints-ui'. The owner can read it via GET /kernel/events/aggregates/debug_breakpoints/:rich_document_id; another account reads 0.

Persistence/reload: breakpoints written by PUT survive closing and reopening the embedded store (same data directory) and are returned by GET after reopen, in (source_url, line) order, with condition and verified preserved; a second PUT replaces the set (no leftovers); uniqueness (rich_document_id, source_url, line) still enforced.

original_closure.outcome: A Locus job (job_kind locus_operation) can be created and resumed only through an authenticated account session holding the named workspace's write grant. The job and every Locus row it writes (work_packets, micro_tasks, mt_iterations, dependencies, the dependency-graph anchor) are written by the account's record user and are private to that account.

specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings.

**[LM-RLS-002]** Authority tables default to `PERMISSIONS NONE`; every grant is explicit at the database layer and rechecked by ResourceBroker. Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions.

Every durable or derived ProtectedResource MUST carry, directly or through a canonical registry row: [...] - `owner_account_id`, `created_by_principal_id`, `created_in_session_id`, and current `access_space_id` or explicit Space links;

The request names its workspace (top-level workspace_id, or job_inputs.workspace_id / job_inputs.wsid). api::authority::authorize_request(state, headers, 'fs.write', Workspace, ws, Create) runs BEFORE any table access. specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings.

**[LM-RLS-002]** Authority tables default to `PERMISSIONS NONE`; every grant is explicit at the database layer and rechecked by ResourceBroker. Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions.

Every durable or derived ProtectedResource MUST carry, directly or through a canonical registry row: [...] - `owner_account_id`, `created_by_principal_id`, `created_in_session_id`, and current `access_space_id` or explicit Space links;

7. Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists.
1. Default visibility is private to the owning LocalAccount until an explicit ResourceGrant says otherwise.

A doc_id is resolved only under that scope and must belong to the named workspace. Anonymous, workspace-less, foreign-workspace or foreign-document requests get the constant 403 and create no ai_jobs row. Spec: 02:2758: "6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary."

GET /jobs and GET /jobs/:id require the account session and read ai_jobs as the record user (fn::mt154_job_access): the list holds only jobs of workspaces the caller can read; a job of another account and an unknown id both get the identical constant 403. Spec: 02:2759: "7. Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists."

POST /jobs/:id/resume and POST /jobs/:id/cloud_escalation/consent resolve the job as the record user (invisible or unknown -> the same constant 403), re-authorize the job's workspace (fs.write + Update) and run the resume / consent write under that scope; a job with no single workspace ref is denied. Spec: 02:2773: "- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;"

Locus ids are owner-scoped (D-154-3 extension). A record user's work_packets / micro_tasks / mt_iterations / dependencies rows are keyed [owner_scope, id] with owner_scope = fn::mt158_dependency_graph_scope() ('account:<id>'); root/system rows keep their plain id. The id fields assert the id component of the record key; uniqueness indexes become (owner_account_id, id); record-user create requires the record key's owner component to be the caller's own scope. The same wp_id/mt_id/dependency_id created by two accounts yields two independent rows. Spec: 02:2752: "1. Default visibility is private to the owning LocalAccount until an explicit ResourceGrant says otherwise." 02:2759: "7. Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists."

No Locus response reveals another account's ids: a create of an id another account owns succeeds for the caller (its own row); reads through the Locus routes answer 404 identical to a missing id for ids the caller does not own. Spec: 02:2759: "7. Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists." LM-RLS-001: "**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings."

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Each of fn::mt109_has_grant, fn::mt109_has_workspace_access, fn::mt109_source_read, fn::mt120_document_access and fn::mt120_loom_block_access first resolves the protected_resources record by (resource_kind, external_resource_id) through protected_resources_external_unique (parent/grandparent via that record's links), then selects resource_grants with account_id, principal_id, access_space_id and resource_id = <resolved record> equality, so resource_grants_exact_idx serves all four fields. No resource_id.* link predicate remains in those resource_grants WHERE clauses.

Allow/deny semantics are identical for every existing condition: live session; session and principal delegated_capabilities ('*' or the capability); grant status active, revoked_at NONE, expiry; account/principal/access_space equality; resource lifecycle_state active, owner_account_id, access_space_id, created_by_principal_id.status enabled; resource policy_version <= grant policy_version <= $auth.policy_version where currently checked; resource_kind/external_resource_id; parent and grandparent chain conditions (mt109_source_read, mt120_document_access, mt120_loom_block_access); actions and capability_ids; delegation_chain equality; the reconciliation_queue service-identity special case; the memory.propose/memory.read delegation rule in mt109_source_read. A missing resource returns false without error. Function signatures, callers, table PERMISSIONS clauses and the record-user execution context are unchanged; no privileged/root path is introduced.

Existing authority and denial tests stay green on the candidate: every test in storage::surreal::resource_authority_tests, plus the union's existing core authority selections (schema catalog/pin/upgrade tests, schema::tests::document_grant_single_live_policy_witness_controls_record_user_visibility, api::loom::tests::mt153_loom_route_family_authority_matrix, mt154_non_loom_route_authority_tests, knowledge_fail_closed_tests, knowledge_documents_api_tests, loom_atomic_receipt_tests).

New focused core timing test storage::surreal::resource_authority_tests::grant_check_cost_is_independent_of_grant_count runs as record user on the existing embedded SurrealDB resource-authority harness. For N=50 and N=500 active grants held by the same principal on distinct protected resources, it times (i) one SELECT of a knowledge_idempotency_keys row by record id and (ii) one fn::mt120_document_access check; each metric is the median of 5 timed samples after 1 warm-up. It asserts median(N=500)/median(N=50) < 2.0 and every median < 250 ms, asserts every timed probe returned the authorized row/true (no vacuous timing) and a no-grant probe returns empty/false, prints the measured values, and removes everything it creates outside the artifact root (CX-GIT-003).

The schema catalog stays consistent: because the fn text is part of the pinned catalog, SCHEMA_REVISION advances with a predecessor-upgrade path following the existing revision-160/161 pattern in schema.rs (re-emit the changed DEFINE FUNCTION statements, record the predecessor pins, update GENERATED/INFO pins). A revision-161 store upgrades in place; existing pin/upgrade tests change only as the bump requires and pass.
No SQLite/PostgreSQL connectivity, fallback, cache or fixture path is introduced (CX-503R); the proof uses the Handshake-managed embedded SurrealDB harness only.

materialized_acceptance.requirement: First step, before any product edit: record in implementation_record.first_step_evidence, from surrealdb-core 3.2.0 source (src/idx/planner/tree.rs:514-520, plan.rs:92-179) plus, if needed, ONE recorded EXPLAIN probe named in a remediation, whether SELECTs inside a DEFINE FUNCTION body evaluated from a PERMISSIONS predicate are planned by the index planner and which WHERE shapes it serves (all-AND, bare LET params, IN-subquery). The rewrite shape in AC-168-2/3 is chosen from this evidence.

The grant SELECTs in fn::mt109_has_grant (schema.surql:6044), fn::mt109_has_workspace_access (:6081), fn::mt109_source_read (:6117), fn::mt120_document_access (:6171) and fn::mt109_ledger_access (:6392) select candidate rows by the exact resource_grants_exact_idx key (account_id, principal_id, access_space_id, resource_id; :5850) with an all-AND WHERE of bare LET params only; expiry, reconciliation_queue, actions/capabilities CONTAINS and delegation_chain filters run as a second step over that candidate set. Flattened sequential early exits (MT164-UDF-AND-CHAIN-STACK-OVERFLOW). Allow/deny results identical for every existing input. Contract revision 2: also fn::mt120_loom_block_access (schema.surql:6236 at dbdae422) and fn::mt166_resource_select_grant (:6384), which carry the same OR-shaped resource_grants query (seven queries in total).

fn::mt120_workspace_delete (schema.surql:6771-7036): the :6782 OR/two-hop protected_resources lookup is replaced by all-AND index-served lookups (a new DEFINE INDEX on protected_resources.parent_resource_id is allowed); the per-owned-resource grant (:6789) and child (:6798) lookups and the per-block/entity (resource_kind, external_resource_id) lookups (:6822, :7015-7016) compare against LET-bound bare params. W allow/deny unchanged, including MT-153 AC-153-8, MT-154 AC-154-6 and MT-157 W rowset behavior.
Existing authority/denial tests stay green (resource_authority_tests, the union core authority selections, MT-153/154/157 workspace-delete tests); stack-overflow count does not rise.

Timing tests in resource_authority_tests.rs (MT-164/MT-166 pattern): for each of the five grant functions and for a workspace delete, the median with 500 unrelated grant/resource rows in other workspaces vs 50 has ratio < 2.0, medians < 250 ms for single grant checks, non-vacuous (asserts the check returned true/false as expected).

Schema pins handled as in MT-164 AC-164-5: one SCHEMA_REVISION bump (schema.rs:18, currently 162), GENERATED_SURREALQL_SHA256 re-derived by the builder; runtime-measured pins (EXPECTED_SCHEMA_INFO_SHA256, schema.rs:3201) marked PIN-MEASURE PENDING and measured by the validator before the confirming round.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Database permission-predicate performance; no operator surface change. Visible effect is proven downstream by MT-167/MT-153/MT-042 timing proofs.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: No control or documented behavior changes; allow/deny identical (AC-168-2/3).

enforcement_boundaries: record-user PERMISSIONS unchanged in meaning; no root/privileged path
cross_account_negative_cases: existing resource_authority denial tests stay green (AC-168-4)

original_scope.summary: Make the visible Atelier work surface a central, filling pane with internal sibling tabs for Castkit Codex, Posekit, and Ingest. Reuse current native widgets where possible and add stable model-facing IDs for all tabs and content regions.
base_scope: Replace the old right-edge Atelier/CKC side-panel role with a main-pane Atelier surface for `PaneType::AtelierEditor`.
Render internal tabs inside the Atelier pane: `Castkit Codex`, `Posekit`, and `Ingest`.
Make CKC, Posekit, and Ingest siblings so more than one can be represented and addressed by parallel agents.
Reuse the existing `AtelierSidePanel` list/drag-source behavior inside the CKC tab instead of deleting it.
Provide visible placeholder/preview surfaces for Posekit and Ingest if full behavior is not implemented in this MT, but make them stable, nonblank, and model-addressable.
Remove or disable the duplicate right-edge Atelier side panel if it makes the main Atelier panel confusing or steals layout width.

Remove the four-window grid interpretation from Atelier. Atelier is one filling panel with internal CKC, Posekit, and Ingest tabs; multi-window/file/tab behavior belongs to Notes/workbench surfaces, not Atelier.

The Atelier pane contains sibling tabs for Castkit Codex, Posekit, and Ingest.
Each internal tab has a stable AccessKit author_id and exposes a click action.
Each internal tab content region has a stable AccessKit author_id and is nonblank.
The CKC tab reuses current native Atelier/CKC list and drag-source behavior.

Visual inspection confirms the main panel fills the work area and the old side-panel layout is not the primary CKC home.

original_lifecycle.claim_recovery_reason: Status recovery: legacy RFV contract lacked lifecycle.claimed_by; Kernel Builder inspected current MT state and accepts implementer-side handoff responsibility without claiming validator PASS/FAIL.

original_scope.summary: Add the first product-native Argus surface by naming and exposing Argus operations over the existing native MCP/AccessKit inspection and steering stack.
base_scope: Add a Rust-native `mcp::argus` facade that defines the canonical Argus method namespace and maps it to existing MCP primitives.
Expose model-callable Argus methods for inspect/list, click, set_value, and screenshot without removing the existing generic MCP methods.
Ensure Argus read operations use the existing shared snapshot lease and mutating operations use the existing per-target exclusive lease and attribution path.
Ensure Argus screenshot uses the existing focus-safe screenshot closure/path and does not call foreground, keyboard, mouse, or z-order APIs.
Return or preserve enough metadata for a model to recognize that the response came through Argus and what underlying primitive was used.
Add focused Rust tests that fail before implementation and pass after implementation for Argus method dispatch, session attribution/leases, and screenshot compatibility.
must_preserve: Existing MCP methods: list_widgets, click_widget, set_value, screenshot
McpSession lease registry and attributed action log
No foreground-window, keyboard-injection, OS mouse, SetForegroundWindow, BringWindowToTop, or z-order APIs
acceptance_criteria: Argus has a named Rust module or public API under the native MCP stack.
A model can call Argus inspect/list through JSON-RPC and receive the same UI tree snapshot shape as list_widgets, plus Argus-identifying metadata or method routing evidence.
A model can call Argus click and Argus set_value against stable author_id targets and the calls enqueue through the existing ActionChannel.
Argus mutating calls are leased and attributed the same way as click_widget/set_value, including agent_id stamping and action-log records.
Argus screenshot dispatches through the existing screenshot adapter/closure and returns VisualCaptureResult-compatible JSON.
Unknown/unauthorized Argus requests fail with typed JSON-RPC errors and do not take leases, log actions, or enqueue actions.
Focused tests prove the Argus aliases/facade are headless and do not require launching or foregrounding Handshake.
This MT does not claim full Argus visual-workbench parity; it only establishes the named native product surface that future MTs can extend.
The internal UserManual names the Argus MCP methods and the required inspect -> steer -> re-inspect -> screenshot evidence loop.
proof_targets: Failing test first for Argus inspect/list method routing.
Failing test first for Argus click session attribution/lease behavior.
Failing test first for Argus screenshot result compatibility.
Focused cargo test over the native MCP unit tests after implementation.
No new foreground-window or keyboard/mouse API usage introduced by diff review.

Represent unsupported or unconfigured models as explicit degraded-state records, not fake results.

original_scope.summary: Add optional real YuNet/ArcFace/PIPNet-backed identity analysis with model provenance, degraded no-model behavior, and LoRA-ready identity gate artifacts.
base_scope: Add model configuration discovery for detector/embedder/landmark assets without hardcoded absolute paths.

original_scope.summary: Make Facial command failures and degraded outcomes produce durable, model-usable command envelopes and receipt artifacts instead of only generic HTTP error bodies.
base_scope: Define a Facial command failure/degraded envelope that carries command, actor when available, status, error code, recovery hint, result schema if relevant, and source artifact refs.
Persist failure/degraded command receipt artifacts through ArtifactStore when the request has enough context to do so safely.
Keep missing or malformed actor/header failures as normal HTTP validation errors unless a safe actor placeholder and audit policy are explicitly implemented.
Update backend Facial command routes so semantic blocked/degraded states return the command envelope shape instead of parser-invisible generic errors.
Update frontend parser/tests to accept only backend-produced statuses and require correct artifacts when a receipt is promised.
acceptance_criteria: At least one semantic blocked path, such as export without allow_partial while undecided items remain, returns a structured Facial command envelope and receipt artifact.
Frontend parser accepts degraded/blocked/error statuses only after backend tests prove those statuses are produced.
Failure receipts include actor attribution when an actor header is present, command name, status, error code, recovery hint, and source/session refs where available.
HTTP transport status and command-envelope status are documented in tests so models know which failures are parser-visible and which remain transport validation errors.
No generic non-Facial ArtifactStore JSON read surface is introduced.
risks_and_controls: Risk: models confuse malformed transport errors with command-level failures. Control: keep extractor/header failures as HTTP errors unless explicitly envelope-wrapped.
Risk: failure envelopes write misleading receipts without enough context. Control: only persist receipts after command, actor, and session/artifact context are known.
Risk: frontend accepts statuses the backend still cannot produce. Control: parser tests must pair every accepted status with a backend route proof.

original_lifecycle.claim_recovery_reason: Status recovery: legacy RFV contract lacked lifecycle.claimed_by; Kernel Builder inspected current MT state and accepts implementer-side handoff responsibility without claiming validator PASS/FAIL.

original_scope.summary: Add a focused native panel/backend roundtrip proof for CKC media album create, media link, and image notes/tags save.
base_scope: Build or reuse an in-process TcpListener mock backend for the AtelierClient CKC media routes without adding new dependencies.
Load a CKC character with at least one album/media row through the client path, not the local fallback harness only.
Drive Argus click/set_value on album create, media link, and media notes/tags save from the Atelier CKC tab.
Assert captured backend requests include the exact POST routes, JSON bodies, and x-hsk-actor-id for the selected actor.
Return backend rows from the mock and assert the panel updates Argus-visible album/media/readout/status nodes from those rows.

After create/link/save, force a reload/refetch/new-panel path and assert albums, linked media, notes, tags, actor-visible status, and selected refs reconstruct from backend authority rather than in-memory state.
Document the proof in the internal manual or MT closeout so future models know this is the backend-authority proof path.
acceptance_criteria: The test drives the production AtelierPanel with an AtelierClient, not only a no-client local fallback harness.
The mock backend captures album create, album link, and media notes/tags save requests with correct paths, bodies, and actor headers.
The mock backend responses are parsed and reflected in Argus-visible CKC album/media/status/readout nodes.
The proof reloads/refetches/rebuilds the panel after write operations and verifies the same album/media/notes/tags state comes back from backend authority.
The proof distinguishes backend:persistent from local-preview:not-persisted and does not overclaim local fallback persistence.
The test is focused and runnable without launching the foreground Handshake GUI.
risks_and_controls: Risk: a mock can drift from backend response shape. Control: use existing parser DTO shapes and include route/body/header assertions.
Risk: the panel passes from POST echo or in-memory state without persistence. Control: require reload/refetch/new-panel reconstruction from backend-returned authority state after the write sequence.

original_contract_records.title: Audit Atelier full-window module vs workbench-pane mounting and specify CKC/PoseKit/Ingest full-size sub-module rewiring

original_lifecycle.audit_relationship_note: Inspects the outputs of MT-004 (COMPLETED, renamed CKC shell to Atelier) and MT-006 (READY_FOR_VALIDATION, promoted Atelier to a filling PaneType::AtelierEditor with CKC/PoseKit/Ingest sibling tabs). This MT does NOT depend on those MTs being validator-confirmed; it inspects their current code state. MT-006 is the primary audit target because it implemented Atelier as PaneType::AtelierEditor (the workbench pane mechanism also used by notes/terminals), which is the operator's suspected root cause.
original_lifecycle.claim_recovery_reason: Status recovery: legacy RFV contract lacked lifecycle.claimed_by; Kernel Builder inspected current MT state and accepts implementer-side handoff responsibility without claiming validator PASS/FAIL.

original_scope.summary: Read-only audit of how the Atelier surface is mounted in the native Handshake GUI shell. Determine with file:line evidence whether Atelier opens as a top-level FULL-WINDOW MODULE or is still hosted inside the workbench PANE grid (compartmentalized sub-window like notes/terminals). Establish the correct target model, produce a concrete rewiring change plan, and recommend whether the fix lands as MT-006 remediation or as one/more new implementation MTs. No product code is edited by this MT.

target_model.atelier: Top-level, full-window MODULE experience. When Atelier is active it owns the full work area (module-level), not a pane inside the workbench grid.
target_model.atelier_sub_modules: CKC, INGEST, and PoseKit are full-size tabbed sub-modules INSIDE Atelier. Selecting a tab fills the Atelier module area.
target_model.notes_module_reservation: The compartmentalized VS-Code-style pattern (multiple sub-windows/panes with tabs inside the main window) is INTENDED and must be PRESERVED, but only under the Notes Module (WP-KERNEL-012). The audit change plan must not regress Notes/workbench pane behavior.

original_scope.inspect_notes: inspect_paths are the known candidate surfaces from packet.relevant_product_files_initial and MT-006.scope.target_files. The auditor MUST also follow references from these files to the real Notes/terminal module and pane mounting so the module-vs-pane contrast is grounded, and MUST confirm whether any legacy React/TSX Atelier path (App.tsx/AtelierPanel.tsx) is still live or already superseded by the native Rust surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Document the current Atelier mount path with file:line evidence. State exactly whether Atelier is reached via a top-level module (module_switcher.rs / ModuleId) and how it is then rendered: as a full-window module region, or as a workbench PaneType (PaneType::AtelierEditor via pane_registry.rs / pane_header.rs). Name the exact enums, types, and factory functions.

AC2: For contrast, document with file:line evidence how the Notes module and at least one genuine pane (terminal or note) are mounted, to establish which mechanism is a full-window module and which is a compartmentalized pane-in-main-window.

AC3: Confirm or refute the operator's observation with concrete evidence. When the Atelier top-level entry is activated, does Atelier fill the entire work area as a module, or does it open inside the pane/workbench grid still showing pane chrome (pane header, sibling panes, split handles)? Base the verdict on code paths plus, where practical, a read-only AccessKit/Argus snapshot; do not assert from assumption.

AC4: Determine whether CKC/PoseKit/Ingest are currently pane-internal tabs (inside atelier_panel.rs within a PaneType) or module-internal full-size tabs, and what must change for them to be full-size tabbed sub-modules of a full-window Atelier module.
AC5: Define the target model precisely (Atelier = full-window module; CKC/INGEST/PoseKit = full-size tabbed sub-modules; compartmentalized pane-in-main pattern reserved to Notes/WP-KERNEL-012).

AC6: Produce a concrete change plan naming exact files, types, and the minimal rewiring to move Atelier from pane-hosted to module-hosted (or, if it is already module-hosted, name the actual defect). Include how CKC/PoseKit/Ingest tabs relocate and which stable AccessKit author_ids (module-ckc, atelier-tab-ckc/posekit/ingest, content regions) are preserved vs changed.
AC7: State that the change plan does NOT alter or regress the Notes/WP-KERNEL-012 pane/workbench model (KERNEL-012 is in parallel live development).

AC8: Disposition per operator directive (see disposition_directive): the DEFAULT is to redo MT-006 in parts as MT-006 remediation and LINK the audit's change-plan parts back to MT-006. Break the change plan into parts; for each part, state whether it is IN MT-006 scope (-> MT-006 remediation, the default) or TRULY OUT of MT-006 scope (-> propose a new MT-041+ with concrete rationale for why it exceeds MT-006 scope). Name the HBR obligations the implementation work must carry: HBR-VIS (Argus inspect/steer of the changed surface), HBR-QUIET (no focus/keyboard/mouse steal), HBR-MAN (in-product UserManual update).
AC9: Emit findings as machine-readable MT-040-atelier-window-audit.json. Leave product code untouched.
proof_targets: MT-040-atelier-window-audit.json exists, parses as JSON, and contains: current-mount-path evidence (AC1), notes/pane contrast (AC2), operator-observation verdict with evidence (AC3), tab-model finding (AC4), target model (AC5), change plan (AC6), notes-non-regression statement (AC7), and disposition recommendation (AC8).
Every finding cites concrete file:line evidence in ../wtc-ckc-posekit-overhaul.

original_contract_records.title: Add operator-facing dropdown menu-bar item for Atelier + required Argus menu-leaf expansion

original_lifecycle.claim_recovery_reason: Status recovery: legacy RFV contract lacked lifecycle.claimed_by; Kernel Builder inspected current MT state and accepts implementer-side handoff responsibility without claiming validator PASS/FAIL.

original_scope.summary: Add an operator-facing dropdown menu-bar entry for Atelier to the shell menu bar (handshake_menu_bar, app.rs ~7073-7075 / top_menu_bar.rs). The entry opens the Atelier full-window module and offers jump-to CKC / PoseKit / Ingest sub-module tabs. Because menu leaves are dynamically created only while a menu is open, this MT MUST also perform the mandated Argus expansion so a model can discover and steer menu leaves.

menu_bar_facts.menu_bar_panel: handshake_menu_bar (app.rs ~7073-7075); top-level menu buttons menu-file/-edit/-view/-go/-run/-help are Role::MenuItem with Action::Click/Focus + author_id (top_menu_bar.rs:149-156, :411-417); already Argus-visible (proven test_top_menu_bar.rs live_shell_has_six_top_level_menus_with_stable_ids :59).
menu_bar_facts.leaf_gap: Menu leaves (menu.file.quit, menu.edit.undo, menu.view.reset-layout, menu.go.command-palette, menu.run.swarm-board, menu.help.about, menu-go-* nav leaves) exist in the AccessKit tree ONLY while their parent menu is open (top_menu_bar.rs:78-82; asserted absent when closed test_top_menu_bar.rs:114-118). So Argus cannot one-shot a leaf.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: An operator-facing dropdown menu-bar entry exists for Atelier (either a new 'Atelier' top-level menu or an Atelier item under an existing menu) that opens the Atelier module and can select the CKC / PoseKit / Ingest sub-module tabs. Stable author_ids on the entry and its leaves.

AC2 (Argus expansion, MANDATORY per operator): implement a static leaf-id discovery registry (enumerate menu.<x>.<leaf> author_ids per menu) so Argus/models know valid leaf targets WITHOUT first opening the menu; OR expose the same commands via the command registry/palette as a flat, always-present addressable surface.

AC3 (Argus expansion): encode a two-step open-then-steer protocol (argus.click menu-<x> -> drain+repaint -> argus.inspect -> argus.click menu.<x>.<leaf>) and prove with a live test that argus.click on the menu OPENS and HOLDS the menu across the headless action-drain frame so the leaf is clickable (egui popups can close on the next synthesized pointer event).

AC4: Argus can inspect + steer the new Atelier menu entry and its leaves headlessly (HBR-VIS/QUIET). If Argus cannot see/steer, expand Argus (author_ids, AccessKit roles, inspection hooks) in this MT.
AC5: Update the in-product internal UserManual for the new menu entry + the Argus menu-leaf discovery/steer protocol (HBR-MAN).
AC6: No scaffolding; runtime proof (Spec-Realism Gate).

original_contract_records.title: Backend+client byte-fetch endpoints for Posekit source-image and OpenPose artifact display

original_lifecycle.claim_recovery_reason: Status recovery: legacy RFV contract lacked lifecycle.claimed_by; Kernel Builder inspected current MT state and accepts implementer-side handoff responsibility without claiming validator PASS/FAIL.

original_scope.summary: Add a backend route + frontend backend_client method to fetch raw bytes so the Posekit split view displays real pixels at runtime: (1) source-image bytes for PoseRig.source_asset_id / pose_source_ref (DAM/ckc_client asset-bytes endpoint) -> feeds the left source viewport (set_pose_source_image_bytes); (2) artifact-content bytes for the backend OpenPose export (png_artifact_ref) -> lets the right viewport render the literal exported PNG instead of re-rasterizing keypoints. Async fetch wiring on tab open / after export.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A backend route (in api/atelier.rs or the DAM/ArtifactStore API) returns raw source-asset bytes for a source_asset_id/pose_source_ref, and a frontend backend_client method calls it; the left posekit viewport shows the decoded real image at runtime (not the empty state) when a source is set. Runtime-proven.

AC2: A backend/artifact route returns the exported OpenPose PNG bytes for png_artifact_ref; the right viewport can render the literal exported PNG (artifact://) at runtime, matching the backend render_posekit_openpose_png output. Runtime-proven.
AC3: Async fetch is wired (on tab open / after export) without blocking the UI; failures show explicit error state (HBR-QUIET headless, no fake).
AC4: PostgreSQL/EventLedger + ArtifactStore authority (no SQLite); Argus-inspectable; UserManual updated. No scaffolding.
AC5: This closes the MT-014 left-viewport empty-state and right-viewport keypoints-vs-PNG limitations.

original_scope.summary: Define and implement modern Handshake local/cloud/subagent swarm lane launch and communication so models speak through typed Handshake state rather than hidden chat or peer channels.
original_scope.why: The original v02.122 multi-model spec predated current subagent and cloud/local swarm practice. Handshake now needs explicit ModelLaneRun, ModelLane, ModelLaneMessage, ContextBundle, artifact promotion, consent, diagnostics, and recovery contracts.
forbidden_paths: wholesale spec restructuring outside the owning LLM Infrastructure module
direct cloud calls outside LlmClient/CloudLane boundaries
npm/JavaScript proof targets for this WP
acceptance_criteria: Local model lanes launch through LlmClient -> ModelRuntime and produce ModelLane state.
Cloud model lanes launch through CloudLane/BYOK with ProjectionPlan and ConsentReceipt where required.
Subagents are modeled as ModelLane records with stable lane ids, session ids, status, and recovery metadata.
All cloud/local/subagent exchange is represented as coordinator-mediated ModelLaneMessage plus payload artifacts.
A downstream model receives prior model output through ContextBundle or artifact refs, not hidden conversational memory.
Lane outputs remain advisory until promoted into code, WP/MT contracts, or validator verdicts.
Diagnostics expose ModelLaneRun, lane status, messages, artifact refs, and recoverability failures.
Validation covers local-only, cloud-only, mixed cloud/local, subagent, disagreement, consent-block, orphan, restart, and missing-payload cases.
Durable model-lane state uses Rust backend code and PostgreSQL/EventLedger/ArtifactStore authority; SQLite is not allowed as runtime, cache, fixture, fallback, or test authority.
Collaborative/operator-model state uses CRDT draft semantics where live shared edits are possible, then promotes through ValidationRunner/PromotionGate before becoming authority.
Every observable lane behavior records Flight Recorder/EventLedger evidence plus the HBR-INT-009 three-tier diagnostic outcome for Flight Recorder, internal_diagnostics, and Palmistry.

The project-named internal viewing tool renders lane topology, message flow, artifacts, validation, promotion, runtime errors, and recovery hints for visual/debug verification; naming is owned by the separate viewing-tool worktree/session.

The in-product internal UserManual reflects every ModelLane/cloud/local/subagent orchestration behavior introduced by this WP, including usage, recovery, verification, Flight Recorder/EventLedger linkage, and HBR-INT-009 Flight Recorder/internal_diagnostics/Palmistry posture.

All product implementation and proof for this WP is Rust-only: Rust backend plus Rust native egui/Argus surfaces. Legacy TypeScript/React/app/src surfaces are reference-only and must not become implementation or proof authority.

The ModelLaneRun/ModelLane/ModelLaneMessage contract explicitly carries trace/span, runtime, capability, tool, payload, replay, recovery, promotion, CRDT, and Locus ownership fields: trace_id, run_span_id, lane_span_id, message_span_id, parent_span_id or linked_span_contexts, adapter_id, runtime_binding, capability_token_ids or effective_capability_snapshot_ref, projection_plan_ref, consent_receipt_ref, tool_gate_decision_refs, idempotency_key, payload_sha256, replay_order_key, event_ledger_stream_id, event_ledger_append_id or event_ledger_event_id, event_ledger_seq, event_stream_version, transaction_seq, replay_after_event_ledger_seq, promoted_artifact_ref, promoted_artifact_sha256, promoted_artifact_version, promotion_gate_ref, promotion_receipt_ref, validator_verdict_ref, operator_decision_ref, crdt_update_ref, crdt_base_snapshot_ref, crdt_state_vector, crdt_proposal_ref, crdt_stale_base_ref, recovery_state, heartbeat_at_utc, lease_expires_at_utc, reclaim_after_utc, restart_generation, cancellation_ref, backpressure_ref, loop_counter_ref, failstate_code, reason_ref, recovery_hint_ref, work_packet_id, micro_task_id, task_board_id, coordinator_session_id, owner_session, and locus_binding_ref.

MT lifecycle/status signaling is restartable: every MT contract carries claimed_by, claimed_at_utc, ready_for_validation_by, ready_for_validation_at_utc, completed_by, blocker, missing_resource, proof_status, hbr_status, kb_ready_checklist_receipt_id, product_worktree_root_resolution, last_recovery_event_ref, and last_runtime_status_ref.

Proof commands for implementation MTs must use exact Rust test targets or exact test names and must fail on zero matching tests. Provider calls may use deterministic fakes; durable authority must touch PostgreSQL/EventLedger/ArtifactStore/CRDT/UserManual/Argus Rust resources.

Dexterity is the internal model switching and launch kernel name for this WP. It is a kernel/manual/display name only; stable schema IDs remain ModelLaneRun, ModelLane, ModelLaneMessage, and hsk.model_lane_*@1.
The provisional Rust-native diagnostics/navigation contract id is native_swarm_lane_diagnostics until the separate naming worktree supplies an approved alias.

Each MT receives post-implementation adversarial review through runtime launch, PostgreSQL/EventLedger/CRDT recovery, Rust native Argus/UserManual, and Spec-Realism/status-signaling lenses before READY_FOR_VALIDATION.

The default LlmClient resolves local inference through the embedded Rust ModelRuntime. MT-003 AC13 is the more-specific implementation contract: CandleRuntime is the compiled-in CPU default, while LlamaCppRuntime remains opt-in. The auto-detecting OllamaAdapter default and src/backend/handshake_core/src/llm/ollama.rs are removed, and no third-party model-server daemon is an authoritative runtime (master-spec-v02.197 3.6.1).

A missing or unconfigured local model fails closed to DisabledLlmClient; there is no daemon fallback. A negative test proves the default runtime path never selects a third-party daemon adapter as authority.

Embedded engine cargo features default to a CPU-only baseline in the default handshake_core build; GPU backends are opt-in features; engine enablement is decoupled from the legacy app/src-tauri build.

The generic ExternalEngineImport OpenAI-compatible endpoint remains available only as a non-authoritative compat lane (provider=external_compat, not Handshake-owned in ProcessOwnershipLedger); removing Ollama does not remove this generic compat lane.

original_scope.summary: Add backend schemas/types for ModelLaneRun, ModelLane, ModelLaneMessage, and lane status.
forbidden_paths: cloud provider direct-call code outside existing lane boundaries
npm/JavaScript proof targets for this WP
app/src-tauri launch or IPC authority for this WP
proof commands that pass with zero matching tests
acceptance_criteria: Types encode run id, lane id, lane kind, backend, role, session id, status, WP/MT refs, message kind, payload ref, summary, and authority state.
Serde roundtrip tests cover local, cloud, CLI, human, subagent, and validator lanes.
Message payload refs are required for non-status payloads.

ModelLaneRun and every side-effecting ModelLane MUST carry a validated Locus binding: work_packet_id/wp_id, micro_task_id/mt_id, task_board_id when present, coordinator_session_id, session_id/model_session_id, and owner_session. Missing, invalid, or mismatched binding against the active WP/MT contract MUST fail closed with diagnostics and Flight Recorder/EventLedger evidence.

ModelLane MUST include adapter_id, runtime_binding, provider_kind, capability_token_ids or effective_capability_snapshot_ref, and tool_gate_decision_refs; any lane tool call without session-scoped capability intersection MUST fail closed.

ModelLaneMessage MUST include idempotency_key, event_ledger_ref or event_ledger_seq, payload_sha256, proposal_ref when kind=PROPOSAL, base_snapshot_ref/state_vector when the payload targets shared editable state, and replay_order_key. Duplicate retries with the same idempotency_key and payload hash MUST be idempotent; same key with different payload hash MUST fail closed.

Schemas carry trace_id, run_span_id/lane_span_id/message_span_id, parent_span_id or linked_span_contexts, model_session_id/session_id, wp_id, mt_id, Locus work-unit refs, and EventLedger aggregate/event refs so every lane can be joined across Flight Recorder, Locus, and replay surfaces.

Schemas MUST carry deterministic EventLedger replay ordering fields: event_ledger_stream_id, event_ledger_append_id or event_ledger_event_id, event_ledger_seq, event_stream_version, transaction_seq, replay_order_key, and replay_after_event_ledger_seq. created_at_utc MUST NOT be the ordering authority.

Promoted ModelLaneMessage records MUST carry promotion_gate_ref, promotion_receipt_ref, validator_verdict_ref or operator_decision_ref as applicable, plus promoted_artifact_ref, promoted_artifact_sha256, and promoted_artifact_version when authority artifacts are created or updated.

CRDT-targeting ModelLaneMessage records MUST carry crdt_update_ref, crdt_base_snapshot_ref, crdt_state_vector, crdt_proposal_ref, and crdt_stale_base_ref as applicable; missing CRDT base/proposal metadata for shared editable state MUST fail closed before promotion.

ModelLane recovery fields MUST include recovery_state, heartbeat_at_utc, lease_expires_at_utc, reclaim_after_utc, restart_generation, cancellation_ref, backpressure_ref, loop_counter_ref, last_runtime_status_ref, last_recovery_event_ref, failstate_code, reason_ref, and recovery_hint_ref.

Side-effecting ModelLaneMessage records MUST carry immutable Locus binding fields on the message itself: coordinator_session_id, task_board_id when present, work_packet_id/wp_id, micro_task_id/mt_id, owner_session, and locus_binding_ref.

Every ModelLaneRun invocation records FEMS posture: memory_pack_ref, memory_pack_hash, determinism_mode, budget summary, selected/candidate ids for replay mode, procedural-review status, truncation warnings, and exclusion/rejection reasons.

Implement canonical Rust/PostgreSQL model-lane aggregate storage for ModelLaneRun, ModelLane, ModelLaneMessage, schema registry rows, and EventLedger append/list/replay APIs; structs-only or in-memory-only schema work is not acceptable.

Negative proof MUST cover missing Locus binding, idempotency-key conflict with different payload hash, missing payload_sha256, malformed trace/span linkage, and unsupported provider capability snapshot.

After implementation and before READY_FOR_VALIDATION, this MT MUST receive post-implementation adversarial review against the actual diff. Findings must be fixed or converted into explicit lifecycle blocker/missing_resource/proof_status state; the implementer may not self-certify COMPLETED.

original_scope.summary: Normalize launch adapters for local, cloud, CLI, human, subagent, and validator lanes.
forbidden_paths: direct model endpoint calls outside LlmClient
npm/JavaScript proof targets for this WP
app/src-tauri launch or IPC authority for this WP
proof commands that pass with zero matching tests
acceptance_criteria: Local lanes launch through LlmClient -> ModelRuntime.
When a future user explicitly configures a cloud provider, cloud lanes launch through the existing CloudLane/BYOK boundary; BYOK is optional and disabled/fail-closed by default.
CLI, human/operator, validator, and subagent lanes have normalized records and startup failure status.

All local/cloud/CLI/human/subagent/validator lane launches MUST resolve through the Rust backend SwarmCoordinator/ModelRuntime adapter registry; LlmClient may be used only as an existing service facade when it delegates to that registry. No frontend, app/src, direct endpoint, or terminal-only path may become launch authority.

Launch adapter output records capability negotiation results, provider feature profile, requested/effective execution policy, trace_id/span_id, owner_session, reclaim policy, cancellation token boundary, and startup failure code for every lane kind.

Local OpenAI-compatible servers such as llama.cpp and Rust-native runtimes such as Candle are adapter backends only; no MT may call them as authoritative side channels outside the ModelRuntime boundary.
Tool-capable lanes route tool calls through capability check, consent/projection where needed, Flight Recorder/EventLedger logging, execution, result capture, and ModelLaneMessage result refs.

Every lane kind (local, BYOK cloud, official CLI, CLI bridge, human/operator, subagent, validator) MUST declare cancellation_token_ref, reclaim_policy, owner_session, terminal status mapping, and EventLedger START/STOP or explicit no-OS-process equivalent at launch time.

Required BYOK proof MUST NOT require Operator-provisioned or paid-provider credentials. It MUST use generated inert test credentials in an isolated test vault and a controlled no-egress recording provider, prove that the secret value is never logged or persisted outside the vault contract, and prove zero provider calls when provider configuration or ProjectionPlan/ConsentReceipt authority is absent, expired, mismatched, or revoked. Real-provider end-to-end execution is optional certification only.
Source/negative proof MUST fail closed for direct endpoint launch, app/src/app-src-tauri launch authority, terminal-only launch state, and unsupported tool capability.

After implementation and before READY_FOR_VALIDATION, this MT MUST receive post-implementation adversarial review against the actual diff. Findings must be fixed or converted into explicit lifecycle blocker/missing_resource/proof_status state; the implementer may not self-certify COMPLETED.

REOPENED SCOPE (operator decision 2026-07-01): The default LlmClient boot path (src/backend/handshake_core/src/main.rs) MUST resolve local inference through the embedded ModelRuntime (LlamaCppRuntime default, CandleRuntime for hook/non-transformer lanes), NOT the auto-detected Ollama daemon. src/backend/handshake_core/src/llm/ollama.rs OllamaAdapter and its /api/tags auto-detect default are removed.

REOPENED SCOPE: A missing or unconfigured local model fails closed to DisabledLlmClient with no daemon fallback; a negative test proves the default runtime path never selects a third-party daemon adapter as authority (master-spec-v02.197 3.6.1).

REOPENED SCOPE (feature design hardened by pre-impl review): Candle (pure-Rust, CPU) is the compiled-in default embedded engine via a new `local-inference-default = ["candle-runtime-engine"]` feature added to Cargo `default`. llama.cpp (`llama-cpp-runtime-engine`, heavy C++ `llama-cpp-sys-2`) stays OPT-IN and MUST NOT be added to `default` (it breaks the RC-004 non-target `cargo check` and forces a C++ compile on every proof run). GPU backends (candle-cuda/metal, llama-cpp-cuda/metal/vulkan) are declared opt-in features, never in `default`, not built under load. Engine enablement is decoupled from app/src-tauri (remove `candle-runtime-engine` from app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml; the engine comes from handshake_core's own default). 'CPU-only baseline' means the enabled engine selects the CPU backend; GPU is a separate opt-in.

REOPENED SCOPE: The generic ExternalEngineImport OpenAI-compatible endpoint is retained as a non-authoritative compat lane only (provider=external_compat, not Handshake-owned in ProcessOwnershipLedger); no bespoke Ollama adapter or auto-wiring survives.

REOPENED SCOPE (spec MUSTs per master-spec-v02.197 3.6.2/4.6.1): the embedded default engine load path MUST box under a SandboxAdapter (default HandshakeNativeSandboxAdapter) and emit ProcessOwnershipLedger START/STOP rows; implementer verifies the existing ModelRuntime load path already satisfies this or wires it, else records a blocking HBR gap (a 5.6 HBR-gate failure if missed).

REOPENED SCOPE (spec MUSTs per 4.2.3.2(3)/4.2.3.1.1 + CX-101/CX-102): every completion still emits a Flight Recorder event with trace_id/model_id/TokenUsage on ALL default paths (embedded ModelRuntime success, DisabledLlmClient fail-closed, external_compat); the retained OpenAI-compatible compat lane stays mediated by LlmClient with no leftover direct HTTP from the deleted ollama.rs; max_tokens budget enforcement (BudgetExceeded) survives the swap.

REOPENED SCOPE (proof hardening per pre-impl review): the prior 14 lane proof targets exercise only swarm_orchestration::model_lane and DO NOT touch the Ollama-kill path (they can pass while main.rs still builds OllamaAdapter). The reopened MT requires NEW engine-free proof: (a) a negative test that the default LlmClient boot resolution with no local model returns DisabledLlmClient and never an Ollama/daemon adapter, and that init_llm_client/ProviderRegistry no longer has an OllamaAdapter arm; (b) a positive test that the generic external_compat OpenAI-compatible lane is retained and non-authoritative; (c) `cargo check --features app-runtime` proving main.rs compiles. Refactor init_llm_client's provider resolution into a testable function. The prior 14 proofs count as prior-scope evidence only.

REOPENED SCOPE (scope guard): MT-003 WIRES the default LlmClient to the already-shipped WP-KERNEL-004 ModelRuntime adapters (LlamaCppRuntime/CandleRuntime); it does NOT re-implement engines. Real embedded-engine inference (real GGUF through llama.cpp / real weights through Candle) is recorded DEFERRED-with-reason (heavy host-toolchain build under heavy load) citing tests/llama_cpp_e2e_smoke.rs and tests/candle_e2e_smoke.rs as the unfaked reproduction commands; it MUST NOT be faked green.

REOPENED SCOPE (wiring approach per pre-impl review): the embedded-runtime LlmClient bridge already exists (llm/local_router.rs: LocalRouter + LocalModelRuntimeLlmClient, LlmClient-implementing, LlamaCpp-default/Candle-for-hooks, currently constructed only in tests). MT-003 does NOT add a new LlmClient impl; it (a) adds a net-new local-model config surface to llm/registry.rs from_env (GGUF artifact_path + sha256 + RuntimeBinding + display name); (b) in main.rs init_llm_client replaces the ProviderKind::Ollama auto-detect arm with a local-runtime arm that builds LlamaCppRuntime+CandleRuntime, loads+registers the artifact (minting a UUIDv7 ModelId, provider=Local, matching binding; ModelRegistry.register requires non-empty artifact_path + non-zero sha256; validate_binding forbids LlamaCpp+activation_steering so steering lanes use Candle), constructs LocalRouter + LocalModelRuntimeLlmClient with a DisabledLlmClient fallback; (c) fails closed to DisabledLlmClient AT INIT (no /api/tags probe, no daemon fallback) when no local model is configured or load() fails (do not hard-abort startup, mirror existing degradations at main.rs:396/407/439).

REOPENED SCOPE (HIGH regression guard 1 - profile.model_id identity): the wired client's profile().model_id MUST be the minted UUIDv7 of the registered model, because call sites pass profile().model_id as CompletionRequest.model_id and LocalModelRuntimeLlmClient::completion only routes to the runtime for UUIDv7 ids (non-UUID silently falls back to the DisabledLlmClient fallback). A test MUST prove completion routes to the embedded runtime, not the fallback.

REOPENED SCOPE (HIGH regression guard 2 - embedding not dropped): OllamaAdapter implemented embedding(); LocalModelRuntimeLlmClient inherits the trait default embedding()->EmbeddingUnsupported. The swap MUST wire LlmClient::embedding() to ModelRuntime::embed() in llm/local_router.rs (or record an explicit operator waiver), else semantic embeddings silently drop and LoomSearchV2 degrades to keyword/trigram. A test MUST prove embedding() is not silently unsupported after the swap.

SCOPE ACCURACY (post-review): 'kill' is LlmClient-DEFAULT-scoped, not repo-wide. The OllamaAdapter type + InMemoryLlmClient are retained ONLY as test doubles (never constructed in the default path; no ProviderKind::Ollama variant remains). Ollama couplings intentionally remain OUTSIDE the default LlmClient path and are NOT part of MT-003: tokenization.rs OllamaTokenizerConfigCache, atelier ollama: model-server scheme, bin/capability_registry_workflow.rs OLLAMA_MODEL, dependency_policy tripwires. Removing those is out of MT-003 scope; if desired, a future WP/MT should own it.

original_scope.summary: Implement coordinator routing policies and explicit advisory-to-authority promotion.
forbidden_paths: automatic code/contract promotion without explicit policy
npm/JavaScript proof targets for this WP
app/src-tauri launch or IPC authority for this WP
proof commands that pass with zero matching tests
acceptance_criteria: Routing policies cover local-first, cloud-review, cloud-plan-local-execute, parallel-debate, validator lane, and operator lane.
Advisory output cannot modify authority until promoted through a typed decision.
Disagreement produces explicit messages and a coordinator decision artifact.

Promotion MUST be modeled as an explicit deterministic state machine: advisory -> promotion_requested -> pending_policy|pending_approval -> approved|denied|expired -> executing -> executed|skipped|unsupported, keyed by stable action/request ids and idempotency keys. Only PromotionGate resolution records may mutate authority.

PromotionGate MUST deny CRDT/model-lane promotions when base_snapshot_ref, state_vector, schema_id, or expected EventLedger aggregate/version is stale or mismatched. The denial MUST be typed, durable, replayable, and include the current state_vector/base snapshot or recovery hint; stale proposals MUST NOT auto-rebase into authority.

Routing and promotion decisions persist as EventLedger-backed decision artifacts with idempotency key, selected input refs, rejected input refs, validator/operator authority, and trace/span correlation.
Disagreement and stalled progress produce bounded state transitions and explicit recovery/next-action records instead of recursive agent chatter.

ModelLane promotion input MUST include stable sorted input refs, canonical hash basis, selected/rejected refs, validator/operator authority identity, expected EventLedger aggregate/version, base_snapshot_ref, state_vector, schema_id, deterministic tie-break rule, and decision identity.

Negative proof MUST cover duplicate idempotency, stale base, mismatched schema, mismatched aggregate version, direct authority mutation, and reordered input refs producing the same deterministic decision.

After implementation and before READY_FOR_VALIDATION, this MT MUST receive post-implementation adversarial review against the actual diff. Findings must be fixed or converted into explicit lifecycle blocker/missing_resource/proof_status state; the implementer may not self-certify COMPLETED.

acceptance_criteria: A downstream lane can receive previous lane output by ContextBundle or artifact ref.
Message payload artifact refs are replayable after process restart.
ContextBundle records selected, rejected, and unresolved lane outputs.

When a ModelLaneMessage carries a CRDT proposal for shared editable state, the payload artifact MUST include schema_id, document_id, workspace_id, actor_id, actor_kind, lane_id, crdt_site_id, update_seq, Yjs-compatible update_bytes_ref, update_sha256, state_vector, base_snapshot_ref, materialized_projection_hash, replay_metadata, and PromotionGate/ValidationRunner refs. CRDT payloads are pre-promotion evidence only until validated and promoted through EventLedger authority.

ContextBundle handoff entries MUST be typed records, not opaque prompt text: source_lane_id, source_message_id, artifact_ref, artifact_sha256/content_hash, source_kind, authority_state, selection_state selected|rejected|unresolved|superseded, reason_code, reviewer/decision_ref, created_at, and replay_hint. Downstream lanes MUST consume these records by id/ref, and tests MUST prove reconstruction without raw prompt replay.

When a ModelLaneMessage or ContextBundle references Loom-derived context or output, it MUST carry stable Loom refs: workspace_id, block_id, optional source_block_id/target_block_id, artifact_ref when materialized, content_hash/version, and EventLedger/Flight Recorder evidence.

FEMS use is bounded: MemoryPack entries are reviewable, scope-tagged, cloud-safe when sent to cloud lanes, and never treated as unverified authority over current EventLedger/CRDT state. Hidden provider/session memory MUST NOT substitute for MemoryPack.
CRDT handoff preserves state-vector/proposal metadata and requires semantic review/promotion for rich editable surfaces; mechanical merge is not acceptance.

ContextBundle handoff MUST add or extend embedded SurrealDB storage for model-lane handoff selection state with run_id, source_lane_id, source_message_id, artifact_ref, artifact_sha256, selection_state, reason_code, decision_ref, EventLedger event id, and replay query API.
Negative proof MUST fail closed when selected, rejected, unresolved, or superseded artifact refs are missing, hash-mismatched, or not replayable.

After implementation and before READY_FOR_VALIDATION, this MT MUST receive post-implementation adversarial review against the actual diff. Findings must be fixed or converted into explicit lifecycle blocker/missing_resource/proof_status state; the implementer may not self-certify COMPLETED.

PostgreSQL and SQLite MUST provide no connectivity, import, reconciliation, fallback, fixture, cache, migration, or proof path for this MT.

acceptance_criteria: A ModelLaneRun can be reconstructed from canonical run, lane, message, artifact, and status records.
Orphaned subagent lanes are detected and marked with CX-MM-009.
Missing payload refs produce CX-MM-006 with recovery hints.
Replay does not require chat history.

ModelLaneRun recovery MUST persist lane checkpoints containing run_id, lane_id, session_id/model_session_id, status, last_event_ledger_seq, last_message_id, open payload refs, lease_id, idempotency scope, and recovery_state. Replay MUST load the latest checkpoint, apply EventLedger records after that sequence in order, ignore duplicate idempotency keys, and emit typed failure if checkpoint or replay order is missing/corrupt.

MT-007 MUST define and test canonical EventLedger/Flight Recorder event families for RUN_CREATED/RUN_COMPLETED/RUN_FAILED, LANE_PLANNED/LANE_STARTED/LANE_STATUS_CHANGED/LANE_COMPLETED/LANE_FAILED/LANE_CANCELLED/ORPHAN_DETECTED, MESSAGE_RECORDED/PAYLOAD_REF_RECORDED/PAYLOAD_REF_MISSING, RECOVERY_REQUESTED/REPLAY_RECONSTRUCTED/RECOVERY_FAILED. Every family row MUST include run_id, lane_id where applicable, session_id/model_session_id, trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id or span links, wp_id, mt_id, error code, artifact refs, and replay hint.

ModelLane recovery MUST persist and inspect lane leases with lease_id, scope_kind, scope_ref, holder_actor_id, holder_session_id, lease_expires_at_utc, takeover_policy, and release/cancel/failure state. Orphan recovery MUST distinguish active lease, expired lease, cancelled lane, crashed lane, and never-started lane, and must emit durable typed denial/reclaim receipts for takeover or unrecoverable CX-MM-009 paths.

Replay reconstructs run/lane/message/artifact/status/checkpoint state from embedded SurrealDB/EventLedger/ArtifactStore/CRDT records without provider trace history, terminal scrollback, UI rows, Flight Recorder rows, or chat history.

Recovery covers never-started, partial-start, interrupted stream, missing payload, stale CRDT base, orphaned subagent, failed cloud consent, cancelled background process, crashed app, and restart-after-crash paths with typed codes and recovery hints.

Recovery MUST also recreate MT lifecycle/status signaling for claimed_by, blocker, missing_resource, proof_status, hbr_status, ready_for_validation state, last_recovery_event_ref, and last_runtime_status_ref before implementation resumes.

Recovery negative proof MUST cover corrupt checkpoint, EventLedger sequence gap, duplicate idempotency, missing payload ref, stale CRDT base, failed cloud consent, cancelled process, crashed app, and orphaned subagent.
HBR-INT-009 posture MUST use a shared Rust typed record with behavior_id, tier, status, reason, follow_up_ref, and evidence_ref; FR-only evidence must fail.

After implementation and before READY_FOR_VALIDATION, this MT MUST receive post-implementation adversarial review against the actual diff. Findings must be fixed or converted into explicit lifecycle blocker/missing_resource/proof_status state; the implementer may not self-certify COMPLETED.

acceptance_criteria: Debug surface shows run id, lanes, statuses, message counts, last activity, payload errors, and orphan state.
UI can inspect a single ModelLaneMessage payload ref and promotion state.
Visual verification confirms readable layout and no overlapping text.

Debug/visual surface MUST expose trace_id, span_id/parent_span_id or span links, EventLedger event ids, Flight Recorder correlation ids, and per-behavior HBR-INT-009 posture for Flight Recorder/internal_diagnostics/Palmistry. If internal_diagnostics or Palmistry are absent in this worktree, the surface MUST show DEFERRED-with-reason and follow-up hook, not a blank/missing tier.

Diagnostics MUST show, filter, and deep-link run_id, lane_id, message_id, Locus wp_id/mt_id/task_board_id, session_id/model_session_id, context_bundle_id, memory_pack_ref/hash, artifact_ref, Loom block refs when present, Flight Recorder/EventLedger ids, promotion/validator decision refs, and recovery hints. Visual proof MUST compare rendered rows against canonical backend counts and refs.
The WP does not name or rename the internal viewing tool; it consumes the approved name when available and otherwise implements backend-equivalent navigation without blocking state recovery.
Legacy app/src swarm components may be inspected only for parity/reference; implementation authority is native Rust/backend state and native UI surfaces.

All GUI/debug implementation and proof for this MT must be Rust native egui/Argus or Rust backend TraceProjection. TypeScript, React, Tauri/WebView, and npm tests are forbidden as implementation or proof authority.

Implement a Rust-native diagnostics surface with provisional contract id native_swarm_lane_diagnostics until the separate naming worktree provides an alias. It MUST register a real SwarmLaneDiagnostics pane/factory instead of placeholder fallback and expose stable author_id targets for run rows, lane rows, message rows, filters, deep links, payload/promotion drilldowns, and recovery actions.

acceptance_criteria: There is one in-product internal UserManual surface for this WP; if legacy ModelManual paths/names exist, they are updated as aliases rather than forked into a second manual.

The UserManual covers ModelLaneRun, ModelLane, ModelLaneMessage, ContextBundle handoff, artifact refs, local/cloud/CLI/human/subagent/validator lane launch, cloud ProjectionPlan/ConsentReceipt, advisory-to-authority promotion, recovery/orphan/replay, diagnostics, validation harnesses, and backend navigation introduced by this WP.

Each entry explains purpose, usage path, startup/invocation command or IPC/API path when applicable, expected inputs/outputs, affected tools/features/primitives, durable authority source, failure modes, recovery steps, and verification proof.

Each observable behavior entry links to Flight Recorder/EventLedger evidence and records the HBR-INT-009 posture for Flight Recorder, internal_diagnostics, and Palmistry as WIRED, NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason, or DEFERRED-with-reason.
Palmistry/internal_diagnostics absence in this worktree is recorded as DEFERRED-with-reason plus the integration follow-up; it is never silently skipped.

UserManual self-consistency proof verifies named commands, IPC channels, backend navigation paths, schema names, storage/event contracts, and diagnostic surfaces exist or are explicitly tagged as roadmap/deferred.

MT-011 proof MUST include a machine-readable per-behavior UserManual coverage matrix keyed by behavior_id/schema/event_family, with columns for implemented command/API/IPC, EventLedger/Flight Recorder evidence path, internal_diagnostics posture, Palmistry posture, and self-consistency result. Keyword grep is supporting evidence only, not acceptance proof.
Every MT that changes product behavior has a corresponding UserManual delta in the same implementation change, and MT-011 verifies coverage by behavior inventory rather than by file-name guesswork.
UserManual entries link each behavior to EventLedger event family/aggregate refs, Flight Recorder trace/span refs, backend navigation paths, diagnostic tier posture, and recovery proof commands.

Palmistry/internal_diagnostics integration is recorded exactly as WIRED, NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason, or DEFERRED-with-reason per behavior; this MT must not claim Palmistry is implemented in this worktree unless product code proves it.
MT-011 owns WP-wide UserManual coverage audit and freshness/self-consistency proof. It does not replace the same-change UserManual obligation in MT-002 through MT-010.

Define and implement Rust-owned coverage matrix schema hsk.user_manual_behavior_coverage@1 generated from ModelLane schema/event/API registries. Required columns: behavior_id, schema_id or event_family, command/API/IPC id, UserManual entry id/version, EventLedger/Flight Recorder evidence path, internal_diagnostics posture, Palmistry posture, self-consistency result, deferred reason, and follow_up_ref.

Coverage proof MUST fail when any behavior lacks a UserManual entry, EventLedger/FR evidence, internal_diagnostics posture, Palmistry posture, runtime route/schema existence, or self-consistency result. Keyword grep is supporting evidence only and cannot be a proof target.

After implementation and before READY_FOR_VALIDATION, this MT MUST receive post-implementation adversarial review against the actual diff. Findings must be fixed or converted into explicit lifecycle blocker/missing_resource/proof_status state; the implementer may not self-certify COMPLETED.

The pane lets the operator select a model lane kind and concrete model for LOCAL and CLOUD via the spec model-selection mechanism / Work Profiles (spec 4.3.9.4.4; the operator-visible selection UI is built here), and select a folder/worktree/project as the session working location by reusing existing workspace surfaces (project_tree/project_tabs), not a bespoke picker.

Same-change in-product UserManual coverage for the operator chat/launch surface (purpose, model+worktree selection, launch, capture, recovery, Flight Recorder linkage).
