MT-003 made the embedded ModelRuntime the default local LlmClient path, but the embedded model-load path (llm/boot.rs build_default_local_client -> CandleRuntime/LlamaCppRuntime::load) has ZERO SandboxAdapter / ProcessOwnershipLedger wiring (the boxed path is the separate SandboxModelRuntime used only by the swarm factory), which violates master-spec-v02.197 3.6.2/4.6.1 (HARD; MUST fail the 5.6 HBR gate). Additionally DisabledLlmClient returns an error without emitting a Flight Recorder event (pre-existing, mod.rs), against 4.2.3.2(3). acceptance_criteria: For the default embedded-model load path (llm/boot.rs build_default_local_client), SandboxAdapter boxing is NOT_APPLICABLE when Candle/llama.cpp is loaded as an in-process Rust library with no OS child or guest. The enforced obligation is artifact integrity plus ProcessOwnershipLedger START on load and STOP on unload (master-spec 4.6.1), using os_pid=null and os_pid_absent_reason=in_process_library_load_no_os_process; any actual spawned model process remains SandboxAdapter-owned. Verify with a REAL Candle CPU model load (feature candle-runtime-engine).

DisabledLlmClient (and any fail-closed error return on the default LLM path) emits a Flight Recorder event carrying the disabled/error reason so 'every call emits a Flight Recorder event' (master-spec 4.2.3.2(3)) holds on the error path too; a test proves the FR event is emitted.

The LocalModelRuntimeLlmClient::embedding() path (added by MT-003) emits a Flight Recorder event with trace_id/model_id (embeddings carry no TokenUsage, so record the embedding-appropriate FR shape) so the embedding lane is Flight-Recorder-correlatable per 4.2.3.2(3)/11.5; a test proves emission. (Deferred from MT-003 post-review: embedding() currently carries EmbeddingRequest.trace_id but does not emit, matching the removed OllamaAdapter parity.)

A real-load runtime proof against the production-composed embedded authorities shows an exact-scope ProcessOwnershipLedger START row on load and matching STOP row on unload for the default embedded model, canonical kernel EventLedger linkage, one cloned SurrealStorage namespace across registry/lifecycle/restart reads, and no bare std::process::Command model spawn.

acceptance_criteria: The default embedded-model registration is exposed through one injected durable registry surface that enumerates UUIDv7, display_name, base_model_tag, artifact identity, capabilities, runtime binding, lifecycle state, and current active selection without creating a duplicate authority island.

original_scope.origin: Operator request 2026-07-02: there is no login screen or key-entry surface for cloud models. The operator personally does NOT use BYOK (they use Claude Code + GPT via subscription PLANS through the official CLI bridge), but BYOK MUST be AVAILABLE for other users. WP-KERNEL-004 already built the backends (model_runtime/cloud/openai_byok.rs, anthropic_byok.rs, official_cli_bridge.rs, cli_bridge_runtime.rs, secrets_vault.rs OS-keychain, consent_gate.rs); what is missing is the operator-facing configuration UI that reaches them.

acceptance_criteria: A native egui settings surface (in the existing Settings Swarm/Models section) lets the operator configure cloud model access. It is reachable from the operator settings and Argus-inspectable with stable author_id targets.

CLI-BRIDGE / PLAN path (operator's primary): the surface shows auth/login status for the official-CLI providers Claude Code and GPT/Codex (logged-in / not-logged-in / expired) and, where the provider's official path allows, guides or triggers the provider's own login. It uses the provider's subscription-plan auth via the official CLI bridge (official_cli_bridge.rs) and stores NO Handshake-held credential for this path. No unofficial automation.

BYOK path (available, not required): a per-provider API-key entry (Anthropic, OpenAI) that stores the key ONLY in the existing OS-keychain secrets vault (secrets_vault.rs / keyring); the key is never written to logs, Flight Recorder, EventLedger, or plaintext. The CloudLane/BYOK backend (openai_byok.rs / anthropic_byok.rs, MT-006 boundary) consumes the stored key. A negative test proves the key never appears in logs/FR/plaintext.
Gemini is NOT offered as a provider in the surface (CLI deprecating).
The configured/authed cloud lanes are enumerable so the MT-012 operator model-picker can list available cloud lanes; an un-authed / un-keyed provider shows as unavailable rather than erroring.

Same-change in-product UserManual coverage (how to log in via plan / enter a BYOK key / which providers are supported); HBR-INT-009 posture recorded; Flight Recorder/EventLedger evidence where the surface affects lane launch or consent.
Pre- and post-implementation adversarial review (incl. a secrets-leakage lens) before READY_FOR_VALIDATION; implementer does not self-certify COMPLETED.

acceptance_criteria: ModelCapabilities exposes supports_embedding and embedding_dimension as an MT-016 product extension; registration rejects inconsistent states such as supports_embedding=false with a dimension or supports_embedding=true without a positive dimension.

A second local embedding model can be configured independently from HANDSHAKE_LOCAL_MODEL_PATH, loaded through the embedded local runtime, registered in the same shared ModelRegistry, marked ready, and exposed in ModelCatalog as distinct from the chat model.

ModelCatalog exposes machine-readable embedding capability fields and a helper that selects a ready embedding-capable local model matching LoomSearchV2's canonical 768-dimensional index; chat-only and wrong-dimension models are ignored.
LocalModelRuntimeLlmClient rejects embedding calls for registered models whose capabilities do not declare supports_embedding, so adding a UUIDv7 registration is not enough to fake embedding support.

LoomSearchV2 reindex and search resolve the embedding-capable model from the catalog instead of hard-coding llm.profile().model_id; embedding calls use the selected model's per-boot routing UUIDv7, while persisted/search `embedding_model` values use the stable embedding-space key derived from artifact sha256 + embedding dimension.
LoomSearchV2 vector scoring and facets compare only rows whose stored embedding_model matches the query embedding model, preventing cross-model embedding-space contamination.
When no matching dedicated embedding model is configured, LoomSearchV2 degrades to keyword/trigram without calling the chat model for embeddings, fabricating vectors, or hard-erroring.
Existing MT-014 dimension mismatch degrade-not-error behavior remains intact and surfaces the typed dim-mismatch reason.

Same-change UserManual page/tool/behavior coverage documents purpose, startup/config variables, routing workflow, expected inputs/outputs, FR/EventLedger evidence, HBR-INT-009 posture, common failures, and recovery.
Pre- and post-implementation adversarial review completed; implementer may move MT-016 only to READY_FOR_VALIDATION, never COMPLETED.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: SingleRun cloud consent is real run-scoped authority, not dead metadata: the plan and receipt bind the canonical target set, each covered lane preflights under the same run and exact resource scope, revocation cancels every covered lane with per-lane CX-MM-007 canonical-event evidence, and replay/revocation are idempotent without broadening SingleLane.
AC-2: CRDT snapshot compaction preserves update hashes, state vectors, replay metadata, promotion evidence, canonical-event links, and bounded replay across restart.
AC-3: CRDT state vectors are derived from real update bytes and converge across permitted replay order and duplicate delivery; no hardcoded vector can satisfy proof.

AC-4: Real mid-stream cancellation at chunk and tool-call boundaries preserves the committed prefix, terminalizes the lane once, rejects late messages/tools/artifacts/telemetry, and records durable canonical evidence.

AC-5: The backend diagnostics producer and native deserializer share a pinned serialized contract proven through a generated artifact and live route; renamed, missing, extra-critical, stale, or malformed fields fail honestly rather than passing separate fixture suites.

AC-6: UserManual self-consistency computes real page, tool, schema, route, compiled-symbol, event, and diagnostic checks and returns structured consistent/inconsistent evidence rather than a constant label.
AC-7: Every internal runtime_surface_id resolves to a compile-anchored symbol and every route resolves to the canonical router; deleted or renamed surfaces fail coverage.

AC-8: ModelLane, operator-chat, cloud-access, embedded-model, and dedicated-embedding matrices are registry-derived or explicitly disclose non-authoritative gaps; self-referential expected sets cannot prove coverage.

AC-9: All six routing policies drive distinct authorized executable waves with durable lineage, bounded retries, cancellation, fencing, idempotency, outbox delivery, crash recovery, and content-sensitive adjudication.

AC-10: Recovery defines and proves post-checkpoint lease semantics: current leases are surfaced or reconciled without moving the replay bound, and stale owners cannot renew, release, or mutate current claims.
AC-11: A cross-platform in-memory-vault canary proof and the platform vault proof establish no secret disclosure; unsupported platforms cannot produce a zero-test success.
AC-12: The frontend key-entry buffer and client transport retain zeroizing secret ownership through submit, error, clear, and drop without logging or serializing the canary outside the request body.

AC-13: Unready local models and unavailable governed sessions are visible but disabled; launch requires canonical owner/parent lineage; no hardcoded session identity or duplicate inventory implementation remains.

AC-14: The production embedded-model boot path cannot access an artifact without a durable ProcessOwnershipLedger; start/stop, shutdown drain, reclaim, exact scope, and restart use the same cloned SurrealStorage.
AC-15: UserManual page detail and same-slug legacy bridge expose the canonical manual_version consistently. UserManual remains product-global and HBR-PRIV NOT_APPLICABLE.

AC-16: The production operator-chat factory wires runtime activity recording while suppressing duplicate agent activity, proving exactly one canonical event and one Flight Recorder event per activity under replay, restart, cancellation, and failure.

original_lifecycle.blocker: Parfit owns the active ModelLane, CRDT provider, composition, and shared test surfaces. Surreal proposal primitives exist but have no production caller, the current proposal service and reusable helper still use superseded authority, and no coherent Surreal MT-018 suite proves scope, hash separation, canonical-event atomicity, or restart continuity.
original_lifecycle.missing_resource: A production proposal lifecycle composed through the same cloned SurrealStorage as ModelLane and CRDT updates/snapshots; exact five-field proposal/update/snapshot/receipt authority; independently validated proposal-diff and Yjs-update hashes; coherent positive, replay, concurrency, stale, revoked, mixed-scope, incomplete-row, and one-field-mismatch tests.
original_lifecycle.proof_status: V6_NOT_RUN_BLOCKED. V5 relational and mixed-suite results are explicitly superseded provenance and are not active V6 proof.
original_lifecycle.hbr_status: HBR-PRIV and HBR-INT remain blocked for proposal, CRDT update, snapshot, lease, message, and receipt resources pending coherent same-storage runtime proof.

original_scope.summary: Preserve the approved-proposal diff-hash versus Yjs-update-hash distinction while proving proposal-backed CRDT ModelLane admission, replay, denial, and restart against one embedded Surreal authority.
forbidden_paths: Parfit-owned ModelLane facade/provider/schema/composition and shared CRDT tests
product source and product tests in this contract-only pass
relational bridge, fixtures, active proof, or alternate-authority path
disabled-code proof, vacuous targets, raw-row shortcuts, or weakened admission gates
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Proposal diff_sha256 is computed over canonical approved-diff bytes; Yjs update_sha256 is computed independently over persisted Yjs v1 update bytes. The values remain distinct invariants, are never equated, and are independently recomputed before admission and replay.

AC-2: An approved and applied proposal binds to the real scoped update by applied_update_id while applied_update_sha256 remains the proposal's approved-diff hash; ModelLane separately verifies the cited update row's update_sha256, Yjs decoding, state-vector advance, causal chain, and terminal identity.

AC-3: Proposal record, approve/reject/promote transition, applied-update binding, CRDT update, snapshot, lease, ModelLane message, and denial/admission receipt use exact owner_account_id, actor_principal_id, authenticated_session_id, access_space_id, and workspace_id predicates on both resource and linked canonical-event rows.

AC-4: Scope derivation never widens. Mixed-source proposal inputs are refused rather than unioned, and each one-field mismatch, stale context, revoked context, incomplete row, malformed ref, or mixed-scope linked event returns no resource metadata and performs zero mutation.

AC-5: Every durable proposal/update/snapshot/lease/message/receipt mutation appends or links the canonical kernel EventLedger atomically in the same Surreal transaction; no domain-local audit island or event-without-resource/resource-without-event state is admissible.

AC-6: Proposal, ModelLane, CRDT update/snapshot, lease, receipt, and replay providers receive clones of one injected SurrealStorage namespace/database. Restart reopens that same authority and preserves both hashes, applied identity, canonical-event links, ordering, and idempotency.

AC-7: A real Proposal-kind ModelLaneMessage backed by an approved applied proposal, real persisted Yjs update, causally prior snapshot, active exact-scope lease, matching actor/session/trace/document identities, and complete CRDT fields is admitted and replays unchanged.

AC-8: Fabricated update/proposal refs, Yjs byte-hash mismatch, approved-diff mismatch, proposal bound to another real update, stale/unrelated vector or snapshot, wrong actor/session/trace/document, unapproved/rejected review state, missing applied binding, duplicate conflict, and tampered linked event all fail closed with stable denial taxonomy.

AC-9: One reusable Surreal admissible-CRDT helper constructs all positive authority only through production APIs and is reused by the MT-002, MT-005, MT-009, and MT-018 positive and negative proof surfaces; no raw insert may manufacture a green posture.

AC-10: The original provisional decision remains explicit: applied_update_sha256 names approved-diff integrity, applied_update_id names the real Yjs update, and the Yjs row owns its independent update_sha256. Any specification enrichment must preserve this separation.
original_scope.risk_if_missed: The proposal path can become false-green by equating unrelated hashes, accepting a cross-scope or stale proposal, linking an update without canonical event integrity, reopening another database after restart, or proving only a hand-built test row that production cannot create.

original_scope.root_cause: Historical defect, now remediated in source: restart-orphan surfacing formerly ran only at boot and a live-instance Official-CLI orphan could remain open until a later boot. Current source composes a bounded boot pass, periodic re-surfacing, and an exact-owner running-app hook over one injected SurrealStorage.
forbidden_paths: weakening the pid + creation-time + exe-sha256 process identity fence
fabricating a STOP from unproven kill evidence
any relational database implementation or compatibility path
acceptance_criteria: F1 (MAJOR): a same-instance mid-run official-CLI (no model_lanes row) orphan whose process terminated/reap-failed is reaped by the RUNNING app (staleness task or a CLI-session-end reclaim trigger), not only at next boot; add a runtime proof.

F2 (MAJOR): after the bounded inline boot pass, every periodic tick re-runs the same restart-orphan reconcile before stale-lane reclaim so skipped, failed-open, or newly visible orphans are retried without another boot; prove the shared path and bounded cancellation.

F3 (operator decision): resilient boot is fail-open only for KillOutcome::Failed, leaving the row open, claim released, fence cleared, no false STOP, processes_kill_failed surfaced, and periodic retry scheduled. Store/surfacing errors and boot timeout fail closed; prove both postures.

F4 (MINOR): HANDSHAKE_STARTUP_RECOVERY_ONLY=1 composes ProcessReclaimRuntime from the same injected SurrealStorage, runs the bounded restart-orphan pass, surfaces its report, drains reclaim and writer, and only then returns; prove this production branch.
F5 (MINOR): docs and counters remain truthful: processes_reclaimed counts only Killed or KilledPendingStop, processes_kill_failed counts Failed, and no failure path fabricates a STOP.
F6 (MINOR): boot and periodic restart reconciliation use one shared implementation with caller-selected error policy and cancellation, and no in-progress sweep reclaim error is silently dropped.

F7 (NIT): production registry, with_registry kill dispatch, production_with_lease timeout, real child termination, and PID-generation mismatch are exercised without weakening the identity fence or accepting a zero-test filter.

P-1 (PREREQUISITE, before F1/F2): stale_sessions excludes a null parent_session_id without aborting the scan; an embedded-Surreal regression test proves a session-less adapter row cannot suppress a genuinely reclaimable sibling session.

P-2 (PREREQUISITE, before F1): the running-app reap can actually claim the target rows - either parent_session_id is populated for auth-status/preflight/login CLI children, or a claim-by-process_uuid path exists. The F1 proof asserts the exact process_uuid appears in processes_reclaimed with KillOutcome::Killed, never merely is_ok().

P-3 (PREREQUISITE, before F1): SurrealProcessLedgerStore performs an exact single-row claim with all five ResourceScope predicates, and an embedded-Surreal test proves a sibling row's reclaim metadata is unchanged.

P-4 (PREREQUISITE, before F2): the periodic restart pass cannot kill a live instance's healthy children - the UDP lease is not released before process exit (or only after proving zero open rows), the dead-owner probe requires two samples at least one scan interval apart, and the claim path carries an explicit owner_runtime_instance_id predicate.

P-5: the reclaim hook is invoked only from record_stop's two branches and the terminate_and_collect reap failure, never from Drop; it runs after the STOP permit is released, via the wait_stop_durability_blocking thread + current_thread-runtime pattern, under an explicit timeout well below 30s, and guards lifecycle.is_none().

P-6 (PROOF HONESTY, applies to every proof command in this MT): each --exact proof asserts a non-zero executed-test count or greps --nocapture output for the test name, because cargo exits 0 when an --exact filter matches nothing.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: All five named production_factory tests remain present under their exact names, are not ignored, and pass both individually and as part of the unfiltered production_factory module on the same frozen source revision.

AC-6: Terminal swarm events are written atomically with a canonical kernel EventLedger receipt in the same Surreal transaction. Identical retries are deterministic, conflicting reuse is denied, and no domain-local audit island, event-without-outbox, or outbox-without-event state is accepted.

original_scope.summary: Make real-SurrealDB integration-test namespace/database teardown bounded, exact, and reliably leak-free for the WP-1 process-ledger and real-process lifecycle suites.
original_scope.root_cause: Sequential cleanup of many task-owned database scopes under one aggregate deadline lets one slow cleanup consume the budget for later scopes. Each disposable SurrealDB namespace/database needs its own bounded cleanup opportunity and independent canonical reread.
forbidden_paths: PostgreSQL or SQLite connection, fixture, migration, fallback, or proof behavior
Broad namespace, database-pattern, or server deletion
Suppressing cleanup failures without a bounded observable receipt
Stopping SurrealDB or any process not started by this MT
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Cleanup operates only on the exact task-owned namespace/database scopes returned by the WP017 MT-341 SurrealDB test allocator; no wildcard, server-wide, or foreign-scope deletion is permitted.

AC-3: Best-effort process-exit cleanup remains non-panicking and observable, while normal per-test cleanup happens early enough that process exit is only a recovery fence.

AC-4: Fresh full process-ledger and real-process lifecycle suites pass against Handshake-managed SurrealDB and an independent official-SDK canonical reread proves zero namespace/database scopes allocated by those runs remain.
AC-5: Failure-path tests prove an individual cleanup timeout/error does not prevent later exact scopes from receiving cleanup attempts and does not target foreign namespaces/databases.
